A lute is any plucked string instrument with a neck and a deep round back enclosing a hollow cavity, usually with a sound hole or opening in the body. It may be either fretted or unfretted.
A mandolin is a stringed musical instrument in the lute family and is generally plucked with a pick.
A wind instrument is a musical instrument that needs air blown through it to create sound.
A brass instrument is a musical instrument that produces sound by sympathetic vibration of air in a tubular resonator in sympathy with the vibration of the player's lips.

The trombone is a musical instrument in the brass family. As with all brass instruments, sound is produced when the player's lips vibrate inside a mouthpiece, causing the air column inside the instrument to vibrate.

The tuba is a large brass instrument in the bass-to-contrabass range. It is a member of the valved bugles, a large and diverse family of instruments characterized by their wide conical bore and use of valves to alter pitch.
Woodwind instruments are a family of musical instruments within the greater category of wind instruments. Common examples include flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, and saxophone.

The recorder is a family of woodwind musical instruments and a member of the family of duct flutes that includes tin whistles and flageolets. It is the most prominent duct flute in the western classical tradition.

The Western concert flute can refer to the common C concert flute or to the family of transverse flutes to which the C flute belongs. Almost all are made of metal or wood, or a combination of the two.
A music genre is a conventional category that identifies some pieces of music as belonging to a shared tradition or set of conventions.
A Christmas carol is a carol, a song or hymn, on the theme of Christmas, traditionally sung at Christmas itself or during the surrounding Christmas and holiday season.
A protest song is a song that is associated with a movement for protest and social change and hence part of the broader category of topical songs. It may be folk, classical, or commercial in genre.
Classical music is a tradition of art music in the Western world, considered to be distinct from Western folk music or popular music.
Chamber music is a form of classical music that is composed for a small group of instruments, traditionally a group that could fit in a palace chamber or a large room.

In classical music, a fugue is a contrapuntal, polyphonic compositional technique in two or more voices, built on a subject that is introduced at the beginning in imitation, which recurs frequently throughout the course of the composition.

Medieval music encompasses the sacred and secular music of Western Europe during the Middle Ages. It is the first and longest major era of Western classical music and is followed by the Renaissance music.
Gregorian chant is the central tradition of Western plainchant, a form of monophonic, unaccompanied sacred song in Latin of the Roman Catholic Church.
Renaissance music is traditionally understood to cover European music of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, later than the Renaissance era as it is understood in other disciplines.

Baroque music refers to the period or dominant style of Western classical music composed from about sixteen hundred to seventeen fifty. The Baroque style followed the Renaissance period, and was followed in turn by the Classical period after a short transition.
The Classical period was an era of classical music between roughly seventeen fifty and eighteen twenty. The classical period falls between the Baroque and Romantic periods.
Romantic music is a stylistic movement in Western Classical music associated with the period of the nineteenth century commonly referred to as the Romantic era.

Twentieth-century classical music is Western art music that was written in the twentieth century. Musical style diverged during the twentieth century as it never had previously, so this century was without a dominant style.
Contemporary classical music is European art music composed close to the present day.
Arabic music is the music of the Arab world with all its diverse music styles and genres.
The music of Africa is vast and highly diverse, with different regions and nations maintaining distinct musical traditions.
Gamelan is the traditional ensemble music of the Javanese, Sundanese, and Balinese peoples of Indonesia, made up predominantly of percussive instruments.
Indian classical music is the classical music of the Indian subcontinent.
Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with South India, including the modern Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

Hindustani classical music, also known as North Indian classical music or Shastriya Sangeet, is the classical music of the Indian subcontinent's northern regions. It is played on instruments like the veena, sitar and sarod.
The music of China consists of many distinct traditions, often specifically originating with one of the country's various ethnic groups.
Bossa nova is a relaxed style of samba developed in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is mainly characterized by a calm syncopated rhythm with chords and fingerstyle mimicking the beat of a samba groove.
Ragtime, also spelled rag-time or rag time, is a musical style noted for its syncopated or ragged rhythm. It originated in African American communities in the late nineteenth century.

Country music, also known as country and western or simply country, is a music genre originating from the United States. It is known for its ballads and dance tunes, identifiable by both traditional lyrics and harmonies accompanied by banjos, mandolins, fiddles, harmonicas, and many types of guitar.

Disco is a genre of dance music and a subculture that emerged from the United States' urban nightlife scene. Its sound is typified by four-on-the-floor beats, syncopated basslines, string sections, brass and horns, electric pianos, synthesizers, and electric rhythm guitars.
Electronic music broadly is a group of music genres that employ electronic musical instruments, circuitry-based music technology and software, or general-purpose electronics in its creation.
Electronic dance music, also referred to as dance music or club music, is a broad range of percussive electronic music genres originally made for nightclubs, raves, and festivals.
Funk is a music genre that originated in African-American communities when musicians created a rhythmic, danceable new form of music through a mixture of various music genres.
Hip-hop, also known as rap music or simply rap, is a genre of popular music that emerged alongside an associated subculture in New York City.

Rapping is an artistic form of vocal delivery and emotive expression that incorporates rhyme, rhythmic speech, and commonly street vernacular. It is usually performed over a backing beat or musical accompaniment.
Pop music, or simply pop, is a genre of popular music that originated in its modern form in the United States and the United Kingdom.
J-pop, an abbreviated form of Japanese popular music, is a form of popular music that entered the musical mainstream of Japan. In Japan it is known simply as pops.

K-pop is a form of popular music originating in South Korea. The music genre that the term is used to refer to colloquially emerged as a form of youth subculture, with Korean musicians influenced by Western dance music, hip-hop, R&B and rock.
Reggae is a music genre that originated in Jamaica. The term also refers to the modern popular music of Jamaica and its diaspora.
Rhythm and blues, frequently abbreviated as R&B, is a genre of popular music that originated within African American communities.

Soul music is a popular music genre that originated in African-American communities throughout the United States. Catchy rhythms, stressed by handclaps and extemporaneous body movements, are an important hallmark of soul.
Rock music is a genre of popular music that originated in the United States as rock and roll.
Alternative rock, also known as alternative music, alt-rock or simply alternative, is a category of rock music that evolved from the independent music underground.

Heavy metal, or simply metal, is a genre of rock music that developed largely in the United Kingdom and United States. Heavy metal bands developed a thick, monumental sound characterized by distorted guitars.
Punk rock, or simply punk, is a genre of rock music. Rooted in rock and roll and garage rock, punk bands rejected the overproduction and corporate nature of mainstream arena rock.
Rock and roll is a genre of popular music that evolved in the United States. The origins of rock and roll are rooted in a blending of African-American musical genres, mainly rhythm and blues.
Salsa is a style of dance music mainly influenced by Caribbean traditions and music from Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, and other countries such as Colombia and Venezuela.
Samba is a broad term for many of the rhythms that compose the better known Brazilian music genres that originated in the Afro-Brazilian communities of Bahia.
The performing arts are arts such as music, dance, and drama that are performed for an audience. They are different from the visual arts, which produce physical or static objects.

An audience is a group of people who participate in a show or encounter a work of art, literature, theatre, music, video games, or academics in any medium. Audience members participate in different ways in different kinds of art.
Acrobatics is the performance of human feats of balance, agility, and motor coordination. Acrobatic skills are used in performing arts, sporting events, and martial arts.

A mime artist, or simply mime, is a kind of performer who uses mime, also called pantomime, by acting or entertaining through the use of body motions without speech, as a theatrical medium or as a performance art.

Performance art is an artwork or art installation in the art world where the artist is present in the work. It may be witnessed live or through documentation, spontaneously developed or written, and is traditionally presented to a public in a fine art context in an interdisciplinary mode.
Choreography is the art of designing sequences of movements of physical bodies in which motion or form or both are specified. Choreography may also refer to the design itself.

Ballroom dance is a set of partner dances, which are enjoyed both socially and competitively around the world, mostly because of its performance and entertainment aspects. Ballroom dancing is also widely enjoyed on stage, film, and television.

Tango is a partner and social dance that originated in the eighteen eighties along the Río de la Plata, the natural border between Argentina and Uruguay. The tango was born in the impoverished port areas of these countries from a combination of Argentine Milonga, Spanish-Cuban Habanera, and Uruguayan Candombe celebrations.

Belly dance is a Middle Eastern dance that originated in Egypt, which features movements of the hips and torso. A Western-coined exonym, it is also referred to as Middle Eastern dance or Arabic dance.
Bharatanatyam is an Indian classical dance form that comes from Tamil Nadu, India. It expresses South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideas, particularly of Shaivism and in general of Hinduism.

Flamenco is an art form based on the various folkloric music traditions of southern Spain, developed within the gitano subculture of the Andalusian region, and also having historical presence in Extremadura and Murcia.
A folk dance is a dance that reflects the life of the people of a certain country or region. Not all ethnic dances are folk dances.
Hip-hop dance is a range of street dance styles primarily performed to hip-hop music or that have evolved as part of hip-hop culture.
Jazz dance is a performance dance and style that arose in the United States in the early twentieth century. Jazz dance may allude to vernacular jazz, Broadway or dramatic jazz.

Modern dance is a broad genre of western concert or theatrical dance which includes dance styles such as ballet, folk, ethnic, religious, and social dancing; and primarily arose out of Europe and the United States in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Improvisational theatre, often called improvisation, improv, or impro in British English, is the form of theatre, often comedy, in which most or all of what is performed is unplanned or unscripted, created spontaneously by the performers.

Musical theatre is a form of theatrical performance that combines songs, spoken dialogue, acting and dance. The story and emotional content of a musical are communicated through words, music, movement and technical aspects of the entertainment as an integrated whole.

Stagecraft is a technical skill in theatrical, film, and video production. It includes constructing and rigging scenery; hanging and focusing of lighting; fabrication and procurement of costumes; make-up; stage management; audio engineering; and procurement of props.
Comedy is a genre of dramatic works intended to be humorous or amusing by inducing laughter, especially in theatre, film, stand-up comedy, television, radio, books, or any other entertainment medium.

Commedia dell'arte was an early form of professional theatre, originating from Italian theatre, that was popular throughout Europe between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries. It was formerly called Italian comedy in English and is also known as commedia alla maschera.
A joke is a display of humour in which words are used within a specific and well-defined narrative structure to make people laugh and is usually not meant to be interpreted literally.
A parody is a creative work designed to imitate, comment on, and/or mock its subject by means of satirical or ironic imitation.
Stand-up comedy is an art form that involves a stand-up comic and an audience. Comics perform on a stage and deliver humorous and satirical monologues, sometimes incorporating physical acts.

Broadway theatre is a theatre genre that consists of the theatrical performances presented in professional theaters, each with five hundred or more seats, in the Theater District and Lincoln Center along Broadway, in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.

West End theatre is mainstream professional theatre staged in the large theatres in and near the West End of London. West End theatre represents the highest level of commercial theatre in the United Kingdom.

Kabuki is a classical form of Japanese theatre, mixing dramatic performance with traditional dance. Kabuki theatre is known for its heavily stylised performances, its glamorous, highly decorated costumes, and for the elaborate kumadori make-up worn by some of its performers.
Noh is a major form of classical Japanese dance-drama. It is Japan's oldest major theater art that is still regularly performed today.
Peking opera, or Beijing opera, is the dominant form of Chinese opera, which combines instrumental music, vocal performance, miming, martial arts, dance and acrobatics.

A theatrical culture flourished in ancient Greece. At its centre was the city-state of Athens, which became a significant cultural, political, and religious place during this period, and the theatre was institutionalised there as part of a festival called the Dionysia, which honoured the god Dionysus.

Academic art, academicism, or academism, is a style of painting and sculpture produced under the influence of European academies of art. This method extended its influence throughout the Western world over several centuries, from its origins in Italy in the mid-sixteenth century, until its dissipation in the early twentieth century.

Ancient Greek art is the visual and applied arts, as well as the architecture, produced by the Hellenes or Greek peoples from the start of the Iron Age to the Hellenistic period, ending with Roman conquest of Greece at the Battle of Corinth.

The Baroque is a Western style of architecture, music, dance, painting, sculpture, poetry, and other arts that flourished from the early sixteen hundreds until the seventeen fifties. It followed Renaissance art and Mannerism and preceded the Rococo and Neoclassical styles.
Classicism, in the arts, refers generally to a high regard for a classical period, classical antiquity in the Western tradition, as setting standards for taste which the classicists seek to emulate.

The Empire style is an early nineteenth-century design movement in architecture, furniture, other decorative arts, and the visual arts, representing the second phase of Neoclassicism. It flourished during the Consulate and the First French Empire periods, although its life span lasted until the late eighteen twenties.

Gothic art was a style of medieval art that developed in Northern France out of Romanesque art in the twelfth century, led by the concurrent development of Gothic architecture. It spread to all of Western Europe, and much of Northern, Southern and Central Europe, never quite effacing more classical styles in Italy.
Hellenistic art is the art of the Hellenistic period generally taken to begin with the death of Alexander the Great and end with the conquest of the Greek world by the Romans.

Mannerism is a style in European art that emerged in the later years of the Italian High Renaissance around fifteen twenty, spreading by about fifteen thirty and lasting until about the end of the sixteenth century in Italy, when the Baroque style largely replaced it.
In the history of art, prehistoric art is all art produced in preliterate, prehistorical cultures.

In archaeology, rock art refers to human-made markings placed on natural surfaces, typically vertical stone surfaces. A high proportion of surviving historic and prehistoric rock art is found in caves or partly enclosed rock shelters; this type also may be called cave art or parietal art.

Renaissance art is the painting, sculpture, and decorative arts of the period of European history known as the Renaissance, which emerged as a distinct style in Italy in about fourteen hundred, in parallel with developments which occurred in philosophy, literature, music, science, and technology.

Rococo, less commonly Roccoco, is a Western style of architecture, art, and decoration that emerged in France in the seventeen thirties as a reaction against the Louis XIV style. It is characterized by extensive ornamentation, fluid curves, asymmetry, and a smaller scale designed to foster intimacy.

The art of Ancient Rome, and the territories of its Republic and later Empire, includes architecture, painting, sculpture and mosaic work. Luxury objects in metal-work, gem engraving, ivory carvings, and glass are sometimes considered to be minor forms of Roman art, although they were not considered as such at the time.

Romanesque art is the art of Europe from approximately the year one thousand to the rise of the Gothic style in the twelfth century, or later depending on region. The preceding period is known as the Pre-Romanesque period.

Modern art includes artistic work produced during the period extending roughly from the eighteen sixties to the nineteen seventies, and denotes the styles and philosophies of the art produced during that era. The term is usually associated with art in which the traditions of the past have been thrown aside in a spirit of experimentation.
Abstract expressionism in the United States emerged as a distinct art movement in the aftermath of World War II.
Art Deco, short for the French Arts décoratifs, is a style of visual arts, architecture, and product design that first appeared in Paris just before World War I.
Art Nouveau is an international style of art, architecture, and applied art, especially the decorative arts. It was often inspired by natural forms such as the sinuous curves of plants and flowers.

The Arts and Crafts movement was an international trend in the decorative and fine arts that developed earliest and most fully in the British Isles and subsequently spread across the British Empire and to the rest of Europe and North America.

In the arts and literature, the term avant-garde identifies an experimental genre or work of art, and the artist who created it, which usually is aesthetically innovative, whilst initially being ideologically unacceptable to the artistic establishment of the time.

Expressionism is a modernist movement, initially in poetry and painting, originating in Northern Europe around the beginning of the twentieth century. Its typical trait is to present the world solely from a subjective perspective, distorting it radically for emotional effect in order to evoke moods or ideas.

Futurism was an artistic and social movement that originated in Italy, and to a lesser extent in other countries, in the early twentieth century. It emphasized dynamism, speed, technology, youth, violence, and objects such as the car, the airplane, and the industrial city.

Neoclassicism emerged as a Western cultural movement in the decorative and visual arts, literature, theatre, music, and architecture that drew inspiration from the art and culture of classical antiquity.
Post-Impressionism was a predominantly French art movement. Post-Impressionism emerged as a reaction against Impressionists' concern for the naturalistic depiction of light and colour.

Postmodernism encompasses a variety of artistic, cultural, and philosophical movements. It emerged in the mid-twentieth century as a skeptical response to modernism, emphasizing the instability of meaning, rejection of universal truths, and critique of grand narratives.
The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, later known as the Pre-Raphaelites, was a group of English painters, poets, and art critics, founded in eighteen forty-eight.

In the arts, realism is generally the attempt to represent subject-matter truthfully, without artificiality, exaggeration, or speculative or supernatural elements. The term is often used interchangeably with naturalism, although these terms are not necessarily synonymous.

Symbolism was a late nineteenth-century art movement of French and Belgian origin in poetry and other arts seeking to represent absolute truths symbolically through language and metaphorical images, mainly as a reaction against naturalism and realism.
Contemporary art is generally art created from the nineteen seventies onwards. Contemporary artists work in a globally influenced, culturally diverse, and technologically advancing world.

Conceptual art, also referred to as conceptualism, is art in which the concept or ideas involved in the work are prioritized equally to or more than traditional aesthetic, technical, and material concerns. Some works of conceptual art may be constructed by anyone simply by following a set of written instructions.

Minimalism is an art movement that emphasizes reducing art to its essentials, focusing on the object itself and the viewer's experience, with as little mediation from the artist as possible. It emerged in the post-World War II era in Western art, and is often interpreted as a reaction to abstract expressionism and modernism.
Outsider art is art made by self-taught individuals who are untrained and untutored in the traditional arts with typically little or no contact with the conventions of the "art world".

African art refers to works of visual art, including works of sculpture, painting, metalwork, and pottery, originating from the various peoples of the African continent and influenced by distinct, indigenous traditions of aesthetic expression.
Chinese art is visual art that originated in or is practiced in China, Greater China or by Chinese artists.
Indian art consists of a variety of art forms, including painting, sculpture, pottery, and textile arts such as woven silk.
Islamic art is a part of Islamic culture and encompasses the visual arts produced since the seventh century CE by people who lived within territories inhabited or ruled by Muslim populations.

Japanese art consists of a wide range of art styles and media that includes ancient pottery, sculpture, ink painting and calligraphy on silk and paper, ukiyo-e paintings and woodblock prints, ceramics, origami, bonsai, and more recently manga and anime.

Ukiyo-e is a genre of Japanese art that flourished from the seventeenth through nineteenth centuries. Its artists produced woodblock prints and paintings of such subjects as female beauties; kabuki actors and sumo wrestlers; scenes from history and folk tales; travel scenes and landscapes; flora and fauna.

Persian art or Iranian art has one of the richest art heritages in world history and has been strong in many media including architecture, painting, weaving, pottery, calligraphy, metalworking and sculpture.
The visual arts of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas encompasses the visual artistic practices of the Indigenous peoples of the Americas from ancient times to the present.
The visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
Art criticism is the discussion or evaluation of visual art. Art critics usually criticize art in the context of aesthetics or the theory of beauty.

Carving is the act of using tools to shape something from a material by scraping away portions of that material. The technique can be applied to any material that is solid enough to hold a form even when pieces have been removed from it, and yet soft enough for portions to be scraped away with available tools.
Ceramic art, one of the plastic arts, is art made from ceramic materials, including clay. Ceramic art may take forms such as pottery, tiles, figurines, sculptures, and tableware.

The decorative arts are arts or crafts whose aim is the design and manufacture of objects that are both beautiful and functional. This includes most of the objects for the interiors of buildings, as well as interior design, but typically excludes architecture.
A design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system. The word design refers to something that is or has been intentionally created by a thinking agent.

Fashion design is the art of applying design, aesthetics, clothing construction, and natural beauty to clothing and its accessories. It is influenced by diverse cultures and different trends and has varied over time and place.
Interior design is the art and science of enhancing the interior of a building to achieve a healthier and more aesthetically pleasing environment for the people using the space.

Industrial design is the process of identifying problems and creating products, systems, and experiences that make everyday activities more efficient or meaningful. It is the creative act of determining and defining a product's form and features, which takes place in advance of the manufacture or production of the product.
Web design encompasses many different skills and disciplines in the production and maintenance of websites.

Digital art, or the digital arts, is artistic work that uses digital technology as part of the creative or presentational process. It can also refer to computational art that uses and engages with digital media.

Computer graphics deals with generating images and art with the aid of computers. Computer graphics is a core technology in digital photography, film, video games, digital art, cell phone and computer displays, and many specialized applications.
Folk art covers all forms of visual art made in the context of folk culture. Definitions vary, but generally the objects have practical utility of some kind, rather than being exclusively decorative.

A handicraft is a traditional main sector of craft making and applies to a wide range of creative and design activities that are related to making things with one's hands and skill, including work with textiles, moldable and rigid materials, paper, plant fibers, clay, etc.

In visual perception, an optical illusion, also called a visual illusion, is an illusion caused by the visual system and characterized by a visual percept that arguably appears to differ from reality.

Landscape painting, also known as landscape art, is the depiction in painting of natural scenery such as mountains, valleys, rivers, trees, and forests, especially where the main subject is a wide view with its elements arranged into a coherent composition.

Oil painting is a painting method involving the procedure of painting with pigments combined with a drying oil as the binder. It has been the most common technique for artistic painting on canvas, wood panel, or copper for several centuries.

Perspective is the representation of objects on the basis of how they may appear in real-life. Perspective is an approximate representation, generally on a flat surface, of an object as it is seen by the eye.
Engraving is the practice of incising a design on a hard, usually flat surface by cutting grooves into it with a burin.

Religious art is a visual representation of religious ideologies and their relationship with humans. Sacred art directly relates to religious art in the sense that its purpose is for worship and religious practices.
Textile art is art created from natural or synthetic fibers or from fabric or textile. Textile art is synonymous with fiber art.
The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait painting by the Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci.
The Last Supper is a mural painting by the Italian High Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, housed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy.
The Sistine Chapel is a chapel in the Apostolic Palace, the pope's official residence in Vatican City. Originally known as the Cappella Magna, it takes its name from Pope Sixtus IV, who had it built.

The Birth of Venus is a painting by the Italian artist Sandro Botticelli, probably executed in the mid-fourteen-eighties. It depicts the goddess Venus arriving at the shore after her birth, when she had emerged from the sea fully grown.

The School of Athens is a fresco by the Italian Renaissance artist Raphael. It was painted as part of a commission by Pope Julius II to decorate the rooms now called the Stanze di Raffaello in the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City.

The Starry Night is an oil-on-canvas painting by the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh. Painted in June eighteen eighty-nine, it depicts the view from the east-facing window of his asylum room at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, just before sunrise, with the addition of an imaginary village.

The Scream is an image first created by the Norwegian artist Edvard Munch in eighteen ninety-three, and later repeated by him in different versions. The agonized face in the painting has become one of the most iconic images in art, seen as representing a profound experience of existential dread related to the human condition.
The Persistence of Memory is a nineteen thirty-one painting by artist Salvador Dalí regarded as his most famous, and one of the most recognizable works of Surrealism as a whole.

Guernica is a large nineteen thirty-seven oil painting by Spanish artist Pablo Picasso. It is one of his best-known works, regarded by many art critics as the most moving and powerful anti-war painting in history.

Las Meninas is a sixteen fifty-six oil painting in the Museo del Prado in Madrid, by Diego Velázquez, the leading artist in the court of King Philip IV of Spain and Portugal, and of the Spanish Golden Age.
Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, commonly referred to as The Night Watch, is a sixteen forty-two painting by Rembrandt van Rijn.
Liberty Leading the People is a painting of the Romantic era by the French artist Eugène Delacroix, commemorating the July Revolution of eighteen thirty that toppled King Charles X.

Campbell's Soup Cans is a series of thirty-two paintings produced by American artist Andy Warhol between nineteen sixty-one and nineteen sixty-two. Each painting depicts a different variety of Campbell's soup cans in a uniform twenty-by-sixteen-inch format.

Water Lilies is a series of approximately two hundred fifty oil paintings by French Impressionist Claude Monet. The paintings depict his flower garden at his home in Giverny, and were the main focus of his artistic production during the last thirty-one years of his life.

The Great Wave off Kanagawa is a woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Hokusai, created in late eighteen thirty-one during the Edo period of Japanese history. The print depicts three boats moving through a storm-tossed sea, with a large, cresting wave forming a spiral in the centre over the boats and Mount Fuji in the background.

A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte was painted from eighteen eighty-four to eighteen eighty-six and is Georges Seurat's most famous work. It is recognised as a leading example of pointillist technique and as a founding work of the neo-impressionist movement.

The Garden of Earthly Delights is the modern title given to a five-panel triptych, three oil-painted panels when open and two oak panels when closed, painted by the Early Netherlandish master Hieronymus Bosch.
The Arnolfini Portrait is an oil painting on oak panel by the Early Netherlandish painter Jan van Eyck, dated fourteen thirty-four and now in the National Gallery, London.
Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski.

Fountain was a readymade sculpture attributed to Marcel Duchamp in nineteen seventeen, consisting of a porcelain urinal signed "R. Mutt". The work is regarded by art historians and theorists of the avant-garde as a major landmark in twentieth-century art.
The Great Sphinx of Giza is a limestone statue of a resting sphinx, a mythical creature with the head of a human and the body of a lion.
The Olmec colossal heads are stone representations of heads sculpted from large basalt boulders.

The Thinker, by Auguste Rodin, is a bronze sculpture depicting a nude male figure of heroic size, seated on a large rock, leaning forward, his right elbow placed upon his left thigh, with the back of his right hand supporting his chin in a posture evocative of deep thought and contemplation.
The Venus de Milo or Aphrodite of Melos is an ancient Greek marble sculpture that was created during the Hellenistic period.
The Venus of Willendorf is a Venus figurine estimated to have been made about thirty thousand years ago. It was recovered at a Paleolithic site near Willendorf, a village in Lower Austria.

The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered cloth nearly seventy metres long and fifty centimetres tall that depicts the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England, led by William, Duke of Normandy, and the Battle of Hastings in ten sixty-six.
The Blue Marble is a photograph of Earth taken by one of the astronauts aboard the Apollo seventeen spacecraft on its way to the Moon.
The Book of Kells is an illustrated manuscript and Celtic Gospel book in Latin, containing the four Gospels of the New Testament together with various prefatory texts and tables.
Along the River During the Qingming Festival is a handscroll painting by the Song dynasty painter Zhang Zeduan and copied or recreated many times in the following centuries.

Computer animation is the process used for digitally generating moving images. The more general term computer-generated imagery encompasses both still images and moving images, while computer animation only refers to moving images.

Traditional animation, or classical animation, cel animation, or hand-drawn animation, is a term retronymically applied to the dominant form of animation of the twentieth century in the United States until the shift to computer animation in the industry, in which each frame is drawn by hand.

A silent film is a film without synchronized recorded sound, or more generally, no audible spoken dialogue. Though silent films convey narrative and emotion visually, various plot elements such as a setting or era or key lines of dialogue may, when necessary, be conveyed by the use of intertitles.

Filmmaking, or film production, is the process of creating a motion picture, for example, feature films, episodic series for streaming and network broadcasting, commercials and advertisements, animations, music videos, documentaries, or any other filmed product.

Special effects are illusions or visual tricks used in the theater, film, television, video game, amusement park, and simulator industries to simulate the fictional events in a story or virtual world.
A studio system is a method of filmmaking wherein the production and distribution of films is dominated by a small number of large movie studios.

A television show, TV program, or TV show, is content produced for viewing on a television set that is transmitted via over-the-air, satellite, and cable, or distributed digitally on streaming platforms.

The film industry of the United States, primarily associated with major film studios collectively referred to as "Hollywood", has significantly influenced the global film industry since the early twentieth century. Classical Hollywood cinema, a filmmaking style developed in the nineteen-tens, continues to shape many American films today.

The cinema of France comprises the film industry and its film productions, whether made within the nation of France or by French film production companies abroad. It is the oldest and largest precursor of national cinemas in Europe, with primary influence also on the creation of national cinemas in Asia and especially in China.
The cinema of India, consisting of motion pictures made by the Indian film industry, has had a large effect on world cinema since the second half of the twentieth century.
The cinema of Japan, also known domestically as hōga, began in the late eighteen-nineties. Japan has one of the oldest and largest film industries in the world.

The cinema of China is the filmmaking and film industry of mainland China, one of three distinct historical threads of Chinese-language cinema together with the cinema of Hong Kong and the cinema of Taiwan.

The cinema of the Soviet Union includes films produced by the constituent republics of the Soviet Union reflecting elements of their pre-Soviet culture, language and history, albeit they were all regulated by the central government in Moscow.

A film festival is an organized, extended presentation of films in one or more cinemas or screening venues, usually annually and in a single city or region. Some film festivals show films outdoors or online.
The Cannes Film Festival is considered the most prestigious film festival in the world. Held in Cannes, France, it previews new films of all genres, including documentaries.

The Academy Awards, more commonly known as the Oscars, are awards based on artistic and technical merit in film. They are presented annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in the United States in recognition of excellence in cinematic achievements around the world.
Action film is a film genre that predominantly features chase sequences, fights, shootouts, explosions, stunt work and various other intense or fast paced scenes.
A documentary film, often called simply a documentary, is a nonfiction motion picture intended to "document reality, primarily for instruction, education or maintaining a historical record".

A game show, or gameshow, is a genre of broadcast viewing entertainment where contestants compete in a game for rewards. The shows are typically directed by a host, who explains the rules of the program as well as commentating and narrating where necessary.
Reality television is a genre of television programming that documents purportedly unscripted real-life situations, often starring ordinary people instead of professional actors.

A sitcom, short for situation comedy or situational comedy, is a genre of comedy produced for radio and television that centers on a recurring cast of characters as they navigate humorous situations within a consistent setting, such as a home, workplace, or community.

A soap opera, also called a daytime drama or soap, is a genre of a long-running radio or television serial, frequently characterized by melodrama, ensemble casts, and sentimentality. The term soap opera originated from radio dramas' original sponsorship by soap manufacturers.
A talk show or chat show is a television programming, radio programming and podcast genre structured around the act of spontaneous conversation.

The James Bond franchise focuses on the character of James Bond, a fictional British Secret Service agent created in nineteen fifty-three by writer Ian Fleming, who featured him in twelve novels and two short-story collections.
Sholay is a nineteen seventy-five Indian Hindi-language action-adventure film directed by Ramesh Sippy, produced by his father G. P. Sippy, and written by Salim-Javed.
Looney Tunes is an American media franchise owned by Warner Bros. Entertainment.

Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is a nineteen thirty-seven American animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney and released by RKO Radio Pictures, based on the eighteen twelve German fairy tale "Snow White" by the Brothers Grimm.
Spirited Away is a two thousand and one Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki. It was produced by Toshio Suzuki, animated by Studio Ghibli, and distributed by Toho.
Toy Story is a nineteen ninety-five American animated adventure comedy film directed by John Lasseter.

City Lights is a nineteen thirty-one American synchronized sound romantic comedy-drama film written, produced, directed by, and starring Charlie Chaplin. While the film has no audible dialog, it was released with a synchronized musical score with sound effects.
Eight and a half is a nineteen sixty-three Italian avant-garde comedy-drama film directed and co-written by Federico Fellini.
The Apu Trilogy is a series of three Indian Bengali-language drama films directed by Satyajit Ray: Pather Panchali, Aparajito and The World of Apu. The trilogy's score was composed by Ravi Shankar.

Bicycle Thieves, also known as The Bicycle Thief, is a nineteen forty-eight Italian neorealist drama film directed by Vittorio De Sica. It follows the story of a poor father searching in post-World War II Rome for his stolen bicycle, without which he will lose the job which was to be the salvation of his young family.

Breathless is a nineteen sixty French New Wave crime drama film written and directed by Jean-Luc Godard. It stars Jean-Paul Belmondo as a wandering criminal named Michel, and Jean Seberg as his American girlfriend Patricia.
Citizen Kane is a nineteen forty-one American drama film directed, produced by, and starring Orson Welles and co-written by Welles and Herman J. Mankiewicz, and was Welles's first feature film.

The Godfather is a nineteen seventy-two American epic gangster film directed by Francis Ford Coppola, who co-wrote the screenplay with Mario Puzo based on Puzo's best-selling nineteen sixty-nine novel.

Tokyo Story is a nineteen fifty-three Japanese drama film directed by Yasujirō Ozu and starring Chishū Ryū and Chieko Higashiyama, about an aging couple who travel to Tokyo to visit their grown children.

Battleship Potemkin is a nineteen twenty-five Soviet silent epic film produced by Mosfilm. Directed and co-written by Sergei Eisenstein, it presents a dramatization of the mutiny that occurred in nineteen oh five when the crew of the Russian battleship Potemkin rebelled against their officers.

Lawrence of Arabia is a nineteen sixty-two epic biographical drama film directed by David Lean and produced by Sam Spiegel through the latter's British company Horizon Pictures and distributed by Columbia Pictures.
Seven Samurai is a nineteen fifty-four Japanese epic jidaigeki film directed by Akira Kurosawa from a screenplay co-written with Shinobu Hashimoto and Hideo Oguni.
The Seventh Seal is a nineteen fifty-seven Swedish historical fantasy film written and directed by Ingmar Bergman.
Jaws is a nineteen seventy-five American thriller film directed by Steven Spielberg, based on the nineteen seventy-four novel by Peter Benchley.

Psycho is a nineteen sixty American horror thriller film produced and directed by Alfred Hitchcock. The screenplay, written by Joseph Stefano, is based on the nineteen fifty-nine novel by Robert Bloch.
Vertigo is a nineteen fifty-eight American psychological thriller film produced and directed by Alfred Hitchcock.
The Jazz Singer is a nineteen twenty-seven American part-talkie musical drama film directed by Alan Crosland and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.
Singin' in the Rain is a nineteen fifty-two American musical romantic comedy film directed and choreographed by Gene Kelly and Stanley Donen.
The Sound of Music is a nineteen sixty-five American musical drama film produced and directed by Robert Wise from a screenplay written by Ernest Lehman.

Gone with the Wind is a nineteen thirty-nine American epic historical romance film adapted from the nineteen thirty-six novel by Margaret Mitchell. It was produced by David O. Selznick of Selznick International Pictures and directed by Victor Fleming.
Two thousand and one: A Space Odyssey is a nineteen sixty-eight epic science fiction film produced and directed by Stanley Kubrick, who co-wrote the screenplay with Arthur C. Clarke.
Metropolis is a nineteen twenty-seven German expressionist science-fiction, silent film directed by Fritz Lang and written by Thea von Harbou in collaboration with Lang.
Star Wars is an American media franchise created by George Lucas. The space opera saga began with the original Star Wars film and quickly became a worldwide pop culture phenomenon.

The Wizard of Oz is a nineteen thirty-nine American musical fantasy film produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. Based on the nineteen hundred novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum, it was primarily directed by Victor Fleming, who left production to take over the troubled Gone with the Wind.

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is a nineteen sixty-six Italian epic spaghetti Western film directed by Sergio Leone and starring Clint Eastwood as "the Good", Lee Van Cleef as "the Bad", and Eli Wallach as "the Ugly".

The Brandenburg Concertos by Johann Sebastian Bach are a collection of six instrumental works presented by Bach to Christian Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg-Schwedt, in seventeen twenty-one, though probably composed earlier.
The Four Seasons is a group of four violin concerti by Italian composer Antonio Vivaldi, each of which gives musical expression to a season of the year.

The Mass in B minor is an extended setting of the Mass ordinary by Johann Sebastian Bach. The composition was completed in seventeen forty-nine, the year before Bach's death, and was to a large extent based on earlier work, such as a Sanctus Bach had composed in seventeen twenty-four.
The Well-Tempered Clavier consists of two sets of preludes and fugues in all twenty-four major and minor keys for keyboard by Johann Sebastian Bach.

Frédéric Chopin wrote twenty-one nocturnes for solo piano between eighteen twenty-seven and eighteen forty-six. They are generally considered among the finest short solo works for the instrument and hold an important place in contemporary concert repertoire.
Ludwig van Beethoven wrote thirty-two mature piano sonatas between seventeen ninety-five and eighteen twenty-two.

The Second Symphony in C minor by Gustav Mahler, also known as the Resurrection Symphony, was written between eighteen eighty-eight and eighteen ninety-four, and first performed in eighteen ninety-five. This symphony was one of Mahler's most popular and successful works during his lifetime.

The Third Symphony in E-flat major, titled as the Eroica Symphony, is a symphony in four movements by Ludwig van Beethoven. One of Beethoven's most celebrated works, the Eroica symphony is a large-scale composition that marked the beginning of the composer's innovative "middle period".

The Fifth Symphony in C minor is a symphony composed by Ludwig van Beethoven between eighteen oh four and eighteen oh eight. It is one of the best-known of all symphonies and one of the most frequently played.

The Ninth Symphony in D minor is a choral symphony, the final complete symphony by Ludwig van Beethoven, composed between eighteen twenty-two and eighteen twenty-four. It was first performed in Vienna in May eighteen twenty-four.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart completed his Symphony Number Forty-One in C major in August seventeen eighty-eight. The longest and last symphony that he composed, it is regarded by many critics as among the greatest symphonies in classical music.
La bohème is an opera in four acts, composed by Giacomo Puccini to an Italian libretto by Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa, based on Scènes de la vie de bohème by Henri Murger.
Carmen is an opera in four acts by the French composer Georges Bizet. The libretto was written by Henri Meilhac and Ludovic Halévy, based on the novella of the same title by Prosper Mérimée.

Don Giovanni is an opera in two acts with music by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart to an Italian libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte. Its subject is a centuries-old Spanish legend about a libertine, Don Juan, as told by playwright Tirso de Molina in his sixteen thirty play El burlador de Sevilla y convidado de piedra.
The Magic Flute is an opera in two acts by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart to a German libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder. It is a Singspiel, a popular form that included both singing and spoken dialogue.

The Marriage of Figaro is a commedia per musica in four acts composed in seventeen eighty-six by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, with an Italian libretto written by Lorenzo Da Ponte. It premiered at the Burgtheater in Vienna in May seventeen eighty-six.

Der Ring des Nibelungen, The Ring of the Nibelung, is a cycle of four German-language epic music dramas composed by Richard Wagner. The works are based loosely on characters from Germanic heroic legend, namely Norse legendary sagas and the Nibelungenlied.

La traviata is an opera in three acts by Giuseppe Verdi set to an Italian libretto by Francesco Maria Piave. It is based on La Dame aux camélias, a play by Alexandre Dumas fils, which he adapted from his own eighteen forty-eight novel.

Tristan und Isolde is a music drama in three acts by Richard Wagner set to a German libretto by the composer, loosely based on Gottfried von Strassburg's medieval twelfth-century romance Tristan and Iseult.

The Nutcracker is an eighteen ninety-two two-act classical ballet by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, set on Christmas Eve at the foot of a Christmas tree in a child's imagination featuring a Nutcracker doll.

The Rite of Spring is a ballet and orchestral concert work by the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky. It was written for the nineteen thirteen Paris season of Sergei Diaghilev's Ballets Russes company; the original choreography was by Vaslav Nijinsky with stage designs and costumes by Nicholas Roerich.

Swan Lake is a ballet composed by Russian composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in eighteen seventy-five and seventy-six. Despite its initial failure, it is now one of the most popular ballets of all time.
The Phantom of the Opera is a musical with music by Andrew Lloyd Webber, lyrics by Charles Hart, and additional lyrics by Richard Stilgoe, with a libretto by Lloyd Webber and Stilgoe.

West Side Story is a musical conceived by Jerome Robbins with music by Leonard Bernstein, lyrics by Stephen Sondheim, and a book by Arthur Laurents. Inspired by William Shakespeare's play Romeo and Juliet, the story is set in the mid-nineteen-fifties on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City.
"Garota de Ipanema", or "The Girl from Ipanema", is a Brazilian bossa nova and jazz song. It was a worldwide hit in the mid-nineteen-sixties and won a Grammy for Record of the Year.
Kind of Blue is a studio album by the American jazz musician Miles Davis, released through Columbia Records.

Rhapsody in Blue is a nineteen twenty-four musical composition for solo piano and jazz band by George Gershwin. Commissioned by bandleader Paul Whiteman, the work combines elements of classical music with jazz-influenced effects.

"Bohemian Rhapsody" is the penultimate song from British rock band Queen's fourth studio album, A Night at the Opera. It is a suite composed of five main elements: an introduction, a ballad, an opera, a hard rock segment, and a reflective coda.
"Gangnam Style" is a K-pop song by South Korean singer Psy, released by YG Entertainment as the lead single of his sixth studio album.
"Johnny B. Goode" is a song by American musician Chuck Berry, written and sung by Berry in nineteen fifty-eight.
"Like a Rolling Stone" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Bob Dylan, released by Columbia Records in nineteen sixty-five.
Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band is the eighth studio album by the English rock band the Beatles.

Doctor Who is a British science fiction television series first broadcast by the BBC in nineteen sixty-three. The series, created by Sydney Newman, C. E. Webber and Donald Wilson, follows the adventures of the Doctor, an extraterrestrial being from a humanoid species known as Time Lords.
The Eurovision Song Contest, often known simply as Eurovision, is an international song competition organised annually by the European Broadcasting Union since nineteen fifty-six.

Sesame Street is an American educational children's television series that combines live-action, sketch comedy, animation, and puppetry. It is produced by Sesame Workshop and was created by Joan Ganz Cooney and Lloyd Morrisett.

The Simpsons is an American animated sitcom created by Matt Groening and developed by Groening, James L. Brooks and Sam Simon for the Fox Broadcasting Company. It is a satirical depiction of American life, epitomized by the Simpson family, which consists of Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and Maggie.
The Sopranos is an American crime drama television series created by David Chase for HBO. The series follows Tony Soprano, a New Jersey Mafia boss.

Star Trek is an American science fiction media franchise created by Gene Roddenberry and owned by Paramount, which began with the series of the same name and became a worldwide pop culture phenomenon.

Peter Pan is a fictional character created by Scottish novelist and playwright J. M. Barrie. A free-spirited and mischievous young boy who can fly and never grows up, he spends his never-ending childhood having adventures on the mythical island of Neverland as the leader of the Lost Boys.

Sherlock Holmes is a fictional detective created by British author Arthur Conan Doyle. Referring to himself as a "consulting detective" in his stories, Holmes is known for his proficiency with observation, deduction, forensic science and logical reasoning that borders on the fantastic.
Winnie-the-Pooh, also known as Edward Bear, Pooh Bear or simply Pooh, is a fictional anthropomorphic teddy bear created by the English author A. A. Milne and the English illustrator E. H. Shepard.
Donald Fauntleroy Duck is a cartoon character created by Walt Disney and Dick Lundy. Donald is an anthropomorphic white duck with a yellow-orange bill, legs, and feet.

Hello Kitty, also known by her real name Kitty White, is a fictional character created by Yuko Shimizu, designed by Yuko Yamaguchi, and owned by the Japanese company Sanrio. Sanrio depicts Hello Kitty as a British anthropomorphic white cat with a red bow and no visible mouth.

Mario is a character created by Japanese video game designer Shigeru Miyamoto. He is the star of the Mario franchise, a recurring character in the Donkey Kong franchise, and the mascot of their owner, the Japanese company Nintendo.

Mickey Mouse is a cartoon character co-created in nineteen twenty-eight by Walt Disney and Ub Iwerks. The longtime corporate icon and mascot of the Walt Disney Company and a figurehead of American animation, Mickey is an anthropomorphic mouse who typically wears red shorts, large shoes, and white gloves.
Batman is a superhero who appears in American comic books published by DC Comics. Batman was created by writer Bill Finger and artist Bob Kane.

Spider-Man is a superhero in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. Created by writer-editor Stan Lee and artist Steve Ditko, he first appeared in the anthology comic book Amazing Fantasy in the Silver Age of Comic Books.
Superman is a superhero created by writer Jerry Siegel and artist Joe Shuster, first appearing in the first issue of Action Comics, published in the United States in nineteen thirty-eight.

Wonder Woman is a superheroine appearing in American comic books published by DC Comics. The character first appeared in All Star Comics, published in October nineteen forty-one, with her first feature in Sensation Comics in January nineteen forty-two.

Archaic humans emerged out of Africa between five hundred thousand and one million eight hundred thousand years ago. This was followed by the emergence of modern humans in East Africa around three hundred thousand to two hundred fifty thousand years ago who spread across the world.

The history of North Africa is typically divided into its prehistory, the classical period, the arrival and spread of Islam, the colonial era, and finally the post-independence period, in which the current nations were formed. The region has been influenced by a wide range of cultures.

The history of Europe can be traced back to the appearance of the first modern humans identified as ancestors of contemporary Europeans about thirty-seven thousand years ago during the Paleolithic. Early European Farmers migrating from Anatolia spread agriculture across the continent during the Neolithic, a period that also included early metallurgy.
The history of Scandinavia is the history of the geographical region of Scandinavia and its peoples. The region is located in Northern Europe, and consists of Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
The History of North America encompasses the past developments of people populating the continent of North America.

The history of the Caribbean reveals the region's significant role in the colonial struggles of the European powers since the fifteenth century. In the modern era, it remains strategically and economically important.

The history of South America is the study of the past, particularly the written record, oral histories, and traditions, passed down from generation to generation on the continent of South America. The continent continues to be home to indigenous peoples, some of whom built high civilizations prior to the arrival of Europeans in the late fourteen hundreds and early fifteen hundreds.
The history of Oceania includes the history of Australia, Easter Island, Fiji, Hawaii, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Western New Guinea and, other Pacific island nations.

The history of Asia can be seen as the collective history of East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, North Asia and West Asia. The continent is home to two of the world's oldest, continuous civilizations, Chinese civilization and Indian civilization.

The history of East Asia generally encompasses the histories of China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and Taiwan from prehistoric times to the present. Each of its countries has a different national history, but East Asian studies scholars maintain that the region is also characterized by a distinct pattern of historical development.

The history of Southeast Asia covers the people of Southeast Asia from prehistory to the present in two distinct sub-regions: Mainland Southeast Asia, or Indochina, and Maritime Southeast Asia, or Insular Southeast Asia.

The history of Central Asia concerns the history of the various peoples that have inhabited Central Asia. The lifestyle of such people has been determined primarily by the area's climate and geography.

The Middle East, or the Near East, was one of the cradles of civilization: after the Neolithic Revolution and the adoption of agriculture, many of the world's oldest cultures and civilizations were created there. Since ancient times, the Middle East has had several lingua franca: Akkadian, Hebrew, Aramaic, Greek, and Arabic.

The history of Antarctica emerges from early Western theories of a vast continent, known as Terra Australis, believed to exist in the far south of the globe. The term Antarctic, referring to the opposite of the Arctic Circle, was coined by Marinus of Tyre in the second century AD.
Algeria's history has been shaped by its position between the Mediterranean, the Maghreb, and the Sahara.

The earliest known human settlements in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo date back to the Middle Stone Age, approximately ninety thousand years ago. The first 'states', such as the Kongo, the Lunda, the Luba and Kuba, appeared south of the equatorial forest on the savannah, from the fourteenth century.

Egypt, one of the world's oldest civilizations, was unified around thirty-one fifty BC by King Narmer. It later came under Persian, Greek, Roman, and Arab rule before being joined to the Ottoman Empire in fifteen seventeen.
Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in Africa; the emergence of Ethiopian civilization dates back thousands of years.
The history of human habitation in Morocco extends back to the Lower Paleolithic.
The history of Nigeria can be traced to the earliest inhabitants from at least nine thousand BC through to early civilizations such as the Nok culture which began around fifteen hundred BC.
The first modern humans are believed to have lived in South Africa more than one hundred thousand years ago. They were collectively known as the Khoisan, the Khoekhoe, and the San.

The history of Sudan refers to the territory that today makes up Republic of the Sudan and the state of South Sudan, which became independent in two thousand eleven. The territory of Sudan is geographically part of a larger African region, also known as "Sudan".
The history of Argentina can be divided into four main parts: the pre-Columbian time or early history, the colonial period, the period of nation-building, and the history of modern Argentina.
Before the arrival of the Europeans, the lands that now constitute Brazil were inhabited and settled by diverse tribes for thousands of years.

The history of Canada covers the period from the arrival of the Paleo-Indians to North America thousands of years ago to the present day. The lands encompassing present-day Canada have been inhabited for millennia by Indigenous peoples, with distinct trade networks, spiritual beliefs, and styles of social organization.
The history of Colombia includes its settlement by indigenous peoples and the establishment of agrarian societies, notably the Muisca Confederation, Quimbaya Civilization, and Tairona Chiefdoms.

The history of Mexico encompasses over thirteen thousand years between the initial migration of indigenous peoples and the modern day. Central and southern Mexico, termed Mesoamerica, saw the rise and fall of complex indigenous civilizations such as the Olmecs, Mayas and Aztecs.

The history of Peru spans fifteen millennia, extending back through several stages of cultural development along the country's desert coastline and in the Andes mountains. Peru's coast was home to the Norte Chico civilization, the oldest civilization in the Americas and one of the six cradles of civilization in the world.
The history of the United States spans tens of thousands of years of Indigenous civilization.
The Commonwealth of Australia was proclaimed on the first of January nineteen oh one as a federation of six self-governing former British colonies.
The history of present-day Afghanistan in the pre-modern times is largely shared with the neighbouring regions in Central, South and West Asia.

The history of Bangladesh dates back over four millennia to the Chalcolithic period. The region's early history was characterized by a succession of Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms and empires that fought for control over the Bengal region.

The history of China spans several millennia across a wide geographical area. Chinese civilization originated in the Yellow and Yangtze river basins, evolving into one of the world's oldest cradles of civilization.

The Lower Paleolithic era on the Korean Peninsula and in Manchuria began roughly half a million years ago. The earliest known Korean pottery dates to around eight thousand BC and the Neolithic period began thereafter, followed by the Bronze Age by two thousand BC, and the Iron Age around seven hundred BC.

Anatomically modern humans are estimated to have first arrived on the Indian subcontinent between seventy-three thousand and fifty-five thousand years ago. The earliest known human remains in South Asia date to thirty thousand years ago.

The history of Indonesia has been shaped by its geographic position, natural resources, a series of human migrations and contacts, wars and conquests, as well as by trade, economics and politics. Indonesia is an archipelagic country of more than seventeen thousand islands stretching along the equator in Southeast Asia and Oceania.

The history of Iran is intertwined with Greater Iran, a region encompassing all areas that have witnessed significant settlement or influence by the Iranian peoples and Iranian languages, chiefly the Persians and the Persian language. Central to this region is the Iranian plateau, now covered by modern Iran.
Iraq, a country located in West Asia, largely coincides with the ancient region of Mesopotamia, often referred to as the cradle of civilization.

The civilization of Mesopotamia ranges from the earliest human occupation in the Paleolithic period up to Late antiquity. This history is pieced together from evidence retrieved from archaeological excavations and, after the introduction of writing in the late fourth millennium BC, an increasing amount of historical sources.

Malaysia is a modern concept, created in the second half of the twentieth century. However, contemporary Malaysia regards the entire history of Malaya and Borneo, spanning thousands of years back to prehistoric times, as its own history.
The history of Myanmar covers the period from the time of first-known human settlements thirteen thousand years ago to the present day.

The history of Israel spans the Southern Levant, from prehistoric African migrations and the Natufian culture to the emergence of Canaanite civilization. During the Iron Age, the kingdoms of Israel and Judah formed, serving as the foundation for Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

The first human inhabitants of the Japanese archipelago have been traced to the Paleolithic, around thirty-eight to thirty-nine thousand years ago. The Jōmon period, named after its cord-marked pottery, was followed by the Yayoi period in the first millennium BC when new inventions were introduced from Asia.

The history of Pakistan preceding the country's independence in nineteen forty-seven is shared with that of neighbouring Afghanistan, India, Iran and Tibet. Spanning the western expanse of the Indian subcontinent and the eastern borderlands of the Iranian plateau, the region of contemporary Pakistan served both as the fertile ground of a major civilization and as the gateway of South Asia to Central Asia and the Near East.

The history of the Philippines dates from the earliest hominin activity in the archipelago at least by seven hundred nine thousand years ago. Homo luzonensis, a species of archaic humans, was present on the island of Luzon at least by one hundred thirty-four thousand years ago.
The history of Saudi Arabia as a nation state began with the emergence of the Al Saud dynasty in central Arabia in seventeen twenty-seven and the subsequent establishment of the Emirate of Diriyah.

The History of Thailand begins with the earliest Bronze and Iron Age sites such as Ban Chiang around fifteen hundred BCE. The region of present-day Thailand was inhabited by the main indigenous groups: Mon, Lawa, Khmer, and Malay in the first millennium.

Vietnam, with its coastal strip, rugged mountainous interior, and two major deltas, became home to numerous cultures throughout history. Its strategic geographical position in Southeast Asia also made it a crossroads of trade and a focal point of conflict, contributing to its complex and eventful past.

The history of the British Isles began with its sporadic human habitation during the Palaeolithic from around nine hundred thousand years ago. The British Isles has been continually occupied since the early Holocene, the current geological epoch, which started around eleven thousand seven hundred years ago.

The history of the United Kingdom begins in seventeen oh seven with the Treaty of Union and Acts of Union. The core of the United Kingdom as a unified state came into being with the political union of the kingdoms of England and Scotland, into a new unitary state called Great Britain.
The concept of Germany as a distinct region can be traced to Julius Caesar, who referred to the area east of the Rhine as Germania, meaning the land where the Germani live.
The history of Greece encompasses the history of the territory of the modern nation-state of Greece as well as that of the Greek people and the areas they inhabited and ruled historically.
The first written records for the history of France appeared in the Iron Age. What is now France made up the bulk of the region known to the Romans as Gaul.

Italy has been inhabited by humans since the Paleolithic. During antiquity, there were many peoples in the Italian peninsula, including Etruscans, Latins, Samnites, Umbri, Cisalpine Gauls, Greeks in Magna Graecia and others. Most significantly, Italy was the cradle of the Roman civilization.

The history of Poland spans over a thousand years, from medieval tribes, Christianization and monarchy; through Poland's Golden Age, expansionism and becoming one of the largest European powers; to its collapse and partitions, two world wars, communism, and the restoration of democracy.
The history of Portugal can be traced from circa four hundred thousand years ago, when the region of present-day Portugal was inhabited by Homo heidelbergensis.

The history of Russia begins with the histories of the East Slavs. The traditional start date of specifically Russian history is the establishment of the Rus' state in the north in the year eight sixty-two, ruled by Varangians.

The history of Spain dates to contact between the pre-Roman peoples of the Mediterranean coast of the Iberian Peninsula with the Greeks and Phoenicians. During Classical Antiquity, the peninsula was the site of multiple successive colonizations of Greeks, Carthaginians, and Romans.

The earliest migrations and expansions of archaic and modern humans across continents are believed to have begun approximately two million years ago with the early expansions out of Africa by Homo erectus. This initial migration was followed by other archaic humans including H. heidelbergensis, which lived around five hundred thousand years ago.

The Lower Paleolithic is the earliest subdivision of the Paleolithic or Old Stone Age. It spans the time from around three point three million years ago when the first evidence for stone tool production and use by hominins appears in the current archaeological record, until around three hundred thousand years ago.

The Middle Paleolithic is the second subdivision of the Paleolithic or Old Stone Age as it is understood in Europe, Africa and Asia. The term Middle Stone Age is used as an equivalent or a synonym for the Middle Paleolithic in African archeology.

The Upper Paleolithic is the third and last subdivision of the Paleolithic or Old Stone Age. Very broadly, it dates to between fifty thousand and twelve thousand years ago, according to some theories coinciding with the appearance of behavioral modernity in humans.

Behavioral modernity is a suite of behavioral and cognitive traits associated with humans, reflecting capacities such as abstract and symbolic thought, planning depth, cumulative culture, and complex social learning.
The earliest human civilizations developed independently of each other and a cradle of civilization is a location and a culture from which one of them emerged.
Prehistoric Egypt and Predynastic Egypt was the period of time starting at the first human occupation of the region and ending at the First Dynasty of Egypt around three thousand one hundred BC.
The Proto-Indo-Europeans are a postulated prehistoric ethnolinguistic group of Eurasia who spoke Proto-Indo-European, the reconstructed common ancestor of the Indo-European language family.
The Chalcolithic was an archaeological period characterized by the increasing use of smelted copper. It followed the Neolithic and preceded the Bronze Age.

Classical antiquity, also known as the classical era, classical period, classical age, or simply antiquity, is the period of cultural European history between the eighth century BC and the fifth century AD, following the Greek Dark Ages and being succeeded by late antiquity.
Late antiquity is a time period between classical antiquity and the Early Middle Ages. The exact start and end dates are debatable.
In ancient Egyptian history, the Old Kingdom is the period spanning about twenty-seven hundred to twenty-two hundred BC.

The New Kingdom, also called the Egyptian Empire, refers to ancient Egypt between the sixteenth century BC and the eleventh century BC. This period of ancient Egyptian history covers the Eighteenth, Nineteenth, and Twentieth dynasties.

The Ptolemaic Kingdom or Ptolemaic Empire was an ancient Greek polity based in Egypt during the Hellenistic period. It was founded in three hundred and five BC by the Macedonian Greek general Ptolemy I Soter, a companion of Alexander the Great, and was ruled by the Ptolemaic dynasty until the death of Cleopatra the Seventh in thirty BC.
The Kingdom of Aksum, or the Aksumite Empire, was a kingdom in the Horn of Africa and South Arabia from classical antiquity to the Middle Ages, based in what is now Eritrea and Northern Ethiopia.

The Bantu expansion was a major series of prehistoric migrations of the original Proto-Bantu-speaking group, which spread from an original nucleus around West-Central Africa across Central Africa, Eastern Africa, and Southern Africa.

Ancient Carthage was an ancient civilization based in North Africa. It grew from a small settlement in present-day Tunisia into the Carthaginian Empire, a major power that dominated the western half of the Mediterranean Sea.

Nubia is a region along the Nile river encompassing the area between the confluence of the Blue Nile and White Nile and the First Cataract. It was the seat of one of the earliest civilizations of ancient Africa, the Kerma culture.
The Land of Punt was an ancient kingdom known from Ancient Egyptian trade records. It produced and exported gold, aromatic resins, blackwood, ebony, ivory and wild animals.

The Andean civilizations were South American complex societies of many indigenous people. They stretched down the spine of the Andes from southern Colombia, to Ecuador and Peru, including the deserts of coastal Peru, to north Chile and northwest Argentina.

Caral-Supe, also known as Caral and Norte Chico, was a complex pre-Columbian era society that included as many as thirty major population centers in what is now the Caral region of north-central coastal Peru.

Mesoamerica is a historical region and cultural area comprising the modern-day lands of central and southern Mexico, all of Belize, Guatemala, El Salvador, western Honduras, and the Greater Nicoya region of Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
Paleo-Indians were the first peoples who entered and subsequently inhabited the Americas towards the end of the Late Pleistocene period.

The Clovis culture is an archaeological culture from the Paleoindian period of North America. The type site is Blackwater Draw near Clovis, New Mexico, where stone tools were found alongside the remains of Columbian mammoths.

The peopling of the Americas is believed to have begun when Paleolithic hunter-gatherers entered North America from the North Asian Mammoth steppe via the Beringia land bridge, which had formed between northeastern Siberia and western Alaska due to the lowering of sea level during the Last Glacial Maximum.
The Parthian Empire, also known as the Arsacid Empire, was a major Iranian political and cultural power centered in ancient Iran from two hundred and forty-seven BC to two hundred and twenty-four AD.
The Sasanian Empire, officially Eranshahr, was an Iranian empire that was founded and ruled by the House of Sasan from two hundred and twenty-four to six hundred and fifty-one AD.
The Medes were an Iron Age Iranian people who spoke the Median language and who inhabited an area known as Media between western and northern Iran.
Elam was an ancient civilization centered in the far west and southwest of Iran, stretching from the lowlands of Ilam and Khuzestan as well as a small part of modern-day southern Iraq.

Bactria, or Bactriana, was an ancient civilization in Central Asia, located in the area south of the Oxus River and north of the Hindu Kush mountains, within modern-day Afghanistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

Sogdia or Sogdiana was an ancient Iranian civilisation located between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya rivers. Sogdiana was also a province of the Achaemenid Empire, and is listed on the Behistun Inscription of Darius the Great.
The Xiongnu were a tribal confederation of nomadic peoples who, according to ancient Chinese sources, inhabited the eastern Eurasian Steppe from the third century BC to the late first century AD.

The Xia dynasty is the first dynasty in traditional Chinese historiography. Some scholars consider the Xia dynasty legendary or at least unsubstantiated, while a majority of Chinese archeologists consider it historical and identify it with the archaeological Erlitou culture.

The Zhou dynasty was a royal dynasty of China that existed for seven hundred and ninety years from about one thousand and forty-six BC until two hundred and fifty-six BC, the longest span of any dynasty in Chinese history.

The Spring and Autumn period was a period in Chinese history corresponding roughly to the first half of the Eastern Zhou, characterized by the gradual erosion of royal power as local lords nominally subject to the Zhou exercised increasing political autonomy.
The Warring States period in Chinese history comprises the final centuries of the Zhou dynasty, which were characterized by warfare, bureaucratic and military reform, and political consolidation.
The Qin dynasty, also known as the Qin Empire, was the first imperial dynasty of China. It is named for its progenitor state of Qin, a fief of the confederal Zhou dynasty.
The Three Kingdoms of Cao Wei, Shu Han, and Eastern Wu dominated China from two hundred and twenty to two hundred and eighty AD following the end of the Han dynasty.

The Indus Valley Civilisation, also known as the Indus Civilisation, was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwestern regions of South Asia, lasting from thirty-three hundred BCE to thirteen hundred BCE, and in its mature form from twenty-six hundred BCE to nineteen hundred BCE.

The Vedic period, or the Vedic age, is the period in the late Bronze Age and early Iron Age of the history of India when the Vedic literature, including the Vedas, was composed in the northern Indian subcontinent.
Magadha was a region and kingdom in ancient India, based in the eastern Ganges Plain. It was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas during the second urbanisation period.
