An anatomical variation is a body structure whose form differs from the one described in most individuals.
A body is the physical material of an organism, the word being used for organisms that are in one piece.
Body fluids are liquids within the body of an organism.
In cell biology, extracellular fluid is all the body fluid outside the cells of a multicellular organism.
A digit is one of the outermost parts of a limb, such as a finger or a toe, present in many vertebrates.
The peritoneum is the serous membrane forming the lining of the abdominal cavity in amniotes and in some invertebrates.
The abdominal cavity is a large body cavity in humans and many other animals that holds organs.
A flipper is a broad flattened limb adapted for moving through water.
The webbed foot is a limb with membranes between the digits that help in moving through water, found in a variety of four limbed vertebrates.
The torso or trunk is the central part of the body of many animals, from which the head, neck, limbs and tail extend.
An arteriole is a small blood vessel that branches out from an artery and leads to the capillaries.
A venule is a very small vein that lets blood return from the capillary beds and drain into ever larger veins.
The lymphatic vessels are thin walled tubes, built like blood vessels, that carry lymph.
All living cephalopods have a two part beak, set in the mouthparts and surrounded by the muscular head appendages.
The vocal sac is the flexible membrane of skin possessed by most male frogs and toads.
Eosinophils are a variety of white blood cell and one of the parts of the immune system responsible for combating multicellular parasites and certain infections in vertebrates.
Basophils are a type of white blood cell, the least common kind of granulocyte and the largest.
The outer ear is the external part of the ear, consisting of the auricle and the ear canal.
Bitterness is one of the most sensitive of tastes, and many experience it as unpleasant or sharp, though it is sometimes wanted and deliberately added.
The sensation of bitterness evolved in the common ancestor of jawed vertebrates, since the family of bitter taste receptor genes is limited to that group.
Pungency, commonly called spiciness or heat, is a sensation that contributes to the flavour of certain foods such as chilli peppers.
Saltiness is one of the basic tastes, and it appears to have two components, a signal for a little salt and a signal for a lot.
Sourness is a basic taste perceived through hydrogen ions from acidic compounds meeting receptors in the taste buds.
Sweetness is a basic taste most commonly perceived when eating foods rich in sugar.
A nostril is either of the two openings of the nose, letting air and other gases in and out of the nasal cavities.
Eye colour is a trait set by many genes and determined by two things, the pigment of the iris and the scattering of light within it.
Monochromacy is the ability of organisms to perceive only the intensity of light, without regard to its spectrum.
Dichromacy is the state of having two types of working cone cell in the eye.
Tetrachromacy is the condition of having four independent channels for colour information, or four types of cone cell in the eye.
The Purkinje effect is the tendency for the peak sensitivity of the eye to shift toward the blue end of the spectrum as the light grows dim.
An udder is an organ formed of mammary glands on the females of dairy animals and ruminants such as cattle, goats and sheep.
The carpal bones are the small bones that make up the wrist, which connects the hand to the forearm.
The hyoid bone, also known as the tongue bone, is a horseshoe shaped bone in the front of the neck between the chin and the thyroid cartilage.
The metacarpal bones, the palm bones, form the middle part of the hand between the fingers and the bones of the wrist.
The metatarsal bones are a group of long bones in the midfoot, lying between the bones of the heel and ankle and the toes.
The patella, the kneecap, is a flat rounded triangular bone that covers and protects the front of the knee joint.
The phalanges are the bones of the digits in the hands and feet of most vertebrates.
An intervertebral disc lies between neighbouring vertebrae in the spine, forming a joint of fibrous cartilage.
The mollusc shell is a chalky exoskeleton that encloses, supports and protects the soft parts of an animal in the phylum of the molluscs.
Adipocytes, also known as fat cells, are the cells that make up adipose tissue and store energy as fat.
A fibroblast is a cell, usually spindle shaped, that makes the extracellular matrix and collagen and so builds the framework of animal tissues.
The basement membrane is a specialised form of extracellular matrix common to all multicellular animals.
Bird anatomy shows many unique adaptations, mostly aiding flight.
Fish anatomy is the study of the form of fish.
Plant nutrition is the study of the chemical elements and compounds a plant needs for growth, reproduction and metabolism, and of how they are supplied.
The hypocotyl is the stem of a germinating seedling, below the seed leaves and above the first root.
In botany, the radicle is the first part of a seedling to emerge from the seed during germination.
A tumbleweed is a part of the above ground anatomy of a number of plants that, once mature and dry, detaches and rolls with the wind.
Herbaceous plants are vascular plants that have no lasting woody stems above ground.
A liana is a long stemmed woody vine, rooted in the soil at ground level, that uses trees and other supports to climb to the canopy in search of direct sunlight.
In botany, a tendril is a specialised stem, leaf or leaf stalk with a thread like shape, used by climbing plants for support and attachment.
A branch is a stem that grows off another stem, or a vein in a leaf that divides into smaller veins.
In botany, a cortex is the outer layer of a stem or root in a vascular plant, lying below the skin but outside the vascular bundles.
A strobilus is a structure on many land plants consisting of spore bearing parts densely gathered along a stem.
The endodermis is the innermost layer of the cortex in vascular plants, a cylinder of compact living cells.
A conidium is an asexual, non motile spore of a fungus.
Plant physiology is the part of botany concerned with how plants function.
Vegetative reproduction is a form of asexual reproduction in plants, in which a new plant grows from a fragment or cutting of the parent or from a special structure.
A protocarnivorous plant traps and kills insects or other animals but lacks the ability to digest them or to absorb the nutrients directly.
Blinking is a bodily function, a partly automatic rapid closing of the eyelid.
Regurgitation is the backward movement of the contents of the digestive tract into the throat and the mouth.
Belching is the audible release of gas from the upper digestive tract through the throat, and usually out through the mouth.
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines.
Acid and base homeostasis is the regulation of the acidity of the fluid outside the cells of the body.
Warm blooded refers to animal species whose bodies hold a temperature higher than that of their surroundings.
A eurytherm is an organism that can function across a wide range of surrounding temperatures.
A poikilotherm is an animal whose internal temperature varies considerably.
A mesotherm is an animal with a strategy of temperature control lying between the cold blooded and the warm blooded.
Homeothermy is a form of thermoregulation in which an animal holds a stable internal temperature whatever the world outside is doing.
A stenotherm is an organism able to survive only within a narrow range of temperature.
Kleptothermy is any form of thermoregulation by which an animal shares in the heat made by the body of another animal.
Bradymetabolism refers to organisms with a high metabolism while active and a much slower one at rest.
Gigantothermy is the way large bulky animals that do not make their own heat hold a steady and relatively high body temperature more easily than small ones.
Aestivation is a state of animal or plant dormancy, like hibernation but taken in summer rather than winter.
Embryology is the branch of zoology that studies the development of the gametes, fertilisation, and the development of embryos.
In biology, offspring are the young of living organisms, produced either sexually or asexually.
In biology and genetics, the germline is the population of the cells of a multicellular organism that develop into germ cells.
Among animals that produce eggs, the yolk is the nutrient bearing part of the egg.
Pregnancy is the period during which the young of a creature are carried in the body after the joining of egg and sperm, a word used of fish as well as of placental mammals.
Animal embryonic development is the stage of an animal embryo that begins with the fertilisation of an egg cell by a sperm cell.
Blastulation is the stage in early animal development that produces the blastula.
A multiple birth is the end of a multiple pregnancy, in which the mother gives birth to two or more young.
Preterm birth is the birth of a baby well before the usual length of a pregnancy has run.
Plant embryonic development is the process that follows the fertilisation of an ovule and produces a fully formed plant embryo.
An antheridium is a structure or organ producing and containing the male gametes of a plant.
An archegonium is a multicellular structure of the gametophyte phase of certain plants, producing and containing the female gamete.
An oogonium is a small cell which on maturing forms a primordial follicle, or the female gametangium of certain lower plants.
Structural biology is concerned with the structural analysis of biological material at every level of organisation.
Biopolymers are natural polymers produced by the cells of living organisms.
Antioxidants are compounds that inhibit oxidation, a chemical reaction that can produce free radicals.
Lutein is a xanthophyll and one of the many carotenoids that occur in nature.
Monosaccharides, also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds and the units from which every larger sugar is built.
Glyceraldehyde is a monosaccharide of three carbons.
A disaccharide is a sugar formed when two simple sugars are joined by a glycosidic linkage.
Polysaccharides are compounds consisting of a large number of simple sugars linked together.
Dietary fibre, or roughage, is the portion of plant derived food that human digestive enzymes cannot fully break down.
Glutathione is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine and glycine.
An androgen is any natural or synthetic steroid hormone that regulates the development and maintenance of male physiological characteristics in vertebrates.
Ghrelin is a hormone made chiefly by cells of the gastrointestinal tract, especially the stomach, and is called the hunger hormone because it increases the drive to eat.
Glucocorticoids are a class of corticosteroids, which are in turn a class of steroid hormones.
Leptin is a protein hormone made mostly by the cells of adipose tissue.
Progestogens are a class of natural or synthetic steroid hormones that bind to and activate the progesterone receptors.
Secretin is a hormone that regulates the balance of water through the body and sets the conditions in the first part of the small intestine.
A catecholamine is a monoamine neurotransmitter, an organic compound carrying a catechol and a side chain with an amine.
Brassinosteroids are a class of polyhydroxysteroids recognised as a sixth class of plant hormone.
Florigens, or flowering hormones, are proteins capable of setting the time of flowering in flowering plants.
Jasmonate and its derivatives are lipid based plant hormones that regulate a wide range of processes, from growth and photosynthesis to reproduction.
Strigolactones are a group of chemical compounds produced by the roots of plants.
Omega three fatty acids are polyunsaturated fatty acids with a double bond three atoms from the end of the chain.
Omega six fatty acids are a family of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids sharing a final double bond at the sixth bond, counted from the methyl end.
Malacology is the branch of invertebrate zoology that deals with the study of the molluscs, the second largest phylum of animals by described species after the arthropods.
Animal cognition encompasses the mental capacities of animals other than humans, insects included.
Animal consciousness is the quality or state of self awareness within an animal, or of being aware of something outside itself or within itself.
Sleep is broadly considered a biological necessity in virtually all animals.
A midday nap is a short sleep taken in the early afternoon, often after the midday meal.
Wakefulness is a daily recurring brain state in which an individual is conscious and responds coherently to the world outside.
A yawn is a reflex in vertebrate animals, a long slow breath in with the mouth gaping, a brief stretch of the muscles and a quick breath out.
In psychology and ethology, imprinting is a rapid learning process that happens during a particular phase of life and sets the behaviour that follows.
Grooming is the practice of cleaning and maintaining parts of the body.
A maternity den is a lair where a mother animal gives birth and raises her young while they are at their most vulnerable.
In biology, mating refers to the pairing of organisms for the purpose of sexual reproduction.
The fight or flight response is a reaction of the body that occurs in response to a perceived harmful event, attack or threat to survival.
A flock is a gathering of individual birds to forage or travel together.
Any group of fish that stay together for social reasons are shoaling, and if the group swims the same way in a coordinated manner they are schooling.
Bird vocalisation includes both the calls and the songs of birds.
Hematophagy is the practice by certain animals of feeding on blood.
A hypercarnivore is a carnivorous animal whose diet is mostly meat, taken either by hunting or by scavenging.
An insectivore is a carnivorous animal or plant that eats insects.
Browsing is a type of herbivory in which an animal feeds on the leaves, soft shoots or fruit of high growing woody plants such as shrubs.
A hypocarnivore is an animal that eats little meat, the greater part of its diet being fungi, fruit and other plant material.
A mesocarnivore is an animal whose diet is about half meat, the balance made up of insects, fungi, fruit and whatever else is to hand.
Aquatic locomotion, or swimming, is motion through a liquid driven by the animal itself.
Arboreal locomotion is the locomotion of animals in trees.
A facultative biped is a four legged animal able to stand, walk or run on its hind limbs for a time, while going on all fours the rest of the time.
Quadrupedalism is a form of locomotion in which an animal has four legs that bear its weight and move it about.
Terrestrial locomotion is the method by which an organism moves on land.
Tripedalism is locomotion by the use of three limbs, and it is rare.
A number of animals are capable of moving through the air, by active flight, by passive gliding, or in rare cases by ballooning on a thread.
A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug into the ground by an animal to make a space fit to live in or to shelter in.
A nest is a structure built by certain animals to hold their eggs or their young.
Antibiotic sensitivity testing is the measurement of how susceptible bacteria are to antibiotics.
Cell death is the event of a biological cell ceasing to carry out its functions.
Protein targeting is the mechanism by which proteins are carried to their proper destinations within the cell or outside it.
Facilitated diffusion is the spontaneous passive transport of molecules or ions across a biological membrane by way of particular proteins that span it.
A biochemical cascade is a series of chemical reactions that occur within a cell when a stimulus sets them off.
Second messengers are signalling molecules released inside the target cell in response to a signal arriving from outside.
Haematopoietic stem cells are the stem cells that give rise to the other blood cells.
Cell junctions are cellular structures of many proteins that hold neighbouring cells together, or hold a cell to the matrix around it.
A biological membrane is a selectively permeable membrane that separates the interior of a cell from the world outside, or divides one part of a cell from another.
Membrane potential is the difference in electric potential between the interior and the exterior of a biological cell.
Membrane proteins are proteins that are part of, or interact with, biological membranes.
The endomembrane system is the set of membranes suspended in the cytoplasm within a cell that has a nucleus.
A plastid carries a genome of its own, held in the chloroplasts and other plastids within the cells of some organisms.
Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that cross the cell walls of plant cells and of some algae, allowing transport and communication between them.
An autotroph is an organism that can turn sources of energy from the non living world into energy stored in organic compounds.
A biogeographic realm is the broadest division of the land surface of the Earth, based on the patterns in which land organisms are spread.
In ecology, a disturbance is a change in environmental conditions that causes a pronounced change in an ecosystem.
Niche construction is the process by which an organism alters its own local environment, or that of another species.
An ecosystem model is an abstract, usually mathematical, representation of an ecological system, studied in order to understand the real one better.
Energy flow is the flow of energy through living things within an ecosystem.
Island biogeography is the field that examines what governs the richness and the variety of species in isolated natural communities.
The equations of Lotka and Volterra are a pair of nonlinear differential equations used to describe the dynamics of two species, one of which eats the other.
The theory of selection for many or for few examines the trade between the number of offspring and the care given to each.
In ecology, a species interaction is the effect that a pair of organisms living together in a community have on each other.
An ecosystem is a collection of interacting organisms within a physical environment, and it is never static.
Habitat fragmentation is the appearance of breaks in the environment an organism prefers, which breaks the population up with it.
Ecological restoration is the process of assisting the recovery of an ecosystem that has been degraded, damaged, destroyed or transformed.
Wildlife refers to undomesticated animals and uncultivated plants living in their natural habitat, and has come to mean all organisms that live wild in an area without being brought there by people.
In genetics, an enhancer is a short region that proteins can bind to in order to make the transcription of a particular gene more likely.
Post transcriptional modification is the set of processes by which a fresh ribonucleic acid transcript is chemically altered after it is copied from a gene, to make a mature working molecule.
Post translational modifications are the chemical changes made to proteins after they are built and released from the ribosomes.
A non coding ribonucleic acid is a functional molecule of that acid which is not translated into a protein.
An expression vector is usually a plasmid or a virus designed to have a gene expressed inside cells.
Penetrance in genetics is the proportion of individuals carrying a particular variant of a gene who also show the associated trait.
A sex determination system is a biological system that settles the development of the sex of an organism.
Extranuclear inheritance is the handing on of genes that lie outside the nucleus.
Genetic recombination is the exchange of genetic material that leads to offspring with combinations of traits found in neither parent.
Homologous recombination is a type of genetic recombination in which information is exchanged between two similar or identical molecules of nucleic acid.
Quantitative genetics is the study of traits that vary continuously, such as height or mass, rather than falling into distinct kinds.
Heritability is a statistic used in breeding and genetics that estimates how much of the variation in a trait within a population is due to genetic variation between individuals.
Reverse genetics is a method used to understand what a gene does by altering it deliberately and seeing what changes.
Molecular genetics is the branch of biology that addresses how differences in the structure or the expression of genetic molecules show up as variation among organisms.
Molecular evolution describes how inherited genetic material changes over evolutionary time, and what that means for proteins and the other parts of cells.
Epigenomics is the study of the complete set of epigenetic modifications on the genetic material of a cell.
The epigenome of an organism is the collection of chemical changes to its genetic material and to the proteins it is wound on, which affect when, where and how it is read.
Heterosis, or hybrid vigour, is the improved function of a biological quality in a hybrid offspring.
Evolutionary biology is the subfield of biology that analyses the four mechanisms of evolution, which are natural selection, mutation, genetic drift and gene flow.
Sexually reproducing animals, plants, fungi and protists are thought to have evolved from a common ancestor that was a single celled species with a nucleus.
Viral evolution is the subfield of evolutionary biology and virology concerned with the evolution of viruses.
Genetic admixture occurs when previously isolated populations interbreed, giving a population with ancestry from both sources.
A haplotype is a group of alleles inherited together from a single parent, and a haplogroup is a group of similar haplotypes that share a common ancestor.
Nucleic acid structure refers to the structure of the nucleic acids, which carry the information of heredity.
Glycated haemoglobin is any form of haemoglobin that is chemically linked to a sugar.
Protein biosynthesis is a core biological process, occurring inside cells, that balances the loss of proteins by making fresh ones.
Protein structure is the arrangement in three dimensions of the atoms in a chain of amino acids.
A proteome is the entire set of proteins that is, or can be, expressed by a genome, a cell, a tissue or an organism at a given time.
Proteinogenic amino acids are the amino acids that are built into proteins during translation.
A steroid hormone is a steroid that acts as a hormone.
Biosynthesis is chemical synthesis occurring in a living context.
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that break molecules down into smaller units, which are either burned for energy or used to build something else.
Gluconeogenesis is a metabolic pathway that makes glucose out of carbon compounds that are not carbohydrates.
Metabolomics is the study of the small molecules that are the substrates, intermediates and products of the metabolism of a cell.
Secondary metabolites are organic compounds produced by a living thing that are not directly involved in its normal growth, development or reproduction.
Oxidative phosphorylation is the metabolic pathway in which cells use enzymes to oxidise nutrients and so release the chemical energy that makes adenosine triphosphate.
Photosystems are the functional and structural units of protein complexes involved in photosynthesis.
Biological carbon fixation is the process by which living organisms convert inorganic carbon into organic compounds.
Carbon fixation by three carbons is the most common of the three metabolic pathways for fixing carbon in photosynthesis.
Carbon fixation by four carbons is one of the three known photosynthetic processes for fixing carbon in plants.
In phylogenetics, the crown group is a collection of species made up of the living members of a group, their most recent common ancestor, and all of its descendants.
A thallus is the vegetative tissue of organisms in such diverse groups as the algae, the fungi, some liverworts and the lichens.
Accommodation is the process by which the vertebrate eye changes its optical power to keep an object in focus as its distance changes.
A primary vein, also known as the midrib, is the main vascular structure running through the centre of a leaf.
Healing is the repairing of damaged tissue, organs and the whole biological system after injury or disease, and the return to normal function.
A gamete, or sex cell, is a cell carrying one set of chromosomes that fuses with another such cell at fertilisation.

The evolution of plants runs from the earliest algal mats, through green algae of sea and fresh water, to the spore bearing mosses, clubmosses and ferns on land, and at last to the seed bearing plants.
The Bryopsida constitute the largest class of mosses, containing almost all moss species.
Polysporangiophytes are plants in which the spore bearing generation has branching stems that carry the spore cases.
The rhyniophytes are a group of extinct early vascular plants thought to be similar to the genus Rhynia, found in the early Devonian.
Cooksonia is an extinct group of primitive land plants, treated as a genus although probably not a single branch.
The progymnosperms are an extinct group of woody, spore bearing plants that gave rise to the seed plants.
Archaeopteris is an extinct genus of tree with fernlike leaves, standing between the spore plants and the seed plants.
Isoetes, commonly known as the quillworts, is a genus of lycopod.
Lepidodendron is an extinct genus of primitive vascular plants that grew as great treelike forms.
The Lycopodiaceae are an old family of vascular plants, taking in all the core clubmosses and firmosses.
Lycopodium powder is a yellow and tan dustlike powder consisting of the dry spores of clubmoss plants and some fern relatives.
Selaginella, also known as the spikemosses or lesser clubmosses, is a genus of lycophyte.
The zosterophylls are a group of extinct land plants that first appeared in the Silurian period.
The leptosporangiate ferns are one of the four subclasses of ferns, and much the largest group of living ferns.
The Aspleniaceae, the spleenworts, are a family of ferns.
The Dryopteridaceae are a family of ferns known colloquially as the wood ferns.
Lygodium, the climbing ferns, is a genus of about forty species of ferns native to tropical regions across the world.
The Salviniales, commonly known as waterferns, are a widespread order of aquatic and semi aquatic ferns.
The order Cyatheales includes most of the tree ferns.
Marattiaceae is the only family of living ferns in the order Marattiales.
A seed plant is any plant that produces seeds.
Pteridosperms, also known as seed ferns, are a grouping of extinct seed producing plants that looked like ferns.
The Bennettitales are an extinct order of seed plants that appeared in the Permian and died out around the end of the Cretaceous.
Araucariaceae is a family of conifers with three living genera.
Podocarpaceae is a large family of mainly southern hemisphere conifers, of trees and shrubs.
Sciadopitys, commonly called the umbrella pine, is a genus of conifers with a single living species, found only in Japan.
Taxaceae, the yew family, is a family of coniferous trees and shrubs.
The Pacific yew is a species of conifer in the yew family, native to the Pacific Northwest of North America.
Cupressaceae, the cypress family, is a family of conifers, taking in the cypresses, the junipers and the redwoods.
Cryptomeria is a genus of conifer in the cypress family with only one species.
The common juniper is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family.
The Pinaceae, or pine family, is a large family of conifers that includes the cedars, firs, hemlocks, larches, pines and spruces.
The Great Basin bristlecone pine is a long living species of pine found in the higher mountains of California, Nevada and Utah.
Old Tjikko is a very old Norway spruce in the province of Dalarna in Sweden.
The dicotyledons are one of the two groups into which the flowering plants were formerly divided.
Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the water lily family.
Victoria, the giant waterlily, is a genus of aquatic herbs in the water lily family.
The Magnoliaceae are a flowering plant family, the magnolia family.
Piper, the pepper plants or pepper vines, is a genus of great economic and ecological importance.
The palmyra palm is a fan palm native to tropical and subtropical South Asia and Southeast Asia.
The talipot palm is a species of palm native to eastern and southern India and Sri Lanka.
Phytelephas is a genus of palms occurring from southern Panama along the Andes.
The royal palm is a species of palm native to Mexico, the Caribbean, Florida and parts of Central America.
The saw palmetto is a small palm, growing to a height of a few metres at most.
Asparagaceae, known as the asparagus family, is a family of flowering plants among the monocots.
Allium is a large genus of flowering plants, the largest in its family and among the largest plant genera in the world.
Dracaena is a genus of a couple of hundred species of trees and woody shrubs.
The moth orchid is a species of flowering plant in the orchid family.
Xanthorrhoea is a genus of about thirty species of succulent flowering plants found only in Australia.
Tradescantia is a genus of herbaceous perennial wildflowers native to the Americas.
Pandanaceae is a family of flowering plants native to the tropics and subtropics of the Old World.
Carex is a vast genus of grasslike plants in the sedge family, commonly known as the sedges.
Typha latifolia is a perennial wetland plant known in English as the bulrush and in North America as the broadleaf cattail.
Cynodon is a genus of plants in the grass family, native to warm temperate and tropical regions of the Old World.
Oryza is a genus of plants in the grass family that includes the major food crop rice.
Musa acuminata is a species of banana native to southern Asia.
The saba banana is a hybrid banana cultivar from the Philippines.
Ravenala is a genus of flowering plants in the bird of paradise family.
Zingiberaceae, the ginger family, is a family of flowering plants spread through the tropics and subtropics.
Taraxacum is a genus of flowering plants in the daisy family whose species are commonly known as dandelions.
Brassica rapa is an annual to biennial plant species native to Eurasia.
Beta vulgaris, the beet, is a species of flowering plant in the amaranth family.
Reynoutria japonica, commonly called Japanese knotweed, is a herbaceous perennial plant in the knotweed and buckwheat family.
Bougainvillea is a genus of thorny ornamental vines, bushes and trees native to the tropical forests of South America.
Opuntia, commonly called the prickly pear cactus, is a genus of flowering plants in the cactus family, many known for their fruit and their showy flowers.
Hydrangea is a genus of more than seventy species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
Momordica charantia, commonly called the bitter melon, is a tropical and subtropical vine of the gourd family, grown across Asia, Africa and the Caribbean for its edible fruit.
Winter squash is an annual fruit of several species of squash, late growing, hard rinded and long keeping.
Honeysuckle is an arching shrub or twining vine in the genus Lonicera.
Sambucus is a genus of flowering plants whose species are commonly called elder.
Fungi diverged from other life more than a billion years ago, and probably colonised the land during the Cambrian.
Aspergillus is a genus of several hundred mould species found in climates worldwide.
Neurospora crassa is a type of red bread mould of the sac fungi.
The fungi imperfecti are fungi which do not fit the usual classifications because no sexual form of reproduction has been found for them.
Glomeromycota are one of the recognised divisions within the kingdom of the fungi.
A dimorphic fungus is a fungus that can exist in the form of both mould and yeast.
Microsporidia are a group of spore forming parasitic single celled fungi.
Rhizopus is a genus of common fungi living on dead matter, with some specialised parasites on animals.
Schizosaccharomyces pombe, also called the fission yeast, is a species of yeast used in traditional brewing and as a model organism in cell biology.
Edible mushrooms are the fleshy fruit bodies of numerous species of properly identified and prepared fungi.
Pleurotus is a genus of gilled mushrooms known as the oyster mushrooms.
The straw mushroom is a species of edible mushroom grown throughout East and Southeast Asia.
Cordyceps is a genus of sac fungi, many of which are parasitic.
Ergot is a group of fungi of the genus Claviceps.
The Lecanorales are an order of mostly lichen forming fungi.
The Parmeliaceae is a large and diverse family of fungi, and the largest family of lichen forming ones.
Cetraria islandica, also known as Iceland moss, is a lichen of the Arctic and the mountains whose upright leaflike form makes it look like a moss.
Oakmoss is a species of lichen found in mountainous temperate forests throughout the northern hemisphere.
Usnea is a genus of shrubby lichens in the large family Parmeliaceae.
Cladonia rangiferina, known as the reindeer lichen, is a light coloured cup lichen that grows in both hot and cold climates in open, well drained ground.
Lobaria pulmonaria is a large lichen growing on trees, made of a fungus, a green alga and a cyanobacterium living together.
The Myxogastria are a class of slime moulds.
Dictyostelium discoideum is a species of soil dwelling amoeba.
Euglenids are one of the best known groups of single celled organisms with whiplike tails.
The kinetoplastids are a group of flagellated protists marked by a distinctive organelle, a granule holding a large mass of genetic material.
The Archaeplastida are a large group of organisms with a nucleus, comprising the green algae and land plants, the red algae and the glaucophytes.
The glaucophytes are a small group of single celled algae found in fresh water and damp places on land.
Porphyra is a genus of cold water seaweeds that grow in cold shallow seawater.
Spirogyra is a genus of filamentous green algae named for the spiral arrangement of the chloroplasts inside it.
Chlamydomonas is a genus of green algae of single celled swimmers, found in stagnant water, on damp soil, in the sea and even in snow.
Chlorella is a genus of single celled or colonial green algae.
Coccolithophores are single celled organisms that are part of the plankton which feed themselves.
Laminaria is a genus of brown seaweed in the order of the kelps.
Fucus is a genus of brown algae found in the intertidal zones of rocky seashores almost throughout the world.
The golden algae are a large group of algae found mostly in fresh water.
The Asgard archaea are a kingdom of the archaea that carry proteins once thought to belong only to organisms with a nucleus.
Methanobacterium is a genus of archaea which produce methane as a byproduct of their metabolism.
Halobacterium is a genus of archaea that needs a very high concentration of salt to live.
Thermoplasma is a genus of archaea that thrive in acidic and hot surroundings.
Sulfolobus is a genus of microorganism belonging to the archaea.
The evolution of bacteria has gone on for billions of years, since their first great divergence from the line that led to the archaea and to us.
Gram negative bacteria are bacteria that do not hold the violet stain used in the method of Gram for telling bacteria apart.
Anabaena is a genus of filamentous cyanobacteria that live as plankton.
Aliivibrio fischeri is a harmless rod shaped bacterium found in the sea the world over.
Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterium of the family Pasteurellaceae.
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a rod shaped bacterium wrapped in a capsule.
Legionella pneumophila is the bacterium chiefly responsible for the disease named after a legion convention.
Rhizobia are bacteria that fix nitrogen once established inside the root nodules of legumes.
Borrelia is a genus of bacteria of the spirochete phylum.
Corynebacterium is a genus of bacteria that hold the violet stain, and most of them need air.
Mycobacterium is a genus of nearly two hundred species of bacteria in its own family.
Lactobacillus is a genus of bacteria that hold the violet stain, within the family Lactobacillaceae.
Staphylococcus is a genus of bacteria that hold the violet stain.
Virus latency is the ability of a disease causing virus to lie dormant within a cell.
Orthomyxoviridae is a family of ribonucleic acid viruses with nine genera.
Influenza B virus is the only species in its genus within the family of the influenza viruses.
The respiratory syncytial virus is a virus that causes infections of the respiratory tract.
A first aid kit is a collection of supplies and equipment used to give immediate medical care for minor injuries and emergencies until professional treatment can be had.
A medical device is any device intended to be used for medical purposes.
A medical emergency is an acute injury or illness that puts a person's life or long term health at immediate risk.
Medicalisation is the process by which human conditions and problems come to be defined and treated as medical conditions.
The healthcare industry is the group of sectors within the economy that provides the goods and services with which patients are treated.
Search and rescue is the search for, and the giving of aid to, people who are in distress or in imminent danger.
In medicine, triage is the process by which those giving care decide the order in which the injured are treated, and how limited supplies are shared out.
A universal health care system is one in which all the citizens of a country have some level of health coverage.
A white coat is a knee length overcoat worn by professionals in medicine or by those working in a laboratory.
A health professional is a provider of health care treatment and advice, based on formal training and experience.
Allied health professionals are health professionals who provide diagnostic, preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative services alongside medicine and nursing.
An emergency medical technician is a professional who provides emergency medical services.
Midwifery is the health science and profession that deals with pregnancy, with childbirth and with the weeks that follow, the care of the newborn included.
A general practitioner is a doctor who practices general medicine.
In medicine, a surgeon is a medical doctor who performs surgery.
A health facility is, in general, any place where health care is provided.
A clinic is a health facility that is chiefly concerned with the care of patients who do not stay the night.
A doctor's office, called a doctor's surgery in British English, is a medical facility in which one or more doctors receive and treat patients.
An intensive care unit is a special department of a hospital that provides intensive care medicine.
A trauma centre is a hospital equipped and staffed to care for patients with major traumatic injuries, such as falls or collisions.
Human anatomy is the scientific study of the form of the human body.
A cadaver is a dead human body used by medical students and scientists to study anatomy, to identify disease and to find causes of death.
Human variability is the range of possible values for any characteristic, of body or of mind, among human beings.
The coeliac plexus, also called the solar plexus because its nerve fibres radiate outward, is a complex network of nerves in the abdomen.
In human anatomy, the head is the uppermost part of the body, joined to the torso by the neck.
The scalp is the area of the head where the hair of the head grows.
In human anatomy, the forehead is an area of the head bounded by two features of the skull and one of the scalp.
The brow ridge is a bony ridge above the eye sockets of all primates and of some other animals.
The facial skeleton comprises the facial bones that build a portion of the skull.
In human anatomy, the mouth is the first portion of the alimentary canal, receiving food and producing saliva.
Human teeth break food down mechanically, cutting and crushing it ready for swallowing and digestion.
A root canal is the naturally occurring space within the root of a tooth.
The uvula is a conic projection from the back edge of the middle of the soft palate.
The chin is the forward pointing part of the lower jaw, below the lower lip.
Human hair colour is the pigmentation of the hair follicles and shafts, due to two types of melanin.
The anterior cruciate ligament is one of the cruciate ligaments in the human knee.
The latissimus dorsi is a large flat muscle on the back that stretches to the sides and behind the arm.
The human shoulder is made up of three bones, the collarbone, the shoulder blade and the upper arm bone, with their muscles, ligaments and tendons.
The deltoid muscle is the muscle that forms the rounded contour of the human shoulder.
The pelvic floor is a tapered muscular sheet that closes the bottom of the pelvis.
The rectus abdominis is a pair of segmented skeletal muscles on the front of the abdomen.
The human skin is the outer covering of the body and the largest organ of the integumentary system.
Human skin colour ranges from the darkest brown to the lightest hues.
A wrinkle is a fold, ridge or crease in an otherwise smooth surface, such as skin or fabric.
The biceps is a large muscle lying on the front of the upper arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
The thumb is the first digit of the hand, next to the index finger.
The index finger is the second digit of a human hand, lying between the thumb and the middle finger.
The middle finger is the third digit of the human hand, lying between the index finger and the ring finger.
The ring finger is the fourth digit of the human hand, lying between the middle finger and the little finger.
The little finger is the smallest digit of the human hand, next to the ring finger.
Handedness is the preferential use of one hand, which both follows from and causes that hand being stronger, faster or more dextrous.
In vertebrate anatomy, the hip refers either to a region or to a joint on the outer side of the pelvis.
The gluteus maximus is the main extensor muscle of the hip in humans.
A hamstring is any one of the three muscles at the back of the thigh, between the hip and the knee.
In anatomy, the thigh is the area between the hip and the knee.
A medical specialty is a branch of medical practice focused on a defined group of patients, diseases, skills or ways of thinking.
Anaesthesiology is the medical specialty concerned with the care of patients before, during and after surgery.
Angiology is the medical specialty dedicated to the circulatory and lymphatic systems, which is to say the arteries, the veins and the lymphatic vessels.
Audiology is the branch of science that studies hearing, balance and the disorders of both.
Clinical neuroscience is the branch of neuroscience that studies the mechanisms underlying diseases and disorders of the brain and the central nervous system.
Endocrinology is the branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases and the hormones it secretes.
Emergency medicine is the medical specialty concerned with illnesses or injuries that need immediate attention.
Family medicine is a medical specialty that provides continuing and comprehensive health care for the individual and the family across all ages and all parts of the body.
Hepatology is the branch of medicine that takes in the study of the liver, the gallbladder, the biliary tree and the pancreas, and the management of their disorders.
Internal medicine is the specialty for doctors concerned with the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diseases in adults.
Acute medicine is a specialty within internal medicine concerned with the immediate and early management of adults who come into hospital as emergencies.
Intensive care medicine is the medical specialty that deals with seriously or critically ill patients, those at risk of becoming so, and those recovering.
Life extension is the idea of extending the human lifespan, either by steady improvements in medicine or by pushing past the limit that biology seems to set.
A supercentenarian is a person who has reached the age of a hundred and ten or older.
Medical genetics is the branch of medicine that involves the diagnosis and management of inherited disorders.
Medical microbiology is the branch of medical science concerned with the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases.
Nephrology is the specialty concerned with the kidneys, with how they work normally, with their diseases, and with the treatment of those diseases.
Nuclear medicine is the medical specialty that applies radioactive substances in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.
Occupational medicine is the medical specialty that concerns itself with the prevention and treatment of illnesses and injuries that come from work.
Orthopaedic surgery is the branch of surgery concerned with the musculoskeletal system.
Orthotics is the medical specialty that focuses on the design and application of braces, calipers and splints.
Neonatology is a subspecialty of paediatrics concerned with the care, development and diseases of newborn infants, especially those born early or in need of critical care.
Podiatry is the branch of medicine devoted to the study, diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the foot, the ankle and the lower limb.
Reproductive medicine is the branch of medicine concerning the reproductive systems.
Obstetrics is the field of study concentrated on pregnancy, childbirth and the weeks that follow.
Rheumatology is the branch of medicine devoted to the diagnosis and management of disorders whose common feature is inflammation in the bones, muscles, joints and organs.
Sports medicine is the branch of medicine that deals with physical fitness and with the treatment and prevention of injuries from sport and exercise.
In medicine, traumatology is the study of wounds and injuries caused by accident or by violence, and the surgical repair of the damage.
Health education is the profession of educating people about health.
Infant mortality is the death of an infant before its first birthday.
Maternal death is the death of a mother from causes related to pregnancy, or from conditions the pregnancy made worse.
Chiropractic is a form of alternative medicine concerned with the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of mechanical disorders of the musculoskeletal system, especially of the spine.
Medicinal plants have been found and used in traditional medicine since before history was written.
Homeopathy is a pseudoscientific system of alternative medicine.
Naturopathy is a form of alternative medicine.
Osteopathy is a pseudoscientific system of alternative medicine that emphasises physical manipulation of muscle tissue and bone.
African traditional medicine is a range of traditional disciplines involving indigenous herbalism and African spirituality.
The medicine of the ancient Egyptians is some of the oldest that is documented.
Ancient Greek medicine was a body of theories and practices that kept expanding through new ideas and new trials.
A folk healer is an unlicensed person who practices the art of healing using traditional practices, herbal remedies and the power of suggestion.
Humorism was a system of medicine describing a supposed make up and working of the human body, adopted by ancient Greek and Roman physicians and philosophers.
Bloodletting is the deliberate withdrawal of blood from a patient to prevent or cure illness.
Islamic medicine is the science of medicine developed in the Middle East and usually written in Arabic, the common tongue of Islamic civilisation.
Chinese herbology is the theory of traditional Chinese pharmacotherapy, which accounts for most of the treatments in traditional Chinese medicine.
Tui na is a form of alternative medicine similar to shiatsu.
A medical procedure is a course of action intended to achieve a result in the delivery of healthcare.
General anaesthesia is drug induced loss of consciousness that renders a subject unarousable even by painful stimuli.
Local anesthesia is any technique to induce the absence of sensation in a specific part of the body, generally to bring about local insensitivity to pain.
End of life care is health care provided in the time leading up to a person's death.
Hospice care is a type of health care that focuses on easing the pain and symptoms of a terminally ill patient and attending to their emotional and spiritual needs at the end of life.
In vitro fertilisation is a process of fertilisation in which an egg is combined with sperm in vitro, which means in glass.
Surrogacy is an arrangement whereby a woman gets pregnant and gives birth on behalf of another person or couple who will become the child's legal parents after birth.
In medicine, screening is a strategy used to test for as yet unrecognised conditions or risk markers in individuals or populations without symptoms or signs of the disease being screened.
Auscultation is listening to the internal sounds of the body, usually using a stethoscope.
Heart sounds are the noises generated by the beating heart and the resultant flow of blood through it.
Respiratory sounds, also known as lung sounds or breath sounds, are the specific sounds generated by the movement of air through the respiratory system.
A blood culture is a medical laboratory test used to detect bacteria or fungi in a person's blood.
A complete blood count is a set of medical laboratory tests that provide information about the cells in a person's blood.
Many types of glucose tests exist and they can be used to estimate blood sugar levels at a given time or, over a longer period, to obtain average levels.
A lipid profile or lipid panel is a panel of blood tests used to find abnormalities in blood lipid concentrations, such as cholesterol and triglycerides.
Diagnostic microbiology is the study of microbial identification.
Palpation is the process of using one's hands to check the body, especially while perceiving or diagnosing a disease or illness.

Telehealth is the use of electronic information and telecommunication technologies to support long distance clinical health care, patient and professional health related education, health administration and public health.
A urine test is any medical test performed on a urine specimen.
A drug test is a technical analysis of a biological specimen, for example urine, hair, blood, breath, sweat or saliva, to determine the presence or absence of specified drugs or their metabolites.
A pregnancy test is used to determine whether a woman is pregnant or not.
Vital signs are a group of the most crucial medical signs that indicate the status of the body's life sustaining functions.
Normal human body temperature is the typical temperature range found in humans.
The respiratory rate is the rate at which breathing occurs; it is set and controlled by the respiratory center of the brain.

Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is an emergency procedure used during cardiac or respiratory arrest that involves chest compressions, often combined with artificial ventilation, to preserve brain function and maintain circulation until spontaneous breathing and heartbeat can be restored.
Cauterization is a medical practice or technique of burning a part of a body to remove or close off a part of it.
The Heimlich maneuver, also known as an abdominal thrust, is a first aid procedure used to treat upper airway obstructions, or choking, by foreign objects.
Hemodialysis, or simply dialysis, is a process of filtering the blood of a person whose kidneys are not working normally.
Massage is the rubbing or kneading of the body's soft tissues.
Occupational therapy is a healthcare profession that helps people take part in the everyday activities, or occupations, that are important for daily life.
Oxygen therapy, also referred to as supplemental oxygen, is the use of oxygen as medical treatment.
Phage therapy is the therapeutic use of bacteriophages for the treatment of pathogenic bacterial infections.
Stem cell therapy uses stem cells to treat or prevent a disease or condition.

Tracheal intubation, usually simply referred to as intubation, is the placement of a flexible plastic tube into the trachea to maintain an open airway or to serve as a conduit through which to administer certain drugs.
Dental braces are devices used in orthodontics that align and straighten teeth and help position them with regard to a person's bite, while also aiming to improve dental health.
A dental extraction is the removal of teeth from the dental alveolus in the alveolar bone.
A dental implant is a prosthesis that interfaces with the bone of the jaw or skull to support a dental prosthesis such as a crown, bridge, denture or facial prosthesis.
Angioplasty, also known as balloon angioplasty, is a minimally invasive endovascular procedure used to widen narrowed or obstructed arteries or veins.
Caesarean section is the surgical procedure by which one or more babies are delivered through an incision in the mother's abdomen.
Coronary artery bypass surgery is a surgical procedure to treat coronary artery disease, the buildup of plaques in the arteries of the heart.
Debridement is the medical removal of dead, damaged or infected tissue to improve the healing potential of the remaining healthy tissue.
Hysterectomy is the surgical removal of the uterus and cervix.
LASIK, commonly referred to as laser eye surgery or laser vision correction, is a type of refractive surgery for the correction of myopia, hypermetropia and astigmatism.

Neurosurgery, also known in common parlance as brain surgery, is the medical specialty that focuses on the surgical treatment or rehabilitation of disorders that affect any portion of the nervous system.
A heart transplant is a surgical transplant procedure performed on patients with end stage heart failure when other medical or surgical treatments have failed.
Kidney transplant is the organ transplant of a kidney into a patient with end stage kidney disease.

Pharmacotherapy, also known as drug therapy, is medical treatment that uses one or more pharmaceutical drugs to improve ongoing symptoms, treat the underlying condition, or act as a prevention for other diseases.
An adverse effect is an undesired harmful effect resulting from a medication or other intervention, such as surgery.
A drug class is a group of medications and other compounds that share similar chemical structures, act through the same mechanism of action, or are used to treat similar diseases.
In pharmaceutical sciences, drug interactions occur when a drug's mechanism of action is affected by the concomitant administration of substances such as foods, beverages or other drugs.
A psychoactive drug is a chemical substance that alters psychological functioning by modulating central nervous system activity.

Depressants, also known as central nervous system depressants, are a class of psychoactive drugs characterised by decreasing neurotransmission levels, decreasing the electrical activity of brain cells, or reducing arousal or stimulation in various areas of the brain.

Hallucinogens, also known as psychedelics, are a broad and diverse class of psychoactive drugs that can induce altered states of consciousness characterised by marked changes in perception, mood, cognition and self experience.
A sedative, or tranquilizer, is a substance that induces sedation by reducing irritability or excitement.
In the fields of medicine, biotechnology and pharmacology, drug discovery is the process by which new candidate medications are discovered.
In medicine, a side effect is an unintended effect caused by a medicinal drug or other treatment's capacities or properties.
Drug delivery involves various methods and technologies designed to transport pharmaceutical compounds to their target sites, helping therapeutic effect.
Dosage forms are pharmaceutical drug products presented in a specific form for use.
Intravenous therapy is a medical process that administers fluids, medications and nutrients directly into a person's vein.
Oral administration is a route of administration whereby a substance is taken through the mouth, swallowed, and then processed via the digestive system.
A topical medication is a medication applied to a particular place on or in the body.
An anticoagulant, commonly known as a blood thinner, is a chemical substance that prevents or reduces the coagulation of blood, prolonging the clotting time.
Anticonvulsants, also known as antiepileptic drugs, are a diverse group of pharmacological agents used in the treatment of epileptic seizures.
An antidote is a substance that can counteract a form of poisoning.
A bronchodilator is a substance that dilates the bronchi and bronchioles, decreasing resistance in the respiratory airway and increasing airflow to the lungs.
Drugs used in diabetes treat types of diabetes mellitus by decreasing glucose levels in the blood.
Hormone replacement therapy, also known as menopausal hormone therapy, is a form of hormone therapy used to treat symptoms associated with female menopause.
Immunosuppressive drugs, also known as immunosuppressants and antirejection medications, are drugs that inhibit or prevent the activity of the immune system.
Statins are a class of medications that lower the concentration of cholesterol in the blood.
Antihistamines are drugs that counteract the effects of histamine in the body, such as allergies.
An antimicrobial is an agent that kills microorganisms or stops their growth.
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic medication belonging to the aminopenicillin class of the penicillin family.
Doxycycline is a broad spectrum antibiotic of the tetracycline class used in the treatment of infections caused by bacteria and certain parasites.
Aciclovir, also known as acyclovir, is an antiviral medication.
Fluconazole is an antifungal medication used for a number of fungal infections.
Antiparasitics are a class of medications which are indicated for the treatment of parasitic diseases, such as those caused by worms, amoebae, ectoparasites and protozoa.
Nonsteroidal anti inflammatory drugs are members of a therapeutic drug class which reduces pain, decreases inflammation, decreases fever and prevents blood clots.
Opioids are a class of drugs that derive from, or mimic, natural substances found in the opium poppy plant.
Codeine is an opiate and prodrug of morphine mainly used to treat pain, coughing and diarrhea.
Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Methadone is a potent synthetic opioid used medically to treat chronic pain and opioid use disorder.
An anxiolytic is a medication or other intervention that reduces anxiety.

Antipsychotics, previously known as neuroleptics and major tranquilizers, are a class of psychotropic medication primarily used to manage psychosis, principally in schizophrenia but also in a range of other psychotic disorders.
Antidepressants are a class of medications used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, chronic pain and addiction.
A mood stabilizer is a psychiatric medication used to treat mood disorders characterised by intense and sustained mood shifts, such as bipolar disorder.
The DPT vaccine is a class of combination vaccines to protect against three infectious diseases in humans: diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus.
The Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccine, also known as Hib vaccine, is a vaccine used to prevent Haemophilus influenzae type b infection.
Human papillomavirus vaccines are vaccines that prevent infection by certain types of human papillomavirus.
Influenza vaccines, colloquially known as flu shots or flu jabs, are vaccines that protect against infection by influenza viruses.
A malaria vaccine is a vaccine that prevents malaria, a mosquito borne infectious disease.
Meningococcal vaccine refers to any vaccine used to prevent infection by Neisseria meningitidis.
The MMR vaccine is a combination vaccine against measles, mumps and rubella.
Pneumococcal vaccines are subunit vaccines against the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae.
A rabies vaccine is a vaccine used to prevent rabies.
A rotavirus vaccine is a vaccine used to protect against rotavirus infections, which are the leading cause of severe diarrhea among young children.
Typhoid vaccines are vaccines that prevent typhoid fever.
Varicella vaccine, also known as chickenpox vaccine, is a vaccine that protects against chickenpox.
Yellow fever vaccine is a vaccine that protects against yellow fever.
A chronic condition, also known as a chronic disease or chronic illness, is a health condition or disease that is persistent or otherwise long lasting in its effects.

The International Classification of Diseases is the globally authoritative medical classification and terminology used in epidemiology, health management, clinical diagnosis and health information management.
Dermatitis is a term used for different types of skin inflammation, typically characterised by itchiness, redness and a rash.
In anatomy, a fistula is an abnormal connection joining two hollow spaces, such as blood vessels, intestines or other hollow organs to one another.
Kidney failure, also known as renal failure, is a medical condition in which the kidneys can no longer adequately filter waste products from the blood.
Periodontal disease, also known as gum disease, is a set of inflammatory conditions affecting the tissues surrounding the teeth.
Gingivitis is a non destructive disease that causes inflammation of the gums.
A pleural effusion is accumulation of excessive fluid in the pleural space, the potential space that surrounds each lung.
Angina, in full angina pectoris, is chest pain or pressure, usually caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart muscle.
Arrhythmias, also known as cardiac arrhythmias, are irregularities in the heartbeat, which may be too fast or too slow.
Atrial fibrillation is an abnormal heart rhythm characterised by rapid and irregular beating of the atrial chambers of the heart.
Atherosclerosis is a pattern of the disease arteriosclerosis, characterised by the development of atheromatous plaques in the walls of arteries.
Hypotension, also known as low blood pressure, is a cardiovascular condition characterised by abnormally reduced blood pressure.
Thrombosis is the formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel, obstructing the flow of blood through the circulatory system.
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Gastritis is the inflammation of the lining of the stomach.
Inflammatory bowel disease is a group of inflammatory conditions of the colon and small intestine, with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis being the principal types.
A genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
An allergen is an otherwise harmless substance that triggers an allergic reaction in sensitive individuals by stimulating an immune response.
A food allergy is an abnormal immune response to food.
Psoriasis is a long lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterised by patches of abnormal skin.
Starvation is a severe deficiency in caloric energy intake, below the level needed to maintain an organism's life.
Chronic pain is pain that persists or recurs for longer than three months.
A neurodegenerative disease is caused by the progressive loss of neurons, in the process known as neurodegeneration.
Tension headache, also called stress headache, is the most common type of primary headache.
Respiratory diseases, or lung diseases, are pathological conditions affecting the organs and tissues that make gas exchange difficult in air breathing animals.
Emphysema is a condition of the lung characterised by abnormal enlargement of the alveoli with loss of pulmonary elasticity.
Sinusitis, commonly known as a sinus infection, is an inflammation of the mucous membranes that line the sinuses.
Rheumatoid arthritis is a long term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.
The human back, also called the dorsum, is the large posterior area of the human body, rising from the top of the buttocks to the back of the neck.
The pectoralis major is a thick, fan shaped or triangular convergent muscle of the human chest.
The triceps, or triceps brachii, is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
Orthodontics is a dentistry specialty that addresses the diagnosis, prevention, management and correction of mal positioned teeth and jaws, as well as misaligned bite patterns.
Pharmacodynamics is the study of the biochemical and physiologic effects of drugs, especially pharmaceutical drugs.
WASH, from the letters of water, sanitation and hygiene, is a sector in development cooperation, or within local governments, that provides water, sanitation and hygiene services to communities.
A doctor's visit, also known as a physician office visit or a consultation, is a meeting between a patient and a physician to get health advice or a treatment plan for a symptom or condition.
The comprehensive metabolic panel, or chemical screen, is a panel of blood tests that serves as an initial broad medical screening tool.
A cure is a substance or procedure that resolves a medical condition.

Mouth to mouth resuscitation, a form of artificial ventilation, is the act of assisting or stimulating respiration in which a rescuer presses their mouth against that of the victim and blows air into the person's lungs.
Reperfusion therapy is a medical treatment to restore blood flow, either through or around blocked arteries, typically after a heart attack.

Root canal treatment is a treatment sequence for the infected pulp of a tooth, an abscess, that is intended to eliminate the infection and protect the decontaminated tooth from future microbial invasion.
Bariatric surgery, also known as metabolic surgery or weight loss surgery, is a group of surgical procedures used to manage obesity and related conditions.
Incision and drainage, also known as clinical lancing, are minor surgical procedures to release pus or pressure built up under the skin, such as from an abscess or boil.
An inhaler, also called a puffer or asthma pump, is a medical device used for delivering medicines into the lungs through the work of a person's breathing.
In medicine, a nebulizer is a drug delivery device used to administer medication in the form of a mist inhaled into the lungs.
A tablet, also known as a pill, is a pharmaceutical oral dosage form, or solid unit dosage form.
An injection, often called a shot or a jab, is the act of administering a liquid, especially a drug, into a person's body using a needle and a syringe.
Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors are a class of medication used primarily for the treatment of cardiovascular and kidney diseases.
Warfarin is used as an anticoagulant medication.
Carbamazepine is an anticonvulsant medication used in the treatment of epilepsy and neuropathic pain.
Gabapentin is an anticonvulsant medication used to treat neuropathic pain and partial seizures of epilepsy.
Barbiturates are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
Salbutamol, also known as albuterol, is a medication that opens up the medium and large airways in the lungs.
Calamine, also known as calamine lotion, is a medication made from a combination of powdered zinc oxide and ferric oxide that is used to treat mild itching.
Metformin is the main medication for the treatment of type two diabetes, particularly in people who are overweight.
Ephedrine is a central nervous system stimulant and sympathomimetic agent that is often used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia.
Heparin, also known as unfractionated heparin, is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
Hydrocortisone is the name for the hormone cortisol when supplied as a medication.
A hypnotic, also known as a somnifacient or soporific, and commonly known as sleeping pills, is one of a class of psychoactive drugs whose primary function is to induce sleep and to treat insomnia.
Loperamide, sold under the brand name Imodium among others, is a medication of the opioid receptor agonist class used to decrease the frequency of diarrhea.
Naloxone is an opioid antagonist, a medication used to reverse or reduce the effects of opioids.
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class.
Atorvastatin, sold under the brand name Lipitor among others, is a statin medication used to prevent cardiovascular disease in those at high risk and to treat abnormal lipid levels.

A throat lozenge, also known as a cough drop or pastille, is a small, typically medicated tablet intended to be dissolved slowly in the mouth to temporarily stop coughs and soothe irritated tissues of the throat.
An anesthetic or anaesthetic is a drug used to induce anesthesia, in other words, to result in a temporary loss of sensation or awareness.
General anaesthetics are often defined as compounds that induce a loss of consciousness in humans or loss of righting reflex in animals.
Halothane, sold under the brand name Fluothane among others, is a halocarbon.
Isoflurane, sold under the brand name Forane among others, is a halogenated ether used as a general anesthetic.
Ketamine is a dissociative general anesthetic with analgesic and hallucinogenic properties, used medically for anesthesia, depression and pain management.

Midazolam, sold under the brand name Versed among others, is a benzodiazepine medication used for anesthesia, premedication before surgical anesthesia and procedural sedation, and to treat severe agitation.
Propofol is the active component of an intravenous anesthetic used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia.
A local anesthetic is a medication that causes absence of all sensation, including pain, in a specific body part without loss of consciousness, providing local anesthesia.
Benzocaine, sold under the brand name Orajel amongst others, is a local anesthetic, belonging to the amino ester drug class, commonly used as a topical painkiller or in cough drops.
Bupivacaine, sold under the brand name Marcaine among others, is a medication used to decrease sensation in a specific small area.
Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.
Procaine is a local anesthetic drug of the amino ester group.
Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Azithromycin, sold under the brand name Zithromax in oral form, is an antibiotic medication used to treat several bacterial infections.
Cefalexin, also spelled cephalexin, is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections.
Erythromycin is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Ampicillin is an antibiotic belonging to the aminopenicillin class of the penicillin family.
Amphotericin B is an antifungal medication used for serious fungal infections and leishmaniasis.
Medical cannabis, medicinal cannabis or medical marijuana includes cannabis products and cannabinoid molecules that are prescribed by physicians for their patients.

Naproxen, sold under the brand name Aleve among others, is a nonsteroidal anti inflammatory drug used to treat pain, menstrual cramps and inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, gout and fever.
Hydrocodone, also known as dihydrocodeinone, is a semi synthetic opioid used to treat pain and as a cough suppressant.
Oxycodone, sold under the brand names Roxicodone and OxyContin among others, is a semi synthetic opioid used medically for the treatment of moderate to severe pain.
Clonazepam, sold under the brand name Klonopin among others, is a benzodiazepine medication used to prevent and treat anxiety disorders and seizures.
Chlorpromazine, marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.
Amitriptyline, formerly sold under the brand names Elavil or Endep, among others, is a tricyclic antidepressant primarily used to treat major depressive disorder and a variety of pain syndromes.

Bupropion, formerly called amfebutamone, and sold under the brand name Wellbutrin among others, is an atypical antidepressant that is indicated in the treatment of major depressive disorder and seasonal affective disorder and to support smoking cessation.

Fluoxetine, sold under the brand name Prozac among others, is an antidepressant medication of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor class used for the treatment of major depressive disorder and anxiety.

Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are a class of drugs that are typically used as antidepressants in the treatment of major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders and other psychiatric conditions.
A COVID vaccine is designed to induce immunity against the coronavirus responsible for coronavirus disease.
Kidney stone disease or urinary stone disease is a condition that occurs when there is an excess of minerals in the urine and not enough liquid or hydration.
Raynaud syndrome, also known as Raynaud's phenomenon, is a medical condition in which the spasm of small arteries causes episodes of reduced blood flow to the ends of the body.

A skin condition, also known as a cutaneous condition, is any medical condition that affects the integumentary system, the organ system that encloses the body and includes skin, nails and related muscle and glands.

Arteriosclerosis, literally meaning hardening of the arteries, is an umbrella term for a set of vascular disorders characterized by abnormal thickening, hardening and loss of elasticity in the walls of arteries.
High cholesterol, also called hypercholesterolemia, is the presence of high levels of cholesterol in the blood.
Type two diabetes, formerly known as adult onset diabetes, is a form of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance and relative lack of insulin.
Gestational diabetes is a condition in which an individual without diabetes develops high blood sugar levels during pregnancy.
Hyperthyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.

Diverticulitis, also called colonic diverticulitis, is a gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of abnormal pouches, called diverticula, that can develop in the wall of the large intestine.
A gallstone is a stone formed within the gallbladder from precipitated bile components.
Crohn's disease is a type of inflammatory bowel disease that may affect any segment of the gastrointestinal tract.
Ulcerative colitis is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease, with the other type being Crohn's disease.

Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by a group of symptoms that commonly include abdominal pain, abdominal bloating and changes in the consistency of bowel movements.
Huntington's disease, also known as Huntington's chorea, is a fatal neurodegenerative disease that is usually inherited.
Allergic rhinitis, of which the seasonal type is called hay fever, is a type of inflammation in the nose that occurs when the immune system overreacts to allergens in the air.
Fibromyalgia is a long term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
Sunburn is a form of radiation burn that affects living tissue, such as skin, and that results from an overexposure to ultraviolet radiation, usually from the Sun.
A hernia is the abnormal exit of tissue or an organ, such as the bowel, through the wall of the cavity in which it normally resides.
Sciatica is pain going down the leg from the lower back.
Scoliosis is a medical condition in which the spine has an irregular curve in the coronal plane, associated with a rotational component.
A sprain is a soft tissue injury of the ligaments within a joint, often caused by a sudden movement abruptly forcing the joint to exceed its functional range of motion.
Carpal tunnel syndrome is the symptoms and signs characteristic of compressive median neuropathy at the carpal tunnel of the wrist.
Tennis elbow, also known as lateral epicondylitis, is a disease of the attachment point of a forearm muscle on the outer bump of the elbow.
A snakebite is an injury caused by the bite of a snake.
Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can lead to damage of the optic nerve, which transmits visual information from the eye to the brain.
Myopia, also known as nearsightedness or short sightedness, is an eye condition where light from distant objects focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina.
Astigmatism is a vision problem that occurs when the lens or cornea of an eye are slightly egg shaped rather than spherical.
Presbyopia is a physiological insufficiency of optical accommodation associated with the aging of the eye.
Insomnia, also known as sleeplessness, is a sleep disorder causing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for as long as desired.
Jet lag is a temporary physiological condition that occurs when a person's circadian rhythm is out of sync with the time zone they are in.

Sleep apnea is a sleep related breathing disorder in which repetitive pauses in breathing, periods of shallow breathing or collapse of the upper airway during sleep result in poor ventilation and sleep disruption.
Major trauma is any injury that has the potential to cause prolonged disability or death.
Choking, also known as foreign body airway obstruction, is a phenomenon that occurs when breathing is impeded by a blockage inside of the respiratory tract.
Internal bleeding, also called internal haemorrhage, is a loss of blood from a blood vessel that collects inside the body, and is not usually visible from the outside.
A nosebleed, also known medically as epistaxis, is bleeding from the nasal cavity caused by rupture of small blood vessels in the nasal mucosa.
A hip fracture is a break that occurs in the upper part of the femur, the thigh bone, at the femoral neck or rarely the femoral head.
Mandibular fracture, also known as fracture of the jaw, is a break through the mandibular bone.
A nasal fracture, commonly referred to as a broken nose, is a fracture of one of the bones of the nose.
An open fracture, also called a compound fracture, is a type of bone fracture that has an open wound in the skin near the fractured bone.
A skull fracture is a break in one or more of the bones that form the cranial portion of the skull, usually occurring as a result of blunt force trauma.
Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head.
Scalding is a form of thermal burn resulting from heated fluids such as boiling water or steam.
Dental trauma refers to trauma, or injury, to the teeth or periodontium and nearby soft tissues such as the lips and tongue.
