The ruff, Calidris pugnax, is a medium-sized wading bird that breeds in marshes and wet meadows across northern Eurasia, a gregarious sandpiper that is migratory.
A snipe is any of about twenty-six wading bird species in three genera in the family Scolopacidae, distinguished by a very long, slender bill, eyes placed high on the head and camouflaging plumage.
Turnstones are two bird species that constitute the genus Arenaria in the family Scolopacidae, closely related to calidrid sandpipers.
The skuas are a group of predatory and kleptoparasitic seabirds with seven species forming the genus Stercorarius, in the family Stercorariidae.
The four species of avocets are a genus, Recurvirostra, of waders in the same avian family as the stilts, the genus name coming from Latin recurvus, curved backwards, and rostrum, bill.
The Barbary dove, also called the ringed turtle dove or ring dove, Streptopelia risoria, is a domestic member of the dove and pigeon family, Columbidae.
The crowned pigeons, genus Goura, are a genus of birds in the family Columbidae, containing four large species of pigeon endemic to the island of New Guinea and a few surrounding islands.
The Eurasian collared dove, Streptopelia decaocto, often called the collared dove, is a dove species that is grey-buff to pinkish-grey, with a black half-collar edged with white.
The mourning dove, Zenaida macroura, is a member of the dove family, Columbidae, also known as the American mourning dove and the rain dove.
The roadrunners, genus Geococcyx, also known as chaparral birds or chaparral cocks, are two species of fast-running ground cuckoos with long tails and crests.
The grey junglefowl, Gallus sonneratii, also known as Sonnerat's junglefowl, is one of the wild ancestors of the domestic chicken together with the red junglefowl and other junglefowls.
Lady Amherst's pheasant, Chrysolophus amherstiae, is a bird of the order Galliformes and the family Phasianidae.
The limpkin, Aramus guarauna, is a large wading bird related to rails and cranes, found mostly in wetlands in warm parts of the Americas.
Coots are medium-sized water birds that are members of the rail family, Rallidae, constituting the genus Fulica, the name being the Latin term for coot.
Moorhens are medium-sized water birds in the genus Gallinula, Latin for little hen, in the rail family Rallidae.
The South Island takahē, Porphyrio hochstetteri, is a flightless swamphen indigenous to New Zealand and a very large living member of the rail family.
The American crow, Corvus brachyrhynchos, is a large passerine bird species of the family Corvidae, a common bird found throughout much of North America.
The hooded crow, Corvus cornix, also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow in the genus Corvus.
The house crow, Corvus splendens, also known as the Indian, greynecked, Ceylon or Colombo crow, is a common bird of the crow family that is of Asian origin but now found in many parts of the world.
The rook, Corvus frugilegus, is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds, found in the Palearctic from Scandinavia and western Europe to eastern Siberia.
The western jackdaw, Coloeus monedula, also known as the Eurasian jackdaw or simply the jackdaw, is a passerine bird in the crow family, found across Europe and western Asia.

Dippers are members of the genus Cinclus in the bird family Cinclidae, so called because of their bobbing or dipping movements, and are unique among passerines for their ability to dive and swim underwater.
Wagtails are a group of passerine birds that form the genus Motacilla in the family Motacillidae, the common name and genus name derived from their characteristic tail pumping behaviour.
The nuthatches constitute a genus, Sitta, of small passerine birds belonging to the family Sittidae, characterised by large heads, short tails and powerful bills and feet.
The red-billed quelea, also known as the red-billed weaver or red-billed dioch, is a small, seasonally nomadic, sparrow-like bird of the weaver family, Ploceidae, native to sub-Saharan Africa.
The common hill myna, Gracula religiosa, sometimes spelled mynah, is a species of starling found in the hills of South and Southeast Asia.
The common blackbird, Turdus merula, is a species of true thrush, also known as the Eurasian blackbird, to distinguish it from the New World blackbirds.

The waxwings are three species of passerine birds classified in the genus Bombycilla, pinkish-brown and pale grey with distinctive smooth plumage in which many body feathers are not individually visible.
The cocks-of-the-rock, which compose the genus Rupicola, are large cotingid birds native to South America.
The European shag or common shag, Gulosus aristotelis, is a species of cormorant and a member of the genus Gulosus.
The hamerkop, Scopus umbretta, also called the umbrette, is a medium-sized water bird with brown plumage, found in mainland Africa, Madagascar and Arabia, living in a wide variety of wetlands.
Spoonbills are a genus, Platalea, of large, long-legged wading birds with a global distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
Bitterns are birds belonging to the subfamily Botaurinae of the heron family Ardeidae, tending to be shorter-necked and more secretive than other members of the family.
Gannets are seabirds comprising the genus Morus in the family Sulidae, closely related to boobies, and known as solan or solan goose in Scotland.
Kookaburras are terrestrial tree kingfishers of the genus Dacelo native to Australia and New Guinea.
The bee-eaters are a group of birds in the family Meropidae, containing three genera and thirty-one species, many found in Africa and Asia, with a few in southern Europe, Australia and New Guinea.
The rufous hummingbird, Selasphorus rufus, is a small hummingbird with a long, straight and slender bill, known for its extraordinary flight skills.
The oilbird, Steatornis caripensis, locally known as the guácharo, is a bird species found in the northern areas of South America including the Caribbean island of Trinidad.
Potoos, family Nyctibiidae, are a group of birds related to the oilbird, sometimes called poor-me-ones after their haunting calls.
Sandgrouse is the common name for Pteroclidae, a family of sixteen species of bird, members of the order Pterocliformes.
Tropicbirds are a family, Phaethontidae, of tropical pelagic seabirds, the sole living representatives of the order Phaethontiformes.
Grebes are aquatic diving birds in the order Podicipediformes, widely distributed freshwater birds, with some species also found in marine habitats during migration and winter.
The red kangaroo, Osphranter rufus, is a very large kangaroo, a large terrestrial mammal native to Australia and a large extant marsupial, found across mainland Australia.
The eastern grey kangaroo, Macropus giganteus, also called the great grey kangaroo or forester kangaroo, is a marsupial found in the eastern third of Australia.
The western grey kangaroo, Macropus fuliginosus, also referred to as the black-faced kangaroo, mallee kangaroo or sooty kangaroo, is a large and relatively common kangaroo.
A wallaby is a small or middle-sized macropod native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations in New Zealand, Hawaii, the United Kingdom and other countries.
Wallaroo is a common name for several species of moderately large macropods, intermediate in size between the kangaroos and the wallabies, native to Australia and Papua New Guinea.
Tree-kangaroos are marsupials of the genus Dendrolagus, adapted for arboreal locomotion, inhabiting the tropical rainforests of New Guinea and far northeastern Queensland.
Potoroo is a common name for species of Potorous, a genus of smaller marsupials allied to the kangaroos and wallabies.
The quokka is a macropod native to Australia, about the size of a domestic cat, and a member of the genus Setonix.
Pademelons are small marsupials in the genus Thylogale, found in Australia, New Guinea and surrounding islands, and are small members of the macropod family.
The honey possum or noolbenger, Tarsipes rostratus, is a tiny species of marsupial in the genus Tarsipes, assigned to the family Tarsipedidae.
Marsupial moles, from the genus Notoryctes, are two species of highly specialised marsupial mammals found in the Australian interior, small burrowing marsupials.
A dunnart is a narrow-footed marsupial the size of a European mouse, of the genus Sminthopsis, with a largely insectivorous diet.

Cancer pagurus, commonly known as the edible crab or brown crab, is a species of crab found in the North Sea, North Atlantic Ocean and perhaps the Mediterranean Sea, a robust crab of a reddish-brown colour.
Callinectes sapidus, commonly known as the blue crab or Atlantic blue crab, is a species of crab native to the waters of the western Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico.
Carcinus maenas is a common littoral crab, known by different names around the world, and referred to in the British Isles as the shore crab or green shore crab.
Ranina ranina, also known as the red frog crab or spanner crab, is a species of crab found throughout tropical and subtropical habitats, often fished for its meat.
Scylla serrata, often called mud crab or mangrove crab, is an ecologically important species of crab found in the estuaries and mangroves of Africa, Australia and Asia.
Ghost crabs are semiterrestrial crabs of the subfamily Ocypodinae, common shore crabs in tropical and subtropical regions.
Maja squinado, the European spider crab or spiny spider crab, is a species of migratory crab found in the Mediterranean Sea.
The velvet crab, Necora puber, also known as the velvet swimming crab or devil crab, is a species of crab from the North-East Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
Freshwater crabs are distributed throughout the tropics and subtropics, divided among eight families, showing direct development and maternal care of a small number of offspring.

Procambarus clarkii, known variously as the red swamp crayfish, Louisiana crawfish or mudbug, is a species of cambarid crayfish native to freshwater bodies of northern Mexico and the southern United States.
Astacus astacus, the European crayfish, noble crayfish or broad-fingered crayfish, is a common species of crayfish in Europe and a traditional food source.
Homarus gammarus, known as the European lobster or common lobster, is a species of clawed lobster from the eastern Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea and parts of the Black Sea.
Nephrops norvegicus, known variously as the Norway lobster, Dublin Bay prawn, langoustine or scampi, is a slim, coral-colored lobster.
Penaeus monodon, commonly known as the giant tiger prawn, Asian tiger shrimp or black tiger shrimp, is a marine crustacean that is widely reared for food.
Whiteleg shrimp, Penaeus vannamei, also known as Pacific white shrimp, is a species of prawn of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
Pandalus borealis is a species of caridean shrimp found in cold parts of the northern Atlantic and northern Pacific Oceans.
Crangon crangon is a species of caridean shrimp found across the northeastern Atlantic Ocean, its range extending from the White Sea in the north of Russia to the coast of Morocco.
Macrobrachium rosenbergii is a commercially important species of palaemonid freshwater prawn, native throughout the tropical and subtropical areas of the Indo-Pacific region.
Cleaner shrimp is a common name for a number of swimming decapod crustaceans that clean other organisms of parasites.
Pollicipes pollicipes, known as the goose neck barnacle, goose barnacle or leaf barnacle, is a species of goose barnacle, also known under the taxonomic synonym Pollicipes cornucopia.
Sea-Monkeys is a marketing term for brine shrimp sold as novelty aquarium pets, developed in the United States and sold under the Sea-Monkeys name from the early nineteen sixties.
Solifugae is an order of arachnids known variously as solifuges, sun spiders, camel spiders, wind scorpions and jerrymanders.
Uropygi is an arachnid order comprising invertebrates commonly known as whip scorpions or vinegaroons, also spelled vinegarroons and vinegarones, and often called uropygids.
Amblypygi is an order of arachnids also known as whipspiders or tailless whipscorpions, the name meaning blunt tail, a reference to a lack of the flagellum seen in related orders.
The flour mite, Acarus siro, a pest of stored grains and animal feedstuffs, is one of many species of grain and flour mites.
Trombiculidae, commonly referred to in North America as chiggers and in Britain as harvest mites, and also known as berry bugs, bush-mites, red bugs or scrub-itch mites, are a family of mites.
Tityus serrulatus, the Brazilian yellow scorpion, is a species of scorpion of the family Buthidae, native to Brazil, and its venom is extremely toxic.
Phoneutria is a genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae, mainly found in northern South America, with one species in Central America.
Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species commonly known as the true widows.
Bagheera kiplingi is a species of jumping spider found in Central America, including Mexico, Costa Rica and Guatemala, and the type species of the genus Bagheera.
Portia is a genus of jumping spider that feeds on other spiders, remarkable for an intelligent hunting behaviour.
Pholcus phalangioides, commonly known as the cosmopolitan cellar spider, long-bodied cellar spider or a daddy long-legs spider, is a spider of the family Pholcidae.
The spider species Tegenaria domestica, commonly known as the barn funnel weaver in North America and the domestic house spider in Europe, is a member of the funnel-web family Agelenidae.
The Thomisidae are a family of spiders, and the common name crab spider is often linked to species in this family, though it may also be used for spiders from other families.
Dolomedes is a genus of large spiders of the family Dolomedidae, also known as fishing spiders, raft spiders, dock spiders or wharf spiders.
Brachypelma hamorii is a vulnerable species of tarantula found in Mexico, confused with a related species, both having been called Mexican redknee tarantulas.
Aphonopelma chalcodes, commonly known as the western desert tarantula, desert blonde tarantula, Arizona blonde tarantula or Mexican blonde tarantula, is a species of spider.
Poecilotheria metallica, also known as the peacock tarantula or the Gooty sapphire tarantula, is an Old World species of tarantula.
The Agelenidae are a large family of spiders in the suborder Araneomorphae, well-known examples including the common grass spiders of the genus Agelenopsis.
Linyphiidae, spiders commonly known as sheet weavers or money spiders, is a family of very small spiders.
Theridiidae, also known as the tangle-web spiders, cobweb spiders and comb-footed spiders, is a large family of araneomorph spiders.
The caddisflies, order Trichoptera, are a group of insects with aquatic larvae and terrestrial adults.
Snakeflies are a group of predatory insects comprising the order Raphidioptera, the name from Ancient Greek meaning needle wing.
Thrips, order Thysanoptera, commonly known as thunderflies or thunderbugs, are minute, slender insects with fringed wings and unique asymmetrical mouthparts.
The dog flea, Ctenocephalides canis, is a species of flea that lives as an ectoparasite on a wide variety of mammals, particularly the domestic dog and cat.

Pyrochroa coccinea, commonly known as the black-headed cardinal beetle, is a species of cardinal beetle in the family Pyrochroidae, found mainly in wooded areas and pastures throughout central and northern Europe.
Ground beetles are a large, cosmopolitan family of beetles, known as Carabidae, with many thousands of species worldwide.
The rove beetles are a family, Staphylinidae, of beetles primarily distinguished by their short elytra that typically leave more than half of their abdominal segments exposed.
Coccinella septempunctata, commonly known as the seven-spot ladybird, or seven-spotted ladybug in North America, is a carnivorous beetle.
Honeypot ants, also called honey ants, are ants with specialized workers that consume large amounts of food to the point that their abdomens swell enormously.
Formica rufa, also known as the red wood ant, southern wood ant or horse ant, is a boreal member of the Formica rufa group of ants, described by Linnaeus.
The yellow crazy ant, Anoplolepis gracilipes, also known as the long-legged ant or Maldive ant, is a species of ant thought to be native to Asia.
Halobates, colloquially the sea skaters or ocean striders, are an insect genus of water striders, mostly coastal and found in sheltered marine habitats.
Belostomatidae is a family of freshwater hemipteran insects known as giant water bugs or colloquially as toe-biters, Indian toe-biters and electric-light bugs.
Corixidae is a family of aquatic insects in the order Hemiptera, found worldwide in virtually any freshwater habitat and a few species live in saline water.
Notonectidae is a cosmopolitan family of aquatic insects in the order Hemiptera, commonly called backswimmers because they swim supine in a kind of backstroke.
Ranatra is a genus of slender predatory insects of the family Nepidae, known as water mantis, water scorpions or water stick-insects.
The Pentatomoidea are a superfamily of insects in the suborder Heteroptera of the order Hemiptera, which possess a common arrangement of sucking mouthparts.
The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae, easily recognisable by its striking red and black coloration.
The Reduviidae is a large cosmopolitan family of the suborder Heteroptera of the order Hemiptera, commonly known as assassin bugs.
The family Fulgoridae is a large group of hemipteran insects, especially abundant and diverse in the tropics, mostly of moderate to large size.
The superfamily Cercopoidea, some members of which are called froghoppers and others known as spittlebugs, are a group of hemipteran insects in the suborder Auchenorrhyncha.
Macrotermes bellicosus is a species of Macrotermes, whose queens are very large termites when physogastric.
Coptotermes gestroi, commonly known as the Asian subterranean termite, is a small species of termite that lives underground.
Parasitoid wasps are a large group of hymenopteran superfamilies, which as parasitoids lay their eggs on or in the bodies of other arthropods.
The Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths; many of their caterpillars are known as hornworms.
The Noctuidae, commonly known as noctuid moths or owlet moths, and their caterpillars as cutworms or armyworms, are a family of moths.
The Lasiocampidae are a family of moths also known as eggars, tent caterpillars, snout moths or lappet moths.
The Tortricidae are a family of moths, commonly known as tortrix moths or leafroller moths, in the order Lepidoptera.
Empusidae is a family of plant-mimicking mantises, consisting of ten genera in two subfamilies.
The chasers, darters, skimmers and perchers and their relatives form the Libellulidae, a large family of dragonflies.
The orthopteran family Rhaphidophoridae of the suborder Ensifera has a worldwide distribution, with common names including cave crickets, camel crickets and spider crickets.
Tetrigidae is an ancient family in the order Orthoptera, which also includes crickets, grasshoppers and their allies.
Heteropteryx is a genus of stick insects containing the described species Heteropteryx dilatata, which gives its name to the family Heteropterygidae.
The family Phylliidae is a family of stick insects containing the extant true leaf insects or walking leaves, remarkably camouflaged leaf mimics.
Timema is a genus of relatively short-bodied, stout and wingless stick insects native to the far western United States.
Psocodea is a taxonomic group of insects comprising the barklice, booklice and parasitic lice.
Cecidomyiidae is a family of flies known as gall midges or gall gnats, whose larvae mostly feed within plant tissue, creating abnormal plant growths called galls.
Psychodidae, common name moth flies, is a family of true flies, many genera having short, hairy bodies and wings that give a furry moth-like appearance.
The Tachinidae are a large and variable family of true flies within the insect order Diptera.
The Tephritidae are one of two fly families referred to as fruit flies, the other being the Drosophilidae.
Coreidae is a large family of predominantly sap-sucking insects in the Hemipteran suborder Heteroptera.
A cockle is a marine bivalve mollusc; true cockles are species in the family Cardiidae and live in sandy, sheltered beaches.
The Veneridae or venerids, common name Venus clams, are a very large family of minute to large, saltwater clams, marine bivalve molluscs.
The Pinnidae are a taxonomic family of large saltwater clams sometimes known as pen shells, marine bivalve molluscs in the order Pteriida.
Rudists are a group of extinct box-, tube- or ring-shaped marine heterodont bivalves belonging to the order Hippuritida that arose during the Late Jurassic.
Unionida is a monophyletic order of freshwater mussels, aquatic bivalve molluscs, including the freshwater pearl mussels.
Nautiloids are a group of cephalopods that originated in the Late Cambrian and are represented today by the living Nautilus and Allonautilus.
Amphioctopus marginatus, also known as the coconut octopus and veined octopus, is a medium-sized cephalopod found in the tropical waters of the western Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean.
Spirula spirula is a species of deep-water squid-like cephalopod mollusk, a member of the genus Spirula, the family Spirulidae and the order Spirulida.
The order Aplysiida, commonly known as sea hares, are medium-sized to very large opisthobranch gastropod molluscs with a soft internal shell made of protein.
Clione limacina, known as the naked sea butterfly, sea angel and common clione, is a pelagic sea slug found from the surface to great depths.
A land snail is any of the numerous species of snail that live on land, as opposed to the sea snails and freshwater snails.
Achatina is a genus of medium-sized to very large, air-breathing, tropical land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusks in the family Achatinidae.
Helicidae is a large, diverse family of western Palaearctic, medium to large-sized, air-breathing land snails, sometimes called the typical snails.
Sea snails are slow-moving marine gastropod molluscs, usually with visible external shells, such as whelk or abalone.
Charonia is a genus of very large sea snail, commonly known as Triton's trumpet or Triton snail, marine gastropod mollusks.
Muricidae is a large and varied taxonomic family of small to large predatory sea snails, marine gastropod mollusks, commonly known as murex snails or rock snails.
Turritellidae, with the common name tower shells or tower snails, is a taxonomic family of small- to medium-sized sea snails that are filter feeders.
Wentletraps are small, often white, very high-spired, predatory or ectoparasitic sea snails, marine gastropod mollusks in the family Epitoniidae.
Scotoplanes globosa, commonly known as the sea pig, is a species of sea cucumber that lives in the deep sea.
Culcita is a genus of sea stars found in tropical waters, some of which are kept in home aquariums.
Arenicola, also known as sandworms, is a genus of capitellid annelid worms comprising the lugworms and black lugs.
Nereididae is a family of polychaete worms, mostly marine, grouped into many genera.
Tubifex is a widespread genus of tubificid segmented worms that inhabits the sediments of lakes, rivers and occasionally sewer lines, and is globally distributed.
Nematomorpha, sometimes called Gordiacea and commonly known as horsehair worms, hairsnakes or Gordian worms, are a phylum of parasitoid animals similar to yet distinct from nematode worms.
The Chaetognatha or chaetognaths, meaning bristle-jaws, are a phylum of predatory marine worms that are a major component of plankton worldwide.
The rotifers, sometimes called wheel animals or wheel animalcules, make up a phylum, Rotifera, of microscopic and near-microscopic pseudocoelomate animals.
Hallucigenia is a genus of lobopodian known from Cambrian-aged fossils in Burgess Shale-type deposits in Canada and China, and from isolated spines around the world.
Ottoia is a stem-group archaeopriapulid worm known from Cambrian fossils.
Dickinsonia is a genus of extinct organism that lived during the late Ediacaran period in what is now Australia, China, Russia, Canada and Ukraine.
Trichoplax is a genus placed in the phylum Placozoa, and the species Trichoplax adhaerens is one of four placozoan species.
Ascidiacea, commonly known as the ascidians or sea squirts, is a paraphyletic class in the subphylum Tunicata of sac-like marine invertebrate filter feeders.
A salp is a barrel-shaped, planktonic tunicate in the family Salpidae, moving by contracting its gelatinous body in order to pump water through it.
Praya dubia, the giant siphonophore, is a species of siphonophore hydrozoan that lives in the mesopelagic zone to bathypelagic zone below sea level.
Chrysaora fuscescens, the Pacific sea nettle or West Coast sea nettle, is a regionally distributed jellyfish that lives in the northeastern Pacific Ocean.
Alcyonacea, in English soft corals or alcyonacians, is a former order, or suborder, of Octocorallia.
Hexactinellid sponges are sponges with a skeleton made of four- and or six-pointed siliceous spicules, often referred to as glass sponges.
Demosponges or common sponges are sponges of the class Demospongiae, a very diverse group in the phylum Porifera that includes nearly all extant sponges.
The calcareous sponges or calcereans are sponges that make up the class Calcarea, characterized by spicules made of calcium carbonate.
The Sipuncula or Sipunculida, common names sipunculid worms or peanut worms, is a class of marine annelid worms that have secondarily lost their segmentation.
Wiwaxia is a genus of prehistoric soft-bodied animals that were covered in carbonaceous scales and spines that protected it from predators.
Canadaspis, meaning shield of Canada, is an extinct genus of bivalved Cambrian marine arthropod, known from North America and China.
Sidneyia is an extinct marine arthropod known from fossils found from the Early to the Mid Cambrian of China and the Burgess Shale of British Columbia, Canada.
Jaekelopterus is an extinct genus of eurypterid, a group of extinct aquatic arthropods, with fossils from deposits of Middle Silurian to Early Devonian age.
Megarachne is a genus of eurypterid, an extinct group of aquatic arthropods, with fossils discovered in deposits of Late Carboniferous age.
The curlews are a group of nine species of birds in the genus Numenius, characterised by their long, slender, downcurved bills and mottled brown plumage.
A phalarope is any of three living species of slender-necked shorebirds in the genus Phalaropus of the bird family Scolopacidae.
The common wood pigeon, Columba palumbus, also known simply as the wood pigeon, is a large pigeon native to the western Palearctic.
The Himalayan monal, Lophophorus impejanus, also called the Impeyan monal, is a landfowl native to Himalayan forests and shrublands, part of the family Phasianidae.
Pheasants are birds of several genera within the family Phasianidae in the order Galliformes, found all over the world in introduced and captive populations.
The Australian magpie, Gymnorhina tibicen, is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand.
The oriental pied hornbill, Anthracoceros albirostris, is an Indo-Malayan pied hornbill, a large canopy-dwelling bird belonging to the family Bucerotidae.
A feathered dinosaur is any species of dinosaur possessing feathers, including all species of birds.
Saurischia is one of the two basic divisions of dinosaurs, the other being Ornithischia, classified by their hip structure.
Thescelosaurus is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in western North America.
Pachycephalosauria is a clade of ornithischian dinosaurs that, along with Ceratopsia, makes up the clade Marginocephalia, and lived in the Northern Hemisphere.
Pachyrhinosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of North America.
Yinlong is a genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period of China, a small, primarily bipedal herbivore.
Ornithopoda is a clade of ornithischian dinosaurs, called ornithopods, representing one of the successful groups of herbivorous dinosaurs during the Cretaceous.
Hypsilophodon is a neornithischian dinosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous period of England.
Leaellynasaura, meaning Leaellyn's lizard, is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous.
Hadrosauridae is a family of ornithischian dinosaurs informally referred to as duck-billed dinosaurs, for the flat duck-bill appearance of their snouts.
Lambeosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of western North America.
Thyreophora, meaning shield bearers, often known simply as armored dinosaurs, is a group of armored ornithischian dinosaurs that lived from the Early Jurassic until the end of the Cretaceous.
Ankylosauria is a group of herbivorous dinosaurs of the clade Ornithischia, including the great majority of dinosaurs with armor in the form of bony osteoderms.
Nodosauridae is a family of ankylosaurian dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic to the Late Cretaceous periods in what is now Asia, Europe, North America and possibly South America.
Scelidosaurus is a genus of herbivorous armoured ornithischian dinosaur from the Jurassic of England.
Stegosauria is a group of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs that lived during the Jurassic and early Cretaceous periods.
Camarasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in North America.
Europasaurus, meaning Europe lizard, is a basal macronarian sauropod, a form of quadrupedal herbivorous dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic.
Mamenchisauridae is a family of sauropod dinosaurs belonging to the Eusauropoda known from the Jurassic and Early Cretaceous of Asia and Africa.
Titanosaurs, members of the group Titanosauria, were a diverse group of sauropod dinosaurs, including genera from every continent.
Saltasauridae, named after the Salta region of Argentina where they were found, is a family of armored herbivorous sauropods from the Upper Cretaceous.
Carnosauria is an extinct group of carnivorous theropod dinosaurs that lived during the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.
Abelisauridae, meaning Abel's lizards, is a family of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaurs that thrived during the Cretaceous period, mainly on the ancient southern continents.
Masiakasaurus is a genus of small predatory theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar, the name meaning vicious lizard.
Spinosauridae is a clade or family of tetanuran theropod dinosaurs comprising ten to seventeen known genera, with fossils recovered worldwide.
Coelurosauria, meaning hollow-tailed lizards, is the clade containing all theropod dinosaurs more closely related to birds than to carnosaurs.
Alvarezsauridae is a family of small, long-legged dinosaurs, once thought to represent early flightless birds.
Anchiornis is a genus of small, four-winged paravian dinosaurs, named for its similarity to modern birds.
Caenagnathidae is a family of derived caenagnathoid dinosaurs from the Cretaceous of North America and Asia, a member of the Oviraptorosauria.
Dromaeosauridae is a family of feathered coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs, generally small to medium-sized feathered carnivores that flourished in the Cretaceous period.
Halszkaraptor is a genus of waterfowl-like dromaeosaurid dinosaurs from Mongolia that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Incisivosaurus, meaning incisor lizard, is a genus of small, probably herbivorous theropod dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous period of what is now China.
Ornithomimosauria, meaning bird-mimic lizards, are theropod dinosaurs which bore a superficial resemblance to the modern-day ostrich.
Ornithomimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of western North America, a swift, bipedal animal.
Scansoriopterygidae, meaning climbing wings, is an extinct family of climbing and gliding maniraptoran dinosaurs.
Troodontidae is a clade of bird-like theropod dinosaurs from the Late Jurassic to Late Cretaceous.
Tyrannosauroidea, meaning tyrant lizard forms, is a superfamily of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs that includes the family Tyrannosauridae as well as more basal relatives.
Anurognathidae is a family of small, short-tailed pterosaurs that lived in Europe, Asia and possibly North America during the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.
Azhdarchidae is a family of pterosaurs known mostly from the Late Cretaceous, including very large flying animals, though smaller cat-size members have also been found.
Hatzegopteryx is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur found in the late Maastrichtian deposits of the Densuș-Ciula Formation in Transylvania, Romania.
Dimorphodon is a genus of medium-sized pterosaur that lived in Europe during the early Jurassic period, named by the paleontologist Richard Owen.
Dsungaripterus is a genus of dsungaripterid pterosaur which lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now China.
Peteinosaurus is an extinct genus of pterosaur that lived during the late Norian age of the Late Triassic.
Pterodaustro is a genus of ctenochasmatid pterodactyloid pterosaur from South America, with fossil remains from the Early Cretaceous period.
Rhamphorhynchus is a genus of long-tailed pterosaurs in the Jurassic period, less specialized than contemporary short-tailed pterodactyloid pterosaurs.
Ornithocheirus is a pterosaur genus known from fragmentary fossil remains uncovered from sediments in the United Kingdom and possibly Morocco.
Tapejaridae is a family of azhdarchoid pterosaurs from the Cretaceous period, known from Africa, Asia, Europe, South America and possibly North America.
Thalassodromeus is a genus of pterosaur that lived in what is now Brazil during the Early Cretaceous period.
Aetosaurs are heavily armored reptiles belonging to the extinct order Aetosauria, medium- to large-sized omnivorous or herbivorous pseudosuchians.
Euparkeria is an extinct genus of archosauriform reptile from the Triassic of South Africa, close to the ancestry of Archosauria, the reptile group that includes crocodilians and dinosaurs.
Phytosaurs are an extinct group of large, mostly semiaquatic Late Triassic archosauriform or basal archosaurian reptiles of the order Phytosauria.
Postosuchus, meaning crocodile from Post, is an extinct genus of rauisuchid that lived in what is now North America during the Late Triassic.
Proterosuchus is an extinct genus of archosauriform reptiles that lived during the Early Triassic.
Teleosauridae is a family of extinct typically marine crocodylomorphs similar to the modern gharial that lived during the Jurassic period.
Notosuchia is a clade of primarily Gondwanan mesoeucrocodylian crocodylomorphs that lived during the Jurassic and Cretaceous.
Kaprosuchus is an extinct genus of mahajangasuchid crocodyliform, known from a single nearly complete skull collected from the Upper Cretaceous Echkar Formation of Niger.
Simosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodyliforms from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar, named for its unusually short skull.
Voay is an extinct genus of crocodile from Madagascar that lived during the Late Pleistocene to Holocene.
Longisquama is a genus of extinct reptile known from a poorly preserved skeleton and several incomplete fossil impressions.
Tanystropheus is an extinct genus of archosauromorph reptile which lived during the Triassic period in Europe, Asia and North America, recognizable by its extremely elongated neck.
Rhynchosaurs are a group of extinct herbivorous Triassic archosauromorph reptiles, belonging to the order Rhynchosauria, distinguished by their triangular skulls and elongated beaks.
Scutosaurus, meaning shield lizard, is an extinct genus of pareiasaurian sauropsid.
Megalania, Varanus priscus, is an extinct species of giant monitor lizard, part of the megafaunal assemblage that inhabited Australia during the Pleistocene.
Tylosaurus is a genus of russellosaurine mosasaur, an extinct group of predatory marine lizards, that lived about ninety-two to sixty-six million years ago.
Champsosaurus is an extinct genus of crocodile-like choristodere reptile, known from the Late Cretaceous and early Paleogene periods of North America and Europe.
Meiolania is an extinct genus of meiolaniid stem-turtle native to Australasia throughout much of the Cenozoic.
Proganochelys is a genus of extinct, primitive stem-turtle, named by Georg Baur in the eighteen eighties.
Ophthalmosaurus is a genus of ichthyosaur known from the Middle to Late Jurassic.
Temnodontosaurus, meaning cutting-tooth lizard, is an extinct genus of large ichthyosaurs that lived during the Lower Jurassic in what is now Europe.
Mesosaurus, meaning middle lizard, is an extinct genus of marine reptile from the late Early Permian of southern Africa and South America.
Nothosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropterygian reptile from the Triassic period, with fossils distributed throughout the former Tethys Ocean.
Placodonts, meaning tablet teeth, are an extinct order of marine reptiles that lived during the Triassic period.
Cryptoclidus is a genus of plesiosaur reptile from the Middle Jurassic period of England, France and Cuba.
Kronosaurus is an extinct genus of large short-necked pliosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Australia.
Diadectes, meaning crosswise-biter, is an extinct genus of large reptiliomorphs that lived during the early Permian period.
Seymouria is an extinct genus of seymouriamorph from the Early Permian of North America and Europe, well adapted to life on land though in a biological sense an amphibian.
Edaphosaurus, meaning pavement lizard for the dense clusters of its teeth, is a genus of extinct edaphosaurid synapsids that lived in what is now North America and Europe.
Thrinaxodon is an extinct genus of cynodonts which lived in what are now South Africa and Antarctica during the Early Triassic.
Lystrosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous dicynodont therapsids from the late Permian and Early Triassic epochs.
Moschops, Greek for calf face, is an extinct genus of dinocephalian therapsids that lived in what is now South Africa during the Middle Permian.
Gorgonops is an extinct genus of gorgonopsian therapsid, of which it is the type genus, living from the late Middle Permian to the Late Permian.
Inostrancevia is an extinct genus of large carnivorous therapsids which lived during the Late Permian in what is now European Russia and Southern Africa.
Hylonomus is an extinct genus of early possible amniote that lived during the Late Carboniferous.
Hyaenodonta, meaning hyena teeth, is an extinct order of carnivorous placental mammals that were important mammalian predators.
Mesonychidae, meaning middle claws, is an extinct family of small to large omnivorous-carnivorous mammals, one of the two families in the order Mesonychia.
Oxyaenidae, meaning sharp hyenas, is a family of extinct carnivorous placental mammals, traditionally classified in the order Creodonta.
Pantodonta is an extinct order of eutherian mammals, herbivorous mammals that were among the early groups of large mammals to evolve.
Notoungulata is an extinct order of ungulates that inhabited South America from the early Paleocene to the end of the Pleistocene.
Litopterna is an extinct order of South American native ungulates that lived from the Paleocene to the Pleistocene.
Brontotheres, literally thunder beasts, also called titanotheres, are an extinct group of perissodactyl mammals belonging to the family Brontotheriidae.
Chalicotheriidae is an extinct family of herbivorous, perissodactyl mammals that lived in North America, Eurasia and Africa from the Oligocene to the Early Pleistocene.
Anoplotherium is the type genus of the extinct Palaeogene artiodactyl family Anoplotheriidae, which was endemic to Western Europe.
Entelodontidae is an extinct family of pig-like artiodactyls that inhabited the Northern Hemisphere from the Middle Eocene to the Early Miocene.
Dorcatherium is an extinct genus of tragulid ruminant which existed in Europe, East Africa and the Siwaliks during the Miocene.
Odobenocetops is an extinct genus of small toothed whale that inhabited the southwestern coast of South America during the late Miocene.
Moeritherium, meaning Lake Moeris' beast, is an extinct genus of basal proboscideans from the Eocene of North and West Africa.
Gomphotheres are an extinct group of proboscideans related to modern elephants.
Desmostylia is an extinct order of aquatic mammals native to the North Pacific from the Early Oligocene to the Late Miocene.
Castorocauda is an extinct, semi-aquatic, superficially otter-like genus of docodont mammaliaforms with one species, Castorocauda lutrasimilis.
Megazostrodon is an extinct genus of basal mammaliaforms belonging to the order Morganucodonta.
Repenomamus, from Latin words for reptile and mammal, is a genus of opossum- to badger-sized gobiconodontid mammal containing two species.
Eomaia, meaning dawn mother, is a genus of extinct fossil mammals containing the species Eomaia scansoria, discovered in the Yixian Formation, Liaoning Province, China.
Sparassodonta is an extinct order of carnivorous metatherian mammals related to modern marsupials.
Didelphodon is a genus of extinct metatherian mammal from the Late Cretaceous of North America.
Ceratogaulus is an extinct genus of rodents, a member of the extinct fossorial, or burrowing, rodent family Mylagaulidae.
Dryopithecus is a genus of extinct great apes from the middle to late Miocene boundary of Europe.
Sivapithecus, literally Shiva's Ape, is a genus of extinct apes, with fossil remains from the Miocene.
The Hominidae, whose members are known as the great apes, are a taxonomic family of primates that includes the orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and humans.
The Homininae is a subfamily of the family Hominidae, and encompasses humans, and is also called African hominids or African apes.
The Hominini form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae, comprising the genera Homo, the humans, and Pan, the chimpanzees and bonobos.
The australopithecines, formally Australopithecina or Hominina, are generally any species in the related genera of Australopithecus and Paranthropus.
Australopithecus anamensis is a hominin species that lived roughly between four point three and three point eight million years ago.
Australopithecus bahrelghazali is an extinct species of australopithecine discovered at Koro Toro, Bahr el Gazel, Chad, existing around three and a half million years ago in the Pliocene.
Australopithecus deyiremeda is an extinct species of australopithecine from Woranso-Mille, Afar Region, Ethiopia, about three and a half to three point three million years ago during the Pliocene.

Australopithecus garhi is a species of australopithecine from the Bouri Formation in the Afar Region of Ethiopia, living two point six to two point five million years ago during the Early Pleistocene.
Ardipithecus kadabba is the scientific classification given to fossil remains of a hominid known from teeth and bits and pieces of skeletal bones.
Ardi is the designation of the fossilized skeletal remains of an Ardipithecus ramidus, thought to be an early human-like female anthropoid around four point four million years old.

Kenyanthropus, meaning man from Kenya, is a genus of extinct hominin identified from the Lomekwi site by Lake Turkana, Kenya, dated to three point three to three point two million years ago during the Middle Pliocene.
Paranthropus aethiopicus is an extinct species of robust australopithecine from the Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene of East Africa about two point seven to two point three million years ago.
Homo ergaster is an extinct species or subspecies of archaic humans who lived in Africa in the Early Pleistocene.

Homo gautengensis is a species name proposed by anthropologist Darren Curnoe in two thousand ten for South African hominin fossils otherwise attributed to Homo habilis, Homo ergaster, or in some cases Australopithecus.
Homo luzonensis, also known as Callao Man, is an extinct, possibly pygmy, species of archaic human from the Late Pleistocene of Luzon, the Philippines.
Penghu One is a fossil jaw, a mandible, belonging to an extinct hominin species of the genus Homo, collected from seafloor sediments of the Penghu Channel off the coast of Taiwan.

The Dmanisi hominins, Dmanisi people, or Dmanisi man were a population of Early Pleistocene hominins whose fossils have been recovered from the Dmanisi Paleolithic site, Georgia in the Southern Caucasus.
Lantian Man is a subspecies of Homo erectus known from an almost complete mandible from Chenchiawo Village discovered in nineteen sixty-three, and a partial skull from Gongwangling Village.
Nanjing Man is a specimen of Homo erectus found in China, with large fragments of one male and one female skull and a molar tooth discovered in Hulu Cave.
Solo Man is a subspecies of Homo erectus that lived along the Solo River in Java, Indonesia, in the Late Pleistocene.
Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans who inhabited the Caune de l'Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Yuanmou Man is a subspecies of Homo erectus which inhabited the Yuanmou Basin in Yunnan Province, southwestern China, roughly one point seven million years ago.
Ceprano Man is a Middle Pleistocene archaic human fossil, a single skull cap, accidentally unearthed in a highway construction project near Ceprano in the Province of Frosinone, Italy.

Homo rhodesiensis is the species name proposed by Arthur Smith Woodward to classify the Kabwe skull, also called the Broken Hill skull or Rhodesian Man, a Middle Stone Age fossil recovered from a mine.
Herto Man is a set of human remains discovered in the Upper Herto member of the Bouri Formation in the Afar Triangle, Ethiopia.
Manot One is a fossil specimen designated to a skullcap that represents an archaic modern human discovered in Manot Cave, Western Galilee, Israel.
The Red Deer Cave people were a prehistoric population of modern humans known from bones found in Red Deer Cave and Longlin Cave in Yunnan and Guangxi, China.
Graecopithecus is an extinct genus of hominid that lived in southeast Europe during the late Miocene.
In human genetics, the Mitochondrial Eve is the matrilineal common ancestor of all living humans, the mother from whom every living person descends.
The lar gibbon, also known as the white-handed gibbon, is an endangered primate in the gibbon family, Hylobatidae.
The Cross River gorilla is a critically endangered subspecies of the western gorilla.
The eastern lowland gorilla or Grauer's gorilla is a Critically Endangered subspecies of eastern gorilla endemic to the mountainous forests of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The western lowland gorilla is one of two critically endangered subspecies of the western gorilla that lives in montane, primary and secondary forest and lowland swamps.
The Sumatran orangutan is one of the three species of orangutans, critically endangered and found in the north of the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
The four species of lion tamarins or maned marmosets make up the genus Leontopithecus, and are small New World monkeys.
Pygmy marmosets are small New World monkeys of the genus Cebuella, which consists of two species.
Night monkeys, also known as owl monkeys or douroucoulis, are nocturnal New World monkeys of the genus Aotus, the sole living member of the family Aotidae.
The tamarins are squirrel-sized New World monkeys from the family Callitrichidae in the genus Saguinus.
Uakari is the common name for the New World monkeys from the genus Cacajao.
The Colobinae or leaf-eating monkeys are a subfamily of the Old World monkey family that includes the black-and-white colobus, the large-nosed proboscis monkey, and the gray langurs.
The genus Colobus comprises the black-and-white colobus monkeys, a genus of Old World monkey native to Africa.
Semnopithecus is a genus of Old World monkeys native to the Indian subcontinent, with all species with the exception of two being commonly known as gray langurs.
The Cercopithecinae are a subfamily of the Old World monkeys, which includes the baboons, the macaques, and the vervet monkeys.
Chlorocebus is a genus of medium-sized primates from the family of Old World monkeys.
Macaca fascicularis, variously known by common names such as crab-eating macaque, long-tailed macaque, or cynomolgus monkey, is a macaque species native to Southeast Asia.
The sooty mangabey is an Old World monkey found in forests from Senegal along the coast down to the Ivory Coast.
The ruffed lemurs of the genus Varecia are strepsirrhine primates and are large lemurs within the family Lemuridae, found on the island of Madagascar.
Subfossil lemurs are lemurs from Madagascar that are represented by recent subfossil remains, and include both extant and extinct species.
The evolution of cetaceans is thought to have proceeded in modern day Pakistan during the Eocene epoch.
Remingtonocetidae is a diverse family of early aquatic mammals of the order Cetacea, named after paleocetologist Remington Kellogg.
Baleen whales, also known as whalebone whales, are marine mammals of the parvorder Mysticeti in the infraorder Cetacea, which use baleen plates in their mouths to sift food from the water.
The bowhead whale, sometimes known as the Greenland right whale, Arctic whale, and polar whale, is a species of baleen whale belonging to the family Balaenidae.
Right whales are three species of large baleen whales of the genus Eubalaena.
The toothed whales, also called odontocetes, are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, porpoises, and all other whales with teeth.
Beaked whales are members of the cetacean family Ziphiidae, noted as being a little known group of mammals because of their deep-sea habitat and reclusive behavior.
Mesoplodont whales are sixteen species of toothed whale in the genus Mesoplodon.
Oceanic dolphins or Delphinidae are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.
The false killer whale is a species of oceanic dolphin found in oceans worldwide but mainly in tropical regions.
The long-finned pilot whale or pothead whale is a large species of oceanic dolphin.
Hector's dolphin is one of six dolphin species belonging to the genus Cephalorhynchus, and is endemic to New Zealand.
Right whale dolphins are cetaceans belonging to the genus Lissodelphis, which contains the northern right whale dolphin and the southern right whale dolphin.
River dolphins, also called freshwater dolphins, are a polyphyletic group of fully aquatic mammals that reside in freshwater or even in brackish water.
The pygmy sperm whale is one of two extant species in the family Kogiidae in the sperm whale superfamily.
The treeshrews, also called tree shrews, are small mammals native to the tropical forests of South and Southeast Asia, making up the entire order Scandentia.
Ungulates are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
Marine mammals are mammals that rely on marine ecosystems for their existence, including cetaceans, pinnipeds, sirenians, marine otters, sea otters and polar bears.
Placentalia is one of the three extant subdivisions of the class Mammalia, the other two being Monotremata and Marsupialia.
Taeniodonta, meaning banded teeth, is an extinct order of eutherian mammals that lived in North America and Europe from the late Cretaceous to the middle Eocene.
Vespertilionidae is a family of microbats, flying, insect-eating mammals variously described as the common, vesper, or simple nosed bats.
Erinaceidae is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
The moonrat is a fairly small and primarily carnivorous mammal native to Southeast Asia.
Desmans are aquatic insectivores of the tribe Desmanini in the mole family, Talpidae, with two living species found in Europe.
The eastern mole or common mole is a medium-sized North American mole.
The antelope jackrabbit, also known as Allen's hare, is a species of North American hare in the family Leporidae found in southern Arizona and northwestern Mexico.
A pika is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America, resembling a rabbit but with short limbs, a very round body and no external tail.
Cottontail rabbits comprise the genus Sylvilagus, which is in the family Leporidae, and are found in the Americas.
Lophiodon is an extinct genus of perissodactyls and the type genus of the Lophiodontidae, endemic to western Europe.
Rhinocerotoidea is a superfamily of perissodactyls which includes the living rhinoceroses and their extinct relatives.
A feral horse is a free-roaming horse of domesticated stock.
A duiker is a small to medium-sized antelope native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Oryx is a genus consisting of four large antelope species called oryxes, with pale pelage with contrasting dark markings in the face and on the legs, and long horns that are almost straight.
The serow is any of four species of medium-sized goat-like or antelope-like mammals in the genus Capricornis in the family Bovidae.
Tahrs are large artiodactyl ungulates related to goats and sheep, with three species, all native to Asia.
Aepycamelus is an extinct genus of camelids from the Middle Miocene to early Pleistocene of North America.
The wild Bactrian camel or simply the wild camel is an endangered species of camel endemic to Northwest China and southwestern Mongolia.
The European fallow deer, also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
The Siberian roe deer, eastern roe deer, or Asian roe deer is a species of roe deer found in northeastern Asia.
The Giraffidae are a family of ruminant artiodactyl mammals that share a recent common ancestor with deer and bovids.
The northern giraffe, also known as the three-horned giraffe, is a species of giraffe native to North Africa.
The reticulated giraffe, also known as the Somali giraffe, is a species of giraffe native to the Horn of Africa.
The southern giraffe, also known as two-horned giraffe, is a species of giraffe native to Southern Africa.
Suidae is a family of artiodactyl mammals which are commonly called pigs, hogs, or swine.
The Bornean bearded pig, also known as the Sunda bearded pig or simply bearded pig, is a species in the pig genus, Sus, recognized by its prominent beard.
The Antilocapridae are a family of ruminant artiodactyls endemic to North America.
Moschidae is a family of pecoran even-toed ungulates, containing the musk deer and its extinct relatives, characterized by long saber teeth instead of horns or antlers.
Protoceratidae is an extinct family of herbivorous North American artiodactyls that lived during the Eocene through Pliocene.
The Palaeomerycidae is an extinct family of Neogene ruminants belonging to the infraorder Pecora, living in Europe and Asia during the Miocene.
Cainotheriidae is an extinct family of artiodactyls known from the Late Eocene to Middle Miocene of Europe.
Anthracotheriidae is a paraphyletic family of extinct, hippopotamus-like artiodactyl ungulates related to hippopotamuses and whales.
Machairodontinae is an extinct subfamily of carnivoran mammals of the cat family Felidae.
Cave lions are large extinct carnivorous felids that are classified either as subspecies of the lion or as distinct but closely related species.
Megalictis, meaning great weasel, is an extinct genus of large predatory mustelids that existed in North America during the Miocene epoch.
Amphicyonidae, also known as bear-dogs, is an extinct family of terrestrial carnivorans belonging to the suborder Caniformia.
Nimravidae is an extinct family of carnivorans, sometimes known as false saber-toothed cats, whose fossils are found in North America, Africa, and Eurasia.
Caninae, whose members are known as canines, is the sole extant subfamily within Canidae, and includes wolves, dogs, jackals, coyotes and foxes.
The African wolf is a canine native to North Africa, West Africa, the Sahel, northern East Africa, and the Horn of Africa.
The bush dog is a canine found in Central and South America.
Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
The Ethiopian wolf, also called the red jackal, the Simien jackal or Simien fox, is a canine native to the Ethiopian Highlands, including the Simien Mountains.
The Falkland Islands wolf, also known as the warrah or the Falkland Islands fox, was the sole native land mammal of the Falkland Islands.
The crab-eating fox, also known as the forest dog, wood fox, bushfox or maikong, is an extant species of medium-sized canid.
Vulpes is a genus of the subfamily Caninae, and the members of this genus are colloquially referred to as true foxes.
The black-backed jackal is a medium-sized canine native to eastern and southern Africa.
The side-striped jackal is a canine native to Central and Southern Africa.
Nyctereutes is a genus of Asian canid with two extant species, the raccoon dogs: the common raccoon dog and the Japanese raccoon dog.
The South American foxes, commonly called raposa in Portuguese, or zorro in Spanish, are a genus inhabiting South America.
A feral cat is an unowned domestic cat that lives freely outdoors and avoids human contact.
The wildcat is a species complex comprising two small wild cat species: the European wildcat and the African wildcat.
The rusty-spotted cat is a very small wild cat native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
The Sunda clouded leopard is a medium-sized wild cat native to Borneo and Sumatra.
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae, containing the large living members of the cat family.
Ferret-badgers are the six species of the genus Melogale, which is a genus of the mustelid subfamily Helictidinae.
Ictonychinae is a subfamily of the mammal family Mustelidae found mainly in the Neotropics and Africa, with one Eurasian member.
The yellow-throated marten is a marten species native to the Himalayas, Southeast and East Asia, with a bright yellow-golden coat.
Neogale, colloquially referred to as the New World weasels, is a genus of carnivorous, highly active small mammals belonging to the Mustelidae family.
The European mink, also known as the Russian mink and Eurasian mink, is a semiaquatic species of mustelid native to Europe.
The genus Bassaricyon consists of small Neotropical procyonids, popularly known as olingos, relatives of the raccoon.
The African palm civet, also known as the two-spotted palm civet, is a small feliform mammal widely distributed in sub-Saharan Africa.
Ailuridae is a family in the mammal order Carnivora, consisting of the red panda, the sole living representative, and its extinct relatives.
The Asiatic linsang is a genus comprising two species native to Southeast Asia: the banded linsang and the spotted linsang.
Eupleridae is a family of carnivorans endemic to Madagascar, commonly known as euplerids or Malagasy carnivorans.
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers, noted for the great development of their anal scent glands, which they use to deter predators.
Viverridae is a family of small to medium-sized feliform mammals.
The banded palm civet, also called the banded civet, is a viverrid native to Indomalaya.
The Asian black bear, also known as the Asiatic black bear, moon bear and white-chested bear, is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia.
The quagga is an extinct subspecies of the plains zebra which was endemic to South Africa until it was hunted to extinction in the late nineteenth century.
Husky is a general term for a type of dog used in the polar regions, primarily for work as sled dogs.
Balto was a Siberian Husky and sled dog belonging to musher and breeder Leonhard Seppala.
Palomino is a genetic color in horses, consisting of a gold coat and white mane and tail.
Seabiscuit was a champion thoroughbred racehorse in the United States.
The livestock guardian or flock guardian dog is a type of dog bred to protect livestock from predators.
Scent hounds are a type of hound that primarily hunts by scent rather than sight.
A water dog is a type of gundog bred to flush and retrieve game from water.
The blesmols, also known as mole-rats or African mole-rats, are burrowing rodents of the family Bathyergidae.
Pocket gophers, commonly referred to simply as gophers, are burrowing rodents of the family Geomyidae.
Octodon is a genus of octodontid rodents native to South America, in particular in the Chilean Andes.
Pedetes is a genus of rodent, the springhares, in the family Pedetidae, distributed across southern and Eastern Africa.
The Old World porcupines, or Hystricidae, are large terrestrial rodents, distinguished by the spiny covering from which they take their name.
The prehensile-tailed porcupines or coendous are found in Central and South America.
Spalax is a genus of rodent in the family Spalacidae, subfamily Spalacinae, the blind mole-rats.
Viscacha or vizcacha are rodents of two genera in the family Chinchillidae, native to South America and convergently resembling rabbits.
The Mongolian gerbil, also referred to as the Mongolian jird, is a rodent belonging to the subfamily Gerbillinae.
The Polynesian rat, Pacific rat or little rat, also called kiore, is a widespread species of rat found across the Pacific.
Callosciurus is a genus of squirrels collectively referred to as the beautiful squirrels, found mainly in Southeast Asia.
Ground squirrels are rodents of the squirrel family that generally live on the ground or in burrows, rather than in trees like the tree squirrels.
Xerini is a tribe of ground squirrels occurring in Africa and Asia.
Tree squirrels are the members of the squirrel family commonly referred to as squirrels.
The American red squirrel is one of three species of tree squirrels currently classified in the genus Tamiasciurus, known as the pine squirrels.
Oriental giant squirrels are cat-sized tree squirrels from the genus Ratufa in the subfamily Ratufinae.
The genus Sciurus contains many of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
Deinotheriidae is a family of prehistoric elephant-like proboscideans that lived during the Cenozoic era.
Mammutidae is an extinct family of proboscideans belonging to Elephantimorpha, known for the mastodons.
Stegodontidae is an extinct family of proboscideans from Africa and Asia, from the Early Miocene to the Late Pleistocene.
Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants as well as extinct genera like Mammuthus.
The African forest elephant is an elephant species native to humid tropical forests in West Africa and the Congo Basin.
Dwarf elephants are prehistoric members of the order Proboscidea which, through allopatric speciation on islands, evolved much smaller body sizes in comparison with their ancestors.
The giant otter shrew is a semiaquatic, carnivorous afrotherian mammal found in the rainforest of central Africa.
Ground sloths are a diverse group of extinct sloths in the mammalian superorder Xenarthra.
Macrotis is a genus of desert-dwelling marsupial omnivores known as bilbies or rabbit-bandicoots.
Phalangeriformes are quadrupedal marsupials with long tails, a paraphyletic suborder of Diprotodontia native to Australia and New Guinea.
The common ringtail possum is an Australian marsupial that lives in a variety of habitats.
The Vombatiformes are one of the three suborders of the large marsupial order Diprotodontia.
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, and the quokka.
Sthenurus, meaning strong tail, is an extinct genus of kangaroos.
Mammaliaformes, meaning mammal-shaped animals, is a clade of synapsid tetrapods that includes the crown group mammals and their near extinct relatives.
Eutriconodonta is an order of early mammals that existed in Asia, Africa, Europe, North and South America during the Jurassic and the Cretaceous periods.
Cotylorhynchus is an extinct genus of herbivorous caseid synapsids that lived during the late Lower Permian.
Pelycosaur is an older term for basal or primitive Late Paleozoic synapsids, excluding the therapsids and their descendants.
Therapsida is a major group of eupelycosaurian synapsids that includes mammals, as well as their ancestors and close relatives.
Cynodontia is a clade of eutheriodont therapsids that appeared in the Late Permian, and extensively diversified after the Permian-Triassic extinction event.
Dicynodontia is an extinct clade of anomodonts, an extinct type of non-mammalian therapsid, typically bearing a pair of tusks, hence the name, which means two dog tooth.
Placerias, meaning broad body, is an extinct genus of dicynodonts that lived during the Carnian and Norian stages of the Triassic period.
Gorgonopsia is an extinct clade of sabre-toothed therapsids from the Middle to the Upper Permian.
Therocephalia is an extinct group of therapsids from the Permian and Triassic periods, named for their large skulls, the name meaning beast-heads.
Fowl are birds belonging to one of two biological orders, namely the gamefowl or landfowl and the waterfowl.
The lesser florican, also known as the likh or kharmore, is a small member of the bustard family and endemic to the Indian Subcontinent.
The mousebirds are birds in the order Coliiformes.
Buteo is a genus of medium to fairly large, wide-ranging raptors with a robust body and broad wings.
The crested caracara is a bird of prey in the falcon family, Falconidae.
A sea eagle or fish eagle, also called erne or ern, is any of the birds of prey belonging to the subfamily Haliaeetinae of the bird of prey family Accipitridae.
The bateleur, also known as the bateleur eagle, is a medium-sized eagle in the family Accipitridae.
An elanine kite is any of several small, lightly-built raptors with long, pointed wings.
The European honey buzzard is an insectivorous bird of prey in the family Accipitridae breeding in Europe and western Asia, and wintering in Africa.
A vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
The Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
The diving ducks, commonly called pochards or scaups, are a category of duck which feed by diving beneath the surface of the water.
Mergus is the genus containing the typical mergansers, fish-eating ducks in the subfamily Anatinae.
The swan goose is a large goose with a natural breeding range in inland Mongolia, Northeast China, and the Russian Far East.
The black geese or white-cheeked geese of the genus Branta are waterfowl belonging to the true goose and swan subfamily Anserinae.
The screamers are three South American bird species placed in family Anhimidae.
The shelducks, many species of which are found in the genus Tadorna, are a group of large birds in the tribe Tadornini.
The whistling ducks or tree ducks are a subfamily, Dendrocygninae, of the duck, goose and swan family of birds, Anatidae.
The frogmouths are a group of nocturnal birds related to owlet-nightjars, swifts, and hummingbirds.
Owlet-nightjars are small crepuscular birds related to the nightjars and frogmouths.
The giant hummingbirds are hummingbirds of the genus Patagona, which includes two species, the sedentary giant hummingbird and the migratory giant hummingbird.
Swiftlets are birds from the four genera Aerodramus, Collocalia, Hydrochous and Schoutedenapus, which form the tribe Collocaliini within the swift family Apodidae.
The tree kingfishers, also called wood kingfishers or Halcyoninae, are one of the three subfamilies of birds in the kingfisher family.
The ground rollers, Brachypteraciidae, are a small family of non-migratory birds restricted to Madagascar.
The ground hornbills are birds belonging to the genus Bucorvus, in the hornbill family, Bucerotidae.
The motmots or Momotidae are a family of birds in the order Coraciiformes, which also includes the kingfishers, bee-eaters and rollers.
Nine families of largely arboreal birds make up the order Piciformes, including the Picidae, which includes the woodpeckers and close relatives.
Lybiidae is a family of birds also known as the African barbets.
Coraciidae is a family of Old World birds, which are known as rollers because of the aerial acrobatics some of these birds perform during courtship or territorial flights.
Guillemot is the common name for several species of seabird in the Alcidae or auk family, part of the order Charadriiformes.
The coursers are a subfamily Cursoriinae of birds which, together with the pratincoles, make up the family Glareolidae in the order Charadriiformes.
The greater painted-snipe is a species of wader in the small painted-snipe family Rostratulidae, widely distributed across Africa and southern Asia.
The jacanas, sometimes referred to as Jesus birds or lily trotters, are a group of tropical waders in the family Jacanidae.
Laridae is a family of seabirds in the order Charadriiformes that includes the gulls, terns, noddies, and skimmers.
Larus is a large genus of gulls with worldwide distribution.
Stilt is a common name for several species of birds in the family Recurvirostridae, which also includes those known as avocets.
The stone-curlews, also known as dikkops or thick-knees, consist of ten species within the family Burhinidae.
The eared dove is a New World dove and a resident breeder throughout South America.
The zebra dove, also known as the barred ground dove, or barred dove, is a species of bird of the dove family, Columbidae, native to Southeast Asia.
Clamator is a genus of large brood-parasitic cuckoos with crests and graduated tails.
The true koels, Eudynamys, are a genus of cuckoos from Asia, Australia and the Pacific.
Chachalacas are galliform birds from the genus Ortalis, found in wooded habitats in the far southern United States, Mexico, and Central and South America.
Curassows are one of the three major groups of cracid birds.
Francolins are birds in the tribe Gallini that traditionally have been placed in the genus Francolinus, but now commonly are divided into multiple genera.
The guans are a number of bird genera which make up a large group in the family Cracidae.
The megapodes, also known as incubator birds or mound-builders, are stocky, chicken-like birds with small heads and large feet in the family Megapodiidae.
A partridge is a medium-sized galliform bird in any of several genera, with a wide native distribution throughout parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Phasianidae is a family of heavy-bodied, ground-living birds that includes junglefowls, pheasants, grouse, partridges, turkeys, Old World quail and peafowl.
Tragopan is a bird genus in the pheasant family Phasianidae, whose members are colloquially called horned pheasants because males have two brightly coloured, fleshy horns on their head.
The blue eared pheasant is a large pheasant endemic to China.
The green pheasant, also known as the Japanese green pheasant or Kiji, is an omnivorous bird native to the Japanese archipelago.
A domesticated quail is a domestic form of the quail, a collective name which refers to a group of several small species of fowl.
The New World quail are small birds that belong to the family known as the Odontophoridae.
Old World quail is a collective term for several unrelated genera of smaller galliform species under the tribe Coturnicini of the subfamily Phasianinae.
The king quail, also known as the Asian blue quail, blue-breasted quail, or Chinese painted quail, is a very small galliform.
A chough is any of two species of passerine birds that constitute the genus Pyrrhocorax of the Corvidae family.
Jays are a paraphyletic grouping of passerine birds within the family Corvidae.
A drongo is a member of the family Dicruridae of passerine birds of the Old World tropics.
Emberiza is a genus of Old World buntings in the family Emberizidae.
Crossbills are birds of the genus Loxia within the finch family, distinguished by their mandibles with crossed tips.
The northern mockingbird is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae.
The pipits are a cosmopolitan genus, Anthus, of small passerine birds with medium to long tails.
The white-browed wagtail or large pied wagtail is a medium-sized bird of the wagtail family, conspicuously patterned with black above and white below.
The Old World orioles are an Old World family of passerine birds.
The tree sparrow is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek.
The oxpeckers are two species of bird which make up the genus Buphagus, from Ancient Greek meaning ox eater.
Delichon is a small genus of passerine birds that belongs to the swallow family and contains four species called house martins.
The vireos make up a family, Vireonidae, of small to medium-sized passerine birds found in the New World and Southeast Asia.
The wallcreeper is a small passerine bird found throughout the high mountains of the Palearctic from southern Europe to central China.
The white-eyes are a family, Zosteropidae, of small passerine birds native to tropical, subtropical and temperate Sub-Saharan Africa, southern and eastern Asia, and Australasia.
Austral storm petrels, or southern storm petrels, are seabirds in the family Oceanitidae, part of the order Procellariiformes.
Giant petrels form a genus, Macronectes, from the family Procellariidae, which consists of two living and one extinct species.
The New Zealand parrot family, Strigopidae, consists of at least three genera of parrots.
The true parrots are about three hundred and fifty species of hook-billed, mostly herbivorous birds forming the superfamily Psittacoidea.
Loriini is a tribe of small to medium-sized arboreal parrots characterized by their specialized brush-tipped tongues for feeding on nectar of various blossoms and soft fruits.
A parakeet is any one of many small- to medium-sized species of parrot, in multiple genera, that generally has long tail feathers.
The true owls or typical owls, family Strigidae, are one of the two generally accepted families of owls, the other being the barn owls and bay owls.
Strix is a genus of owls in the typical owl family, Strigidae.
The evolution of birds began in the Jurassic Period, with the early birds derived from a clade of theropod dinosaurs named Paraves.
Treeswifts, or crested swifts, are a family, the Hemiprocnidae, of aerial birds, closely related to the true swifts.
The river kingfishers or pygmy kingfishers, subfamily Alcedininae, are one of the three subfamilies of kingfishers.
The water kingfishers or Cerylinae are one of the three subfamilies of kingfishers, and are also known as the cerylid kingfishers.
The todies are a family, Todidae, of tiny Caribbean birds in the order Coraciiformes, which also includes the kingfishers, bee-eaters and rollers.
Megalaimidae, the Asian barbets, are a family of birds native to the forests of the Indomalayan realm from Tibet to Indonesia.
The jacamars are a family, Galbulidae, of birds from tropical South and Central America, extending up to Mexico.
The New World barbets are a family, Capitonidae, of birds in the order Piciformes, which inhabit humid forests in Central and South America.
Charadriiformes is a diverse order of small to medium-large birds with members in all parts of the world.
Buttonquail or hemipodes are members of a small family of ground birds, Turnicidae, in the order Charadriiformes.
Lapwings, subfamily Vanellinae, are any of various ground-nesting birds, family Charadriidae, akin to plovers and dotterels.
Plovers are members of a widely distributed group of wading birds of the family Charadriidae.
The pratincoles are a genus of birds, Glareola, that comprise the subfamily Glareolinae, which together with the coursers make up the family Glareolidae.
The three dowitchers are medium-sized long-billed wading birds in the genus Limnodromus.
Tringa is a genus of waders, containing the shanks and tattlers.
The fruit doves, also known as fruit pigeons, are a genus of birds in the pigeon and dove family, Columbidae.
Gallicolumba is a mid-sized genus of ground-dwelling doves, many of which occur in rainforests on the Philippines.
The laughing dove is a small pigeon that is a resident breeder in Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, and Western Australia.
The spotted dove or eastern spotted dove is a small and somewhat long-tailed pigeon that is a common resident breeding bird across its native range on the Indian subcontinent.
Couas are large, mostly terrestrial birds of the cuckoo family, endemic to the island of Madagascar.
A coucal is one of about thirty species of birds in the cuckoo family.
Porphyrio, also known as swamphens or swamp hens, is a genus of semi-aquatic birds in the rail family Rallidae.
Bowerbirds make up the bird family Ptilonorhynchidae, renowned for their unique courtship behaviour, where males build a structure and decorate it with sticks and brightly coloured objects.
The accentors are a genus of birds in the family Prunellidae, which is endemic to the Old World.
Estrildidae, or estrildid finches, is a family of small seed-eating passerine birds of the Old World tropics and Australasia.
Hawaiian honeycreepers are a group of small birds endemic to Hawaii, members of the finch family Fringillidae.
The gnatcatchers are a family of small passerine birds in the family Polioptilidae.
The kinglets or crests are small birds in the family Regulidae.
Locustellidae is a recently recognised family of small insectivorous songbirds, formerly placed in the Old World warbler wastebin family.
The manakins are a family, Pipridae, of small suboscine passerine birds distributed through the American tropics.
The wagtails, longclaws, and pipits are a family, Motacillidae, of small passerine birds with medium to long tails.
The penduline tits constitute the family Remizidae, of small passerine birds related to the true tits.
The Old World warblers are a large group of birds formerly grouped together in the bird family Sylviidae.
The mynas are a group of birds in the starling family, passerine birds native to large parts of Central Asia and South Asia.
The tanagers comprise the bird family Thraupidae, in the order Passeriformes, with a Neotropical distribution.
The Tyranni, the suboscines, are a suborder of passerine birds that includes more than one thousand species, a large majority of which are South American.
The cotingas are a large family, Cotingidae, of suboscine passerine birds found in Central America and tropical South America.
A booby is a seabird in the genus Sula, part of the family Sulidae.
Northern storm petrels are seabirds in the genus Hydrobates in the family Hydrobatidae, part of the order Procellariiformes.
The family Procellariidae is a group of seabirds that comprises the fulmarine petrels, the gadfly petrels, the diving petrels, the prions, and the shearwaters.
Reptiles arose about three hundred and twenty million years ago during the Carboniferous period.
