Sauria is the clade of diapsids containing the common ancestor of Archosauria, which includes crocodilians and birds, and Lepidosauria, which includes squamates and the tuatara.
Archosauromorpha, Greek for ruling lizard forms, is a clade of diapsid reptiles containing all reptiles more closely related to archosaurs than to lepidosaurs.
Cuvier's dwarf caiman is a small crocodilian in the alligator family from northern and central South America.
The dwarf crocodile, also known as the African dwarf crocodile, West African dwarf crocodile, or broad-snouted crocodile, is an African crocodile.
The freshwater crocodile, also known as the Australian freshwater crocodile, Johnstone's crocodile, or the freshie, is a species of crocodile endemic to northern Australia.
The false gharial, also known by the names Malayan gharial, Sunda gharial and tomistoma, is a freshwater crocodilian of the family Gavialidae.
Cordylidae is a family of small- to medium-sized lizards that occur in southern and eastern Africa, commonly known as girdled lizards, spinytail lizards, or girdle-tail lizards.
Dibamidae or blind skinks is a family of lizards characterized by their elongated cylindrical body and an apparent lack of limbs.
Eublepharis is a genus of terrestrial geckos native to eastern and southwestern Asia.
Gekkonidae, the common geckos, is a large family of geckos containing many of the widespread gecko species.
The Mediterranean house gecko is a species of house gecko native to the Mediterranean region, from which it has spread to many parts of the world.
The Lacertidae are the family of the wall lizards, true lizards, or sometimes simply lacertas, which are native to Afro-Eurasia.
The viviparous lizard or common lizard is a Eurasian lizard that lives far to the north and is named for the fact that it gives birth to live young.
Legless lizard may refer to any of several groups of lizards that have independently lost limbs or reduced them to the point of being of no use in locomotion.
Anguinae is a subfamily of legless lizards in the family Anguidae, commonly called glass lizards, glass snakes or slow worms.
Monitor lizards are lizards in the genus Varanus, the sole extant genus in the family Varanidae, native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania.
The Bengal monitor, also called the common Indian monitor, is a species of monitor lizard distributed widely in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia.
Teiidae is a family of lacertoidean lizards native to the Americas, generally known as whiptails or racerunners, though tegus also belong to this family.
The New Mexico whiptail is a species of lizard made up entirely of females found in New Mexico and Arizona in the southwestern United States.
Agamidae is a family of iguanian lizards indigenous to Africa, Asia, Australia, and a few locations in Southern Europe.
The frilled lizard, also known commonly as the frilled agama, frillneck lizard, frill-necked lizard or frilled dragon, is a species of lizard in the family Agamidae.
Hydrosaurus, commonly known as the sailfin dragons or sailfin lizards, is a genus in the family Agamidae.
The oriental garden lizard, also called the eastern garden lizard, Indian garden lizard, common garden lizard, bloodsucker or changeable lizard, is an agamid lizard.
Pogona is a genus of reptiles containing eight lizard species, which are often known by the common name bearded dragons or informally beardies.
Uromastyx is a genus of lizards in the family Agamidae, native to Africa and the Middle East, commonly called spiny-tailed lizards.
The common collared lizard, also commonly called eastern collared lizard or mountain boomer, is a lizard of North America.
Anolidae is a family of lizards commonly known as anoles and native to warmer parts of the Americas.
The Iguanidae is a family of lizards composed of the iguanas, chuckwallas, and their prehistoric relatives, including the widespread green iguana.
Iguana is a genus of herbivorous lizards that are native to tropical areas of Mexico, Central America, South America, and the Caribbean.
The Pythonidae, commonly known as pythons, are a family of non-venomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia.
Python is a genus of constricting snakes in the Pythonidae family native to the tropics and subtropics of the Eastern Hemisphere.
The Scolecophidia, commonly known as blind snakes or thread snakes, are an infraorder of snakes.
Xenopeltis, the sunbeam snakes, are the sole genus of the monotypic family Xenopeltidae, found in Southeast Asia and known for their highly iridescent scales.
Colubridae is a family of snakes with a great many genera, a very large snake family.
Ahaetulla, commonly referred to as Asian vine snakes or Asian whip snakes, is a genus of colubrid snakes distributed throughout tropical Asia.
Chrysopelea is a genus of snakes, commonly known as flying snakes or gliding snakes, that belong to the family Colubridae.
Elapidae is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.
The common death adder is a species of death adder, a venomous snake in the family Elapidae, endemic to Australia.
Bungarus, commonly known as kraits, is a genus of venomous snakes in the family Elapidae, native to Asia.
The red-bellied black snake is a species of venomous snake in the family Elapidae, indigenous to Australia.
The inland taipan, also commonly known as the western taipan, small-scaled snake, or fierce snake, is a species of extremely venomous snake in the family Elapidae.
The Crotalinae, commonly known as pit vipers, or pit adders, are a subfamily of vipers found in Asia and the Americas, distinguished by a pair of heat-sensing organs.
Rhynchocephalia, meaning beak-heads, is an order of lizard-like reptiles that includes one living species, the tuatara of New Zealand.
Pleurosauridae, from Ancient Greek meaning rib lizard, is an extinct family of sphenodontian reptiles.
Chelodina, collectively known as snake-necked turtles, is a large and diverse genus of long-necked chelid turtles.
Trionychidae is a family of turtles, commonly known as softshell turtles or simply softshells.
Marginocephalia is a clade of ornithischian dinosaurs that is characterized by a bony shelf or margin at the back of the skull.
Lagerpetidae is a family of basal avemetatarsalians, early-diverging members of the reptile lineage leading to birds and other dinosaurs.
Metriorhynchidae is an extinct family of specialized, aquatic metriorhynchoid crocodyliforms from the Middle Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous.
Poposauroidea is a clade of advanced pseudosuchians, including poposaurids, shuvosaurids and ctenosauriscids.
Arizonasaurus, meaning Arizona reptile, is a genus of ctenosauriscid archosaur from the Middle Triassic Moenkopi Formation of what is now Arizona.
Effigia is an extinct genus of shuvosaurid known from the Late Triassic of New Mexico, with a bipedal stance, long neck, and a toothless beaked skull.
Scleromochlus is an extinct genus of small pterosauromorph archosaurs from the Late Triassic Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland.
Silesauridae is an extinct family of early dinosauriforms which lived during the Triassic Period.
Boverisuchus is an extinct genus of planocraniid crocodyliforms known from the early to middle Eocene of Germany and western North America.
Baurusuchidae is a Gondwanan family of mesoeucrocodylians that lived during the Late Cretaceous, a group of terrestrial hypercarnivorous crocodilians from South America.
Mekosuchus is a genus of extinct Australasian mekosuchine crocodilian, generally small-sized and terrestrial.
Stomatosuchidae is an extinct family of neosuchian crocodylomorphs.
Drepanosaurs are a group of extinct reptiles that lived between the Carnian and Rhaetian stages of the late Triassic Period.
Youngina, named after John Young, is an extinct genus of small, lizard-like stem-group reptile from the Late Permian of South Africa.
Sharovipteryx is a genus of early gliding reptiles containing the single species Sharovipteryx mirabilis.
Shringasaurus, meaning horned lizard, from Sanskrit and Ancient Greek, is an extinct genus of archosauromorph reptile from the Triassic of India.
Parareptilia, literally near-reptiles, is an extinct subclass of basal sauropsids.
Pareiasauria, meaning cheek lizards, is an extinct clade of large, herbivorous neoreptilians that existed during the Permian period.
Madtsoiidae is an extinct family of mostly Gondwanan snakes with a fossil record extending from the Upper Cretaceous to the late Pleistocene.
Najash is an extinct genus of basal snake from the Early Cretaceous Candeleros Formation of Patagonia that retained hindlimbs.
Choristodera is an extinct order of semiaquatic diapsid reptiles that ranged from the Middle Jurassic to the Miocene.
Ichthyosauria is an order of large extinct marine reptiles sometimes referred to as ichthyosaurs.
Platypterygius, meaning flat fin, is a historically paraphyletic genus of platypterygiine ichthyosaur from the Cretaceous period.
Thalattosauria, Greek for sea lizards, is an extinct order of marine reptiles that lived during the Triassic Period.
Plesiosauroidea is an extinct clade of carnivorous marine reptiles with a snake-like neck of long length compared to the body.
Polycotylidae is a family of plesiosaurs from the Cretaceous.
Pliosauroidea is an extinct clade of plesiosaurs, known from the Triassic to the Late Cretaceous.
Reptiliomorpha, meaning reptile-shaped, is a clade containing the amniotes and those tetrapods that share a more recent common ancestor with amniotes than with living amphibians.
The Alytidae are a family of primitive frogs, commonly called painted frogs or midwife toads, mostly endemic to Europe.
The common midwife toad is a species of midwife frog in the family Alytidae.
The Ceratophryidae, also known as common horned frogs, are a family of frogs found in South America.
Darwin's frog, also called the Southern Darwin's frog, is a species of frog of the family Rhinodermatidae, discovered by Charles Darwin during his voyage on the Beagle.
The European spadefoot toads are a family of frogs, the Pelobatidae, with one extant genus Pelobates, native to Europe, the Mediterranean and western Asia.
Agalychnis is a genus of tree frogs native to forests in Mexico, Central America and northwestern South America.
Mantella, also known as golden frogs or Malagasy poison frogs, are a prominent genus of aposematic frogs in the family Mantellidae, endemic to Madagascar.
The tailed frogs are two species of frogs in the genus Ascaphus, with a tail that is actually an extension of the male cloaca.
Toad, also known as a hoptoad, is a generic common name for certain groups of frogs, especially those of the family Bufonidae, characterized by short legs and dry, leathery skin.
Rana, derived from Latin meaning frog, is a genus of frogs commonly known as the Holarctic true frogs, pond frogs or brown frogs.
Duttaphrynus melanostictus is commonly called Asian common toad, Asian black-spined toad, Asian toad, black-spectacled toad, common Sunda toad, and Javanese toad.
The Asiatic salamanders are primitive salamanders found all over Asia, and in European Russia, closely related to the giant salamanders.
The Cryptobranchidae, commonly known as giant salamanders, are a family of large salamanders that are fully aquatic.
The mole salamanders, genus Ambystoma, are a group of advanced salamanders endemic to North America, famous for the study of the axolotl.
Necturus is a genus of aquatic salamanders in the family Proteidae, native to the eastern United States and Canada.
Sirenidae, the sirens, are a family of neotenic aquatic salamanders with very small fore limbs and no hind limbs.
Lepospondyli is a grouping of five early tetrapod orders from the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
Diplocaulus, meaning double stalk, is an extinct genus of lepospondyl amphibians which lived from the Late Carboniferous to the Late Permian of North America and Africa.
Microsauria is an extinct, possibly polyphyletic order of tetrapods from the late Carboniferous and early Permian periods.
Temnospondyli or temnospondyls is a diverse ancient order of small to giant tetrapods, often considered primitive amphibians, that flourished worldwide during the Carboniferous, Permian and Triassic.
Koolasuchus is an extinct genus of brachyopoid temnospondyl in the family Chigutisauridae, with fossils found in the Wonthaggi Formation in Victoria, Australia.
The Stereospondyli are a group of extinct temnospondyl amphibians that existed during the Mesozoic period.
Triadobatrachus is an extinct genus of salientian frog-like amphibians, including one known species, Triadobatrachus massinoti.
The yellow-lipped sea krait, also known as the banded sea krait or colubrine sea krait, is a species of highly venomous snake found in tropical Indo-Pacific oceanic waters.
Unenlagiinae is a subfamily of long-snouted paravian theropods.
Dallasaurus, meaning Dallas lizard, is a basal mosasauroid from the Upper Cretaceous of North America.
The banded bullfrog is a species of frog in the narrow-mouthed frog family Microhylidae, native to Southeast Asia.
Jameson's mamba is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Elapidae, native to equatorial Africa.
An aquatic animal is any animal, whether vertebrate or invertebrate, that lives in a body of water for all or much of its lifetime.
The Ediacaran biota is a group of large, soft-bodied, biologically complex Precambrian organisms that lived during the Ediacaran period.
Fish began evolving about five hundred and thirty million years ago during the Cambrian explosion, when early chordates developed the skull and the vertebral column.
Coastal fish, also called inshore fish or neritic fish, inhabit the sea between the shoreline and the edge of the continental shelf.
The term coldwater fish can have different meanings in different contexts.
Demersal fish, also known as groundfish, live and feed on or near the bottom of seas or lakes.
Pelagic fish live in the pelagic zone of ocean or lake waters, neither close to the bottom nor near the shore.
Marine fish, also termed saltwater fish or sea fish, are fish that live in seawater and can live alone or in a large group called a school.
Trygonorrhina, also known as the fiddler rays or banjo rays, is a genus of guitarfish found along the eastern and southern coasts of Australia.
The whiptail stingrays are a family, the Dasyatidae, of rays in the order Myliobatiformes, found worldwide in tropical to temperate marine waters.
River stingrays or freshwater stingrays are Neotropical freshwater fishes of the family Potamotrygonidae, one of the four orders of batoids, cartilaginous fish.
Callorhinchus, the plough-nosed chimaeras or elephantfish, are a living genus in the family Callorhinchidae.
Chimaera monstrosa, commonly known as the rabbit fish or rat fish, is a northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean species of cartilaginous fish in the family Chimaeridae.
The bullhead sharks are members of the genus Heterodontus, the family Heterodontidae and the order Heterodontiformes, all relatively small sharks.
Carpet sharks are sharks classified in the order Orectolobiformes, named because many species resemble ornately patterned carpets.
Scyliorhinidae is a family of sharks, one of a few families whose members share the common name catsharks, in the order Carcharhiniformes.
The Lamniformes are an order of sharks commonly known as mackerel sharks, including many familiar species of shark.
Sand sharks are mackerel sharks of the family Odontaspididae, found worldwide in temperate and tropical waters.
Glyphis is a genus in the family Carcharhinidae, commonly known as the river sharks, living in rivers and coastal regions around southeast Asia and Australia.
The Indonesian coelacanth, also called the Sulawesi coelacanth, is one of two living species of coelacanth.
The West Indian Ocean coelacanth, sometimes known as the gombessa or African coelacanth, is a crossopterygian and one of two extant species of coelacanth.
Teleostei, members of which are known as teleosts, is a very large group of ray-finned fishes, with ninety-six percent of all living species of fish.
Snipe eels are a family, Nemichthyidae, of eels with nine species in three genera, pelagic fishes found in every ocean.
The garden eels are infaunal ray-finned fish of the subfamily Heterocongrinae in the conger eel family Congridae.
The tripod fish, also known as the tripod spiderfish, is a grinner in the family Ipnopidae, found at lower latitudes and known for its unique way of standing on the seabed.
The Synodontidae or lizardfishes are benthic marine and estuarine bony fishes that belong to the aulopiform fish order.
Tetra is the common name of many small freshwater characiform fishes from Africa, Central America and South America.
Nannostomus is a genus of fish belonging to the characin family Lebiasinidae, all known as pencil fish.
Clupeiformes is the order of ray-finned fish that includes the herring family, the anchovy family and sardines.
Alosa is a genus of fish, the river herrings, in the family Alosidae, generally known as shads.
Cyprinidae is a family of medium-to-large freshwater ray-finned fishes commonly referred to as the carp family, including the true carps, barbs and barbels.
Carassius is a genus in the ray-finned fish family Cyprinidae, with species commonly known as crucian carps.
The danionins are a group of small, slender minnow-type freshwater fish in the family Danionidae.
The Gonorynchiformes are an order of ray-finned fish that includes the important food source, the milkfish, and a number of lesser-known types.
The Gymnotiformes are an order of teleost bony fishes commonly known as Neotropical knifefish or South American knifefish, which inhabit fresh water.
The black ghost knifefish is a tropical ornamental fish belonging to the ghost knifefish family, originating in freshwater habitats of South America.
Glass knifefishes are fishes in the family Sternopygidae in the order Gymnotiformes, also known as rattail knifefishes.
The Myctophiformes are an order of ray-finned fishes consisting of two families of deep-sea marine fish, notably the abundant lanternfishes.
Osteoglossiformes, meaning bony tongues in Ancient Greek, is a relatively primitive order of ray-finned fish.
The family Notopteridae contains eleven species of bony-tongued fishes, commonly known as featherbacks and knifefishes.
The Mormyridae, sometimes called elephantfish, are a family of weakly electric fish in the order Osteoglossiformes native to Africa.
Antarctic fishes are a specialized group of species adapted to extreme cold in the Southern Ocean, many of them white-blooded icefish.
The crocodile icefish or white-blooded fish comprise a family, Channichthyidae, of notothenioid fish found in the Southern Ocean around Antarctica.
Batrachoididae is a family in the ray-finned fish order Batrachoidiformes, usually called toadfish or frogfish.
Beloniformes is an order composed of six families of freshwater and marine ray-finned fish, including needlefish, flying fish and halfbeaks.
The ricefishes are a family, Adrianichthyidae, of small ray-finned fish found in fresh and brackish waters from India to Japan and the Malay Archipelago.
The wrestling halfbeak, also known as the Malayan halfbeak, is a species of viviparous halfbeak native to the fresh and brackish waters of rivers and coastal regions of southeast Asia.
Blennies are a diverse clade of ray-finned fish in the suborder Blennioidei, inhabiting marine, brackish and occasionally freshwater habitats.
Gadiformes, also called the Anacanthini, are an order of ray-finned fish that include the cod, hakes, pollock, haddock, burbot, rocklings and moras.
Grenadiers or rattails are large, brown to black marine fish of the family Macrouridae, found at great depths.
Gasterosteoidei is a suborder of ray-finned fishes that includes the sticklebacks and relatives.
Gobiidae or gobies is a family of bony fish in the order Gobiiformes, a very large fish family, with over two thousand species in more than two hundred genera.
Lampriformes is an order of ray-finned fishes, including the open-ocean and deep-sea opahs, sailfin velifer and oarfish.
The ribbonfish are any lampriform fishes in the family Trachipteridae, with about ten recognized species.
Black seadevils are small, deep-sea lophiiform fish of the family Melanocetidae, with six known species all within the genus Melanocetus.
The sea toads and coffinfishes are a family, the Chaunacidae, of deep-sea ray-finned fishes within the order Lophiiformes, the anglerfishes.
The striped mullet is an important food fish species in the mullet family Mugilidae, found in coastal temperate, subtropical and tropical waters worldwide.
The cusk-eel family, Ophidiidae, is a group of marine bony fishes in the Ophidiiformes order, named from the Greek for snake because of their eel-like appearance.
A flathead is one of a number of small to medium fish species with notably flat heads, in the family Platycephalidae.
Sebastinae is a subfamily of marine fish in the family Scorpaenidae, with common names including rockfishes, rock perches and ocean perches.
Triglidae, commonly known as gurnards or sea robins, is a family of bottom-feeding scorpaenoid ray-finned fish distributed in temperate and tropical seas worldwide.
Anthias anthias, the swallowtail sea perch or marine goldfish, is a species of marine ray-finned fish native to the eastern Atlantic Ocean.
The Syngnathiformes are an order of ray-finned fishes that includes the pipefishes, seahorses, trumpetfishes, goatfish, dragonets, flying gurnards and sea moths.
Dragonets are small marine fish of the family Callionymidae found mainly in the tropical waters of the western Indo-Pacific, spending much of their time near the bottom.
Tetraodontiformes, also known as the Plectognathi, is an order of ray-finned fishes that includes the pufferfishes and related kinds.
Ostraciidae is a family of squared, bony fish in the order Tetraodontiformes, closely related to the pufferfishes and filefishes.
Takifugu, also known by the Japanese name fugu, is a genus of pufferfish with twenty-five species, many native to salt and brackish waters of the northwest Pacific.
Anomalopidae, the lanterneye fishes or flashlight fishes, are a family of fish distinguished by bioluminescent organs located underneath their eyes.
Slimeheads, also known as roughies and redfish, are small, long-lived, deep-sea fish constituting the family Trachichthyidae.
Tilefishes or sand tilefishes are small marine fish comprising the family Malacanthidae, usually found in sandy, shallow areas near coral reefs.
The Acanthuridae are a family of ray-finned fishes which includes surgeonfishes, tangs and unicornfishes, living in tropical seas.
Paracanthurus hepatus is a species of Indo-Pacific surgeonfish, a popular fish in marine aquaria and the sole member of its genus.
Platax is a genus of Indo-Pacific, reef-associated fish belonging to the family Ephippidae, with five accepted living species.
The billfish are saltwater predatory ray-finned fish characterised by prominent pointed bills, and some are longer than five metres.
Caranx is a genus of tropical to subtropical marine fishes in the jack family Carangidae, commonly known as jacks, trevallies and kingfishes.
The reedfish, ropefish or snakefish, Erpetoichthys calabaricus, is a species of fish in the family Polypteridae alongside the bichirs.
Esox is a genus of freshwater fish commonly known as pike or pickerel, and the type genus of the family Esocidae.
Oncorhynchus is a genus of ray-finned fish in the subfamily Salmoninae of the family Salmonidae, native to coldwater tributaries of the North Pacific basin.
The Atlantic salmon is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae, a large member of its family.
Basa is a species of primarily freshwater catfish in the shark-catfish family Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya basins.
The black bullhead or black bullhead catfish is a species of bullhead catfish with the ability to thrive in waters that are low in oxygen.
Stomiiformes is an order of deep-sea ray-finned fishes of very diverse morphology, including dragonfishes, lightfishes and loosejaws.
The Gonostomatidae are a family of mesopelagic marine fish, commonly named bristlemouths or anglemouths.
Marine hatchetfishes or deep-sea hatchetfishes are small deep-sea mesopelagic ray-finned fish of the stomiiform subfamily Sternoptychinae.
Hybodontiformes, commonly called hybodonts, are an extinct group of shark-like cartilaginous fish which existed from the late Devonian to the Late Cretaceous.
Cyclostomi is a superclass of vertebrates that comprises the living jawless fish classes, the lampreys and hagfishes.
The pouched lamprey, also known as the piharau in New Zealand, is a species of lamprey also called the wide-mouthed lamprey.
Anaspida, meaning shieldless ones, is an extinct group of jawless fish that existed from the early Silurian period to the late Devonian period.
Galeaspida is an extinct taxon of jawless marine and freshwater fish, named from the Latin word for helmet because of their massive bone shield on the head.
Haikouichthys is an extinct genus of fish-like, stem-vertebrate chordate animal that lived during the Cambrian period, about five hundred and eighteen million years ago, in what is now Yunnan, China.
Pikaia gracilens is an extinct, primitive chordate marine animal known from the Middle Cambrian Burgess Shale of British Columbia.
Thelodonti is a class of extinct Palaeozoic jawless fishes with distinctive scales instead of large plates of armor.
Vetulicolia is a group of bilaterian marine animals encompassing several extinct species from the early Cambrian period.
The red mullets or surmullets are two species of goatfish found in the Mediterranean Sea, the east North Atlantic Ocean and the Black Sea.
Lutjanidae, the snappers and fusiliers, are a family of percomorph fishes, mainly marine but with some members inhabiting estuaries and fresh water.
The Priacanthidae, the bigeyes, are a family of eighteen species of marine ray-finned fishes, with Catalufa an alternate common name.
Rabbitfishes or spinefoots, genus Siganus, are perciform fishes in the family Siganidae, with twenty-nine species.
Sparidae, the seabreams and porgies, is a family of ray-finned fishes belonging to the order Acanthuriformes.
Coregonus is a diverse genus of fish in the salmon family Salmonidae, whose species are known as whitefishes.
Mawsonia is an extinct genus of prehistoric coelacanth fish and a large one among all coelacanths.
The weatherfish is a species of true loach that has a wide range in Europe and some parts of Asia, an omnivorous scavenger and bottom feeder.
Elacatinus is a genus of small marine gobies, often known collectively as the neon gobies.
Weevers or weeverfish are nine extant species of ray-finned fishes of the family Trachinidae in the order Perciformes.
Marine angelfish are perciform fish of the family Pomacanthidae, found on shallow reefs in the tropical Atlantic, Indian and western Pacific Oceans.
Branchiopoda is a class of crustaceans comprising the fairy shrimp, clam shrimp, water fleas and tadpole shrimp.
Cladocera is an order of aquatic, largely freshwater crustaceans, commonly known as water fleas, and many of them feed on microscopic bits of organic matter.
The order Notostraca, containing the single family Triopsidae, is a group of crustaceans known as tadpole shrimp or shield shrimp, living fossils that look much as they did in the Triassic.
Cumacea is an order of small marine crustaceans, occasionally called hooded shrimp or comma shrimp.
Ligia is a genus of isopods, commonly known as rock lice or sea slaters, and many species live on tidal zone cliffs and rocky beaches.
Leptostraca is an order of small marine crustaceans whose members, including Nebalia, occur throughout the world's oceans and are usually considered filter-feeders.
Squilla mantis, also called the spot-tail mantis shrimp, is a species of mantis shrimp found in shallow coastal areas of the Mediterranean Sea and the eastern Atlantic Ocean.
Axiidea is an infraorder of decapod crustaceans colloquially known as mud shrimp, ghost shrimp or burrowing shrimp, though they are distantly related to true shrimp.
The Stenopodidea or boxer shrimps are a small group of decapod crustaceans that belong to their own group, neither Caridea shrimp nor Dendrobranchiata prawns.
Anomura is a group of decapod crustaceans, including hermit crabs, king crabs and porcelain crabs.
King crabs or stone crabs are marine decapod crustaceans of the family Lithodidae, found chiefly in deep waters and adapted to cold environments.
Squat lobsters are flattened crustaceans with long tails held curled beneath the body, in the superfamilies Galatheoidea and Chirostyloidea.
Kiwa hirsuta is a crustacean discovered in two thousand five in the South Pacific Ocean, notable for the silky blond setae on its claws that resemble fur.
Dromiidae is a family of crabs, often referred to as sponge crabs, which get their name from shaping a living sponge into a portable shelter for themselves.
Grapsus grapsus is a common crab along the western coast of the Americas, known as the red rock crab or the Sally Lightfoot crab.
The horsehair crab is a species of crab found in the Northwest Pacific, around the Hokkaido coast, the Sea of Okhotsk and the western Bering Sea, and an important commercial species.
Majoidea is a superfamily of crab which contains the spider crabs, along with the decorator crabs.
Chionoecetes is a genus of crabs that live in the northern Pacific and Atlantic Oceans, with common names including queen crab and spider crab.
Mangrove crabs are crabs that live in and around mangroves, and they bury and consume leaf litter, which matters to the ecology of the forest.
A number of lineages of crabs have evolved to live on land, with examples in the families Gecarcinidae and Gecarcinucidae.
Trapeziidae is a family of crabs, commonly known as coral crabs, all of them living in close symbiosis with cnidarians.
Cherax pulcher is a species of crayfish from West Papua in Indonesia, popular as a freshwater aquarium species across Asia, Europe and North America.
Metanephrops challengeri, commonly known as the New Zealand lobster or New Zealand scampi, is a species of slim, pink lobster that lives around the coast of New Zealand.
Reef lobsters, Enoplometopus, are a genus of small lobsters that live on reefs in the Indo-Pacific, the Caribbean and warmer parts of the Atlantic Ocean.
Furry lobsters, sometimes called coral lobsters, are small decapod crustaceans closely related to slipper lobsters and spiny lobsters.
The Caridea, commonly known as caridean shrimp or true shrimp, are an infraorder of shrimp within the order Decapoda.
Palaemon serratus, also called the common prawn, is a species of shrimp found in the Atlantic Ocean from Denmark to Mauritania, and in the Mediterranean Sea and Black Sea.
The Indian prawn is one of the major commercial prawn species of the world, found in the Indo-West Pacific from eastern and southeastern Africa.
The family Argulidae, whose members are commonly known as carp lice or fish lice, are parasitic crustaceans.
Lepas anatifera, commonly known as the pelagic gooseneck barnacle or smooth gooseneck barnacle, is a species of barnacle in the family Lepadidae, often found in large numbers on floating objects.
Characidae, the characids, is a family of freshwater subtropical and tropical fish belonging to the order Characiformes, found throughout much of Central and South America.
Clupeidae is a small family of ray-finned fishes, comprising the true herrings and sprats, inhabiting temperate marine habitats in both hemispheres.
Loaches are ray-finned fishes of the suborder Cobitoidei, freshwater bottom-dwelling fish found in rivers and creeks throughout Eurasia and northern Africa.
The freshwater butterflyfish or African butterflyfish is a species of osteoglossiform fish native to freshwater habitats in the Niger and Congo basins of West Africa.
Centrarchidae, better known as sunfishes or centrarchids, is a family of freshwater ray-finned fish native to North America.
Pterophyllum is a small genus of freshwater fish from the family Cichlidae, known to aquarists as angelfish, all originating in the Amazon and Orinoco basins.
Palpigradi is an order of very small arachnids commonly known as microwhip scorpions or palpigrades.
Ricinulei is a small order of arachnids that are predatory, eating small arthropods, and occur today in west-central Africa and the Americas.
Schizomida, also known as sprickets or short-tailed whip-scorpions, is an order of arachnids, generally less than five millimetres in length, native to subtropical and tropical regions.
Parasitiformes are a superorder of arachnids, constituting one of the two major groups of mites, alongside Acariformes.
The Acariformes, also known as the Actinotrichida, are the more diverse of the two superorders of mites, alongside Parasitiformes.
Spiders have existed for over three hundred million years, with silk-producing forerunners extending back around three hundred and eighty million years.
The Mesothelae are a suborder of spiders, the order Araneae, with a single living family Liphistiidae sometimes accepted.
Heptathela kimurai, also known as the Kimura spider, is an Old World spider native to East Asia and found mainly in Japan.
The Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders, containing more than two thousand species, including those commonly known as cellar spiders and daddy long-legs spiders.
Phalangiotarbida is an extinct arachnid order recorded from the Early Devonian of Germany and widespread in the Upper Carboniferous coal measures of Europe and North America.
The order Trigonotarbida is a group of extinct arachnids whose fossil record extends from the late Silurian to the early Permian.
Freshwater fish are fish species that spend some or all of their lives in fresh water such as rivers, lakes, ponds and inland wetlands.
Tropical fish are fish found in aquatic tropical environments around the world, and fishkeepers often keep them in freshwater and saltwater aquariums.
Hemiramphidae is a family of fishes commonly called halfbeaks, a geographically widespread and numerous family of epipelagic fish inhabiting warm waters.
Portia labiata is a jumping spider of the family Salticidae found in Sri Lanka, India, southern China, Burma, Malaysia, Singapore, Java, Sumatra and the Philippines.
Understanding of the evolution of insects is based on studies of molecular biology, insect morphology, paleontology, taxonomy, evolution and embryology.
The order Embioptera, commonly known as webspinners or footspinners, is a small group of tropical and subtropical insects, classified under the subclass Pterygota.
Grylloblattidae, commonly known as the icebugs or ice crawlers, is a family of extremophile and wingless insects that live in the cold on mountaintops and the edges of glaciers.
Mantophasmatidae is a family of carnivorous wingless insects in southern Africa, discovered in two thousand one.
Mecoptera is an order of insects in the superorder Holometabola with about six hundred species in nine families worldwide, sometimes called scorpionflies.
Megaloptera is an order of insects containing the alderflies, dobsonflies and fishflies, with about three hundred known species.
The insect order Neuroptera, also known as net-winged insects, includes the lacewings, mantidflies, antlions and owlflies.
Plecoptera is an order of insects commonly known as stoneflies, with some three thousand five hundred species described worldwide.
Strepsiptera are an order of insects with eleven living families, many of which are endoparasites of other insects.
Zoraptera is an order of insects, sometimes called angel insects or ground lice, small and soft-bodied with winged and wingless forms.
Cleridae are a family of beetles of the superfamily Cleroidea, commonly known as checkered beetles.
The beetle family Chrysomelidae, commonly known as leaf beetles, includes over thirty-seven thousand species in more than two thousand five hundred genera.
The family Scarabaeidae consists of over thirty-five thousand species of beetles worldwide, often called scarabs or scarab beetles.
A water beetle is a generalized name for any beetle that is adapted to living in water at some point in its life cycle.
Dytiscus is a Holarctic genus of predaceous diving beetles that usually live in wetlands and ponds.
The Curculionidae are a family of weevils, commonly called snout beetles or true weevils.
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.
The Heteroptera are a group of about forty thousand species of insects in the order Hemiptera, sometimes called true bugs.
The Lygaeidae are a family in the Hemiptera, the true bugs, commonly referred to as seed bugs, and less commonly as milkweed bugs or ground bugs.
Nepomorpha is an infraorder of insects in the true bug order Hemiptera, belonging to the suborder Heteroptera.
Acanthosoma is a genus of shield bugs in the family Acanthosomatidae, found in Europe, Asia and Oceania.
Veliidae is a family of gregarious predatory insects in the suborder Heteroptera, commonly known as riffle bugs or small water striders.
A planthopper is any insect in the infraorder Fulgoromorpha, a group exceeding twelve thousand five hundred described species worldwide.
Gall wasps, also traditionally called gallflies or cynipids, are hymenopterans of the family Cynipidae, named for the galls they induce on plants.
Sceliphrini, also known as mud-dauber wasps, is a tribe of thread-waisted wasp that build their nests from mud.
Myrmecia is a genus of ants established by the Danish zoologist Johan Christian Fabricius, in the subfamily Myrmeciinae of the family Formicidae.
Tapinoma melanocephalum is a species of ant in the subfamily Dolichoderinae that goes by the common name ghost ant, recognised by its dark head and pale or translucent legs.
Tapinoma sessile is a species of small ant that goes by the common names odorous house ant, sugar ant, stink ant and coconut ant.
The Erebidae are a family of moths in the superfamily Noctuoidea that contains a wide variety of well-known macromoth groups.
The Nymphalidae are a large family of butterflies, with more than six thousand species distributed throughout much of the world.
Libellula is a genus of dragonflies, called chasers in British English or skimmers in American English, in the family Libellulidae.
Ensifera is a suborder of insects that includes the various types of crickets and their allies, including katydids, grigs, wētā and Cooloola monsters.
Cooloola is a genus of ensiferan orthopterans known as Cooloola monsters, forming the subfamily Cooloolinae of the superfamily Stenopelmatoidea.
Wētā is the common name for a group of about one hundred insect species in the families Anostostomatidae and Rhaphidophoridae endemic to New Zealand, giant flightless crickets.
Psocoptera are a group of insects that are commonly known as booklice, barklice or barkflies.
Zygentoma are an order in the class Insecta, consisting of about five hundred and fifty known species, including the silverfishes and firebrats.
Julida is an order of millipedes whose members are small and cylindrical, with eyes present or absent.
Pauropoda is a class of small, pale, millipede-like arthropods in the subphylum Myriapoda, living in soil and leaf mold.
Symphylans, also known as garden centipedes or pseudocentipedes, are soil-dwelling arthropods of the class Symphyla in the subphylum Myriapoda.
The order Diplura, the two-pronged bristletails, is one of three orders of non-insect hexapods within the class Entognatha.
The Protura, or proturans, are very small, soil-dwelling animals, so inconspicuous they were not noticed until the twentieth century.
Dinocaridida is a proposed fossil taxon of basal arthropods, which flourished during the Cambrian period and survived up to the Early Devonian.
Radiodonta is an extinct order of stem-group arthropods that was successful worldwide during the Cambrian period, distinguished by their frontal appendages.
Tamisiocarididae is a family of radiodonts, extinct marine animals related to arthropods, that bore finely spined appendages presumably used in filter-feeding.
Leanchoilia is a megacheiran marine arthropod known from Cambrian deposits of the Burgess Shale in Canada and the Chengjiang biota of China.
Thylacocephala is an extinct group of mandibulate arthropods, generally regarded as a kind of crustacean, though their exact position within this group is uncertain.
The evolution of the molluscs is the way in which the Mollusca, a large group of invertebrate animals, evolved, a phylum that includes gastropods, bivalves, scaphopods and cephalopods.
Aplacophora is a superclass of small, deep-water, benthic marine molluscs found in all oceans of the world, all of the living forms shell-less.
The halkieriids are a group of fossil organisms from the Lower to Middle Cambrian, their eponymous genus being Halkieria.
Monoplacophora, meaning bearing one plate, is a paraphyletic class of molluscs with a cap-like shell, inhabiting deep sea environments.
Ensis is a genus of medium-sized edible saltwater clams in the family Pharidae, known as razor clams.
Turridae is a taxonomic family name for a number of predatory sea snails, marine gastropod mollusks in the superfamily Conoidea.
A honey bee is a eusocial flying insect from the genus Apis of the bee family Apidae.
Asteriornis is an extinct genus of bird from the Late Cretaceous of Belgium, a small, long-legged bird that lived near the coast.
Dromornis is a genus of large prehistoric birds native to Australia during the Oligocene to Pliocene epochs, flightless birds with greatly reduced wings and large legs.
Pelagornis is an extinct genus of prehistoric pseudotooth birds, a group of extinct seabirds, with species spanning the Oligocene to the Early Pleistocene.
The Pelagornithidae, commonly called pseudodontorns, bony-toothed birds or false-toothed birds, are a prehistoric family of large seabirds.
Phorusrhacidae, colloquially known as terror birds, is a family of large carnivorous, mostly flightless birds.
Kelenken is a genus of phorusrhacid, an extinct group of large, predatory terror birds, which lived in what is now Argentina in the middle Miocene.
Titanis is a genus of phorusrhacid, an extinct family of large, predatory terror birds, named for the Titans of Greek mythology.
Teratornithidae is an extinct family of very large birds of prey that lived in North and South America from the Late Oligocene to Late Pleistocene.
Ichthyornis, meaning fish bird after its fish-like vertebrae, is an extinct genus of toothy seabird-like ornithuran from the Late Cretaceous of North America.
Inkayacu is a genus of extinct penguins that lived in what is now Peru during the Late Eocene, named from a single nearly complete skeleton.
Presbyornis is an extinct genus of presbyornithid bird from North America during the Paleogene period, between the Late Paleocene and Early Eocene.
Plotopteridae is an extinct family of flightless seabirds that lived in the Northern Pacific from the Eocene to Miocene epoch.
The moa-nalo are a group of extinct aberrant, goose-like ducks that lived on the larger Hawaiian Islands, and were the major herbivores on many of these islands.
Balaur bondoc is a species of paravian theropod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous period, in what is now Romania, named after the balaur, a dragon of Romanian folklore.
The skimmers, forming the genus Rynchops, are tern-like birds in the family Laridae, with three species found in South Asia, Africa and the Americas.
Stupendemys is an extinct genus of freshwater side-necked turtle, belonging to the family Podocnemididae, with a carapace over two metres long.
Shonisaurus is a genus of very large ichthyosaurs, with many incomplete fossil specimens found in the Luning Formation of Nevada, United States.
The evolution of tetrapods began about four hundred million years ago in the Devonian Period with early tetrapods evolved from lobe-finned fishes.
The evolution of mammals has passed through many stages since the appearance of their synapsid ancestors in the Pennsylvanian sub-period of the late Carboniferous period.
Mesonychia, meaning middle claws, is an extinct order of small to large-sized omnivorous to carnivorous hoofed mammals related to ungulates.
A saber-tooth is any member of various extinct groups of predatory therapsids, mainly carnivoran mammals, characterized by long, curved saber-shaped canine teeth.
Palaeotheriidae is an extinct family of herbivorous perissodactyl mammals that inhabited Europe, from the mid-Eocene to the early Oligocene.
The evolution of the horse, a mammal of the family Equidae, occurred over fifty million years, transforming the small, dog-sized, forest-dwelling Eohippus into the large modern horse.
Anoplotheriidae is an extinct family of artiodactyls exclusive to the Palaeogene, endemic to western Europe and living from the Middle Eocene to the Early Oligocene.
Merycoidodontoidea, informally known as oreodonts or ruminating hogs, are an extinct superfamily of prehistoric cud-chewing artiodactyls with short faces and fang-like canine teeth.
Dinocephalia is a clade of generally large-bodied therapsids that flourished during the Middle Permian, between about two hundred and seventy-five and two hundred and sixty million years ago.
Euharamiyida, also known as Eleutherodontida, is a clade of early mammals or mammal-like cynodonts from the Middle Jurassic to Early Cretaceous of Eurasia.
In zoology, megafauna are large animals, and the precise definition of the term varies widely, though a common threshold is about forty-five kilograms.
Neophocaena is a genus of porpoise native to the Indian and Pacific oceans, as well as the freshwater habitats of the Yangtze River basin in China, commonly known as finless porpoises.
The North African elephant is an extinct subspecies of the African bush elephant, or possibly a separate elephant species, that existed in North Africa.
Spermophilus, also known as the Old World ground squirrels, sousliks or spermophiles, is an Old World genus of ground squirrels in the squirrel family Sciuridae.
The zebu, also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia, differing from taurine cattle in the fatty hump on its shoulders.
Sus is the genus of domestic and wild pigs, within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae, including the domestic pig and its ancestor the common Eurasian wild boar.
A zebroid is the offspring of any cross between a zebra and any other equine, a hybrid in which the sire is usually a zebra stallion.
A wolfdog is a canine hybrid produced by crossing a domestic dog with a wolf, which can be a gray wolf, an eastern wolf or a red wolf.
Dwarf rabbit refers formally to a rabbit with the dwarfing gene, or informally to any small breed of domestic rabbit.
The domesticated hedgehog kept as a pet is typically the African pygmy hedgehog, and other species kept as pets include the long-eared hedgehog.
The Honduran white bat, also called the Caribbean white tent-making bat, is a species of bat in the family Phyllostomidae and the sole member of the genus Ectophylla.

Australian feral camels are introduced populations of dromedary, or one-humped camel, imported to Australia as valuable beasts of burden from British India and Afghanistan during the nineteenth century.
The Iberian pig, also known in Portugal as the Alentejo Pig, is a traditional breed of the domestic pig that is native to the Iberian Peninsula.
The Spanish Fighting Bull is an Iberian heterogeneous cattle population, bred free-range on extensive estates in countries where bullfighting is organized.
The Basset Hound is a short-legged breed of scent hound, developed in Great Britain from several now-extinct strains of French basset breeds.
The Turkish Angora is a breed of domestic cat, one of the ancient, natural breeds of cat, originating in central Anatolia.
The Enantiornithes, literally opposite birds, are a group of extinct avialans, abundant and diverse birds of the Mesozoic era.
Psophia is a genus of birds restricted to the humid forests of the Amazon and Guiana Shield in South America, the single genus in the family Psophiidae.
Archosauria or archosaurs is a clade of diapsid sauropsid tetrapods, with birds and crocodilians being the sole living representatives.
The short-eared dog, also known as the small-eared dog or short-eared fox, is an elusive canid species endemic to the Amazonian basin.
Fancy pigeon refers to any breed of domestic pigeon, a domesticated form of the wild rock dove, bred by pigeon fanciers for various traits relating to size, shape and color.
Anthozoa is one of the three subphyla of Cnidaria, and it includes sessile marine invertebrates such as sea anemones and stony corals.
Chironex fleckeri, commonly known as the Australian box jelly and nicknamed the sea wasp, is a species of extremely venomous box jellyfish found in coastal waters from northern Australia.
Hydrozoa, also called hydroids, are a taxonomic class of individually very small, predatory cnidarian animals, some of them forming colonies.
The Scyphozoa are a marine class of the phylum Cnidaria, referred to as the true jellyfish, and the class name comes from the Greek word for a kind of drinking cup.
Myxozoa is a class of aquatic cnidarian animals, all of them obligate parasites, containing very small animals indeed.
Homosclerophorida is an order of marine sponges that belongs to the class Homoscleromorpha, its members inhabiting shallow waters.
Placozoa, literally flat animals, is a phylum of free-living marine invertebrates, blob-like animals composed of aggregations of cells.
Deuterostomes are bilaterian animals of the superphylum Deuterostomia, typically characterized by their blastopore becoming their anus during embryonic development.
Protostomia is the clade of animals once thought to be characterized by the blastopore becoming the mouth during embryonic development.
The lancelets, also known as amphioxi, consist of thirty-two described species of somewhat fish-like benthic filter-feeding chordates in the subphylum Cephalochordata.
Ecdysozoa is a group of protostome animals, including the arthropods, the nematodes and several smaller phyla, grouped by molting their outer layer.
Kinorhyncha is a phylum of small marine invertebrates that are widespread in mud or sand at all depths, commonly called mud dragons.
Lobopodians are members of the informal group Lobopodia, panarthropods with stubby legs called lobopods.
Microdictyon, Greek for small net, is an extinct genus of lobopodian worm characterized by its net-like sclerite armour plates, known from Cambrian deposits around the world.
Loricifera, also known as corset animals, is a phylum of very small to microscopic marine sediment-dwelling animals.
Ancylostoma is a genus of nematodes that includes some species of hookworms.
Gnathostomulids, or jaw worms, are a small phylum of nearly microscopic marine animals that inhabit sand and mud beneath shallow coastal waters.
Limnognathia is a genus of microscopic freshwater animal that was discovered on Disko Island, Greenland, in nineteen ninety-four.
Acanthocephala is a group of parasitic worms known as thorny-headed worms or spiny-headed worms, characterized by an eversible proboscis armed with spines.
Lophotrochozoa is a clade of protostome animals within the Spiralia, established as a monophyletic group based on molecular evidence.
Lingulata is a class of brachiopods, an ancient group of brachiopods, existing since the Cambrian period.
Symbion is a genus of commensal aquatic animals, less than half a millimetre wide, found living attached to the mouthparts of cold-water lobsters.
Dicyemida, also known as Rhombozoa, is a phylum of tiny parasites that live in the renal appendages of cephalopods.
Entoprocta, or Kamptozoa, commonly called goblet worms, is a phylum of sessile aquatic animals, the mature individuals being goblet-shaped.
The gastrotrichs, commonly referred to as hairybellies or hairybacks, are a group of microscopic, cylindrical animals widely distributed in freshwater and marine environments.
Orthonectida is a small phylum of poorly known parasites of marine invertebrates that are very simple multicellular organisms.
Phoronids, sometimes called horseshoe worms, are a small phylum of marine animals that filter-feed with a lophophore, a crown of tentacles, and build upright tubes of chitin.
Riftia is a genus of polychaete annelid worms in the Siboglinidae family, containing the species Riftia pachyptila, commonly known as the giant tubeworm or giant beardworm.
Oligochaeta is a subclass of soft-bodied animals in the phylum Annelida, made up of many types of aquatic and terrestrial worms, including all of the various earthworms.
The Turbellaria are one of the traditional subdivisions of the phylum Platyhelminthes, the flatworms, and include all the subgroups that are not exclusively parasitic.
Eucestoda is the larger of the two subclasses of flatworms in the class Cestoda, whose members are commonly known as tapeworms.
Hemichordata is a phylum of marine deuterostome animals, generally considered the sister group of the echinoderms.
Xenacoelomorpha is a small phylum of bilaterian invertebrate animals, consisting of two sister groups, the acoelomorphs and the xenoturbellids.
A genet is a member of the genus Genetta, which consists of seventeen species of small African carnivorans.
Dolichotis is a genus of the cavy family of rodents, large relatives of guinea pigs common in the Patagonian steppes of Argentina.
Vechur is a breed of Zebu cattle, named after the village of Vechoor in Kerala, India, and a very small cattle breed.
The American Rambouillet is an American breed of Merino sheep that derives from the historic Rambouillet of France.
The Baudet du Poitou, also called the Poitevin or Poitou, is a French breed of donkey, named for the former province of Poitou in western France.
The Australian Lowline is a modern Australian breed of small, polled beef cattle, the result of a selective breeding experiment using black Aberdeen Angus cattle.
Pye-dog, also known as the pariah dog, is a term used to describe an ownerless, half-wild, free-ranging dog that lives in or close to human settlements.
Missing link is a non-scientific term that typically refers to transitional fossils, often used in popular science and in the media for any new transitional form.
In human genetics, the Y-chromosomal Adam is the patrilineal common ancestor from whom all the Y chromosomes of living men descend.
The Alpine is a North American breed of medium- to large-sized domestic goat of dairy type, with a straight facial profile and erect ears.
Trimerophytopsida is a class of early vascular plants from the Devonian, informally called trimerophytes. It contains genera such as Psilophyton.
Lycopodium is a genus of clubmosses, also known as ground pines or creeping cedars, in the family Lycopodiaceae. Two very different circumscriptions of the genus are in use.
Tempskya is an extinct genus of tree fern that lived during the Cretaceous period. Fossils have been found across both the Northern and Southern hemispheres.
Wattieza is a genus of prehistoric trees that existed in the mid-Devonian that belong to the cladoxylopsids, close relatives of the modern ferns and horsetails.

Gnetidae, commonly known as gnetophytes, is a subclass of gymnosperms within the class Pinopsida. The group was previously considered the distinct class Gnetopsida within the distinct division Gnetophyta.
Gnetum gnemon is a species of Gnetum, an unusual genus of gymnosperms. Its native area spans from northeast India south through the Malay Peninsula and Archipelago to the Philippines.
Afrocarpus is a genus of conifers in the family Podocarpaceae, native to Africa. Five species are recognized.
Taxus is a genus of coniferous trees or shrubs known as yews in the family Taxaceae. Yews occur around the globe in temperate zones of the northern hemisphere.
Callitropsis nootkatensis is a species of coniferous tree in the cypress family, Cupressaceae, native to the coastal regions of northwestern North America.
Hesperocyparis lusitanica, the Mexican cypress, cedar-of-Goa or Goa cedar, is a species of conifer in the cypress family, Cupressaceae, native to Mexico and Central America.
Juniperus phoenicea, the Phoenicean juniper or Arâr, is a species of juniper found in the western Mediterranean region.
Juniperus scopulorum, the Rocky Mountain juniper, is a species of juniper native to western North America, reaching from Canada to the Great Plains of the United States.
Nymphaea thermarum, also known as Miniature Rwandan water lily, is a species of water lily that is endemic to Rwanda. It was once thought to be extinct in the wild.
Lauraceae, or the laurels, is a plant family that includes the true laurel and its relatives.
The Annonaceae are a family of flowering plants consisting of trees, shrubs, or rarely lianas commonly known as the custard apple family or soursop family.
Acorus calamus, also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root among many other common names, is a species of flowering plant. It is a tall wetland monocot of the family Acoraceae, in the genus Acorus.

Roystonea is a genus of eleven species of monoecious palms, native to the Neotropics, in the Caribbean, the adjacent coasts of Florida in the United States, Mexico, Central America and northern South America.

Roystonea oleracea, sometimes known as the Caribbean royal palm, palmiste, imperial palm or cabbage palm, is a species of palm which is native to the Lesser Antilles, Colombia, Venezuela, and Trinidad.
Asparagales, the asparagoid lilies, are a diverse order of flowering plants in the monocots.
Commelinales is an order of flowering plants. It comprises five families: Commelinaceae, Haemodoraceae, Hanguanaceae, Philydraceae, and Pontederiaceae.
Commelinaceae is a family of flowering plants. In less formal contexts, the group is referred to as the dayflower family or spiderwort family.
Fritillaria, the fritillaries, is a genus of spring flowering herbaceous bulbous perennial plants in the lily family, Liliaceae. The type species is Fritillaria meleagris.
The Poales are a large order of flowering plants in the monocotyledons, and includes families of plants such as the grasses, bromeliads, rushes and sedges.
Fe'i bananas are cultivated plants in the genus Musa, used mainly for their fruit.
Musa balbisiana, also known simply as plantain, is a wild-type species of banana. It is one of the ancestors of modern cultivated bananas, along with Musa acuminata.
Asterales is an order of dicotyledonous flowering plants that includes the large family Asteraceae, known for composite flowers made of florets, and related families.
Boraginaceae, the borage or forget-me-not family, is a family of flowering plants with two significantly different circumscriptions.
Caryophyllales is a diverse and heterogeneous order of flowering plants which includes well-known species such as cacti, carnations, beets, quinoa, spinach, amaranths, pigfaces and ice plants.
Amaranthaceae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as the amaranth family, in reference to its type genus Amaranthus. It includes the former goosefoot family Chenopodiaceae.
The Polygonaceae are a family of flowering plants known informally as the knotweed family or smartweed–buckwheat family in the United States. The name is based on the genus Polygonum.
The Aizoaceae, or fig-marigold family, are a large family of dicotyledonous flowering plants. Several genera are commonly named ice plants or carpet weeds.
Dianthus is a genus of flowering plants in the family Caryophyllaceae, native mainly to Europe and Asia, with a few species in northern and southern Africa.
Droseraceae is a family of carnivorous flowering plants, also known as the sundew family. It consists of three extant genera, the vast majority of species being in the sundew genus Drosera.

Phytolacca is a genus of perennial plants native to North America, South America and East Asia. Some members of the genus are known as pokeweeds or similar names such as pokebush, pokeberry or pokeroot.
The Ericales are a large and diverse order of flowering plants in the asterid group of the eudicots.
Styrax, with common names storax or snowbell, is a genus of large shrubs or small trees in the family Styracaceae, mostly native to warm temperate to tropical regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
Fabales is an order of flowering plants included in the rosid group of the eudicots.
Dalbergia is a large genus of small to medium-size trees, shrubs and lianas in the pea family, Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae.
The Fagales are an order of flowering plants in the rosid group of dicotyledons, including some well-known trees. Members include beeches, chestnuts, oaks, walnut, pecan and hickory.
Betulaceae, the birch family, includes six genera of deciduous nut-bearing trees and shrubs, including the birches, alders, hazels, hornbeams, hazel-hornbeam, and hop-hornbeams.
Alnus rubra, the red alder, is a deciduous broadleaf tree native to western North America, from Alaska to California and inland to Idaho and Montana.

Betula nigra, the black birch, river birch or water birch, is a species of birch native to the Eastern United States, ranging from New Hampshire across to southern Minnesota and south to northern Florida.
The Fagaceae are a family of flowering plants that includes beeches, chestnuts and oaks, and comprises eight genera.
Fagus grandifolia, the American beech or North American beech, is a species of tree growing to between sixteen and thirty-five meters tall. It is one of two beech species native to North America.
The Juglandaceae are an angiosperm family known as the walnuts. They are trees, or sometimes shrubs, in the order Fagales.
The Lamiales, also known as the mint order, are an order of flowering plants in the asterids clade of the eudicots.
The Malpighiales comprise a large and very diverse order of flowering plants, with well-known members including willows, violets, poplars, corpse flower and cassava.
The Salicaceae are the willow family of flowering plants. The traditional family includes the willows and poplars.
Populus is a genus of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to temperate, subarctic, and montane regions of Eurasia, North America, and North Africa.
Rafflesia arnoldii is a species of flowering plant in the parasitic genus Rafflesia within the family Rafflesiaceae. It is native to the rainforests of Sumatra and Borneo.
Adansonia digitata, the African baobab, is a widespread tree species of the genus Adansonia, the baobabs, and is native to the African continent and the southern Arabian Peninsula.

Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested. It is native to tropical and subtropical regions of the Old and New World.
Gossypium arboreum, commonly called tree cotton, is a species of cotton native to India and Sri Lanka. There is evidence of its cultivation long ago in the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Dipterocarpaceae is a family of flowering plants of mainly lowland tropical forest trees. Their distribution is pantropical.
Melastomataceae is a family of dicotyledonous flowering plants found mostly in the tropics.

Rosales are an order of flowering plants. Well-known members include roses, strawberries, blackberries and raspberries, apples, cherries, pears, plums, peaches and apricots, almonds, rowan and hawthorn.
Humulus lupulus, the common hop or hops, is a species of flowering plant in the hemp family, Cannabaceae. It is a perennial, herbaceous climbing plant which sends up new shoots in early spring.
Ficus is a genus of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae. Collectively known as fig trees or figs, they are native throughout the tropics.

Ficus religiosa, or sacred fig, is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to the fig and mulberry family Moraceae. It is also known as the bodhi tree or bo tree.
Malus sieversii is a wild apple. DNA analysis showed that it is the primary ancestor of the domesticated apple Malus domestica.
Pyrus bretschneideri, the ya pear or Chinese white pear, is an interspecific hybrid species of pear native to North China, where it is widely grown for its fruit.
Pyrus pyrifolia is a species of pear tree native to southern China and northern Indochina that has been introduced to Korea, Japan and other parts of the world.

Ulmus davidiana, also known as the David elm, or Father David elm, named after the botanist Armand David, who collected specimens, is a small deciduous tree widely distributed across China, Mongolia and nearby lands.
Ulmus glabra, the wych elm or Scots elm, has a wide range among the European elm species, from Ireland eastwards to the Ural Mountains.
Ulmus laevis, variously known as the European white elm, fluttering elm, spreading elm and stately elm, is a large deciduous tree native to Europe.
Ulmus minor, the field elm, is a polymorphic European elm species, although its taxonomy remains a matter of contention. Its natural range is predominantly south European.
Ulmus parvifolia, the Chinese elm or lacebark elm, is a species of flowering plant native to eastern Asia, including China, India, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Siberia, and Kazakhstan.
Ulmus pumila, the Siberian elm, is a tree native to Asia. It is also known as the Asiatic elm and dwarf elm.
The Anacardiaceae, commonly known as the cashew family or sumac family, are a family of flowering plants.
Schinus is a genus of flowering trees and tall shrubs in the sumac family, Anacardiaceae. Members of the genus are commonly known as pepper trees.
Toxicodendron is a genus of flowering plants in the sumac family, Anacardiaceae. It contains trees, shrubs and woody vines, including poison ivy, poison oak, and the lacquer tree.
Toxicodendron vernicifluum, formerly Rhus verniciflua, also known by the common name Chinese lacquer tree, is an Asian tree species of genus Toxicodendron.
The Rutaceae is a family, commonly known as the rue or citrus family, of flowering plants, usually placed in the order Sapindales.
The citron, Citrus medica, is a large fragrant citrus fruit with a thick, coarse rind. It resembles a lemon, but is larger.
The Sapindaceae are a family of flowering plants in the order Sapindales known as the soapberry family.

Acer saccharinum, commonly known as silver maple, creek maple, silverleaf maple, soft maple, large maple, water maple, swamp maple, or white maple, is a species of maple native to eastern North America.
Ribes is a genus of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. Ribes is the sole genus in the plant family Grossulariaceae.
Convolvulaceae, commonly called the bindweeds or morning glories, is a family of flowering plants. These species are primarily herbaceous vines, but also include trees and shrubs.

Pinguicula, commonly known as butterworts, is a genus of carnivorous flowering plants in the family Lentibulariaceae. They use sticky, glandular leaves to lure, trap, and break down insects in order to supplement nutrients.
Utricularia, commonly and collectively called the bladderworts, is a genus of carnivorous plants.
Polylepis is a genus of shrub and tree species that are endemic to the mid- and high-elevation regions of the tropical Andes.
The Urticaceae are a family, the nettle family, of flowering plants. The family name comes from the genus Urtica.
The peony or paeony is any flowering plant in the genus Paeonia, the sole genus in the family Paeoniaceae. Peonies are native to Asia, Europe, and western North America.
Blastocladiomycota is part of a group of saprotrophic fungus that is one of the currently recognized phyla within the kingdom Fungi.
Mucoromycotina is a subphylum of uncertain placement in Fungi. It was considered part of the phylum Zygomycota, but recent phylogenetic studies have shown that it was polyphyletic.
Neocallimastigomycota are a phylum containing anaerobic fungi, which are symbionts found in the digestive tracts of larger herbivores.
The opisthokonts are a broad group of eukaryotes, including both the animal and fungus kingdoms. The opisthokonts, previously called the Fungi and Metazoa group, are generally recognized as a clade.

Holozoa is a clade of organisms that includes animals and their single-celled relatives, but excludes fungi and all other organisms. Together they are purely heterotrophic organisms, including some unicellular species.
The Ichthyosporea, or DRIP clade, or Mesomycetozoea, are a small group of Opisthokonta in Eukaryota, formerly protists, mostly parasites of fish and other animals.

Diaphoretickes is a major evolutionary lineage, or clade, of eukaryotic organisms. They comprise an enormous diversity of life forms, from single-celled protozoa to multicellular plants and numerous types of algae.

Desmidiales, commonly called the desmids, are an order in the Charophyta, a division of green algae in which the land plants emerged. Desmids consist of single-celled, sometimes filamentous or colonial, microscopic green algae.

The cryptomonads, sometimes called cryptophytes, are a group of algae and colorless flagellates, many of which have plastids. They are traditionally considered a division of algae among phycologists, under the name of Cryptophyta.
SAR is a highly diverse clade of eukaryotes, often considered a supergroup, that includes stramenopiles, alveolates, and rhizarians.
Cercozoa is a phylum of diverse single-celled eukaryotes. They lack shared morphological characteristics at the microscopic level, and are instead united by molecular phylogenies.
Yellow-green algae or the Xanthophyceae are an important group of heterokont algae. Many live in fresh water, but some are found in marine and soil habitats.
A bikont, meaning two flagella, is any of the eukaryotic organisms classified in the group Bikonta. Many single-celled and multi-celled organisms are members of the group.
Chromalveolata was a eukaryote supergroup present in a major classification, then regarded as one of the six major groups within the eukaryotes. It was a refinement of the kingdom Chromista.

Chromista is a proposed but controversial biological kingdom, refined from the Chromalveolata, consisting of single-celled and multicellular eukaryotic species that share similar features in their photosynthetic organelles.
Nanobdellati, synonym DPANN, is a kingdom of archaea. Many members show novel signs of horizontal gene transfer from other domains of life.

Methanobacteriati is a kingdom of archaea. Methanobacteriati are highly diverse and include methanogens, which produce methane and are often found in intestines; halobacteria, which survive extreme concentrations of salt.
Thermoproteati is a kingdom of archaea. Its synonym, TACK, is an acronym for Thaumarchaeota, Aigarchaeota, Crenarchaeota and Korarchaeota, the groups found early on.
The Thermoproteota are archaea that have been classified as a phylum of the domain Archaea. Initially, the Thermoproteota were thought to be sulfur-dependent extremophiles.

Nitrososphaeria, previously phylum Nitrososphaerota or Thaumarchaeota, is a class of Archaea under the phylum Thermoproteota. The species Cenarchaeum symbiosum was found to have a genome distinct from other known archaea.
Acidobacteriota is a phylum of Gram-negative bacteria. Its members are physiologically diverse and ubiquitous, especially in soils, but are under-represented in culture.

The Aquificota phylum is a diverse collection of bacteria that live in harsh environmental settings. The name Aquificota was given to this phylum based on an early genus identified within this group, Aquifex, which is able to produce water by oxidizing hydrogen.
Bacteroides is a genus of Gram-negative, obligate anaerobic bacteria. Bacteroides species are non endospore-forming bacilli, and may be either motile or nonmotile, depending on the species.
Chlamydia pneumoniae is a species of Chlamydia, an obligate intracellular bacterium that infects humans and is a major cause of pneumonia. It was known as the Taiwan acute respiratory agent.

The Chlamydiota, synonym Chlamydiae, are a bacterial phylum and class whose members are remarkably diverse, including pathogens of humans and animals, symbionts of ubiquitous protozoa, and marine sediment forms not yet well understood.
The Chloroflexota are a phylum of bacteria largely described as green non-sulfur bacteria.
Fibrobacterota is a small bacterial phylum which includes many of the major rumen bacteria, allowing for the degradation of plant-based cellulose in ruminant animals.
Pseudomonadota, synonym Proteobacteria, is a major phylum of gram-negative bacteria. They include both pathogenic and free-living, non-parasitic genera.
Neisseria is a large genus of bacteria that colonize the mucous membranes of many animals.

Gram-positive bacteria are bacteria that give a positive result in the Gram stain, which is traditionally used to quickly classify bacteria into two broad categories according to their type of cell wall.
The Actinomycetota, previously known as Actinobacteria, are a diverse phylum of Gram-positive bacteria with high guanine-cytosine content. They can be terrestrial or aquatic.
The Bacillota, synonym Firmicutes, are a phylum of bacteria, many of which have Gram-positive cell wall structure. They have round cells, called cocci, or rod-like forms, called bacillus.
Bacillus, from Latin bacillus, meaning little staff or wand, is a genus of Gram-positive, rod-shaped bacteria, a member of the phylum Bacillota.

Parakaryon myojinensis, also known as the Myojin parakaryote, is a highly unusual species of single-celled organism known from a single specimen. It has features of both prokaryotes and eukaryotes but is apparently distinct from either group.

The phylum Bacteroidota, synonym Bacteroidetes, is composed of three large classes of Gram-negative, nonsporeforming, anaerobic or aerobic, and rod-shaped bacteria that are widely distributed in the environment, including in soil, sediments, and sea water.

A blood cell, also called a hemocyte or hematocyte, is a cell produced through hematopoiesis and found mainly in the blood. Major types of blood cells include red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

The sacrum, in human anatomy, is a triangular bone at the base of the spine that forms by the fusing of the sacral vertebrae. The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.

The ulna or ulnar bone is a long bone in the forearm stretching from the elbow to the wrist. It is on the same side of the forearm as the little finger, running parallel to the radius, the forearm's other long bone.

A taproot is a large, central, and dominant root from which other roots sprout laterally and horizontally. Typically, a taproot is somewhat straight and very thick, is tapering in shape, and grows straight down.
An ascus is the spore-bearing cell produced in ascomycete fungi. Each ascus usually contains eight ascospores.
A sporangium is an enclosure in which spores are formed. It can be composed of a single cell or can be multicellular.

The cardiac cycle is the performance of the human heart from the beginning of one heartbeat to the beginning of the next. It consists of two periods: one during which the heart muscle relaxes and refills with blood, called diastole, following a period of robust contraction and pumping of blood, called systole.
In biology, hemostasis or haemostasis is a process to prevent and stop bleeding, meaning to keep blood within a damaged blood vessel. It is the initial stage of wound healing.

Glycoproteins are proteins which contain oligosaccharide, or sugar, chains covalently attached to amino acid side-chains. The carbohydrate is attached to the protein in a cotranslational or posttranslational modification.
A bird nest is the spot in which a bird lays and incubates its eggs and raises its young.

Cell polarity refers to spatial differences in shape, structure, and function within a cell. Almost all cell types exhibit some form of polarity, which enables them to carry out specialized functions.
ATPases are a class of enzymes that catalyze the decomposition of ATP into ADP and a free phosphate ion or the inverse reaction.

Bacteria, despite apparent simplicity, have highly organized and efficient cell structures, which allow them to fill many ecological niches. While resembling other prokaryotes, many features of bacterial cells are unique to bacteria, and not found among archaea or eukaryotes.
Non-coding DNA sequences are components of an organism's DNA that do not encode protein sequences. Some non-coding DNA is transcribed into functional non-coding RNA molecules.
Micro ribonucleic acid are small, single-stranded, non-coding RNA molecules containing twenty-one to twenty-three nucleotides.

Sex linkage describes the sex-specific patterns of inheritance and presentation when a gene mutation is present on a sex chromosome rather than a non-sex chromosome. In humans, these are termed X-linked recessive, X-linked dominant and Y-linked.

A chromosomal abnormality or chromosomal anomaly is a missing, extra, or irregular portion of chromosomal DNA. These can occur in the form of numerical abnormalities, where there is an atypical number of chromosomes, or as structural abnormalities.

In genetics, chromosome translocation is a phenomenon that results in unusual rearrangement of chromosomes. This includes balanced and unbalanced translocation, with three main types: reciprocal, nonreciprocal and Robertsonian translocation.
A breech birth is the birth of a baby delivered with the bottom or feet leading rather than the head, as is typical.
Postterm pregnancy is a pregnancy continuing past the forty-second week of gestation, two weeks beyond the typical forty-week duration of pregnancy.

Premenstrual syndrome is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period. Symptoms resolve around the time menstrual bleeding begins.

Hot flash is a vasomotor symptom, often caused by the changing hormone levels that are characteristic of menopause. It is typically experienced as a feeling of intense heat with sweating and rapid heartbeat.
Allied health professionals are a category of health professionals that provide a range of diagnostic, preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative services in connection with health care.
The forearm is the region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.
Skin grafting, a type of graft surgery, involves the transplantation of skin without a defined circulation. The transplanted tissue is called a skin graft.
Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine medication. It is used in the treatment of itchiness, anxiety, insomnia, and nausea, including that due to motion sickness.

A psychiatric or psychotropic medication is a psychoactive drug taken to exert an effect on the chemical makeup of the brain and nervous system. Thus, these medications are used to treat mental illnesses.
Hypovolemic shock is a form of shock caused by severe hypovolemia, meaning insufficient blood volume or fluid outside of cells in the body. It can be caused by severe dehydration or blood loss.
