An injury is any physiological damage to living tissue caused by immediate physical stress. Injuries to humans may be caused by blunt trauma, penetrating trauma, burning, toxic exposure, asphyxiation, or overexertion.
Dental avulsion is the complete displacement of a tooth from its socket in alveolar bone owing to trauma, such as a fall, road traffic accident, sports, or occupational injury.
Far-sightedness, also known as long-sightedness, hypermetropia, and hyperopia, is a condition of the eye where distant objects are seen clearly but near objects appear blurred.

Pathogenic bacteria are bacteria that can cause disease. This article focuses on the bacteria that are pathogenic to humans. Many species of bacteria are harmless and many are beneficial but others can cause infectious diseases.

Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila. Signs and symptoms include cough, shortness of breath, high fever, muscle pains, and headaches.

Blurred vision is an ocular symptom where vision becomes less precise and there is added difficulty to resolve fine details, creating a blurry view. Temporary blurred vision may involve dry eyes, eye infections, or low blood pressure.
A rash is a change of the skin that affects its color, appearance, or texture. A rash may be localized in one part of the body, or affect all the skin.

Gerontology is the science of old age and the aging process. It encompasses the understanding, prevention, rehabilitation, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions associated with the changes that occur in humans throughout their entire lifespan.
A moggy is any cat which has not been intentionally bred. Moggies lack a consistent appearance unlike purebred cats that are selectively bred for appearance conforming to a standard.
A free-ranging dog is a dog that is not confined to a yard or house. Free-ranging dogs include street dogs, village dogs, stray dogs, feral dogs, and others, and may be owned or unowned.
Dog crossbreeds, sometimes called designer dogs, are dogs which have been crossbred or selectively bred from two or more recognized dog breeds.
Canid hybrids are the result of interbreeding between the species of the subfamily Caninae.
A Panthera hybrid is a crossbreed between individuals of any of the five species of the genus Panthera: the tiger, lion, jaguar, leopard, and snow leopard.
A sheep-goat hybrid, called a geep in popular media or sometimes a shoat, is a domestic bovid hybrid between a sheep and a goat.
An ursid hybrid is an animal with parents from two different species or subspecies of the bear family, Ursidae.
A puppy is a juvenile dog, generally one less than twelve to eighteen months old.
A kitten is a juvenile cat. After being born, kittens display primary altriciality and are fully dependent on their mothers for survival.
Merlangius merlangus, commonly known as whiting or merling, is an important food fish in the eastern North Atlantic Ocean and the northern Mediterranean, western Baltic, and Black Sea.
Fanfin seadevils or hairy anglerfish comprise the family Caulophrynidae, marine ray-finned fishes of the suborder Ceratioidei, the deep-sea anglerfishes.
Interbreeding between archaic humans, such as Neanderthals and Denisovans, and anatomically modern humans took place during the Middle Paleolithic and early Upper Paleolithic.

An Earth ellipsoid or Earth spheroid is a mathematical figure approximating the Earth's shape and size, used as part of a reference frame for coordinates and computations in geodesy, astronomy, and the geosciences. Various different reference ellipsoids have been used as approximations.

The Schiehallion experiment was an eighteenth-century experiment to determine the mean density of the Earth. Funded by a grant from the Royal Society, it was conducted in the summer around the Scottish mountain of Schiehallion, Perthshire.

Environmental conflicts, socio-environmental conflict or ecological distribution conflicts, are social conflicts caused by environmental degradation or by unequal distribution of environmental resources.
The Dvorak technique is a widely used system to estimate tropical cyclone intensity based solely on visible and infrared satellite images.
Tropical cyclone rainfall forecasting involves using scientific models and other tools to predict the precipitation expected in tropical cyclones such as hurricanes and typhoons.
Tropical cyclone track forecasting involves predicting where a tropical cyclone is going to track over the next five days.
The climate of Antarctica is extremely cold and dry. Snow rarely melts on much of the continent.

The climate of the Arctic is characterized by long, cold winters and short, cool summers. There is a large amount of variability in climate across the Arctic, but all regions experience extremes of solar radiation in both summer and winter.

The Middle East and North Africa region emits billions of tonnes of carbon dioxide and produces a share of global greenhouse gas emissions. These emissions are mostly from the energy sector, an integral component of many Middle Eastern and North African economies due to the extensive oil and natural gas reserves.

Partial melting is the phenomenon that occurs when a rock is subjected to temperatures high enough to cause certain minerals to melt, but not all of them. Partial melting is an important part of the formation of all igneous rocks and some metamorphic rocks.
In rheology, Byerlee's law, also known as Byerlee's friction law, concerns the shear stress required to slide one rock over another.

The theory of tides is the application of continuum mechanics to interpret and predict the tidal deformations of planetary and satellite bodies and their atmospheres and oceans under the gravitational loading of another astronomical body or bodies.
In seismology, a seismic zone or seismic belt is an area of seismicity potentially sharing a common cause. It can be referred to as an earthquake belt as well.

An intraplate earthquake is an earthquake which occurs in the interior of a tectonic plate. They are relatively rare compared to the more familiar interplate earthquakes, which occur on the boundaries of tectonic plates.
The Sturtian glaciation, also known as the Sturt glaciation, was a worldwide glaciation during the Cryogenian Period when the Earth experienced repeated large-scale glaciations.

The Mesoarchean is a geologic era in the Archean Eon, spanning three thousand two hundred to two thousand eight hundred million years ago, which contains early evidence of modern-style plate subduction and expansion of microbial life.
The Paleoproterozoic Era, also spelled Palaeoproterozoic, is a long era that opens the Proterozoic eon, spanning from two thousand five hundred to sixteen hundred million years ago.

The Algoman orogeny, known as the Kenoran orogeny in Canada, was an episode of mountain-building during the Late Archean Eon that involved repeated episodes of continental collisions, compressions and subductions.
The Central Asian Orogenic Belt, also called the Altaids, is one of the world's large Phanerozoic accretionary orogens, and thus a leading laboratory of geologically recent crustal growth.
The Slave craton is an Archaean craton in the north-western Canadian Shield, in Northwest Territories and Nunavut.
An arsenide mineral is a mineral that contains arsenide as its main anion. Arsenides are grouped with the sulfides in both the Dana and Strunz mineral classification systems.
Psilomelane is a group name for hard black manganese oxides including hollandite and romanechite. Psilomelane consists of hydrous manganese oxide with variable amounts of barium and potassium.

Allanite, also called orthite, is a sorosilicate group of minerals within the broader epidote group that contain a significant amount of rare-earth elements. The mineral occurs mainly in metamorphosed clay-rich sediments and felsic igneous rocks.
Cummingtonite is a metamorphic amphibole, a magnesium iron silicate hydroxide.
Hectorite is a rare soft, greasy, white, lithium-rich clay mineral. It was named for an occurrence in the United States near Hector, California.

The feldspathoids are a group of tectosilicate minerals which resemble feldspars but have a different structure and much lower silica content. They occur in rare and unusual types of igneous rocks, and are usually not found in rocks containing primary quartz.
The sulfide minerals are a class of minerals containing sulfide or disulfide as the major anion. Some sulfide minerals are economically important as metal ores.

Boninite is an extrusive rock high in both magnesium and silica, thought to be usually formed in fore-arc environments, typically during the early stages of subduction. The rock is named for its occurrence in the Izu-Bonin arc south of Japan.
Kainite is an evaporite mineral. It is a hydrated potassium-magnesium sulfate-chloride, naturally occurring in irregular granular masses or as crystalline coatings.
Aggradation, or alluviation, in geology is the increase in land elevation, typically in a river system, due to the deposition of sediment.
Soil acidification is the buildup of hydrogen cations, which reduces the soil pH. Chemically, this happens when a proton donor gets added to the soil.
Tilth is a physical condition of soil, especially in relation to its suitability for planting or growing a crop.

A cratonic sequence is a very large-scale lithostratigraphic sequence in the rock record that represents a complete cycle of marine transgression and regression on a craton, a block of continental crust, over geologic time.

A type locality in geology is the specific geographic locality where a particular rock type, stratigraphic unit, unstratified rock unit, mineral species, stratigraphic boundary, or other geological feature was originally defined and named.
Structural geology is the study of the three-dimensional distribution of rock units with respect to their deformational histories.

Boudinage is a geological term for structures formed by extension, where a rigid tabular body such as hornfels, is stretched and deformed amidst less competent surroundings. The competent bed begins to break up, forming sausage-shaped boudins.
The brittle-ductile transition zone is the zone of the Earth's crust that marks the transition from the upper, more brittle crust to the lower, more ductile crust.

In geology, shear is the response of a rock to deformation usually by compressive stress and forms particular textures. Shear can be homogeneous or non-homogeneous, and may be pure shear or simple shear.
Tectonic uplift is the geologic uplift of Earth's surface that is attributed to plate tectonics.

Décollement is a gliding plane between two rock masses, also known as a basal detachment fault. Décollements are a deformational structure, resulting in independent styles of deformation in the rocks above and below the fault.

Volatiles are the group of chemical elements and chemical compounds that can be readily vaporized. In contrast with volatiles, elements and compounds that are not readily vaporized are known as refractory substances.
A complex volcano, also called a compound volcano or a volcanic complex, is a mixed landform consisting of related volcanic centers and their associated lava flows and pyroclastic rock.
Upland and lowland are conditional descriptions of a plain based on elevation above sea level. In studies of the ecology of freshwater rivers, habitats are classified as upland or lowland.
In geology, a depression is a landform sunken or depressed below the surrounding area. Depressions form by various mechanisms.

A point bar is a depositional feature made of alluvium that accumulates on the inside bend of streams and rivers below the slip-off slope. Point bars are found in abundance in mature or meandering streams.
A summit is a point on a planet's surface that is higher in elevation than all points immediately adjacent to it. The topographic terms acme, apex, peak, and zenith are synonymous.
Bay mud consists of thick deposits of soft, unconsolidated silty clay, which is saturated with water; these soil layers are situated at the bottom of certain estuaries.
Water quality refers to the chemical, physical, and biological characteristics of water based on the standards of its usage.

The oceanic zone is typically defined as the area of the ocean lying beyond the continental shelf, but operationally is often referred to as beginning where the water depths drop below two hundred metres, seaward from the coast into the open ocean with its pelagic zone.
A turbidity current is typically an underwater current of usually rapidly moving, sediment-laden water moving down a slope.
Groundwater recharge or deep drainage or deep percolation is a hydrologic process, where water moves downward from surface water to groundwater.
A salt lake or saline lake is a landlocked body of water that has a concentration of salts, typically sodium chloride, and other dissolved minerals significantly higher than typical lakes.

A bedrock river is a river that has little to no alluvium mantling the bedrock over which it flows. However, many bedrock rivers are not pure forms; they are a combination of a bedrock channel and an alluvial channel.
A braided river, also called a braided channel or braided stream, consists of a network of river channels separated by small, often temporary, islands called braid bars.

An endorheic basin is a drainage basin that normally retains water and allows no outflow to other external bodies of water, such as rivers and oceans. Instead, the water drainage flows into permanent and seasonal lakes and swamps that equilibrate through evaporation.
In geography, hydrography, and fluvial geomorphology, a thalweg or talweg is the line or curve of minimum elevation within a valley or watercourse.
A tributary, or an affluent, is a stream that typically flows into a larger stream or lake, or rarely into a smaller stream.
Continental crustal fragments, partly synonymous with microcontinents, are pieces of continents that have broken off from main continental masses to form distinct islands.
An uninhabited island, desert island, or deserted island, is an island, islet, or atoll which lacks permanent human population.
Critical geography is theoretically informed geographical scholarship that promotes social justice, liberation, and leftist politics.
Hypsometry is the measurement of the elevation and depth of features of Earth's surface relative to mean sea level. On Earth, the elevations can take on either positive or negative values.
Bioregionalism is a philosophy that suggests that political, cultural, and economic systems are more sustainable and fair if they are organized around naturally defined areas called bioregions.
Afro-Eurasia, also known as Afroeurasia and Eurafrasia, is a landmass, occasionally described as a supercontinent, comprising the continents of Africa, Asia, and Europe.
Continental Europe or mainland Europe is the contiguous mainland of Europe, excluding its surrounding islands.
The Kerguelen Plateau, also known as the Kerguelen-Heard Plateau, is an oceanic plateau and large igneous province located on the Antarctic Plate, in the southern Indian Ocean.
Zealandia, also known as Te Riu-a-Māui or Tasmantis, is an almost entirely submerged mass of continental crust in Oceania that subsided after breaking away from Gondwana.
Africa is a continent comprising many political territories, and one of the great southward projections from the main mass of Earth's surface.

The geography of Antarctica is dominated by its south polar location and, thus, by ice. The Antarctic continent, located in the Earth's Southern Hemisphere, is centered asymmetrically around the South Pole and largely south of the Antarctic Circle.
Geography of Asia reviews geographical concepts of classifying Asia, comprising many countries and territories.

Europe is traditionally defined as one of seven continents. Physiographically, it is the northwestern peninsula of the larger landmass known as Eurasia, or the larger Afro-Eurasia; Asia occupies the centre and east of this continuous landmass.
North America is a continent, and is also a portion of a supercontinent if North and South America are combined into the Americas.

The geography of South America contains many diverse regions and climates. Geographically, South America is generally considered a continent forming the southern portion of the landmass of the Americas.

The one hundred eightieth meridian, or antimeridian, is the meridian one hundred eighty degrees both east and west of the prime meridian in a geographical coordinate system. The longitude at this line can be given as either east or west.
The north and south celestial poles are the two points in the sky where Earth's axis of rotation, indefinitely extended, intersects the celestial sphere.
The five main latitude regions of Earth's surface comprise geographical zones, divided by the major circles of latitude. The differences between them relate to climate.

The subarctic zone is a region in the Northern Hemisphere immediately south of the true Arctic, north of hemiboreal regions and covering much of Alaska, Canada, Iceland, the north of Fennoscandia, Siberia, and the Cairngorms.
The sub-Antarctic zone is a physiographic region in the Southern Hemisphere, located immediately north of the Antarctic region.

The subtropical zones or subtropics are geographical and climate zones immediately to the north and south of the tropics. Geographically part of the temperate zones of both hemispheres, they cover the middle latitudes.
The Southern Hemisphere is the half of Earth that is south of the equator.
The Eastern Hemisphere is the half of the planet Earth which is east of the prime meridian and west of the antimeridian.
The Western Hemisphere is the half of the planet Earth that lies west of the Prime Meridian and east of the antimeridian. The other half is called the Eastern Hemisphere.
The land hemisphere and water hemisphere are the hemispheres of Earth containing the maximum possible total areas of land and ocean, respectively.

Development geography is a branch of geography which refers to the standard of living and its quality of life of its human inhabitants. In this context, development is a process of change that affects peoples' lives.

Language geography is the branch of human geography that studies the geographic distribution of languages or its constituent elements. Linguistic geography can also refer to studies of how people talk about the landscape.
Health geography is the application of geographical information, perspectives, and methods to the study of health, disease, and health care.

Place identity or place-based identity refers to a cluster of ideas about place and identity in the fields of geography, urban planning, urban design, environmental psychology, ecocriticism and urban sociology.
The New World is an early modern term describing the majority of lands in the Western Hemisphere, particularly the Americas, and sometimes Oceania.
The Old World is a term for Afro-Eurasia coined by Europeans when they became aware of the existence of the Americas, Oceania, and Antarctica.
The Anglosphere is a Western-led sphere of influence among English-speaking countries with strong political, economic, cultural, and military ties.
The Middle East and North Africa, also referred to as West Asia and North Africa, is a geographic region which comprises the Middle East and North Africa together.
The Francophonie or Francosphere or Francophone world is the whole body of people and organisations around the world who use the French language regularly for private or public purposes.

The Sinosphere, also known as the Chinese cultural sphere, East Asian cultural sphere, or the Sinic world, encompasses multiple countries in East Asia and Southeast Asia that were historically heavily influenced by Chinese culture.
In ethnogeography, Greater China is a loosely defined region sharing cultural and economic ties with the Chinese people, often used by international enterprises or organisations in unofficial usage.

Quantitative geography is a subfield and methodological approach to geography that develops, tests, and uses scientific, mathematical, and statistical methods to analyze and model geographic phenomena and patterns.

In geography, the quantitative revolution was a paradigm shift that sought to develop a more rigorous and systematic methodology for the discipline. It came as a response to the inadequacy of regional geography to explain general spatial dynamics.
Physical geodesy is the study of the physical properties of Earth's gravity and its potential field, the geopotential, with a view to their application in geodesy.
Height above mean sea level is a measure of a location's vertical distance, height, elevation or altitude, in reference to a vertical datum based on a historic mean sea level.
A geocode or geographic identifier is a code or unique identifier that represents a geographic entity, as distinguished from other entities in the same geocode system.

Geomatics is defined in international standards as the discipline concerned with the collection, distribution, storage, analysis, processing, presentation of geographic data or geographic information.
Geoinformatics is a scientific field primarily within the domains of Computer Science and technical geography.
Geostatistics is a branch of statistics focusing on spatial or spatiotemporal datasets.
Statistical geography is the study and practice of collecting, analysing and presenting data that has a geographic or areal dimension, such as census or demographics data.

Time geography or time-space geography is an evolving transdisciplinary perspective on spatial and temporal processes and events such as social interaction, ecological interaction, social and environmental change, and biographies of individuals.
In social science, the activity space designates the set of places individuals encounter as a result of their routine activities in everyday life.

The azimuthal equidistant projection is an azimuthal map projection. It has the useful properties that all points on the map are at proportionally correct distances from the center point, and that all points on the map are at the correct azimuth from the center point.
The Gall-Peters projection is a rectangular, equal-area map projection. Like all equal-area projections, it distorts many shapes.
A dot distribution map, or a dot density map or simply a dot map, is a type of thematic map that uses a point symbol to visualize the geographic distribution of a large number of related phenomena.
A flow map is a type of thematic map that uses linear symbols to represent movement between locations. It may thus be considered a hybrid of a map and a flow diagram.
A proportional symbol map, proportional point symbol map, or scaled symbol map is a type of thematic map that uses map symbols that vary in size to represent a quantitative variable.
North is one of the four compass points or cardinal directions. It is the opposite of south and is perpendicular to east and west.
South is one of the cardinal directions or compass points. The direction is the opposite of north and is perpendicular to both west and east.
East is one of the four cardinal directions or points of the compass. It is the opposite direction from west and is the direction from which the Sun rises on the Earth.
West is one of the four cardinal directions or points of the compass. It is the opposite direction from east and is the direction in which the Sun sets on the Earth.

Cartographic generalization, or map generalization, includes all changes in a map that are made when one derives a smaller-scale map from a larger-scale map or map data. It is a core part of cartographic design.

The grade or gradient, also called slope, incline, mainfall, pitch or rise, of a physical feature, landform or constructed line is either the elevation angle of that surface to the horizontal or its tangent.
Terrain, alternatively relief or topographical relief, is the surface of a piece of land, its shape and size. In physical geography, terrain is the lay of the land.
The Chukchi Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is bounded on the west by the Long Strait, off Wrangel Island, and in the east by Point Barrow, Alaska, beyond which lies the Beaufort Sea.

The East Siberian Sea is a marginal sea in the Arctic Ocean. It is located between the Arctic Cape to the north, the coast of Siberia to the south, the New Siberian Islands to the west and Wrangel Island to the east.
James Bay is a body of water located on the southern end of Hudson Bay in Canada. Its shorelines are in the provinces of Quebec and Ontario.
The Laptev Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is located between the northern coast of Siberia, the Taimyr Peninsula, Severnaya Zemlya, and the New Siberian Islands.

The Gulf of Ob, also known as the Bay of Ob, is a bay of the Arctic Ocean, located in the north of Russia at the mouth of the Ob River. It is a very long estuary, one of the great estuaries of the world.

The Atlantic meridional overturning circulation is the main ocean current system in the Atlantic Ocean. It is a major component of Earth's ocean circulation system and plays an important role in the planet's climate system.

The Gulf of Bothnia is an arm of the Baltic Sea lying between Sweden and Finland. It is divided into the Bothnian Sea and the more northerly Bothnian Bay, the two being separated by the Kvarken strait.
The Gulf of Finland is the easternmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It extends between Finland to the north and Estonia to the south, to Saint Petersburg to the east, where the river Neva drains into it.

The Bay of Fundy is a bay between the Canadian provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, with a small portion touching the state of Maine. It is an arm of the Gulf of Maine and part of the Atlantic Ocean.
The Bermuda Triangle, also known as the Devil's Triangle, is a loosely defined region in the North Atlantic Ocean, roughly bounded by Florida, Bermuda, and Puerto Rico.

The Celtic Sea is the area of the Atlantic Ocean off the southern coast of Ireland bounded to the north by Saint George's Channel. Other limits include the Bristol Channel, the English Channel, and the Bay of Biscay.
The Chesapeake Bay is a very large estuary in the United States. The bay is located in the Mid-Atlantic region and is primarily separated from the Atlantic Ocean by the Delmarva Peninsula.
Long Island Sound is a marine sound and tidal estuary of the Atlantic Ocean. It lies predominantly between the state of Connecticut to the north and Long Island in New York state to the south.
The Venetian Lagoon, also Venice Lagoon or Lagoon of Venice, is an enclosed bay of the Adriatic Sea, in northern Italy, in which the city of Venice is situated.

The Alboran Sea is the westernmost portion of the Mediterranean Sea, lying between the Iberian Peninsula and the north of Africa. The Strait of Gibraltar, which lies at the west end of the Alboran Sea, connects the Mediterranean with the Atlantic.
The Ligurian Sea is an arm of the Mediterranean Sea. The sea is thought to have been named after the ancient Ligures people.

New York Harbor is a tidal body of water forming the upper part of New York Bay within the New York and New Jersey Harbor Estuary. Located on the East Coast of the United States at the mouth of the Hudson River, it is connected to Long Island Sound by the East River.
The German Bight, sometimes also the German Bay, is the southeastern bight of the North Sea bounded by the Netherlands and Germany to the south, and Denmark and Germany to the east.
The Wadden Sea is an intertidal zone in the southeastern part of the North Sea. It lies between the coast of northwestern continental Europe and the range of low-lying Frisian Islands.
Pamlico Sound is a large estuarine lagoon in North Carolina. A big lagoon along the North American East Coast, it is long and narrow.

The Sognefjord, nicknamed the King of the Fjords, is a very long and deep fjord in Norway. Located in Vestland county in Western Norway, it stretches inland from the ocean to the small village of Skjolden.

The Gulf of Aqaba or Gulf of Eilat is a large gulf at the northern tip of the Red Sea, southeast of the Sinai Peninsula, and west of the Arabian Peninsula. Its coastline is divided among four countries: Egypt, Israel, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia.
The Arafura Sea lies to the southeast of the Malay Archipelago in the western Pacific Ocean, overlying the continental shelf between Australia and Western New Guinea.
The Banda Sea is one of four seas that surround the Maluku Islands of Indonesia, connected to the Pacific Ocean, but surrounded by hundreds of islands, including Timor.
Bristol Bay is the easternmost arm of the Bering Sea, in Southwest Alaska. It is long and wide at its mouth.
The Ariake Sea is a body of salt water surrounded by Fukuoka, Saga, Nagasaki, and Kumamoto Prefectures, all of which lie on the island of Kyushu in Japan. It is a big bay in Kyushu.

Ironbottom Sound is the name given by Allied sailors to the stretch of water at the southern end of The Slot between Guadalcanal, Savo Island, and Nggela Islands of the Solomon Islands, because of the many ships and planes that sank there.
The Java Sea is an extensive shallow sea in Indonesia. It lies on the Sunda Shelf, between the islands of Borneo to the north, Java to the south, Sumatra to the west, and Sulawesi to the east.
Milford Sound is a fiord in the south west of New Zealand's South Island within Fiordland National Park. It has been judged the world's top travel destination in an international survey.
The Gulf of Panama is a gulf of the Pacific Ocean off the southern coast of Panama, where much of the southern shore of eastern Panama adjoins it.
Sagami Bay lies south of Kanagawa Prefecture in Honshu, central Japan, contained within the Miura Peninsula to the east, the Izu Peninsula to the west, and the Shonan coastline to the north.

The Salish Sea is a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean located in the Canadian province of British Columbia and the state of Washington. It includes the Strait of Georgia, the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Puget Sound, and an intricate network of connecting channels.

Puget Sound is a complex estuarine system of interconnected marine waterways and basins located on the northwest coast of the state of Washington. As a part of the Salish Sea, the sound has connections to the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
San Francisco Bay is a large tidal estuary in the state of California, which gives its name to the San Francisco Bay Area. It is dominated by the cities of San Francisco, San Jose, and Oakland.
The Gulf of Tonkin is a gulf at the northwestern portion of the South China Sea, located off the coasts of Tonkin in northern Vietnam and South China.

Victoria Harbour is a natural landform harbour in Hong Kong separating Hong Kong Island to the south from the Kowloon Peninsula to the north. It is a major trading hub, as well as a tourist attraction.
Suruga Bay is a bay on the Pacific coast of Honshu in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan.

Port Jackson, commonly known as Sydney Harbour, is a natural harbour on the east coast of Australia, around which the city of Sydney is situated. It consists of the waters of Sydney Harbour, Middle Harbour, North Harbour, and the Lane Cove and Parramatta rivers.

Tokyo Bay is a bay located in the southern Kanto region of Japan spanning the coasts of Tokyo, Kanagawa Prefecture, and Chiba Prefecture, on the southern coast of the island of Honshu. Tokyo Bay is connected to the Pacific Ocean by the Uraga Channel.
The Bohai Sea is a gulf or inland sea on the east coast of Mainland China. It is the northwestern and innermost extension of the Yellow Sea, to which it connects via the Bohai Strait.
The Amundsen Sea is an arm of the Southern Ocean off Marie Byrd Land in western Antarctica. It lies between Cape Flying Fish to the east and Cape Dart on Siple Island to the west.
The Bellingshausen Sea is marginal sea located along the west side of the Antarctic Peninsula, west of Alexander Island, east of Cape Flying Fish on Thurston Island, and south of Peter I Island.

The McMurdo Sound is a sound in Antarctica, known as the southernmost passable body of water in the world. Captain James Clark Ross discovered the sound in February and named it after Lieutenant Archibald McMurdo of HMS Terror.
Southern Ocean overturning circulation is the southern half of a global thermohaline circulation, which connects different water basins across the global ocean.
The Tyrrhenian Sea is part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. Its namesake is from the Tyrrhenian people, identified with the Etruscans of Italy.
The Molucca Sea is located in the western Pacific Ocean, bordered by the Indonesian Islands of Celebes to the west, Halmahera to the east, and the Sula Islands to the south.
The Solomon Sea is a sea located within the Pacific Ocean. It lies between Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands. Many battles were fought there during World War II.

The Sulu Sea is a body of water in the southwestern area of the Philippines, separated from the South China Sea in the northwest by Palawan and from the Celebes Sea in the southeast by the Sulu Archipelago.
The Scotia Sea is a sea located at the northern edge of the Southern Ocean at its boundary with the South Atlantic Ocean. It is bounded on the west by the Drake Passage.

The Bismarck Sea lies in the south-western Pacific Ocean within the Papua New Guinean exclusive economic zone. It is located north-east of the island of New Guinea and south of the Bismarck Archipelago.

The Celebes Sea or Sulawesi Sea of the western Pacific Ocean is bordered on the north by the Sulu Archipelago and Sulu Sea and Mindanao Island of the Philippines, on the south by Sulawesi's Minahasa Peninsula.
The Flores Sea is a body of water bounded on the north by the Indonesian island of Sulawesi and on the south by the Sunda Islands of Flores and Sumbawa.

Lake Edward is one of the smaller African Great Lakes. It is located in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift, on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes. It lies on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and is in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift.
Lake Assal is a crater lake in central-western Djibouti. It is located at the western end of the Gulf of Tadjoura, at the top of the Great Rift Valley, west of Djibouti city.
The Cahora Bassa lake, in the Portuguese colonial era known as Cabora Bassa, from a word meaning finish the job, is a very large artificial lake situated in the Tete Province in Mozambique.

The Makgadikgadi Pan is a salt pan situated in the middle of the dry savanna of north-eastern Botswana, one of the great salt flats in the world. The pan is all that remains of the formerly enormous Lake Makgadikgadi.
Lake Nasser is a large reservoir in southern Egypt and northern Sudan. It was created by the construction of the Aswan High Dam and is one of the large man-made lakes in the world.

Lake Natron is a highly alkaline salt lake located in north Ngorongoro District of Arusha Region in Tanzania with its far northern end crossing into Kenya. It is in the Gregory Rift, which is the eastern branch of the East African Rift.
Lake Nyos is a crater lake in the Northwest Region of Cameroon. Nyos is a deep lake high on the flank of an inactive volcano in the Oku volcanic plain along the Cameroon line of volcanic activity.
Lake Tritriva is a volcanic lake in southwest-central Madagascar, in the region of Vakinankaratra, located near the village of Belazao.
The North Aral Sea is the portion of the former Aral Sea that is fed by the Syr Darya River. It split from the South Aral Sea as water levels dropped due to river diversion for agriculture.
The South Aral Sea is a lake in the basin of the former Aral Sea that formed when that body divided in two, due to diversion of river inflow for agriculture.

Lake Biwa is a very large freshwater lake in Japan. It is located entirely within Shiga Prefecture, northeast of the former capital city of Kyoto. Lake Biwa is an ancient lake, over four million years old.
Garabogazkol is a shallow, highly saline lagoon off the Caspian Sea in northwestern Turkmenistan.

Dongting Lake is a large, shallow lake in northeastern Hunan Province, China. Also referred to less frequently as the Dongting Plain, it is a flood basin of the Yangtze River, so its volume depends on the season.
Fuji Five Lakes is the name of the area located at the base of Mount Fuji in the Yamanashi Prefecture of Japan.
Lake Khanka or Lake Xingkai, is a freshwater lake on the border between Primorsky Krai, Russia and Heilongjiang province, Northeast China.

Laguna de Bay, also known as Laguna Lake, is a very large lake in the Philippines. Laguna de Bay remains one of the important freshwater resources in the Philippines, supporting millions of residents through fisheries.
Lake Lanao is a large ancient lake in the province of Lanao del Sur, Philippines. It is a very large lake in Mindanao and in the Philippines.
Lake Mashu is an endorheic crater lake formed in the caldera of a potentially active volcano. It is located in Akan Mashu National Park on the island of Hokkaido, Japan.
Namtso or Lake Nam, also referred to as Tengri Nor, is a mountain lake on the border between Damxung County of Lhasa and Baingoin County of Nagqu in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
The Sea of Galilee, also called Lake Tiberias, Genezareth Lake or Kinneret, is a freshwater lake in northeast Israel. It is a very low freshwater lake on Earth, second to the Dead Sea, a salt lake.
Lake Sevan is a very large body of water in Armenia and the broader Caucasus region. It is one of the large freshwater alpine lakes in Eurasia.
Sun Moon Lake is a lake in Yuchi Township, Nantou County, Taiwan. It is a very large body of water in Taiwan.

Taihu, also known as Lake Tai or Lake Taihu, is a lake in the Yangtze Delta and a very large freshwater lake in China. The lake is in Jiangsu province and a significant part of its southern shore forms its border with Zhejiang.
Lake Taymyr is a lake of the central regions of the Taymyr Peninsula in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russian Federation. It is located south of the Byrranga Mountains.
Lake Toba is a large natural lake in North Sumatra and Indonesia. The lake is the massive caldera of the Toba supervolcano.
Tonle Sap, commonly translated as Great Lake, is a lake in central Cambodia. Belonging to the Mekong river system, Tonle Sap is a very large freshwater lake in Southeast Asia.
Lake Balaton is a freshwater rift lake in the Transdanubian region of Hungary. It is a very large lake in Central Europe, and one of the region's foremost tourist destinations.
Lake Constance refers to three bodies of water on the Rhine at the northern foot of the Alps: Upper Lake Constance, Lower Lake Constance, and a connecting stretch of the Rhine.
Lake Garda is a very large lake in Italy. It is a popular holiday location in northern Italy, between Brescia and Milan to the west and Verona and Venice to the east.
Lake Geneva is a deep lake on the north side of the Alps, shared between Switzerland and France. It is one of the large lakes in Western Europe and large on the course of the Rhone.
The IJsselmeer, also known as Lake IJssel in English, is a closed-off freshwater lake in the central Netherlands bordering the provinces of Flevoland, North Holland and Friesland.
The Lakes of Killarney are a scenic attraction located in Killarney National Park near Killarney, County Kerry, in Ireland. They consist of three lakes: Lough Leane, Muckross Lake and Upper Lake.
The Konigssee is a natural lake in the southeast Berchtesgadener Land district of the German state of Bavaria, near the Austrian border. Much of the lake is within the Berchtesgaden National Park.
Laacher See, also known as Lake Laach or Laach Lake, is a volcanic crater lake in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, northwest of Koblenz and south of Bonn.
Loch Lomond is a freshwater Scottish loch that spans the Highland Boundary Fault, often considered the boundary between the Lowlands and Highlands of Scotland.
Lake Lucerne is a lake in central Switzerland. Its German name means Lake of the four forested settlements, in English usually translated as forest cantons.
Lake Maggiore or Verbano is a large lake on the south side of the Alps divided between the Italian regions of Piedmont and Lombardy to the south, and the Swiss canton of Ticino to the north.
Loch Morar is a freshwater loch in the Rough Bounds of Lochaber, Highland, Scotland. It is a large loch by surface area in Scotland, and a very deep freshwater body in the British Isles.
Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It takes its name from the River Ness, which flows from the northern end.
Lake Peipus is a very large trans-boundary lake in Europe, lying on the international border between Estonia and Russia.
Saimaa is a lake located in the Finnish Lakeland area in southeastern Finland. It is a very large lake in Finland, and a large natural freshwater lake in Europe.
Vattern is a large lake in Sweden. It is a long, finger-shaped body of fresh water in south central Sweden, to the southeast of Vanern, pointing at the tip of Scandinavia.
Lake Athabasca is in the northwest corner of Saskatchewan and the northeast corner of Alberta in Canada.

Lake Bonneville was a very large Late Pleistocene paleolake in the Great Basin of western North America. It was a pluvial lake that formed in response to an increase in precipitation and a decrease in evaporation as a result of cooler temperatures.
Lake Champlain is a large natural freshwater lake in North America. It lies mostly between the states of New York and Vermont, but also extends north into the Canadian province of Quebec.
Lake Chapala is a very large freshwater lake in Mexico. It borders both the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.

Crater Lake is a volcanic crater lake in south-central Oregon in the Western United States. It is the main feature of Crater Lake National Park and is a tourist attraction known for its deep blue color and water clarity.
The Finger Lakes are a group of eleven long, narrow, roughly north to south lakes located in an area called the Finger Lakes region in New York State, in the United States.
The Great Salt Lake is a very large saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere. It lies in the northern part of the state of Utah and has a substantial impact upon the local climate.
Lake Itasca is a glacial lake located in Itasca State Park, in north-central Minnesota, and is the headwater of the Mississippi River.
The Kagera River, also known as Akagera River, or Alexandra Nile, is an East African river, forming part of the upper headwaters of the Nile and carrying water from its far distant source.
Oum Er-Rbia is a large, long and high-throughput river in central Morocco.
The Gambia River is a major river in West Africa, running from the Fouta Djallon plateau in north Guinea westward through Senegal and The Gambia to the Atlantic Ocean at the city of Banjul.
The Volta River is the main river system in the West African country of Ghana. It flows south into Ghana from the Bobo-Dioulasso highlands of Burkina Faso.
Benue River, previously known as the Chadda River or Tchadda, is the major tributary of the Niger River and also is a long river in Nigeria.
The Ogooue, also known as the Nazareth River, is the principal river of Gabon in west-central Africa. Its watershed drains nearly the entire country of Gabon.
The Chambeshi River of northeastern Zambia is the far headstream of the Congo River in length and therefore it is considered the source of the Congo River.

The Kasai River is a left bank tributary of the Congo River, located in Central Africa. The river begins in central Angola and flows to the east until it reaches the border between Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Lualaba River is a river within the Congo River watershed that flows entirely within the eastern part of Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Uele, also known by the phonetically identical Uele, Ouele, or Welle River, is a river in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Great Fish River is a river running through the South African province of the Eastern Cape. It is called great to distinguish it from the Namibian Fish River.

The Jubba River or Juba River is a river in southern Somalia which flows through the region of Jubaland. It begins at the border with Ethiopia, where the Dawa and Ganale Dorya rivers meet, and flows directly south to the Somali Sea.

The Chari River, or Shari River, is a long river, flowing in Central Africa. It is the main source of water of Lake Chad, which is located at the junction of four countries: Nigeria, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon.
The Okavango River is a river in southwestern Africa. It is known by this name in Botswana, as Cubango in Angola, and Kavango in Namibia.

The Omo River in southern Ethiopia is a great Ethiopian river outside the Nile Basin. Its course is entirely contained within the boundaries of Ethiopia, and it empties into Lake Turkana on the border with Kenya.
The Irtysh is a river in Russia, China, and Kazakhstan. It is the chief tributary of the Ob. The river's source lies in the Mongolian Altai in Dzungaria close to the border with Mongolia.

The Angara or Angar is a major river in Siberia, which traces a course through Russia's Irkutsk Oblast and Krasnoyarsk Krai. It drains out of Lake Baikal and is the headwater tributary of the Yenisey.
The Selenga or Selenge is a major river in Mongolia and Buryatia, Russia. Originating from its headwater tributaries, the Ider and the Delger moron, it flows before draining into Lake Baikal.
The Indigirka is a river in the Sakha Republic in Russia between the Yana to the west and the Kolyma to the east.

The Kolyma is a river in northeastern Siberia, whose basin covers parts of the Sakha Republic, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, and Magadan Oblast of Russia. The Kolyma is frozen to depths of several metres for about half the year.

The Songhua or Sunghwa River is one of the primary rivers of China, and a long tributary of the Amur. It flows from Changbai Mountains on the China and North Korea border through China's northeastern Jilin and Heilongjiang provinces.

The Ussuri or Wusuli is a river that runs through Khabarovsk and Primorsky Krais, Russia and the southeast region of Northeast China in the province of Heilongjiang. It rises in the Sikhote-Alin mountain range.
The Tumen River, also known as the Tuman River or Duman River, is a long river that serves as part of the boundary between China, North Korea and Russia, rising on the slopes of Mount Paektu.
The Han River is a major river in South Korea. It flows through the central region of the Korean Peninsula, with some of its tributaries and drainage basin in North Korea.

The Yalu River or Amnok River is a river on the border between China and North Korea. Together with the Tumen River to its east, and a small portion of Paektu Mountain, the Yalu forms the border between China and North Korea.
The Li River or Li Jiang is the name for the upper reaches of the Gui River in northeastern Guangxi, China. It is part of the Xijiang River system in the Pearl River basin.

The Liao River is the principal river in southern Northeast China, and one of the seven main river systems in China. Its name is derived from the Liao region, a historical name for southern Manchuria.
The Hai River, also known as the Peiho, Pei Ho, or Hai Ho, is a Chinese river in Tianjin emptying into the Bohai Sea. Its drainage basin covers much of Hebei, Beijing, and Tianjin.
The Wei River is a major river in west-central China's Gansu and Shaanxi provinces. It is a large tributary of the Yellow River and very important in the early development of Chinese civilization.
The Huai River, formerly romanized as the Hwai, is a major river in East China. It is located about midway between the Yellow River and Yangtze River, two great rivers.
The Han River, also known by its Chinese names Hanjiang and Hanshui, is a major river in Central China. A left tributary of the Yangtze, it is a long tributary of the Yangtze system.

The Jialing River, formerly known by numerous other names, is a major tributary of the Yangtze River in the Sichuan Basin. It is named after the Jialing Valley in Feng County, Shaanxi through which it flows.
The Min River is a long river in central Sichuan province, China. It is a tributary of the upper Yangtze River, which flows through Chengdu and joins at Yibin.
The Xiang River is the chief river of the Lake Dongting drainage system of the middle Yangtze, a large river in Hunan Province, China.
The Dong River is a main tributary of the Pearl River, flowing through Guangdong and Jiangxi in southern China. Its source is Mount Yajibo in Xunwu County in Jiangxi.

The Red River or the Hong River, also known as the Song Cai in Vietnamese and the Yuan River in Chinese, is a river that flows from Yunnan province, in Southwestern China, through northern Vietnam to the Gulf of Tonkin.
The Black River, also known upstream as the Lixian River in China, is a river located in China and northwestern Vietnam.
The Chao Phraya River is the major river in Thailand, with its low alluvial plain forming the centre of the country. It flows through Bangkok and then into the Gulf of Thailand.
The Kapuas River is a river in the Indonesian part of Borneo island, at the geographic center of Maritime Southeast Asia.
The Mahakam River is a long river in Borneo, and is located in East Kalimantan province of Indonesia.

The Yarlung Tsangpo, also called Yarlung Zangbo and Yalu Zangbu River, is the upper course of Brahmaputra River. It flows through the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and Arunachal Pradesh state of India.

Teesta River is a long river that rises in the Pauhunri Mountain of eastern Himalayas, flows through the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal and subsequently enters Bangladesh through Rangpur division.
The Padma is a major river in Bangladesh. It is the eastern and main distributary of the Ganges, flowing generally southeast to its confluence with the Meghna River, near the Bay of Bengal.

The Ghaghara River, called Karnali River in Nepal, Mapcha Tsangpo in Tibet, and Saryu River in India's Awadh, is a perennial trans-boundary river that originates in the northern slopes of the Himalayas in the Tibetan Plateau.
The Kaveri, anglicized as Cauvery, historically known in Tamil as Ponni, is a major river flowing across southern India.
The Narmada River, also known as the Narbada or anglicised as Nerbudda, is a long river in India and a long west-flowing river in the country. It is also a large river in the state of Madhya Pradesh.

The Chenab River is a major river in India and Pakistan, and one of the five major rivers associated with the Punjab region. It is formed by the union of two headwaters, the Chandra and Bhaga, which rise in the upper Himalayas.

The Jhelum River is a major river in South Asia, flowing through India and Pakistan, and is one of the five major rivers of the Punjab region. It originates at Verinag in India-administered Jammu and Kashmir.
The Kabul River is a long river that emerges in the Sanglakh Range of the Hindu Kush mountains in the northeastern part of Maidan Wardak Province, Afghanistan.

The Ravi River is a river in South Asia that flows through northwestern India and eastern Pakistan forming the boundary between the two nations for a stretch. It is one of five major rivers of the Punjab region.
The Shyok River is a major tributary of the Indus River that flows through northern Ladakh in India and into Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan. Originating from the Rimo Glacier in the eastern Karakoram.

The Sutlej River or the Satluj River is a major river in Asia, flowing through China, India and Pakistan, and is a long river of the five major rivers of the Punjab region. It is also known as Satadru, and is a tributary of the Indus River.

The Beas River, anglicized from Vyas River in India, is a river in northwestern India, flowing through the states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab, and is one of the five major rivers of the Punjab region.
The Pechora is a long river in Europe. Flowing from Northwest Russia and into the Arctic Ocean, it lies mainly in the Komi Republic but the northern part crosses the Nenets Autonomous Okrug.
The Northern Dvina is a river in northern Russia flowing through Vologda Oblast and Arkhangelsk Oblast into the Dvina Bay of the White Sea.
The Daugava, also known as the Western Dvina or the Vaina River, is a large river rising in the Valdai Hills of Russia that flows through Belarus and Latvia into the Gulf of Riga of the Baltic Sea.

The Neman, Nemunas in Lithuanian, Niemen in Polish, or Memel in German, is a river in Europe that rises in central Belarus and flows through Lithuania then forms the northern border of Kaliningrad Oblast.
The Oder is a river in Central Europe. It is a long river in Poland and rises in the Czech Republic and flows through western Poland, later forming the border between Poland and Germany.
The Havel is a river in northeastern Germany, flowing through the states of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Brandenburg, Berlin and Saxony-Anhalt. The Havel is a right tributary of the Elbe.
The Meuse or Maas is a major European river, rising in France and flowing through Belgium and the Netherlands before draining into the North Sea from the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt Delta.

The Moselle is a river that rises in the Vosges mountains and flows through north-eastern France and Luxembourg to western Germany. It is a left bank tributary of the Rhine, which it joins at Koblenz.
The Minho or Mino is a long river in the autonomous community of Galicia in Spain. It forms a part of the international border between Spain and Portugal.
The Douro, Duero in Spanish, is a very large river of the Iberian Peninsula by discharge.
The Rhone is a major river in France and Switzerland, rising in the Alps and flowing west and south through Lake Geneva and Southeastern France before discharging into the Mediterranean Sea.
The Ardeche is a river in south-central France, a right-bank tributary of the River Rhone. Its source is in the Massif Central, near the village of Astet.

The Tiber is a long river in Italy and in Central Italy, rising in the Apennine Mountains in Emilia-Romagna and flowing through Tuscany, Umbria, and Lazio, where it is joined by the River Aniene, to the Tyrrhenian Sea.
The Neretva, also known as Narenta, is one of the large rivers of the eastern part of the Adriatic basin.
The Black Drin or Black Drim, is a river in North Macedonia and Albania. It flows out of lake Ohrid in Struga, North Macedonia.
The Iskar is a right tributary of the Danube. It is a long river that runs entirely within Bulgaria, originating as three forks in the Rila mountain range.
The Morava is a river in Central Europe, a left tributary of the Danube. It is the main river of Moravia historical region in the Czech Republic, which derives its name from the river.

The Sava is a river in Central and Southeast Europe, a right-bank and long tributary of the Danube. From its source in Slovenia, it flows through Croatia and along its border with Bosnia and Herzegovina, and finally reaches Serbia.
The Dniester is a transboundary river in Eastern Europe. It runs through Ukraine and then through Moldova, finally discharging into the Black Sea on Ukrainian territory again.
The Kama, also known as the Chulman, is a long river in Russia. It has a large drainage basin.
The Belaya is a river in Bashkortostan, Russia. Its source lies in the south-western Ural Mountains.
The Oka is a river in central Russia, a large right tributary of the Volga. It flows through the regions of Oryol, Tula, Kaluga, Moscow, Ryazan, Vladimir and Nizhny Novgorod.
The Moskva is a river that flows through Western Russia. It rises west of Moscow and flows roughly east through the Smolensk and Moscow Oblasts, passing through central Moscow.
The River Forth is a major river in central Scotland, which drains into the North Sea on the east coast of the country. Its drainage basin covers much of Stirlingshire in Scotland's Central Belt.
The River Shannon is the major river on the island of Ireland and a long river in the British Isles. It drains the Shannon River Basin.
The River Tyne is a river in North East England. It is formed by the North Tyne and the South Tyne, which converge at Warden near Hexham in Northumberland at a place dubbed The Meeting of the Waters.
The Lerma River is a long river in west-central Mexico that begins in the Mexican Plateau and ends where it empties into Lake Chapala.
The Usumacinta River is a river in southeastern Mexico and northwestern Guatemala. It is formed by the junction of the Pasion River and the Salinas River.
The Pecos River originates in north-central New Mexico and flows into Texas, emptying into the Rio Grande.
The Brazos River, called the Rio de los Brazos de Dios, meaning The River of the Arms of God, by early Spanish explorers, is a long river in the United States.
The Arkansas River is a major tributary of the Mississippi River. It generally flows to the east and southeast as it traverses the states of Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Arkansas.
The Canadian River is a long tributary of the Arkansas River. Entirely within the United States, it starts in Colorado and travels through New Mexico, the Texas Panhandle, and Oklahoma.
The Atchafalaya River is a distributary of the Mississippi River and Red River in south central Louisiana in the United States. It flows south, just west of the Mississippi River.
The Red River is a major river in the Southern United States. It was named for its reddish water color from passing through red-bed country in its watershed.

The Platte River is a major river in the state of Nebraska. It is about three hundred ten miles long, and measured to its distant source via its tributary, the North Platte River, it flows much further.
The North Platte River is a major tributary of the Platte River. It flows through the states of Colorado, Wyoming, and Nebraska.
The Yellowstone River is a tributary of the Missouri River, in the Western United States. Considered the principal tributary of the upper Missouri, via its own tributaries it drains a wide area.
The Cumberland River is a major waterway of the Southern United States. The river drains southern Kentucky and north-central Tennessee.

The Tennessee River is a river located in the southeastern United States. Flowing through the Tennessee Valley in the states of Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, and Kentucky, it begins at the confluence of French Broad and Holston rivers.
The James River is a river in Virginia that begins in the Appalachian Mountains and flows from the confluence of the Cowpasture and Jackson Rivers in Botetourt County to the Chesapeake Bay.
The Potomac River is in the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States and flows from the Potomac Highlands in West Virginia to the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland.
The Susquehanna River is a major river located in the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States, crossing three lower Northeast states: New York, Pennsylvania and Maryland.
The Delaware River is a major river in the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States and is a long free-flowing, undammed river in the Eastern United States.

The Hudson River is a river that flows from north to south largely through eastern New York state. It originates in the Adirondack Mountains at Henderson Lake in the town of Newcomb, and flows south to New York Bay.
The Saint John River is a river flowing from headwaters in the Notre Dame Mountains near the Maine and Quebec border through northern Maine and western New Brunswick to the Bay of Fundy.
The Niagara River flows north from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, forming part of the border between Ontario, Canada, to the west, and New York, United States, to the east.
The Ottawa River is a river in the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec. It is named after the Algonquin word to trade, as it was the major trade route of Eastern Canada at the time.
The Saguenay River is a major river of Quebec, Canada. Draining Lac Saint-Jean in the Laurentian Highlands, it leaves Alma and runs east.
The Churchill River, formerly known by other names, is a river in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. It flows east from the Smallwood Reservoir into the Atlantic Ocean via Lake Melville.
The Nelson River is a river of north-central North America, in the Canadian province of Manitoba. The river drains Lake Winnipeg before it ends in Hudson Bay near Port Nelson.
The Red River, also called the Red River of the North to differentiate it from the Red River in the south of the continent, is a river in the north-central United States and the Canadian Prairies.

The White River is a river that flows through the states of Arkansas and Missouri. Originating in the Boston Mountains of northwest Arkansas, it arcs northwards through southern Missouri before turning back into Arkansas.
The Connecticut River is a major river in the New England region of the United States. It is the long river of the region, flowing roughly southward through four states.
The Saskatchewan River is a major river in Canada. It is formed by the joining of the North Saskatchewan River and South Saskatchewan River just east of Prince Albert, Saskatchewan.
The Churchill River is a major river in Saskatchewan and Manitoba, Canada. It is a long river running from the head of the Churchill Lake.
The Slave River is a Canadian river that flows from the confluence of the Riviere des Rochers and Peace River in northeastern Alberta and runs into Great Slave Lake in the Northwest Territories.
The Athabasca River in Alberta, Canada, originates at the Columbia Icefield in Jasper National Park and flows a long way before emptying into Lake Athabasca.
The Tanana River is a tributary of the Yukon River in the state of Alaska.
The Kuskokwim River or Kusko River is a long river in Southwest Alaska in the United States.

The Fraser River is a long river within British Columbia, Canada, rising at Fraser Pass near Blackrock Mountain in the Rocky Mountains and flowing into the Strait of Georgia just south of the City of Vancouver.
The Gila River is a tributary of the Colorado River flowing through New Mexico and Arizona in the United States. The river drains an arid watershed.

The Green River is a long river located in the western states of Wyoming, Utah, and Colorado. The chief tributary of the Colorado River, its watershed, the Green River Basin, begins in the Wind River Range of Wyoming.
The Kootenay River or Kootenai River is a major river of the Northwest Plateau in southeastern British Columbia, Canada, and northern Montana and Idaho in the United States.
The Snake River is a major river in the interior Pacific Northwest region of the United States. It is a large tributary of the Columbia River.

The Willamette River is a major tributary of the Columbia River, accounting for a good share of the Columbia's flow. The Willamette's main stem lies entirely in northwestern Oregon in the United States.

The Sacramento River is the principal river of Northern California in the United States and is a large river in California. Rising in the Klamath Mountains, the river flows south before reaching the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta.

The San Joaquin River is a long river of Central California. The river starts in the high Sierra Nevada and flows through the rich agricultural region of the northern San Joaquin Valley before reaching Suisun Bay.
The Cooper Creek is a river in the Australian states of Queensland and South Australia. It was the site of the death of the explorers Burke and Wills.
The Darling River is a long river in Australia, from its source in northern New South Wales to its confluence with the Murray River at Wentworth.

The Paroo River, a series of waterholes, connected in wet weather as a running stream of the Darling catchment within the Murray-Darling basin, is located in the South West region of Queensland and Far West region of New South Wales, Australia.

The Warrego River is an intermittent river that is part of the Darling catchment within the Murray-Darling basin, which is located in South West Queensland and in the Orana region of New South Wales, Australia.
The Murrumbidgee River is a major tributary of the Murray River within the Murray-Darling basin and a long river in Australia.

The Lachlan River is an intermittent river that is part of the Murrumbidgee catchment within the Murray-Darling basin, located in the Southern Tablelands, Central West, and Riverina regions of New South Wales, Australia.
The Franklin River is a major perennial river located in the Central Highlands and western regions of Tasmania, Australia. The river is located in the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park.
The Fly River is a long river on the island of New Guinea. It is a very large river by volume of discharge in Oceania.
The Mamberamo is a long river on the island of New Guinea and a large river in Oceania by discharge volume. It is located in the Indonesian province of Papua.

The Sepik is a long river on the island of New Guinea, and a large river in Oceania by discharge volume. The majority of the river flows through the Papua New Guinea provinces of Sandaun and East Sepik.

The Waikato River is a long river in New Zealand, running through the North Island. It starts on the eastern slopes of Mount Ruapehu, joining the Tongariro River system and flowing through Lake Taupo.

The Casiquiare river or canal is a natural distributary of the upper Orinoco flowing southward into the Rio Negro in Venezuela. As such, it forms a unique natural canal between the Orinoco and Amazon river systems.
The Japura River or Caqueta River is a long river in the Amazon basin. It rises in Colombia and flows eastward through Brazil to join the Amazon River.
The Maranon River is the principal or mainstem source of the Amazon River, arising northeast of Lima, Peru, and flowing northwest across high plateaus.
The Purus River is a tributary of the Amazon River in South America.
The Tapajos is a river in Brazil. It runs through the Amazon rainforest and is a major tributary of the Amazon River.
The Tocantins River is a river in Brazil, the central fluvial artery of the country. In the Tupi language, its name means toucan's beak.

The Ucayali River is the main headstream of the Amazon River. It rises north of Lake Titicaca, in the Arequipa region of Peru and becomes the Amazon at the confluence of the Maranon close to Nauta city.
The Apurimac River rises from glacial meltwater of the ridge of the Mismi, a high mountain in the Arequipa Province in the south-western mountain ranges of Peru.
The Xingu River is a river in north Brazil. It is a southeast tributary of the Amazon River and one of the large clearwater rivers in the Amazon basin.
The Paraguay River is a major river in south-central South America, running through Brazil and Paraguay and forming parts of the Paraguay-Argentina, Brazil-Bolivia and Brazil-Paraguay borders.

The Peace River is a long river in Canada that originates in the Rocky Mountains of northern British Columbia and flows to the northeast through northern Alberta. The Peace River joins the Athabasca River in the Peace-Athabasca Delta.
The Bab al-Mandab Strait is a strait and global chokepoint between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in the Horn of Africa, connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
The Bungo Channel is a strait separating the Japanese islands of Kyushu and Shikoku. It connects the Philippine Sea and the Seto Inland Sea on the western end of Shikoku.
Davis Strait is a southern arm of the Arctic Ocean that lies north of the Labrador Sea. It lies between mid-western Greenland and Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada.

The Straits of Florida, Florida Straits, or Florida Strait is a strait located south-southeast of the North American mainland, generally accepted to be between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean.
The Strait of Georgia or the Georgia Strait is an arm of the Salish Sea between Vancouver Island and the extreme southwestern mainland coast of British Columbia, Canada.
The Hudson Strait in Nunavut links the Atlantic Ocean and the Labrador Sea to Hudson Bay in Canada. This strait lies between Baffin Island and Nunavik.
The Strait of Juan de Fuca is a body of water that is the Salish Sea's main outlet to the Pacific Ocean. The international boundary between Canada and the United States runs along it.
The Kanmon Straits or the Straits of Shimonoseki is the stretch of water separating Honshu and Kyushu, two of Japan's four main islands.
The Lombok Strait is a strait of the Bali Sea connecting to the Indian Ocean, and is located between the islands of Bali and Lombok in Indonesia. The Gili Islands are on the Lombok side.

The Strait of Messina is a narrow strait between the eastern tip of Sicily and the western tip of Calabria in Southern Italy. It connects the Tyrrhenian Sea to the north with the Ionian Sea to the south.
Oresund, commonly known in English as the Sound, is a strait which forms the Danish-Swedish border, separating Zealand from Scania.
The Strait of Otranto connects the Adriatic Sea with the Ionian Sea and separates Italy from Albania.

La Perouse Strait, or Soya Strait, is a strait dividing the southern part of the Russian island of Sakhalin from the northern part of the Japanese island of Hokkaido, and connecting the Sea of Japan on the west with the Sea of Okhotsk.

The Qiongzhou Strait, also called the Hainan Strait, is the Chinese strait that separates Guangdong's Leizhou Peninsula from the island province of Hainan. It connects the Gulf of Tonkin on its west to the South China Sea on its east.

The Singapore Strait is a long, narrow strait between the Strait of Malacca in the west and the South China Sea in the east. Singapore is on the north of the channel, and the Indonesian Riau Islands are on the south.
The Sunda Strait is the strait between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra. It connects the Java Sea with the Indian Ocean.
Surigao Strait is a strait in the southern Philippines, between the Bohol Sea and Leyte Gulf of the Philippine Sea.
The Strait of Tartary, Gulf of Tartary, or Mamiya Strait is a strait in the Pacific Ocean dividing the Russian island of Sakhalin from mainland Asia, connecting the Sea of Okhotsk on the north.
The Torres Strait, also known as Zenadh Kes, is a strait between Australia and the Melanesian island of New Guinea.
The Tsugaru Strait is a strait between Honshu and Hokkaido in northern Japan connecting the Sea of Japan with the Pacific Ocean. It was named after the western part of Aomori Prefecture.
The Uraga Channel is a waterway connecting Tokyo Bay to the Sagami Gulf. It is an important channel for ships headed from Tokyo, Yokohama, and Chiba to the Pacific Ocean and beyond.
The Yucatan Channel or the Straits of Yucatan is a strait between Mexico and Cuba. It connects the Yucatan Basin of the Caribbean Sea with the Gulf of Mexico.
The Albert Canal is a canal located in northeastern Belgium, which was named for King Albert of Belgium. The Albert Canal connects Antwerp with Liege, and also the Meuse river with the Scheldt river.
The Amsterdam-Rhine Canal is a canal in the Netherlands that was built to connect the port and capital city of Amsterdam to the main shipping artery of the Rhine.

The Bridgewater Canal connects Runcorn, Manchester and Leigh, in North West England. It was commissioned by Francis Egerton, Duke of Bridgewater, to transport coal from his mines in Worsley to Manchester.
Bydgoszcz Canal is a canal between the cities of Bydgoszcz and Naklo nad Notecia in Poland. It connects the Vistula river with the Oder river, through the Brda and Notec rivers.

The Caledonian Canal connects the Scottish east coast at Inverness with the west coast at Corpach near Fort William in Scotland. The canal was constructed in the early nineteenth century by Scottish engineer Thomas Telford.
The Cape Cod Canal is an artificial waterway in Massachusetts connecting Cape Cod Bay in the north to Buzzards Bay in the south, and is part of the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway.
The Chambly Canal is a National Historic Site of Canada in the Province of Quebec, running along the Richelieu River past Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Carignan, and Chambly.
The Chesapeake and Delaware Canal is a wide and deep ship canal that connects the Delaware River with the Chesapeake Bay in the states of Delaware and Maryland in the United States.
The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, occasionally called the Grand Old Ditch, operated along the Potomac River between Washington, D.C., and Cumberland, Maryland. It replaced the Patowmack Canal.
The Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal, historically known as the Chicago Drainage Canal, is a canal system that connects the Chicago River to the Des Plaines River in Northeast Illinois.

The Corinth Canal is a canal in Greece that connects the Gulf of Corinth in the Ionian Sea with the Saronic Gulf in the Aegean Sea. It cuts through the narrow Isthmus of Corinth and separates the Peloponnese peninsula from the Greek mainland.
The Danube-Black Sea Canal is a navigable canal in Romania, which runs from Cernavoda on the Danube river, via two branches, to Constanta and Navodari on the Black Sea.
The Dortmund-Ems Canal is a long canal in Germany between the inland port of the city of Dortmund and the seaport of Emden.

The Elbe-Lubeck Canal is an artificial waterway in eastern Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. It connects the rivers Elbe and Trave, creating an inland water route across the drainage divide from the North Sea to the Baltic Sea.
The Gota Canal is a Swedish canal constructed in the early nineteenth century. Part of it was dug or blasted, and it is narrow and shallow.

The Great Man-Made River Project is a network of pipes that supplies fresh water obtained from the Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System, a fossil aquifer, across Libya. It is a very large irrigation project.
The Red Flag Canal is an irrigation canal located northwest of Anyang in the northern extremity of Henan, China.

The Houston Ship Channel, in Houston, Texas, is part of the Port of Houston, a busy seaport in the world. The channel is the conduit for ocean-going vessels between Houston-area terminals and the Gulf of Mexico.

The Karakum Canal in Turkmenistan is one of the large irrigation and water supply canals in the world. Started in nineteen fifty-four, and completed in nineteen fifty-eight, it is navigable over much of its length.

Khlong Saen Saep is a canal in central Thailand, connecting the Chao Phraya River to Prachinburi Province and Chachoengsao. A portion of the canal is used for public transport by an express boat service in Bangkok.
The Buckingham Canal is a long fresh water navigation canal, that parallels the Coromandel Coast of South India from Kakinada of Andhra Pradesh to Pichavaram near Chidambaram of Tamil Nadu.
The Leidsevaart, also known as Leidse trekvaart, Dutch for Leiden's Pull-Canal, is a canal between the cities of Haarlem and Leiden in the Netherlands. It is one of the old canals in the Netherlands.

The Lingqu is a canal in Xing'an County, near Guilin, in the northwestern corner of Guangxi, China. It connects the Xiang River, which flows north into the Yangtze, with the Li River, which flows south.
The Manchester Ship Canal is an inland waterway in North West England that links Manchester to the Irish Sea.

The Canal du Midi is a long canal in Southern France. Originally named the Canal Royal en Languedoc and renamed by French revolutionaries to Canal du Midi, the canal is considered one of the great feats of civil engineering.

The Mittelland Canal, also known as the Midland Canal, is a major canal in central Germany. It forms an important link in the waterway network of the country, providing the principal east-west inland waterway connection.
The Moscow Canal, named the Moskva-Volga Canal until nineteen forty-seven, is a canal in Russia that connects the River Moskva with the Volga.
The New York State Canal System, formerly known as the New York State Barge Canal, is a successor to the Erie Canal and other canals within New York.
The North Jiangsu Main Irrigation Canal, often called the Subei Canal, is located in the lower reaches of the Huai River, one of the major rivers in the north of Jiangsu Province, China.
The Rhine-Main-Danube Canal is a canal in Bavaria, Germany. Connecting the Main and the Danube rivers across the European watershed, it runs from Bamberg via Nuremberg to Kelheim.
The Rideau Canal is a long canal that links the Ottawa River at Ottawa with the Cataraqui River and Lake Ontario at Kingston, Ontario, Canada.
The Stecknitz Canal was an artificial waterway in northern Germany which connected Lauenburg and Lubeck on the Old Salt Route by linking the tiny rivers Stecknitz and Delvenau.
The Trollhatte Canal is a canal in Sweden. Trollhatte Canal connects the Gota river with the lake Vanern.
Lenin Volga-Don Shipping Canal is a ship canal in Russia. It connects the Volga and the Don where they come near each other.

The Welland Canal is a ship canal in Ontario, Canada, and part of the St. Lawrence Seaway and Great Lakes Waterway. The canal traverses the Niagara Peninsula between Port Weller on Lake Ontario and Port Colborne on Lake Erie.
The Guarani Aquifer is a very large known aquifer system in the world and is an important source of fresh water. Located beneath the parts of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

The Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System is a very large known fossil water aquifer system. It is located underground in the eastern end of the Sahara desert and spans the political boundaries of four countries in northeastern Africa.
The Ogallala Aquifer is a shallow water table aquifer surrounded by sand, silt, clay, and gravel located beneath the Great Plains in the United States.
Geysir, sometimes known as The Great Geysir, is a geyser in south-western Iceland. The English word geyser, a periodically spouting hot spring, derives from Geysir.
Old Faithful is a cone geyser in Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming, United States. It was named in eighteen seventy during the Washburn-Langford-Doane Expedition.
Steamboat Geyser, in Yellowstone National Park's Norris Geyser Basin, is a very tall active geyser. Steamboat Geyser has two vents, northern and southern.
Strokkur is a fountain-type geyser located in a geothermal area beside the Hvita River in Iceland in the southwest part of the country, east of Reykjavik.
Waiotapu, Maori for sacred waters, is an active geothermal area at the southern end of the Okataina Volcanic Centre, just north of the Reporoa caldera, in New Zealand's Taupo Volcanic Zone.
Whakarewarewa is a semi-rural geothermal area in Rotorua, New Zealand. Its name means the gathering place for the war parties of Wahiao.

Dallol is a terrestrial hydrothermal system around a cinder cone volcano in the Danakil Depression, northeast of the Erta Ale Range in Ethiopia. It is known for its unearthly colors and mineral patterns.
The Aletsch Glacier or Great Aletsch Glacier is a very large glacier in the Alps.
The Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf or Ronne-Filchner Ice Shelf is an Antarctic ice shelf bordering the Weddell Sea.
