The Ross Ice Shelf is a very large ice shelf of Antarctica, about the size of France. It is several hundred metres thick.

The Arctic ice pack is the sea ice cover of the Arctic Ocean and its vicinity. The Arctic ice pack undergoes a regular seasonal cycle in which ice melts in spring and summer, reaches a minimum around mid-September, then increases during autumn and winter.

The Columbia Icefield is a very large ice field in North America's Rocky Mountains. Located within the Canadian Rocky Mountains astride the Continental Divide along the border of British Columbia and Alberta, Canada.
The Fedchenko Glacier or the Vanch-Yakh Glacier is a large glacier in the Yazgulem Range, Pamir Mountains, of north-central Gorno-Badakhshan province, Tajikistan. The glacier is long and narrow.
The Franz Josef Glacier is a temperate maritime glacier in Westland Tai Poutini National Park on the West Coast of New Zealand's South Island.
Gangotri glacier is located in Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand, India in a region bordering Tibet. This glacier is one of the primary sources of the Ganges.
Jostedal Glacier or Jostedalsbreen is a very large glacier in continental Europe. It is in Vestland county in Western Norway.
The Malaspina Glacier in southeastern Alaska is a very large piedmont glacier. Situated at the head of the Alaska Panhandle.
Nabesna Glacier is a glacier in the state of Alaska. Fed by deep snowfall in the Wrangell Mountains, the Nabesna is a very long valley glacier in North America.
The Perito Moreno, Francisco Gormaz or Bismarck Glacier is a glacier located in Los Glaciares National Park in southwest Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
The Siachen Glacier is a glacier located in the eastern Karakoram range of the Himalayas, in Indian-administered Ladakh.
Tasman Glacier is a very large glacier in New Zealand, and one of several large glaciers which flow south and east towards the Mackenzie Basin from the Southern Alps in New Zealand's South Island.
Vatnajokull is a very large and voluminous ice cap in Iceland, in the south-east of the island.

Fontaine-de-Vaucluse is a commune in the southeastern French department of Vaucluse. Its name comes from the spring of the same name; the name Vaucluse itself comes from the Latin phrase vallis clausa or closed valley.

Gihon Spring or Fountain of the Virgin, also known as Saint Mary's Pool, is a spring in the Kidron Valley. It was the main source of water for the Pool of Siloam in Jebus and the later City of David, the original site of Jerusalem.
The Amazon Delta is a vast river delta formed by the Amazon River and the Tocantins River in northern South America.

The Ganges Delta, also known the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, the Sundarbans Delta or the Bengal Delta, is a river delta predominantly covering the Bengal region of the Indian subcontinent, consisting of Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.
The Red River Delta, or Hong River Delta, is the flat low-lying plain formed by the Red River and its distributaries that merges with the Thai Binh River in northern Vietnam.

The Mekong Delta, also known as the South-western Region or the Western Region, is the region in southwestern Vietnam where the Mekong River approaches and empties into the sea through a network of distributaries.
The Mississippi River Delta is the confluence of the Mississippi River with the Gulf of Mexico in Louisiana, southeastern United States.
The Nile Delta is the delta formed in Lower Egypt where the Nile River spreads out and drains into the Mediterranean Sea. It is one of the large deltas of the world.
The Volga Delta is a very large river delta in Europe and occurs where the Volga River drains into the Caspian Sea in Russia's Astrakhan Oblast, north-east of the republic of Kalmykia.
The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs straddling the coast of Belize, offshore from the country.
The Central Indian Ridge is a north-south-trending mid-ocean ridge in the western Indian Ocean.

Doggerland was a large area of land in Northern Europe, now submerged beneath the southern North Sea. This region was repeatedly exposed at various times during the Pleistocene epoch due to the lowering of sea levels during glacial periods.
The East Pacific Rise is a mid-ocean rise at a divergent tectonic plate boundary, located along the floor of the Pacific Ocean.
The Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain is a mostly undersea mountain range in the Pacific Ocean that reaches above sea level in Hawaii.
The Izu-Bonin-Mariana arc system is a tectonic plate convergent boundary in Micronesia. The arc system extends south from Tokyo, Japan, to beyond Guam.

The Challenger Deep is a very deep known point of the seabed of Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean at the southern end of the Mariana Trench, in the ocean territory of the Federated States of Micronesia.
The Nankai Trough is a submarine trough located south of the Nankaido region of Japan's island of Honshu. The underlying fault, the Nankai megathrust, is the source of devastating earthquakes.
The Pacific-Antarctic Ridge is a divergent tectonic plate boundary located on the seafloor of the South Pacific Ocean, separating the Pacific plate from the Antarctic plate.
The Peru-Chile Trench, also known as the Atacama Trench, is an oceanic trench in the eastern Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Peru and Chile.
The Philippine Trench, also called the Philippine Deep, Mindanao Trench, and the Mindanao Deep, is a submarine trench to the east of the Philippines.
The Southwest Indian Ridge is a mid-ocean ridge located along the floors of the south-west Indian Ocean and south-east Atlantic Ocean.
The Augrabies Falls is a waterfall on the Orange River, a great river in South Africa. The waterfall, set in a desolate and rugged milieu, is enclosed by the Augrabies Falls National Park.
Ban Gioc-Detian Falls or Ban Gioc Falls is a collective name for two waterfalls on the Quay Son River that straddle the international border between China and Vietnam.
Celilo Falls was a tribal fishing area on the Columbia River, just east of the Cascade Mountains, on what is today the border between the states of Oregon and Washington.
Dettifoss is a waterfall in Vatnajokull National Park in Northeast Iceland, and is reputed to be a very powerful waterfall in Europe.

Hammam Maskhoutine is a thermal complex located in Hammam Debagh, of Guelma Province, Algeria. The dramatic, multicolored travertine walls of the spring have attracted attention from locals and tourists alike.

Helmcken Falls is a waterfall on the Murtle River within Wells Gray Provincial Park in British Columbia, Canada. The protection of Helmcken Falls was one of the reasons for the creation of Wells Gray Provincial Park.
Kaieteur Falls is one of the powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world. It is located on the Potaro River in Kaieteur National Park, central Essequibo Territory, Guyana.
The Khone Falls and Pha Pheng Falls together form a waterfall located in Champasak Province on the Mekong River in southern Laos, near the border with Cambodia.

Lofoi Falls, also known as Chutes Kaloba and Chutes Lofoi, is a waterfall in Kundelungu National Park, Haut-Katanga Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Plunging down for an unbroken drop, it is one of the high waterfalls in Africa.
Maletsunyane Falls is a high waterfall in the Southern African country Lesotho. It is located near the town of Semonkong, which is also named after the falls.
Mardalsfossen is a waterfall in Molde Municipality in More og Romsdal county, Norway. It is sometimes referred to as one of the tall waterfalls in Europe.
Multnomah Falls is a waterfall located on Multnomah Creek in the Columbia River Gorge, east of Troutdale, between Corbett and Dodson, Oregon, United States.
Saint Anthony Falls, or the Falls of Saint Anthony, located at the northeastern edge of downtown Minneapolis, Minnesota, was a natural major waterfall on the Mississippi River.
Shivanasamudra Falls is a series of segmented waterfalls on the Kaveri river. It is situated in Malavalli taluk in Mandya district, Karnataka.
Sutherland Falls is a waterfall near Milford Sound in New Zealand's South Island.
Vøringsfossen or Vøringen, in English Vøring Falls, is a high waterfall in Norway. It lies at the top of the Måbødalen valley in Eidfjord Municipality in Vestland county.
Yosemite Falls is a high waterfall in Yosemite National Park, dropping from the top of the upper fall to the base of the lower fall. Located in the Sierra Nevada of California.
The Continental Divide of the Americas is the principal, and largely mountainous, hydrological divide of the Americas. The Continental Divide extends from the Bering Strait to the Strait of Magellan.
The Chad Basin is a large endorheic basin in Africa, centered approximately on Lake Chad. It has no outlet to the sea and contains large areas of semi-arid desert and savanna.

The Great Basin is a large area of contiguous endorheic watersheds, those with no outlets to the ocean, in North America. It spans nearly all of Nevada, much of Utah, and portions of California, Idaho, Oregon, Wyoming, and Baja California.
The Junggar Basin, also known as the Dzungarian Basin or Zungarian Basin, is one of the large sedimentary basins in Northwest China. It is located in Dzungaria in northern Xinjiang.
The Ordos Plateau, also known as the Ordos Basin, the Ordos, or the Shaan-Gan-Ning Basin, is a highland sedimentary basin in parts of northernmost China.

The Sistan Basin is an inland endorheic basin encompassing parts of southwestern Afghanistan and parts of southeastern Iran. It is one of the dry regions in the world and an area subject to prolonged droughts.
The Tarim Basin is an endorheic basin in Xinjiang, Northwestern China, and a very large basin in Northwest China. Located in China's Xinjiang region.
The Western Plateau is a very large drainage division of Australia and is composed predominantly of the remains of the ancient rock shield of Gondwana. It covers two thirds of the continent.
Uvs Lake Basin is an endorheic basin located on the territorial border of Mongolia and Russia. The basin is part of the Central Asian Internal Drainage Basin and is named after Uvs Lake.
The Camargue is a coastal region in southern France located south of the city of Arles, between the Mediterranean Sea and the two arms of the Rhone river delta.
The Darien Gap is a remote, roadless, and dangerous area of rainforest on the international border between Colombia and Panama.

The Great Dismal Swamp is a large swamp in the Coastal Plain Region of southeastern Virginia and northeastern North Carolina in the Eastern United States, between Norfolk, Virginia, and Elizabeth City, North Carolina.

The Kerala backwaters are a network of brackish lagoons and canals running parallel to the Arabian Sea along the Malabar Coast of Kerala, India. It also includes interconnected lakes, rivers, and inlets.
The Pantanal is a natural region encompassing a very large tropical wetland area, and a very large area of flooded grasslands. It is located mostly within the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul.
The Sudd is a vast swamp in South Sudan, formed by the White Nile's Bahr al-Jabal section. The Arabic word sudd is derived from sadd, meaning barrier or obstruction.

The Fens or Fenlands in eastern England are a naturally marshy region supporting a rich ecology and numerous species. The fens were drained centuries ago, resulting in a flat, dry, low-lying agricultural region.
The Vasyugan Swamp, also called the Great Vasyugan Mire, is a very large swamp in the northern hemisphere as well as a very large peatland. It is located in Russia, in southwestern Siberia.
Ascension Island is an isolated volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean, a short way south of the Equator, far from both the coast of Africa and the coast of South America.
The Cameroon line is a long chain of volcanoes that includes islands in the Gulf of Guinea and mountains on the African mainland, running from Mount Cameroon on the coast towards Lake Chad.
Bioko is an island of Equatorial Guinea, lying off the coast of Cameroon. Malabo, on the north coast of the island, is the former capital city of Equatorial Guinea.
Fuerteventura is one of the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic Ocean, geographically part of Macaronesia, and politically part of Spain. It lies close to the coast of North Africa.
Gran Canaria, also Grand Canary Island, is a populous island of the Canary Islands, a Spanish archipelago off the Atlantic coast of Northwest Africa.
Lanzarote is a Spanish island of the Canary Islands, off the north coast of Africa and far from the Iberian Peninsula.

La Palma, also known as La isla bonita and historically San Miguel de La Palma, is an island of the Canary Islands, a Spanish autonomous community and archipelago in Macaronesia in the North Atlantic Ocean.
Tenerife is a large and populous island of the Canary Islands, an autonomous community of Spain, located in the Atlantic Ocean off the northwestern coast of Africa.

Gough Island, also known historically as Gonçalo Álvares, is a rugged volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is a dependency of Tristan da Cunha and part of the British overseas territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha.
Saint Helena is a volcanic tropical island located in the South Atlantic Ocean, west of Africa. Angola and Namibia are the neighbouring countries geographically.
Santiago is a large island of Cape Verde, its important agricultural centre and home to half the nation's population. Part of the Sotavento Islands, it lies between the islands of Maio and Fogo.
Santo Antão, Portuguese for Saint Anthony, is the northwesternmost island of Cape Verde. It is a large island of the Barlavento Islands group.

Tristan da Cunha, colloquially known as Tristan, is a remote group of volcanic islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is one of three constituent parts of the British Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, with its own constitution.

Djerba, also transliterated as Jerba or Jarbah, is a Tunisian island and one of the large islands of North Africa, in the Gulf of Gabès, off the coast of Tunisia. Administratively, it is part of the Medenine Governorate.
Agaléga is a dependency of Mauritius, as defined by the Constitution of Mauritius, which consists of two outer islands located in the Indian Ocean, far north of Mauritius Island.
Aldabra, a very large coral atoll, is located east of the continent of Africa. It is part of the Aldabra Group of islands in the Indian Ocean that are part of the Outer Islands of the Seychelles.
The Amirante Islands, Les Amirantes, are a group of coral islands and atolls that belong to the Outer Islands of the Seychelles.

The Comoro Islands are a group of volcanic islands in the Mozambique Channel, an arm of the Indian Ocean lying between Madagascar and the African mainland. Three of the islands form the Union of the Comoros, a sovereign nation, while Mayotte belongs to France.

The Island of Mozambique, Ilha de Moçambique in Portuguese, lies off northern Mozambique, between the Mozambique Channel and Mossuril Bay, and is part of Nampula Province. Before eighteen ninety-eight, it was the capital of colonial Portuguese East Africa.

The Mascarene Islands, or Mascarenes or Mascarenhas Archipelago, is a group of islands in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar consisting of islands belonging to the Republic of Mauritius as well as the French department of Réunion.

Rodrigues is an autonomous outer island of the Republic of Mauritius, far to the east of the main island of Mauritius. Along with the French overseas department of Réunion, Rodrigues and Mauritius are part of the Mascarene Islands.
Tromelin Island, once called the Isle of Sand, is a low, flat island in the Indian Ocean north of Réunion and east of Madagascar. Both France and Mauritius claim sovereignty over the island.
The Zanzibar Archipelago is a group of islands off the coast of mainland Tanzania in the Sea of Zanj. The archipelago is also known as the Spice Islands.
The Dahlak Archipelago is an Eritrean island group located in the Red Sea, lying east of Massawa, the regional capital city.

Bouvet Island is an uninhabited subantarctic volcanic island and dependency of Norway. A protected nature reserve situated in the South Atlantic Ocean at the southern end of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, it is a very remote island.
Campbell Island, Motu Ihupuku, is an uninhabited subantarctic island of New Zealand, and the main island of the Campbell Island group. The island lies far south of New Zealand's South Island.
The Crozet Islands are a sub-Antarctic archipelago of small islands in the southern Indian Ocean. They form one of the five administrative districts of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

Île Amsterdam, also known as Amsterdam Island or New Amsterdam, is an island of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands in the southern Indian Ocean that together with neighbouring Île Saint-Paul forms one of the five districts of the territory.
The Kerguelen Islands, also known as the Desolation Islands, are a group of islands in the subantarctic region. They are among the isolated places on Earth.

The Territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands is an Australian external territory in the southern Indian Ocean. Discovered in the mid-nineteenth century, the territory is a group of sub-Antarctic volcanic islands that lie on the Kerguelen Plateau.
James Ross Island is a large island off the southeast side and near the northeastern extremity of the Antarctic Peninsula, from which it is separated by Prince Gustav Channel.
Peter I Island is an uninhabited volcanic island in the Bellingshausen Sea, far from continental Antarctica. It is claimed as a dependency of Norway.

The Prince Edward Islands are two small uninhabited subantarctic volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean that are administered by South Africa. They are named Marion Island and Prince Edward Island.
South Georgia is an island in the South Atlantic Ocean that is part of the British Overseas Territory of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. It lies far east of the Falkland Islands.

The South Sandwich Islands are a chain of uninhabited volcanic islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. They are administered as part of the British Overseas Territory of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.
The South Orkney Islands are a group of islands in the Southern Ocean, north-east of the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula and south-west of South Georgia Island.
The South Shetland Islands are a group of Antarctic islands located in the Drake Passage. They lie north of the Antarctic Peninsula.

Deception Island is in the South Shetland Islands close to the Antarctic Peninsula with a large and usually safe natural harbour, which is occasionally affected by the underlying active volcano. This island is the caldera of an active volcano.
Livingston Island is an Antarctic island in the Southern Ocean, part of the South Shetlands Archipelago, a group of Antarctic islands north of the Antarctic Peninsula.
Elephant Island is an ice-covered, mountainous island off the coast of Antarctica in the outer reaches of the South Shetland Islands, in the Southern Ocean.
Thurston Island is a largely ice-covered, glacially dissected island lying between Amundsen Sea and Bellingshausen Sea a short way off the northwest end of Ellsworth Land, Antarctica.
Diego Garcia is a coral atoll in the central Indian Ocean, a large atoll in the south of the Chagos Archipelago. Its nearly continuous, V-shaped rim of land almost encloses a lagoon.

Lakshadweep is a union territory of India. It is an archipelago of islands divided into three island subgroups: the Amindivi Islands in the north, the Laccadive Islands, and the atoll of Minicoy to the south.
The Maldives consists of natural atolls, along with a few islands and isolated reefs stretching from north of the Equator to just south of it.

The Andaman Islands are an archipelago, made up of two hundred islands, in the northeastern Indian Ocean southwest off the coasts of Myanmar. Together with the Nicobar Islands to their south, the Andamans serve as a maritime boundary.

North Sentinel Island is one of the Andaman Islands, an Indian archipelago in the Bay of Bengal. A protected area of India, it is home to the Sentinelese, an uncontacted indigenous tribe who have defended their protected isolation.

The Nicobar Islands are an archipelagic island chain in the eastern Indian Ocean. They are located in Southeast Asia, northwest of Aceh on Sumatra, and separated from Thailand to the east by the Andaman Sea.
Langkawi, officially known as Langkawi, the Jewel of Kedah, is a duty-free island and an archipelago of islands located off the coast of Malaysia in the Strait of Malacca.
Santa Maria is an island in the eastern group of the Azores archipelago, south of the island of São Miguel. The island is known for its white sand beaches, distinctive chimneys, and dry warm weather.
São Miguel Island, nicknamed The Green Island, Ilha Verde, is a large and populous island in the Portuguese archipelago of the Azores.
Faial Island, also known as Fayal Island, is a Portuguese island contained within the Central Group, or Grupo Central, of the Azores, in the Atlantic Ocean.

Pico Island is an island in the Central Group of the Portuguese Azores. The landscape features an eponymous volcano, Ponta do Pico, which is the high point of Portugal, the Azores, and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

São Jorge is an island in the central group of the Azores archipelago and part of the autonomous region of Portugal. It is separated from its neighbours, Pico and Faial, by the Pico-São Jorge Channel.
Terceira is a volcanic island in the Azores archipelago of Portugal, due west of Lisbon. It is one of the larger islands of the archipelago.
Flores Island is an island of the Western Group, Grupo Ocidental, of the Azores. Together with Corvo Island of the western archipelago, it lies within the North American Plate.

The Berlengas are a Portuguese archipelago consisting of small Atlantic islands off the coast of Peniche, Portugal, in the Oeste region. These islands were traditionally known to British mariners as the Burlings.

Heligoland is a small archipelago in the North Sea, administratively part of the German state of Schleswig-Holstein. The islands are located in the Heligoland Bight in the southeastern corner of the North Sea.
Surtsey is an uninhabited volcanic island located in the Vestmannaeyjar archipelago off the southern coast of Iceland. It is the southern point of Iceland.

Lofoten is an archipelago and a traditional district in the county of Nordland, Norway. Lofoten has distinctive scenery with dramatic mountains and peaks, open sea and sheltered bays, beaches, and untouched lands.

Macaronesia is a collection of four volcanic archipelagos in the North Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of North Africa and Europe. Each archipelago is made up of a number of Atlantic oceanic islands, which were formed by seamounts on the ocean floor.

Anglesey, or Ynys Môn, is an island off the north-west coast of Wales. It forms the majority of the county of the Isle of Anglesey, which also includes Holy Island to the west and some islets and skerries.
Jersey, officially the Bailiwick of Jersey, is an autonomous and self-governing British Crown Dependency in Northwestern Europe off the Cotentin Peninsula of north-west France.

Guernsey is the second large island in the Channel Islands, located west of the Cotentin Peninsula, Normandy. It is the large island in the Bailiwick of Guernsey, which includes five other inhabited islands.
The Isle of Wight is an island off the south coast of England, separated from the mainland by the Solent strait, and otherwise surrounded by the English Channel.
The Isles of Scilly are a small archipelago in Cornwall, England, south-west of Land's End.

The Hebrides are the large archipelago in Scotland and the British Isles, off the west coast of the Scottish mainland. The islands fall into two main groups, based on their proximity to the mainland: the Inner and Outer Hebrides.

The Inner Hebrides is an archipelago off the west coast of mainland Scotland, to the south east of the Outer Hebrides. Together these two island chains form the Hebrides, which experience a mild oceanic climate.
The Isle of Skye, or simply Skye, is a large and northern island of the Inner Hebrides of Scotland. The island's peninsulas radiate from a mountainous hub dominated by the Cuillin.
The Outer Hebrides or Western Isles, sometimes known as the Long Isle or Long Island, is an island chain off the west coast of mainland Scotland. It is a long archipelago in the British Isles.
Lewis and Harris, or Lewis with Harris, is a large island in Scotland. It is the main island of the Outer Hebrides, a short way from the Scottish mainland.
St Kilda, Hiort in Scottish Gaelic, is a remote archipelago situated in the North Atlantic Ocean, west-northwest of North Uist. It contains the western islands of the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
The Northern Isles are two archipelagos comprising Orkney and Shetland that are located off the north coast of the Scottish mainland. The climate is cool and temperate.
Orkney, also known as the Orkney Islands, is an archipelago off the north coast of mainland Scotland. The plural name the Orkneys is also sometimes used.
Shetland, also called the Shetland Islands and formerly Zetland, is an archipelago in Scotland lying between Orkney, the Faroe Islands, and Norway.

The Islands of the Firth of Clyde are a major Scottish island group. They are situated in the Firth of Clyde between Argyll and Bute in the west and Inverclyde, North Ayrshire and South Ayrshire in the east.
The Islands of the Forth are a group of small islands located in the Firth of Forth and in the estuary of the River Forth on the east coast of Scotland.
Achill Island is located off the west coast of Ireland in the historical barony of Burrishoole, County Mayo. It is the large Irish isle.
The Aran Islands or The Arans, are a group of three islands at the mouth of Galway Bay, off the west coast of Ireland. They form the historic barony of Aran in County Galway.

Bornholm is a Danish island in the Baltic Sea, to the east of mainland Denmark, south of Sweden, northeast of Germany and north of Poland. Strategically located, Bornholm has been fought over for centuries.
Gotland, also historically spelled Gottland or Gothland, is a large Swedish island. It is also a province, municipality, and diocese.

Rügen is a large German island. It is located off the Pomeranian coast in the Baltic Sea and belongs to the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The gateway to Rügen island is the Hanseatic city of Stralsund.
The Stockholm Archipelago, Stockholms skärgård in Swedish, is a large archipelago in Sweden, and a large archipelago in the Baltic Sea.
Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Mediterranean Sea off the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula.
Mallorca, also spelled Majorca in English, is a large island of Spain's Balearic Islands. Its capital, Palma, is also the capital of the autonomous community of the Balearic Islands.
Menorca or Minorca is one of the Balearic Islands located in the Mediterranean Sea belonging to Spain. Its name derives from its size, contrasting it with nearby Mallorca.
Gozo, known in antiquity as Gaulos, is an island in the Maltese archipelago in the Mediterranean Sea. The island is part of the Republic of Malta.
Euboea, also known as Evia, is a large Greek island, after Crete, and a large island in the Mediterranean Sea. It is separated from Boeotia in mainland Greece by the narrow Euripus Strait.

The Cyclades is an archipelago in the Aegean Sea, southeast of the Greek mainland and a former administrative prefecture of Greece. The archipelago is one of Greece's island groups which constitute the Aegean archipelago.
Mykonos is a Greek island, part of the Cyclades, lying between Tinos, Syros, Paros and Naxos.
Naxos is a Greek island belonging to the Cyclades island group. It is the large island in the group.

The Dodecanese are a group of larger and smaller Greek islands in the southeastern Aegean Sea and Eastern Mediterranean, off the coast of Anatolia. This island group generally defines the eastern limit of the Sea of Crete.
Karpathos, also Carpathos, is a large Greek Dodecanese island in the southeastern Aegean Sea. Together with the neighboring smaller Saria Island it forms the municipality of Karpathos.
Kos or Cos is a Greek island, part of the Dodecanese island chain in the southeastern Aegean Sea.
Rhodes is a large Greek Dodecanese island and their historical capital. Administratively, Rhodes constitutes a municipality within the Rhodes regional unit, which is part of the South Aegean region.

The Ionian Islands are a group of islands in the Ionian Sea, west of mainland Greece. They are traditionally called the Heptanese, but the group includes many smaller islands in addition to the seven principal ones.
Kefalonia or Cephalonia, formerly also known as Kefallinia or Kephallenia, is a large island of the Ionian Islands in western Greece. It is also a separate regional unit of the Ionian Islands region.
Corfu or Kerkyra is one of the Ionian Islands in western Greece, in the north of Greece's west coast.
Lefkada, also known as Lefkas or Leukas and Leucadia, is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea on the west coast of Greece, connected to the mainland by a long causeway and floating bridge.
Zakynthos, also known as Zante, is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea. It is one of the larger Ionian Islands.
Chios, also known as Scio in English, is a large Greek island, situated in the northern Aegean Sea. The island is separated from the Anatolian mainland by the Chios Strait.
Lemnos or Limnos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean Sea. Administratively the island forms a separate municipality within the Lemnos regional unit, which is part of the North Aegean region.
Lesbos or Lesvos is a Greek island located in the northeastern Aegean Sea. It is a large island in Greece with a long coastline.

Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean Sea, south of Chios, north of Patmos and the Dodecanese archipelago, and off the coast of western Turkey, from which it is separated by the Mycale Strait.

The Saronic Islands or Argo-Saronic Islands is an archipelago in Greece, named after the Saronic Gulf in which they are located, just off the Greek mainland. The main inhabited islands of this group are Salamis, Aegina, Agistri, and Poros.
Salamis or Salamina is a large Greek island in the Saronic Gulf, close to the coast of Athens' port of Piraeus, west of Athens center.

Skiathos is a small Greek island in the northwest Aegean Sea. Skiathos is in the Northern Sporades archipelago, east of the Pelion peninsula in Magnesia on the mainland, and west of the island of Skopelos.
Santorini, officially Thira or Thera, is a Greek island in the southern Aegean Sea, southeast of the mainland. It is a large island of a small, circular archipelago formed by the Santorini caldera.
Cape Breton Island is a rugged and irregularly shaped island on the Atlantic coast of North America, forming part of the Canadian province of Nova Scotia.
Ellis Island is an island in New York Harbor, within the American states of New Jersey and New York. Owned by the national government, it was a busy immigrant inspection and processing station.
The Florida Keys are a coral cay archipelago off the southern coast of Florida, forming the southern part of the continental United States.
Key Largo is an island in the upper Florida Keys archipelago and is a large section of the keys. It is one of the northern Florida Keys in Monroe County.
Key West is a coral cay island in the Straits of Florida, at the southern end of the American state of Florida and its outlying Florida Keys archipelago.

Long Island is a densely populated island in southeastern New York State, extending eastward into the Atlantic Ocean. Geographically, Long Island comprises four divided counties: Kings, Queens, Nassau, and Suffolk.
The Outer Banks, frequently abbreviated OBX, are a long string of barrier islands and spits off the coast of North Carolina and southeastern Virginia, on the east coast of the United States.

Roanoke Island is an island in Dare County, bordered by the Outer Banks of North Carolina. It was named after the historical Roanoke, a Carolina Algonquian people who inhabited the area in the sixteenth century at the time of English colonization.

Saint Pierre and Miquelon, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, is a self-governing territorial overseas collectivity of France in the northwestern Atlantic Ocean, located off the Canadian island of Newfoundland.

The Texas barrier islands are a chain of barrier islands in the Gulf of Mexico along the Texas Gulf Coast. The islands enclose a series of estuaries along the Texas coast and attract tourists for activities such as recreational fishing and dolphin watching.
Alcatraz Island is a small island offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait.
Attu is an island in the Near Islands, part of the Aleutian Islands chain. It is one of the western points of the American state of Alaska.

The Alexander Archipelago is a long archipelago in North America lying off the southeastern coast of Alaska. It contains about eleven hundred islands, the tops of submerged coastal mountains that rise steeply from the Pacific Ocean.
Prince of Wales Island, Taan in Tlingit, is one of the islands of the Alexander Archipelago in the Alaska Panhandle.
Clipperton Island, also known as Clipperton Atoll and previously as Clipperton's Rock, is an uninhabited coral atoll in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
Cocos Island is a volcanic island in the Pacific Ocean administered by Costa Rica, far southwest of the Costa Rican mainland.
Guadalupe Island is a volcanic island located off the western coast of Mexico's Baja California peninsula, southwest of the city of Ensenada in the state of Baja California.
The Gulf Islands is a group of islands in the Salish Sea between Vancouver Island and the mainland coast of British Columbia.
Haida Gwaii, previously known as the Queen Charlotte Islands, is an archipelago located off the northern Pacific coast in the Canadian province of British Columbia.
Kodiak Island is a large island on the south coast of the American state of Alaska, separated from the Alaska mainland by the Shelikof Strait.

Malpelo is an oceanic island in the eastern Pacific Ocean, far west of the Colombian mainland with a military post defended by the Colombian Armed Forces. It consists of a sheer and barren rock with three high peaks.
The Revillagigedo Islands or Revillagigedo Archipelago are a group of four volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean, known for their unique ecosystem.

The San Juan Islands are part of an archipelago in the Pacific Northwest of the United States between the American state of Washington and Vancouver Island in the Canadian province of British Columbia.
Vancouver Island is an island in the northeastern Pacific Ocean and part of the Canadian province of British Columbia.

Navassa Island is an uninhabited island in the Windward Passage of the Caribbean Sea. Located east of Jamaica, south of Cuba, and west of Jérémie on the Tiburon Peninsula of Haiti, it is subject to an ongoing territorial dispute.

The Leeward Antilles are a chain of islands in the Caribbean, specifically part of the southerly islands of the Lesser Antilles along the southeastern fringe of the Caribbean Sea, just north of the Venezuelan coast.

Aruba, officially the Country of Aruba, is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguaná and north-west of Curaçao.
Bonaire is a Caribbean island in the Leeward Antilles. A special municipality of the Netherlands, its seat is the port of Kralendijk, on the west coast of the island.

Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It is an island country located in the southern Caribbean Sea, specifically the Dutch Caribbean region.

The Leeward Islands are a group of islands in the Lesser Antilles of the West Indies in the Caribbean region of the Americas, situated where the northeastern Caribbean Sea meets the western North Atlantic Ocean.

Anguilla is a British Overseas Territory of the Caribbean region in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is one of the northern Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles, lying east of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands and directly north of Saint Martin.
Antigua is an island in the Lesser Antilles. It is one of the Leeward Islands in the Caribbean region and the populous island of the country of Antigua and Barbuda.
Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies.

Nevis is an island in the Caribbean Sea that forms part of the inner arc of the Leeward Islands chain of the West Indies. Nevis and the neighbouring island of Saint Kitts constitute the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, a sovereign state.
Saba is a Caribbean island and a small special municipality of the Netherlands. It consists largely of the dormant volcano Mount Scenery.

Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St. Barths in English or St. Barth in French, is an overseas collectivity of France in the Caribbean.
Saint Kitts, also known as Saint Christopher, is an island in the West Indies. The west side of the island borders the Caribbean Sea, and the eastern coast faces the Atlantic Ocean.

Saint Martin is an island in Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles in the northeastern Caribbean, east of Puerto Rico. The island has been divided since sixteen forty-eight between France and the Netherlands.
Sint Eustatius, known locally as Statia, is an island in the Caribbean. It is a special municipality of the Netherlands.
The Virgin Islands is an archipelago between the North Atlantic Ocean and northeastern Caribbean Sea, located to the immediate east of the main island of Puerto Rico.
The British Virgin Islands, officially the Virgin Islands, is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean, to the east of Puerto Rico and the American Virgin Islands and north-west of Anguilla.
The Spanish Virgin Islands, formerly called the Passage Islands, commonly known as the Puerto Rican Virgin Islands, consist of the islands of Vieques and Culebra.

The Windward Islands are a group of islands in the Lesser Antilles of the West Indies in the Caribbean region of the Americas, situated where the southeastern Caribbean Sea meets the western North Atlantic Ocean.

Saint Vincent is a volcanic island in the southern Caribbean. It is the large island of the country Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and is located in the Caribbean Sea, between Saint Lucia and Grenada.
Tobago, officially the Ward of Tobago, is an island and ward in Trinidad and Tobago. It lies northeast of the larger island of Trinidad and off Venezuela's northeastern coast.
Trinidad is the large and populous island of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago. The island lies off the northeastern coast of Venezuela and sits on the continental shelf of South America.

The Lucayan Archipelago, also known as the Bahamian Archipelago, is an island group comprising the sovereign nation of the Bahamas and the British Overseas Territory of the Turks and Caicos Islands in the North Atlantic Ocean.

Andros is an archipelago in The Bahamas. Politically considered a single island, Andros in total has an area greater than all the other Bahamian islands combined. The land area of Andros consists of hundreds of small islets and cays connected by mangrove estuaries.
Grand Bahama is the north island of the Bahamas. It is a large island in the Bahamas island chain of about seven hundred islands and twenty-four hundred cays.
New Providence is a populous island in the Bahamas. On the eastern side of the island is the national capital city of Nassau.

Turks and Caicos Islands is a British Overseas Territory consisting of the larger Caicos Islands and smaller Turks Islands, two groups of tropical islands in the Lucayan Archipelago of the Atlantic Ocean and northern West Indies.
The Territory of Ashmore and Cartier Islands is an uninhabited external territory of Australia consisting of five low-lying islands in two separate reefs, Ashmore and Cartier.
Bathurst Island, Nguyu in Iwaidja, is one of the Tiwi Islands in the Northern Territory off the northern coast of Australia along with Melville Island.
Christmas Island, officially the Territory of Christmas Island, is an Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean comprising the island of the same name. It lies south of Java and Sumatra.
The Cocos Keeling Islands, officially the Territory of Cocos Keeling Islands, are an Australian external territory located in the Indian Ocean, comprising a small archipelago.
The Coral Sea Islands Territory is an external territory of Australia in the Coral Sea, north-east of Queensland. The territory includes a number of small islands and reefs.
K'gari, also known by its former name Fraser Island, is a World Heritage listed sand island along the south-eastern coast in the Wide Bay-Burnett region of Queensland, Australia.
Lord Howe Island is an irregularly crescent-shaped volcanic remnant in the Tasman Sea between Australia and New Zealand, part of the Australian state of New South Wales.

Macquarie Island is a subantarctic island in the south-western Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Tasmania and Antarctica. It has been governed as a part of Tasmania, Australia, since eighteen eighty.
Norfolk Island is an external territory of Australia located in the Pacific Ocean between New Zealand and New Caledonia, east of Australia and not far from Lord Howe Island.
The Torres Strait Islands are an archipelago of small islands in the Torres Strait, a waterway separating far northern continental Australia's Cape York Peninsula and the island of New Guinea.
The Bismarck Archipelago is a group of islands located just off the northeastern coast of New Guinea in the western Pacific Ocean, part of the Islands Region of Papua New Guinea.

The Admiralty Islands are an archipelago group of forty islands in the Bismarck Archipelago, to the north of New Guinea in the South Pacific Ocean. These are also sometimes known as the Manus Islands.
New Ireland, Niu Ailan in Tok Pisin, or Latangai, is a large island in Papua New Guinea. It is named after the island of Ireland.
The Banks Islands, Bankis in Bislama, are a group of islands in northern Vanuatu. Together with the Torres Islands to their northwest, they make up the northern province of Torba.

Efate, originally named Sandwich Island and also known as Île Vate or just Vate, is an island in the Pacific Ocean. It is part of the Shefa Province in Vanuatu, and the capital city, Port Vila, is located on the island.
Espiritu Santo, usually just called Santo, is a large island in the nation and archipelago of Vanuatu, formerly the New Hebrides.
Rotuma is a self-governing territory generally designated a dependency of Fiji. Rotuma commonly refers to the Rotuma Island, the permanently inhabited island in the Rotuma Group.
Bougainville Island is the main island of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, which is part of Papua New Guinea.
Guadalcanal is the principal island in the Guadalcanal Province of Solomon Islands, located in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, northeast of Australia.
Malaita is the primary island of Malaita Province in Solomon Islands. It is a populous island of the Solomon Islands after Guadalcanal.
Ontong Java Atoll or Luangiua, formerly Lord Howe Atoll, is an atoll in Solomon Islands, and a large atoll on earth. It is inhabited by a Polynesian community.
Tanna, sometimes misspelled Tana, is an island in southern Vanuatu. Tanna is a populous island of Tafea Province.
Vanua Levu, formerly known as Sandalwood Island, is the second large island of Fiji. Located north of the larger Viti Levu.
Viti Levu, meaning Great Fiji, is the large island in Fiji. It is the site of the country's capital and large city, Suva, and home to a large majority of Fiji's population.
The Caroline Islands, or the Carolines, are a widely scattered archipelago of tiny islands in the western Pacific Ocean, to the north of New Guinea.
Chuuk Lagoon, previously Truk Atoll, is an atoll in the central Pacific Ocean. It lies northeast of New Guinea and is part of Chuuk State within the Federated States of Micronesia.
Pohnpei, formerly known as Ponape or Ascension, is an island of the Senyavin Islands which are part of the larger Caroline Islands group. It belongs to Pohnpei State.
Yap traditionally refers to an island group located in the Caroline Islands of the western Pacific Ocean, a part of Yap State.

The Gilbert Islands, Tungaru in Gilbertese, formerly Kingsmill or King's-Mill Islands, are a chain of sixteen atolls and coral islands in the Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Papua New Guinea and Hawaii.
Tarawa is an atoll and the capital of the Republic of Kiribati, in the Micronesia region of the central Pacific Ocean.

The Mariana Islands, also simply the Marianas, are a crescent-shaped archipelago comprising the summits of fifteen longitudinally oriented, mostly dormant volcanic mountains in the north-western Pacific Ocean.
Saipan is the large island and capital of the Northern Mariana Islands, an unincorporated territory of the United States in the western Pacific Ocean.
Wake Island, also known as Wake Atoll, is a coral atoll which is an unincorporated territory of the United States in the Micronesia subregion of the Pacific Ocean.
Enewetak Atoll is a large coral atoll of forty islands in the Pacific Ocean and forms a legislative district of the Ralik Chain of the Marshall Islands.
Kwajalein Atoll is part of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The large island in the atoll is named Kwajalein Island.
The Auckland Islands, Motu Maha or Many islands in Māori, is an archipelago of New Zealand, lying south of the South Island.
The Antipodes Islands, Moutere Mahue or Abandoned Island in Māori, are inhospitable and uninhabited volcanic islands in subantarctic waters to the south of, and territorially part of, New Zealand.
The Bounty Islands, Moutere Hauriri or Island of angry wind in Māori, are a small group of uninhabited granite islets and numerous rocks in the South Pacific Ocean.
The Chatham Islands, Rēkohu or Misty Sun in Moriori and Wharekauri in Māori, officially the Chatham Islands Territory, are an archipelago in the Pacific Ocean east of New Zealand's South Island.
The Kermadec Islands are a subtropical island arc in the South Pacific Ocean northeast of New Zealand's North Island, and a similar distance southwest of Tonga. The islands are part of New Zealand.
Raoul Island, Sunday Island or Rangitāhua in Māori, is the large and northern island of the main Kermadec Islands.
Stewart Island is a large and southern inhabited island of New Zealand, lying south of the South Island, separated by Foveaux Strait. It is a roughly triangular island.
Johnston Atoll is an unincorporated territory of the United States, under the jurisdiction of the United States Air Force. The island is closed to public entry.
Kingman Reef is a largely submerged, uninhabited, triangle-shaped reef, geologically an atoll, in the North Pacific Ocean, roughly halfway between the Hawaiian Islands and American Samoa.
The Line Islands, also known as the Teraina Islands or the Equatorial Islands, are a chain of atolls and coral islands in the central Pacific Ocean.
Kiritimati, also known as Christmas Island, is a Pacific Ocean atoll in the northern Line Islands. It is part of the Republic of Kiribati.

Jarvis Island is an uninhabited coral island located in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Hawaii and the Cook Islands. It is an unincorporated, unorganized territory of the United States.

Malden Island, sometimes called Independence Island in the nineteenth century, is a low, arid, uninhabited atoll in the central Pacific Ocean. It is one of the Line Islands belonging to the Republic of Kiribati.
Starbuck Island, or Volunteer Island, is an uninhabited coral island in the central Pacific, and is part of the Central Line Islands of Kiribati.
Mangaia, traditionally known as Aua Enua, which means terraced island, is a southern island of the Cook Islands and a large one, after Rarotonga. It is a roughly circular island.

The Phoenix Islands, or Rawaki, are a group of eight atolls and two submerged coral reefs that lie east of the Gilbert Islands and west of the Line Islands in the Polynesia sub-region of Oceania, in the central Pacific Ocean.
Baker Island, once known as New Nantucket in the early nineteenth century, is a small, uninhabited atoll located just north of the Equator in the central Pacific Ocean, far southwest of Honolulu.
Howland Island is an uninhabited coral island and strict nature reserve located just north of the equator in the central Pacific Ocean, far southwest of Honolulu.

Canton Island, also known as Kanton or Abariringa, previously known as Mary Island, Mary Balcout's Island or Swallow Island, is a large and northern island of the Phoenix Islands, in the Republic of Kiribati.

The Pitcairn Islands, officially Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands, are a group of four volcanic islands in the southern Pacific Ocean that form the sole British Overseas Territory in the Pacific Ocean.
Rarotonga, sometimes abbreviated Raro, is the large and populous island of the country of the Cook Islands. The island is volcanic.
The Samoan Islands are an archipelago in the central South Pacific, forming part of Polynesia and of the wider region of Oceania.
Tokelau is a dependent territory of New Zealand in the southern Pacific Ocean. It consists of three tropical coral atolls: Atafu, Nukunonu, and Fakaofo.
Fakaofo, formerly known as Bowditch Island, is a South Pacific Ocean atoll located in the Tokelau Group. The land area is small, consisting of islets on a coral reef surrounding a central lagoon.

Wallis and Futuna, officially the Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands, is a French island collectivity in the South Pacific, situated between Tuvalu to the northwest, Fiji to the southwest, Tonga to the southeast, Samoa to the east.

The Hoorn Islands are one of two island groups that make up the French overseas collectivity of Wallis and Futuna. They consist of two volcanic islands, Futuna and Alofi, located in the South Pacific Ocean.
The Acteon Group, Groupe Actéon, is a rather isolated and uninhabited subgroup in the far southeast of the Tuamotu atoll group in French Polynesia.
The Austral Islands are the southern group of islands in French Polynesia, an overseas country of the French Republic in the South Pacific.
The Gambier Islands are an archipelago in French Polynesia, located at the southeast terminus of the Tuamotu archipelago. They are made up of the Mangareva Islands, a group of high islands.
The Marquesas Islands, Îles Marquises in French, are a group of volcanic islands in French Polynesia. The Marquesan names mean the land of men.
The Society Islands are an archipelago in Polynesia in the South Pacific Ocean. Politically, the islands are part of French Polynesia, a semi-autonomous part of France.

Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific.
Moorea is a volcanic island in French Polynesia lying northwest of Tahiti. Moorea and Tahiti are large members of the Windward Islands.
The Tuamotu Archipelago or the Tuamotu Islands are a French Polynesian chain of just under eighty islands and atolls in the southern Pacific Ocean. They constitute a very large chain of atolls.
Moruroa, also Mururoa or Mururura, also historically known as Aopuni, is an atoll which forms part of the Tuamotu Archipelago in French Polynesia in the southern Pacific Ocean.
The Hawaiian Islands are an archipelago of eight major volcanic islands, several atolls, and numerous smaller islets in the North Pacific Ocean.
Kauai is one of the main Hawaiian Islands.
Lanai is a small Hawaiian island. It is colloquially known as the Pineapple Island because of its past as an island-wide pineapple plantation.
Midway Atoll, colloquially the Midway Islands, is a small atoll in the North Pacific Ocean. Its Hawaiian names mean the backbone of heaven and the loud din of birds.
Molokai is one of the eight major islands that make up the Hawaiian Islands archipelago in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
Oahu is a large and populous island of the Hawaiian Islands and of the American state of Hawaii. The state capital, Honolulu, is on its southeastern coast.
The penal colony of Cayenne, commonly known as Devil's Island, Île du Diable in French, was a French penal colony that operated for a hundred years, in the Salvation Islands of French Guiana.
Trindade and Martim Vaz is an archipelago located in the South Atlantic Ocean off the coast of the Brazilian state of Espírito Santo, of which it forms a part.

The Chiloé Archipelago is a group of islands lying off the coast of Chile, in the Los Lagos Region. It is separated from mainland Chile by the Chacao Channel in the north, the Sea of Chiloé in the east and the Gulf of Corcovado.
Chiloé Island, also known as Greater Island of Chiloé, Isla Grande de Chiloé, is the large island of the Chiloé Archipelago off the west coast of Chile, in the Pacific Ocean.
The Desventuradas Islands is a group of four small oceanic islands located off the coast of Chile, northwest of Santiago in the Pacific Ocean. They are considered part of Insular Chile.
Isla Salas y Gómez, also known as Isla Sala y Gómez, is a small uninhabited Chilean island in the Pacific Ocean. It is sometimes considered the eastern point in the Polynesian Triangle.

The Juan Fernández Islands are a sparsely inhabited series of islands in the South Pacific Ocean, reliant on tourism and fishing. They lie off the coast of Chile and are composed of three main volcanic islands.
Chongming, formerly romanized as Chungming, is an alluvial island at the mouth of the Yangtze River in East China.
Gulangyu, Gulang or Kulangsu is an island off the coast of Xiamen, Fujian, southeastern China. A World Heritage Site, the island is one of China's popular tourist attractions.
The Senkaku Islands, known as the Diaoyu Islands in China and the Diaoyutai Islands in Taiwan, are a group of uninhabited islands in the East China Sea, administered by Japan.
Xiamen Island, alternately known as Amoy Island from its Hokkien name, is an island in southeastern Fujian, China, on the Taiwan Strait.
Yeonpyeongdo is a group of South Korean islands in the Yellow Sea, located west of Incheon and south of the coast of Hwanghae Province, North Korea.
Zhoushan is a prefecture-level city in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang. It consists of an archipelago of islands at the southern mouth of Hangzhou Bay off the mainland city of Ningbo.

Coloane is the south area in Macau, connected to Taipa through the area known as Cotai, which is largely built from reclaimed land. Known as Lou Wan in Cantonese, Coloane forms the southern part of Macau.
Ko Samui or Koh Samui, often locally shortened to Samui, is an island off the east coast of Thailand. Geographically in the Chumphon Archipelago, it is part of Surat Thani Province.
Lantau Island, also Lantao Island, Lan Tao or Lan Tau, is the large island in Hong Kong. Located west of Hong Kong Island and the Kowloon Peninsula, it is part of the New Territories.
The Paracel Islands, also known as the Xisha Islands and the Hoàng Sa Archipelago, are an archipelago in the South China Sea.

Pratas Island, also known as the Tungsha Islands or the Dongsha Islands, is a coral island situated in the northern part of the South China Sea administered as part of Cijin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan.
Phu Quoc is a special zone in An Giang province, Vietnam. It is the large island in Vietnam.
Scarborough Shoal, also known as Panacot, Bajo de Masinloc, Huangyan Island, Minzhu Jiao, and Panatag Shoal, is a coral shoal in the South China Sea.

The Spratly Islands are a disputed archipelago in the South China Sea. Composed of islands, islets, cays, and many reefs, sometimes grouped in submerged old atolls, the archipelago lies off the coasts of the Philippines, Malaysia, and southern Vietnam.

Taipa is an area in Macau, formerly a distinct island from Coloane but now connected to it through the reclaimed land of Cotai. Located on the northern half of the combined island, Taipa's population is mostly suburban.
The Wanshan Archipelago, formerly known as the Ladrones Islands, is a large archipelago that is a part of Xiangzhou District in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province, China.

The Liancourt Rocks, known in Korea as Dokdo and in Japan as Takeshima, are a group of islets in the Sea of Japan between the Korean Peninsula and the Japanese archipelago administered by South Korea.

The Japanese archipelago is an archipelago of many islands that constitute the sovereign state of Japan. It spans over a long distance from the Sea of Okhotsk in the northeast to the East China and Philippine seas in the southwest.
Amakusa is a series of islands off the west coast of Kyushu, a main island of Japan.
Awaji Island is an island in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan, in the eastern part of the Seto Inland Sea between the islands of Honshū and Shikoku.
The Gotō Islands are Japanese islands in the Sea of Japan. They are part of Nagasaki Prefecture.
Itsukushima is an island in the western part of the Inland Sea of Japan, located in the northwest of Hiroshima Bay. It is popularly known as Miyajima, which in Japanese means Shrine Island.

The Izu Islands are a group of volcanic islands stretching south and east from the Izu Peninsula of Honshū, Japan. Administratively, they form two towns and six villages, all part of Tokyo Metropolis.
Matsushima is a group of islands in Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. There are tiny islands, shima, covered in pines, matsu, hence the name, and it is considered to be one of the Three Views of Japan.
Sado is a city located on Sado Island in Niigata Prefecture, Japan. The city comprises the entire island, although not all of its total area is urbanized.
Tsushima is an island of the Japanese archipelago situated in-between the Tsushima Strait and Korea Strait, approximately halfway between Kyushu and the Korean Peninsula.
The Bonin Islands, also known as the Ogasawara Islands, are a Japanese archipelago of over thirty subtropical and tropical islands located far south-southeast of Tokyo.

The Amami Islands are a Japanese archipelago in the Satsunan Islands, which is part of the Ryukyu Islands, and is southwest of Kyushu. Administratively, the group belongs to Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan.
Amami Ōshima, also known as Amami, is a large island in the Amami archipelago between Kyūshū and Okinawa. It is one of the Satsunan Islands, all of which belong to Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan.
Okinawa Island, also known as Okinawa Main Island, is a large island of the Okinawa Islands and the Ryukyu Islands of Japan in the Kyushu region.
Tanegashima is one of the Ōsumi Islands belonging to Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan.
The Tokara Islands are an archipelago in the Nansei Islands, and are part of the Satsunan Islands, which are, in turn, part of the Ryukyu Archipelago. The long chain consists of twelve small islands.
The Yaeyama Islands are an archipelago in the southwest of Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The islands are located southwest of the Miyako Islands, part of the Ryukyu Islands archipelago.
Yakushima is one of the Ōsumi Islands in Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan.

The Aru Islands Regency, Kabupaten Kepulauan Aru in Indonesian, is a group of about ninety-five low-lying islands in the Maluku Islands of eastern Indonesia. It also forms a regency of Maluku Province.

Buru, formerly spelled Boeroe, Boro, or Bouru, is a large island within the Maluku Islands of Indonesia. It lies between the Banda Sea to the south and Seram Sea to the north, west of Ambon and Seram islands.
Halmahera, formerly known as Jilolo, Gilolo, or Jailolo, is the large island in the Maluku Islands. It is part of the North Maluku province of Indonesia.
Seram, formerly spelled Ceram, is the large and main island of Maluku province of Indonesia, despite Ambon Island's historical importance.
Tidore is a city, island, and archipelago in the Maluku Islands of eastern Indonesia, west of the larger island of Halmahera. Part of North Maluku Province.
The Sunda Islands is a group of islands composed of the Greater Sunda Islands and the Lesser Sunda Islands, the Nusantara, or outer islands, of the Indonesian Archipelago.

The Greater Sunda Islands are four tropical islands situated within the Indonesian Archipelago, in the Pacific Ocean. The islands, Borneo, Java, Sulawesi and Sumatra, are the larger of the Sunda Islands.
Madura is an Indonesian island off the northeastern coast of Java.
Flores is one of the Lesser Sunda Islands, a group of islands in the eastern half of Indonesia. Administratively, it forms the large island in the East Nusa Tenggara Province.

Lombok is an island in West Nusa Tenggara province, Indonesia. It forms part of the chain of the Lesser Sunda Islands, with the Lombok Strait separating it from Bali to the west and the Alas Strait between it and Sumbawa to the east.
Sumba, natively also spelt as Humba, Hubba, Suba, or Zuba, is an Indonesian island, part of the Lesser Sunda Archipelago group, located in Eastern Indonesia.
Sumbawa is an Indonesian island, located in the middle of the Lesser Sunda Islands chain, with Lombok to the west, Flores to the east, and Sumba further to the southeast.

The Riau Archipelago is a geographic term, as opposed to administrative region, for the core group of islands within the Riau Islands Province in Indonesia, and located south of Singapore and east of Riau on Sumatra.
The Lingga Regency is a group of six hundred islands in Indonesia, located south of Singapore and along both sides of the equator, off the eastern coast of Riau Province on Sumatra island.
Natuna Regency is an islands regency located in the northern part of the Province of Riau Islands, Indonesia.

Penang Island is the main constituent island of the Malaysian state of Penang. It is located off the western coast of Peninsular Malaysia by the Malacca Strait, with the Penang Strait separating the island from Seberang Perai.
Jurong Island is an island located to the southwest of the main island of Singapore. It was formed through the amalgamation of several offshore islands.

Sentosa Island, known mononymously as Sentosa, is an island located off the southern coast of Singapore's main island. The island is separated from the main island of Singapore by a channel of water, the Keppel Harbour.

The Volcano Islands, also known as Iwo Islands, are a group of three Japanese islands in the Northwestern Pacific Ocean. They lie southwest of the Ogasawara Islands and are administered as part of them.
Samosir, or Samosir Island, is a large volcanic island in Lake Toba, located in North Sumatra Province on the island of Sumatra in Indonesia.
Abu Musa is a small island in the eastern Persian Gulf, near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. The island is currently administered by Iran.

Bahrain Island, also known as Awal Island and formerly as Bahrein, is the large island within the archipelago of Bahrain, and forms the bulk of the country's land mass while hosting the majority of its population.
Bubiyan Island is a large island in the Kuwaiti coastal island chain situated in the north-western corner of the Persian Gulf. Bubiyan Island is part of the Shatt al-Arab delta.
Failaka Island is a Kuwaiti island in the Persian Gulf, off the coast of Kuwait City, southeast of the spot where the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers empty into the Gulf.
Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb are two small islands in the eastern Persian Gulf, close to the Strait of Hormuz.

The Hawar Islands are an archipelago of desert islands; all but one are owned by Bahrain, while the southern, small, and uninhabited Jinan Island is administered by Qatar as part of its Al-Shahaniya municipality.
The Pearl Island in Doha, Qatar, is an artificial island. It was the land in Qatar to be available for freehold ownership by foreign nationals.

The Palm Islands consist of three artificial archipelagos: Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Islands, formerly known as Palm Deira or Deira Islands, and Palm Jebel Ali, off the coast of Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
Telegraph Island is located in the Elphinstone Inlet or Khor Ash Sham, the inner inlet of Khasab Bay, off the shore of the Musandam Peninsula.
Hormuz Island, also spelled Hormoz, Ormoz, Ormuz or Ormus, is an Iranian island in the Persian Gulf.
Kharg Island, also spelled Khark Island and often referred to as the Forbidden Island, is a continental island of Iran in the Persian Gulf.
Kish is a resort island in Bandar Lengeh County, Hormozgan Province, off the southern coast of Iran in the Persian Gulf. The island's population center is the city of Kish.
Qeshm is an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz of the Persian Gulf. Separated from the Iranian mainland by the Clarence Strait, Qeshm is the large island in the Persian Gulf.
The Baku Archipelago is a group of coastal islands close to Baku, Azerbaijan. The waters surrounding the islands are shallow.
Ashūradeh, or Ashur Ada, besides Esmail Sai and Akaz islands, is one of the islands off the Iranian coast in the Caspian Sea, in the Gulf of Gorgan.
Chilov, Çilov adası in Azerbaijani, also spelt Zhiloy and Jiloi, is an island in the Caspian Sea. It is located off the Absheron Peninsula, east of Baku.
The Tyuleniy Archipelago is an island group in the north-eastern Caspian Sea off the Mangyshlak Bay west of the Mangyshlak Peninsula.
The Babuyan Islands, also known as the Babuyan Group of Islands, is an archipelago in the Philippines, located in the Luzon Strait north of the main island of Luzon and south of Taiwan.
Batanes, officially the Province of Batanes, is an archipelagic province in the Philippines, administratively part of the Cagayan Valley region. It is the northern province in the Philippines.

The Calamian Islands or the Calamianes is a group of islands in the province of Palawan, Philippines. The archipelago comprises the islands of Coron, Culion, Busuanga, and Linapacan, along with numerous smaller islands.
Catanduanes, officially the Province of Catanduanes, is an island province located in the Bicol Region of Luzon in the Philippines.
Marinduque, officially the Province of Marinduque, is an island province in the Philippines located in Southwestern Tagalog Region or Mimaropa. Its capital is the municipality of Boac.
Masbate Island is the large island of three major islands of Masbate Province in the Philippines. The other two major islands are Ticao Island and Burias Island.
Mindoro is a large and populous island in the Philippines.
Palawan is the large island of the province of Palawan in the Philippines.
The Sulu Archipelago is a chain of islands in the Pacific Ocean in the southwestern Philippines. The archipelago forms the northern limit of the Celebes Sea and southern limit of the Sulu Sea.

Basilan, officially the Province of Basilan, is an island province of the Philippines located primarily in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region. Basilan Island is the large and northern island of the major islands of the Sulu Archipelago.

Jolo, Sūg in Tausug, is a volcanic island in the southwest Philippines and the primary island of the province of Sulu, on which the capital of the same name is situated. It is located in the Sulu Archipelago, between Borneo and Mindanao.
Tawitawi Island, also spelled Tawi Tawi or Tawi-Tawi, is a Philippine island in the Sulu Archipelago between the Sulu Sea and Celebes Sea, east of Borneo. It is the main island of Tawi-Tawi Province.
Bohol, officially the Province of Bohol, is an island province of the Philippines located in the Central Visayas region, consisting of the island itself and many minor surrounding islands.
Cebu, Sugbo in Cebuano, officially the Province of Cebu, is a province of the Philippines located in the Central Visayas region.
Leyte is an island in the Visayas group of islands in the Philippines. It is a large and populous island in the Philippines.
Negros is a large and populous island in the Philippines. The coastal zone of the southern part of Negros is identified as a site of high marine biodiversity.
Panay is a large and populous island in the Philippines, similar in size to Sicily or Bali.
Samar is a large island in the Philippines. It is located in the Eastern Visayas region of the Visayas islands.
Adelaide Island is a large, mainly ice-covered island, lying at the north side of Marguerite Bay off the west coast of the Antarctic Peninsula.
Berkner Island, also known as the Berkner Ice Rise or as Hubley Island, is an Antarctic ice rise, where bedrock below sea level has caused the surrounding ice sheet to create a dome.
Île Saint-Paul is an island forming part of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands in the Indian Ocean. The island is located south of the larger Île Amsterdam.

The McDonald Islands are an uninhabited archipelago in the southern Indian Ocean in the vicinity of Heard Island. Together with Heard Island, they make up the Australian external territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands.
The French Southern and Antarctic Lands is an overseas territory of France.
Seenu Atoll, historically known as Addu Atoll, is the south atoll of the Maldives. Addu Atoll, together with Fuvahmulah, extend the Maldives into the Southern Hemisphere.
São Tomé is an island located in the Gulf of Guinea. It is a large and populous island of São Tomé and Príncipe.
Anvers Island, Antwerp Island, Antwerpen Island, or Isla Amberes is a high, mountainous island in the Palmer Archipelago of Antarctica.
The New Siberian Islands are an archipelago in the Extreme North of Russia, to the north of the East Siberian coast between the East Siberian Sea and the Laptev Sea.
Kotelny Island is part of the Anzhu Islands subgroup of the New Siberian Islands located between the Laptev Sea and the East Siberian Sea in the Russian Arctic.

The Lyakhovsky Islands are the southern group of the New Siberian Islands in the Arctic seas of eastern Russia. The islands are named in honour of Ivan Lyakhov, who explored them in seventeen seventy-three.
New Siberia or Novaya Sibir is the eastern member of the Anzhu Islands, the northern subgroup of the New Siberian Islands lying between the Laptev Sea and East Siberian Sea.
Severnaya Zemlya is an archipelago in the Russian high Arctic. It lies off the Taymyr Peninsula of Siberia, separated from the mainland by the Vilkitsky Strait.
Bolshevik Island is an island in Severnaya Zemlya, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russian Arctic. The island is named after the political faction of the Soviet Union.
Komsomolets Island is the northern island of the Severnaya Zemlya group in the Russian Arctic, and a large island in the group.

October Revolution Island is the large island of the Severnaya Zemlya group in Russia in the Arctic. It is named after the October Revolution which overthrew the Russian Republic and created the Soviet Union.
Wrangel Island is an island of the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Russia. It is roughly the size of Crete.

The Commander Islands, Komandorski Islands, or Komandorskie Islands are a series of islands in the Russian Far East, a part of the Aleutian Islands, located east of the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Bering Sea.
The Empress Eugénie Archipelago, commonly known as the Eugénie Archipelago, is an archipelago in the Peter the Great Gulf in the Sea of Japan, along the southern coast of Primorsky Krai, Russia.
Bolshoi Ussuriysky Island, or Heixiazi Island, is a sedimentary island at the confluence of the Amur and Ussuri rivers. It is divided between China and Russia.
Zhenbao Island or Damansky Island is a small island in Heilongjiang Province, China. It is on the Ussuri River on the border between Primorsky Krai, Russia, and Heilongjiang Province, China.
Franz Josef Land is a Russian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean. It is inhabited by military personnel and has no permanent population.
Jan Mayen is a Norwegian volcanic island in the Arctic Ocean with no permanent population. It is partly covered by glaciers around the Beerenberg volcano.
Severny Island is a Russian Arctic island. It is the northern island of the Novaya Zemlya archipelago. It was historically called Lütke Land after Friedrich Benjamin von Lütke, who explored it.
Yuzhny Island is the southern island of Russia's Novaya Zemlya archipelago, lying north of mainland Russia.
Spitsbergen is the large and permanently populated island of the Svalbard archipelago in northern Norway in the Arctic Ocean. It borders the Arctic Ocean, the Norwegian Sea and the Greenland Sea.
Disko Island is a large island in Baffin Bay, off the west coast of Greenland. It is called Qeqertarsuaq in Greenlandic and Diskoøen in Danish.
Banks Island is one of the larger members of the Arctic Archipelago. It is situated in the Inuvik Region, and is part of the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, of the Northwest Territories, Canada.
King William Island is an island in the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut, which is part of the Arctic Archipelago.
The Queen Elizabeth Islands are the northern cluster of islands in Canada's Arctic Archipelago, split between Nunavut and the Northwest Territories in Northern Canada.
Axel Heiberg Island is an uninhabited island in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It is located in the Arctic Ocean.
Devon Island in Canada is a large uninhabited island, with no permanent human residents. It is in Baffin Bay, Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada.
Melville Island is an uninhabited member of the Queen Elizabeth Islands of the Arctic Archipelago.
Southampton Island is a large island at the entrance to Hudson Bay at Foxe Basin. It is one of the larger members of the Arctic Archipelago, part of the Kivalliq Region in Nunavut, Canada.
Victoria Island is a large island in the Arctic Archipelago that straddles the boundary between Nunavut and the Northwest Territories of Canada.
Manitoulin Island is an island in Lake Huron, located within the borders of the Canadian province of Ontario. It is the large lake island of the world.
The Island of Montreal is an island in southwestern Quebec, Canada, which is the site of a number of municipalities, including much of the city of Montreal.
The Central Siberian Plateau is a vast mountainous area in Siberia, one of the Great Russian Regions.
The East Siberian taiga ecoregion, in the taiga and boreal forests biome, is a very large biogeographic region in eastern Russia.
The Alaska Peninsula extends to the southwest from the mainland of Alaska and ends in the Aleutian Islands. The peninsula separates the Pacific Ocean from Bristol Bay, an arm of the Bering Sea.

Cape Cod is a peninsula extending into the Atlantic Ocean from the southeastern corner of Massachusetts, in the northeastern United States. Its historic, maritime character and ample beaches attract heavy tourism during the summer months.

The Delmarva Peninsula, or simply Delmarva, is a peninsula on the East Coast of the United States, occupied by the majority of the state of Delaware and parts of the Eastern Shore of Maryland and Eastern Shore of Virginia.

The Labrador Peninsula, also called Quebec-Labrador Peninsula, is a large peninsula in eastern Canada. It is bounded by Hudson Bay to the west, the Hudson Strait to the north, and the Labrador Sea to the east.

The Ungava Peninsula is the far northwestern part of the Labrador Peninsula of the province of Quebec, Canada. It is bounded by Hudson Bay to the west, Hudson Strait to the north, and Ungava Bay to the east.

The Olympic Peninsula is a large peninsula in Western Washington that lies across Puget Sound from Seattle, and contains Olympic National Park. It is bounded on the west by the Pacific Ocean, the north by the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and the east by Hood Canal.

The Seward Peninsula is a large peninsula on the western coast of the United States state of Alaska, whose western point is Cape Prince of Wales. The peninsula projects into the Bering Sea between Norton Sound, the Bering Strait and the Chukchi Sea.

The Absheron Peninsula is a peninsula in Azerbaijan. It is the location of Baku, the populous capital city of the country, and the Baku Metropolitan Area, with its satellite cities Sumqayit and Khyrdalan.

The Al-Faw peninsula is a peninsula in the Persian Gulf, located in the extreme southeast of Iraq. The marshy peninsula is part of a delta for the Shatt al-Arab river, formed by the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates.
The Boso Peninsula is a peninsula that encompasses the entirety of Chiba Prefecture on Honshu, the large island of Japan. It is part of the Greater Tokyo Area.
The Chukchi Peninsula is the eastern point of continental Asia.
The Gyda Peninsula is a geographical feature of the Siberian coast in the Kara Sea. It takes its name from the river Gyda, that flows on the peninsula.

The Izu Peninsula is a mountainous peninsula with a deeply indented coastline to the west of Tokyo on the Pacific coast of the island of Honshu, Japan. Formerly known as Izu Province, it is now a part of Shizuoka Prefecture.
The Kii Peninsula is the large peninsula on the island of Honshu, located in the Kansai region of Japan. It is named after the ancient Kii Province.

The Noto Peninsula is a peninsula that projects north into the Sea of Japan from the coast of Ishikawa Prefecture in central Honshu, the main island of Japan. Before the Meiji era, the peninsula belonged to Noto Province.
The Oga Peninsula is a rugged peninsula which projects west into the Sea of Japan from the coast of Akita in northern Honshu, the main island of Japan. Politically it coincides with the city of Oga.
The Oshima Peninsula is the southern part of Hokkaido, the northern of the Japanese islands. Where the peninsula starts is open to interpretation.
The Leizhou Peninsula, alternately romanized as the Luichow Peninsula, is a peninsula in the southern part of Guangdong province in South China.
The Liaodong or Liaotung Peninsula is a peninsula in southern Liaoning province in Northeast China, and makes up the southwestern coastal half of the Liaodong region.
The Shandong Peninsula or Jiaodong Peninsula is a peninsula in Shandong in eastern China, between the Bohai Sea to the north and the Yellow Sea to the south.
The Shimokita Peninsula is the remote northeastern cape of the Japanese island of Honshu, stretching out towards Hokkaido.
The Shiretoko Peninsula is located on the eastern portion of the Japanese island of Hokkaido, protruding into the Sea of Okhotsk. It is separated from Kunashiri Island by the Nemuro Strait.

The Taymyr Peninsula is a peninsula in the Far North of Russia, in the Siberian Federal District, that forms the northern part of the mainland of Eurasia. Administratively it is part of the Krasnoyarsk Krai Federal subject of Russia.

The Yamal Peninsula is located in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug of northwest Siberia, Russia. It is bordered principally by the Kara Sea and its Baydaratskaya Bay on the west, and by the Gulf of Ob on the east.
