The Kola Peninsula is a peninsula in the extreme northwest of Russia, and one of the large peninsulas of Europe. It forms the bulk of the territory of Murmansk Oblast, and lies almost completely inside the Arctic Circle.

The Italian Peninsula extends from the southern Alps in the north to the central Mediterranean Sea in the south and comprises much of the country of Italy and the enclaved microstates of San Marino and Vatican City.
The Scandinavian Peninsula is located in Northern Europe, and roughly comprises the mainlands of Sweden, Norway and the northwestern area of Finland.
The Bird's Head Peninsula, also called Vogelkop or Doberai Peninsula, is a large peninsula that makes up the northwest portion of the island of New Guinea.
The Cape York Peninsula is located in Far North Queensland, Australia. It is a vast wilderness in northern Australia.
The Northland Peninsula, also known as the North Auckland Peninsula, is in the northern part of the North Island of New Zealand. It is joined to the main body of the island by the Auckland isthmus.
The Papuan Peninsula, also known as the Bird's Tail Peninsula, is a large peninsula in Papua New Guinea that makes up the southeastern portion of the island of New Guinea.
The Tasman Peninsula is a peninsula located in south-east Tasmania, Australia, south-east of Hobart.

Cape Agulhas is a rocky headland in Western Cape, South Africa. It is the southern point of South Africa, the geographic southern tip of Africa and the beginning of the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans.

Cape Canaveral is a cape in Brevard County, Florida, in the United States, near the center of the state's Atlantic coast. It is situated east of Merritt Island, and is separated from it by the Banana River.
Cape Fear is a prominent headland jutting into the Atlantic Ocean from Bald Head Island on the coast of North Carolina in the Southeastern United States.

Cape Hatteras is a cape located at a pronounced bend in Hatteras Island, one of the barrier islands of North Carolina. As a temperate barrier island, the landscape has been shaped by wind, waves, and storms.
Cape Reinga is the northwestern tip of the Aupouri Peninsula, at the northern end of the North Island of New Zealand.
Cape Leeuwin is the south-westerly mainland point of the Australian continent, in the state of Western Australia.
Land's End is a headland and tourist and holiday complex in western Cornwall, England, United Kingdom, on the Penwith peninsula, at the western end of the A thirty road.
The North Cape, called Nordkapp in Norwegian, is a cape on the northern coast of the island of Magerøya in Northern Norway. The cape is in Nordkapp Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway.
Cape Soya is the northern point of the island of Hokkaido, Japan. It is situated in Wakkanai, Soya Subprefecture.
The Karelian Isthmus is the stretch of land situated between the Gulf of Finland and Lake Ladoga in northwestern Russia, to the north of the River Neva.

The Kra Isthmus, also called the Isthmus of Kra in Thailand, is the narrow part of the Malay Peninsula. The western part of the isthmus belongs to Ranong province and the eastern part to Chumphon province, both in Southern Thailand.
The Isthmus of Corinth is the narrow land bridge which connects the Peloponnese peninsula with mainland Greece, near the city of Corinth.
The Isthmus of Suez is the land bridge that lies between the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, east of the Suez Canal, the boundary between the continents of Africa and Asia.

The Isthmus of Tehuantepec is an isthmus in Mexico. It represents the short crossing between the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Ocean, thereby also making it the natural border between North America and Central America.
The Niagara Peninsula is a geographic and cultural region lying between the southwestern shore of Lake Ontario and the northeastern shore of Lake Erie, in Ontario, Canada.

The Gulf of Maine is a large gulf of the Atlantic Ocean on the east coast of North America. It is bounded by Cape Cod at the eastern tip of Massachusetts in the southwest and by Cape Sable Island at the southern tip of Nova Scotia in the northeast.
Massachusetts Bay is a bay on the Gulf of Maine that forms part of the central coastline of Massachusetts, United States.
Manicouagan Reservoir is an annular lake in central Quebec, Canada. The lake island in its centre is known as Rene-Levasseur Island, and its high point is Mount Babel.
Lake Manitoba is a large lake in Canada. It is located within the Canadian province of Manitoba northwest of the province's capital, Winnipeg.
Lake Mead is a reservoir formed by the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River in the Southwestern United States. It is located in the states of Nevada and Arizona, east of Las Vegas.
Lake Missoula was a prehistoric proglacial lake in western Montana that existed periodically at the end of the last ice age.
Nettilling Lake is a cold freshwater lake located toward the south end of Baffin Island in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It is a large lake on an island.
Lake of the Woods is a lake occupying parts of the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Manitoba and the United States state of Minnesota. It contains thousands of islands and a very long shoreline.
Lake Okeechobee is a large freshwater lake in the United States state of Florida. It is a large natural freshwater lake contained entirely within the contiguous states.
Lake Patzcuaro is a lake in the municipality of Patzcuaro, Michoacan, Mexico. Lake Patzcuaro lies in an endorheic basin, which does not drain to the sea.
Lake Pontchartrain is an estuary in southeastern Louisiana in the United States.

Pyramid Lake is a saltwater lake in the geographic sink of the basin of the Truckee River, northeast of Reno, Nevada. It is a remnant of ancient Lake Lahontan, a large endorheic lake that once covered much of western Nevada.

The Smallwood Reservoir is the reservoir created for the Churchill Falls Generating Station in the western part of Labrador, Canada. Unlike other reservoirs, water is contained not by a single large dam, but by a series of dikes.
Lake Tahoe is a freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada of the Western United States, straddling the border between California and Nevada. It is a large alpine lake in North America.
Lake Winnipegosis is a large lake in central North America, in Manitoba, Canada, northwest of Winnipeg.

The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties in Southern California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.
Lake Argyle is a large freshwater man-made reservoir in Western Australia. The reservoir is part of the Ord River Irrigation Scheme and is located near the East Kimberley town of Kununurra.

Lake Mackay, known as Wilkinkarra to the Indigenous Pintupi people, is one of hundreds of ephemeral salt lakes scattered throughout the Pilbara and northern parts of the Goldfields-Esperance region of Western Australia and the Northern Territory.

Lake Taupo is a large crater lake in New Zealand's North Island, located in the caldera of Taupo Volcano. The lake is the namesake of the town of Taupo, which sits on a bay in the lake's northeastern shore.
Lake Todos los Santos is a lake located in the Los Lagos Region of southern Chile, northeast of the regional capital Puerto Montt, within the boundaries of the Vicente Perez Rosales National Park.

The Shatt al-Arab is a river that is formed at the confluence of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in the town of al-Qurnah in the Basra Governorate of southern Iraq. The southern end of the river constitutes the Iran-Iraq border.

The Orontes, or Nahr al-Asi, or simply Asi, is a river in West Asia that begins in Lebanon, flowing northwards through Syria before entering the Mediterranean Sea near Samandag in Hatay Province, Turkey.

The Kura, also known in Georgian as Mtkvari, is a transboundary river that flows between the Greater Caucasus and Lesser Caucasus mountains. It drains the southern slopes of the Greater Caucasus and northern slopes of the Lesser Caucasus.

The Aras is a transboundary river in the Caucasus. It rises in eastern Turkey and flows along the borders between Turkey and Armenia, between Iran and both Azerbaijan and Armenia, and through Azerbaijan.

The Tarim River, known in Sanskrit as the Sita, is an endorheic river in Xinjiang, China. It is the principal river of the Tarim Basin, a desert region of Central Asia between the Tian Shan and Kunlun Mountains.

The Maritime Silk Road or Maritime Silk Route is an ancient maritime trade route in the Indian Ocean and the Western Pacific that connected Southeast Asia, East Asia, the Indian subcontinent, the Arabian Peninsula, eastern Africa, and Europe.
The Northeast Passage is the shipping route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, along the Arctic coasts of Norway and Russia.
The Northern Sea Route is a shipping route along the Arctic coast of Russia. It is a short shipping route between the western part of Eurasia and the Asia-Pacific region.

The Northwest Passage is the sea lane between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through the Arctic Ocean, near the northern coast of North America via waterways through the Arctic Archipelago of Canada.
Indian Ocean trade is vital for the global economy and has been described as the cradle for global trade.
The Inside Passage is a coastal route for ships and boats along a network of passages which weave through the islands on the Pacific Northwest coast of the North American Fjordland.

The Intracoastal Waterway is an inland waterway along the Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico coasts of the United States, running from Massachusetts southward along the Atlantic Seaboard and around the southern tip of Florida.
The Yonaguni Monument, also known as the Yonaguni Island Submarine Ruins, is a submerged rock formation off the coast of Yonaguni, the southern of the Ryukyu Islands, in Japan.
Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, Spanish for Great Island of Land of Fire, is an island near the southern tip of South America from which it is separated by the Strait of Magellan.
The Northern Neck is a peninsula, traditionally called a neck in Virginia, on the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

Adam's Bridge, also known as Rama Setu, is a chain of natural limestone shoals between Pamban Island, also known as Rameswaram Island, off the southeastern coast of Tamil Nadu, India, and Mannar Island, off the northwestern coast of Sri Lanka.

Salento is a cultural, historical, and geographic region at the southern end of the administrative region of Apulia, in southern Italy. It is a sub-peninsula of the Italian Peninsula, sometimes described as the heel of the Italian boot.
Jutland is a peninsula in Northern Europe that forms the continental portion of Denmark and part of northern Germany.

Punta Parinas, also known as Punta Balcones, is in the La Brea District, Talara Province, Piura Region, Peru. It is the western point of mainland South America. An active lighthouse is located in Punta Parinas.
Cabo da Roca or Cape Roca is a cape which forms the western point of the Sintra Mountain Range, of mainland Portugal, of continental Europe, and of the Eurasian landmass.

South East Cape is a cape located at the southern point of the main island of Tasmania, the southern state in Australia. The cape is situated in the Southwest National Park, part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.
The Alpide belt, or Alpine-Himalayan orogenic belt, is a seismic and orogenic belt that includes an array of mountain ranges extending for thousands of kilometres across Eurasia.

In biogeography, the Mediterranean basin, also known as the Mediterranean region or sometimes Mediterranea, is the region of lands around the Mediterranean Sea that mostly have a Mediterranean climate, with mild to cool, rainy winters and warm to hot, dry summers.
The Emba in west Kazakhstan rises in the Mugodzhar Hills and flows across the Sub-Ural Plateau and Caspian Depression into the Caspian Sea.

The Ili River is a river in northwestern China and southeastern Kazakhstan. It flows from the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture of the Xinjiang Uighur Autonomous Region to the Almaty Region in Kazakhstan.
The Adirondack Mountains are a massif of mountains in Northeastern New York State which form a circular dome. The region contains many peaks.

The Blue Ridge Mountains are a physiographic province of the larger Appalachian Highlands range. The mountain range is located in the Eastern United States and extends southwest from southern Pennsylvania.

The Great Smoky Mountains are a mountain range rising along the Tennessee and North Carolina border in the southeastern United States. They are a subrange of the Appalachian Mountains and form part of the Blue Ridge Physiographic Province.
The Atlantic Plain is one of eight distinct physiographic divisions of the contiguous United States.

The Basin and Range Province is a vast physiographic region covering much of the inland Western United States and northwestern Mexico. It is defined by unique basin and range topography, characterized by abrupt changes in elevation.
The Black Hills are an outlying subrange of the greater Rocky Mountain system rising from the Great Plains of North America in western South Dakota and eastern Wyoming, United States.

Devils Tower, also known as Bear Lodge, is a laccolithic butte, composed of igneous rock in the Bear Lodge Ranger District of the Black Hills, in Crook County, northeastern Wyoming, above the Belle Fourche River.
The Blue Mountains are a mountain range in the northwestern United States, located largely in northeastern Oregon and stretching into extreme southeastern Washington.
The Brooks Range is a mountain range in far northern North America stretching from west to east across northern Alaska into Canada's Yukon Territory.
The Cascade Range, or Cascades, is a major mountain range of western North America, extending from southern British Columbia through Washington and Oregon to Northern California.

The Cascade Volcanoes, also known as the Cascade Volcanic Arc or the Cascade Arc, are a number of volcanoes in a continental volcanic arc in western North America, extending from southwestern British Columbia through Washington and Oregon to Northern California.
The Columbia River Gorge is a canyon of the Columbia River in the Pacific Northwest of the United States. The canyon stretches for many miles as the river winds westward through the Cascade Range.
The North Cascades are a section of the Cascade Range of western North America. They span the border between the Canadian province of British Columbia and the United States state of Washington.
The Central Valley is a broad, elongated, flat valley that dominates the interior of California, United States. It runs inland from and parallel to the Pacific coast.

The Channeled Scablands are a relatively barren and soil-free region of interconnected relict and dry flood channels, coulees and cataracts and the typically flat-lying basalt flows that remain after cataclysmic floods.
Chimney Rock is a prominent geological rock formation in the United States, located in Morrill County in western Nebraska. It rises above the surrounding North Platte River valley.
The Colorado Plateau is a physiographic and desert region of the Intermontane Plateaus, roughly centered on the Four Corners region of the Southwestern United States.

Monument Valley is a region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of sandstone buttes. The famous butte formations are located in northeastern Arizona along the Utah and Arizona state line.

The Columbia Plateau is an important geologic and geographic region that lies across parts of the United States states of Washington, Oregon, and Idaho. It is a wide flood basalt plateau between the Cascade Range and the Rocky Mountains, cut through by the Columbia River.
Copper Canyon is a system of six distinct canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental in the southwestern part of the state of Chihuahua in northwestern Mexico. The canyons were formed by six rivers.
Glenwood Canyon is a rugged scenic canyon in western Colorado in the United States. Its walls climb high above the Colorado River.
Hells Canyon is a canyon in the Western United States, along the border of eastern Oregon, western Idaho, and a small section of eastern Washington.

The Hudson Bay Lowlands is a vast wetland located between the Canadian Shield and southern shores of Hudson Bay and James Bay. Much of the area lies within the province of Ontario, with smaller portions reaching into Manitoba and Quebec.
The High Plains are a subregion of the Great Plains, mainly in the Western United States, but also partly in the Midwest states of Nebraska, Kansas, and South Dakota.
The Laurentian Mountains, also known as the Laurentians or Laurentides, are a mountain range in Canada.
The Central Mexican Plateau, also known as the Mexican Altiplano, is a large arid-to-semiarid plateau occupying much of northern and central Mexico.
The Mount Edziza volcanic complex is a group of volcanoes and associated lava flows in northwestern British Columbia, Canada. It is located on the Tahltan Highland.
The Ozarks, also known as the Ozark Mountains, Ozark Highlands or Ozark Plateau, is a geo-cultural region located in the Midwest and South Central United States.

The Coast Mountains are a major mountain range in the Pacific Coast Ranges of western North America, extending from southwestern Yukon through the Alaska Panhandle and the Coast of British Columbia south to the Fraser River.
The Olympic Mountains are a mountain range on the Olympic Peninsula of the Pacific Northwest of the United States.

The Piedmont is a plateau region located in the Eastern United States. It is situated between the Atlantic Plain and the Blue Ridge Mountains, stretching from New York in the north to central Alabama in the south.

The Front Range is a mountain range of the Southern Rocky Mountains of North America located in the central portion of the United States state of Colorado, and southeastern portion of the state of Wyoming.

The Teton Range, or simply the Tetons, is a mountain range of the Rocky Mountains in North America. It extends in a north and south direction through the United States state of Wyoming, east of the Idaho state line.
The Sawatch Range or Saguache Range is a high and extensive mountain range in central Colorado which includes eight of the twenty high peaks in the Rocky Mountains.
The Uinta Mountains are an east and west trending mountain range in northeastern Utah extending a short distance into northwest Colorado and slightly into southwestern Wyoming in the United States.

The Wasatch Range or Wasatch Mountains is a mountain range in the western United States that runs from the Utah and Idaho border south to central Utah. It is the western edge of the greater Rocky Mountains.

The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Lowlands, or simply St. Lawrence Lowlands, is a physiographic region of Eastern Canada that comprises a section of southern Ontario bounded on the north by the Canadian Shield.
The Sierra Madre Occidental is a major mountain range system which runs northwest to southeast through northwestern and western Mexico, and along the Gulf of California.
The Sierra Madre Oriental is a mountain range located in northeastern Mexico. It is part of the American Cordillera.
The Sierra Madre is a major mountain range in Central America. It is known as the Sierra Madre de Chiapas in Mexico.
The Sierra Madre de Oaxaca is a mountain range in southeastern Mexico. It is primarily in the state of Oaxaca, and extends north into the states of Puebla and Veracruz.
The Sierra Madre del Sur is a mountain range in southern Mexico, extending from southern Michoacan east through Guerrero, to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in eastern Oaxaca.
The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, also known as the Transvolcanic Belt and locally as the Sierra Nevada, is an active volcanic belt that covers central-southern Mexico.
Stone Mountain is a quartz monzonite dome monadnock and the site of Stone Mountain Park, east of Atlanta, Georgia.

The Willamette Valley is a valley in Oregon, in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States. The Willamette River flows the entire length of the valley and is surrounded by mountains on three sides.
The American Cordillera is a chain of mountain ranges consisting of an almost continuous sequence of mountain ranges that form the western backbone of the Americas.
The Cordillera Blanca, Spanish for white range, is a mountain range in Peru that is part of the larger Andes range and extends in a northwesterly direction.
Caldera Basin is a sedimentary basin located in the coast of northern Chile west of Copiapo. The basin has a fill of marine sediments of Late Cenozoic age.
The Campos Basin is one of the coastal sedimentary basins of Brazil. It spans both onshore and offshore parts of the South Atlantic with the onshore part located near Rio de Janeiro.

Campo del Cielo, Field of Heaven or Field of the Sky in English, refers to a group of iron meteorites and the area in Argentina where they were found. The site straddles the provinces of Chaco and Santiago del Estero.

The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Snowy Mountain Range of Saint Martha in English, is an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, separate from the Andes range that runs through the north of the country.
Valle de la Luna, also called Killa Qhichwa or Moon Valley, is a protected municipal area south of downtown La Paz, in Pedro Domingo Murillo Province, La Paz Department, Bolivia.

The Gamburtsev Mountain Range, also known as the Gamburtsev Subglacial Mountains, is a subglacial mountain range located in East Antarctica, just underneath the lofty Dome A, near the Southern Pole of Inaccessibility.
The Eastern Ghats is a mountain range that stretches along the eastern coast of the Indian peninsula. It traverses the states of Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
The Kashmir Valley, also known as the Vale of Kashmir, is an intermontane valley or basin in the northern part of Jammu and Kashmir. The valley is surrounded by the ranges of the Himalayas.

The Nilgiri Mountains, also known as the Nilgiris, are a mountain range at the junction of the Eastern and Western Ghats ranges in South India. Spanning the states of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala.
The Aladagh Mountains or the Aladagh Range refers to a mountain range situated in the southeastern section of Iran's North Khorasan province, southeast of the Caspian Sea.

The Alborz is a mountain range in northern Iran that stretches from the border of Azerbaijan along the western and southern coast of the Caspian Sea and finally runs northeast and merges into the smaller Aladagh Mountains.
The Armenian highlands comprise the central and the high plateau of the three plateaus that together form the northern sector of West Asia.

The Jordan Valley forms part of the larger Jordan Rift Valley. The term Jordan Valley often applies just to the lower course of the Jordan River, from the spot where it exits the Sea of Galilee in the north.
The Judaean Mountains, or Judaean Hills or the Hebron Hills, is a mountain range in the West Bank and Israel where Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Hebron and several other biblical sites are located.
The Kopet Dag, also known as the Turkmen-Khorasan Mountain Range, is a mountain range on the border between Turkmenistan and Iran that extends along the border southeast of the Caspian Sea.
Mount Lebanon is a mountain range in Lebanon. The range provides a typical alpine climate year-round.
The Pontic Mountains, Pontic Alps or Parhar Mountains form a mountain range stretching along the southern Pontic coast of the Black Sea in northern Anatolia, Turkey.

Safed Koh, also known as Spin Ghar, is a mountain range to the south of the Hindu Kush. It stretches from eastern Afghanistan to northwestern Pakistan, and forms a natural border between the two countries.
The Taurus Mountains are a mountain complex in southern Turkey, separating the Mediterranean coastal region on the Levantine Sea from the central Anatolian Plateau.
Amanohashidate is one of Japan's three scenic views. It is a sandbar located in Miyazu Bay in northern Kyoto Prefecture.
The Central Mountain Range is the principal mountain range on Taiwan Island. It runs from the north of the island to the south.
The Changbai Mountains are a major mountain range in East Asia that extends from the Northeast Chinese provinces of Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, across the China and North Korea border.
The Daisetsuzan Volcanic Group is a volcanic group of peaks arranged around the Ohachi-Daira caldera in Hokkaido, Japan.
Fossa Magna is a great rift lowland in Japan. It is often confused with the Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line, which is a line, while Fossa Magna is an area.
The Greater Khingan Range or Da Hinggan Range is a long volcanic mountain range in the Inner Mongolia region of Northeast China, and in the eastern part of Mongolia.
The Hengduan Mountains are a group of mountain ranges in southwest China that connect the southeast portions of the Tibetan Plateau with the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau.

The Japan Median Tectonic Line, also Median Tectonic Line, is the long fault system of Japan. It begins near Ibaraki Prefecture, where it connects with the Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line and the Fossa Magna.
The Japanese Alps is a series of mountain ranges in Japan which bisect the main island of Honshu. The peaks that tower over central Honshu have long been the object of veneration and pilgrimage.

The Kanto Plain, in the Kanto region of central Honshu, is the large plain in Japan. It extends over Tokyo, Saitama Prefecture, Kanagawa Prefecture, Chiba Prefecture, Gunma Prefecture, Tochigi Prefecture, and Ibaraki Prefecture.

The Mongolian Plateau or Altai Plateau is an inland plateau in East Asia. It is bounded by the Greater Hinggan Mountains in the east, the Yin Mountains to the south, and the Altai Mountains in the west.
Mount Aso or Aso Volcano is a large active volcano in Japan. The name is often used for the somma volcano in the centre of Aso Caldera.
Mount Unzen is an active stratovolcano of several overlapping small, volcanic cones, near the city of Shimabara, Nagasaki on the island of Kyushu, Japan.

The Nanling, also known as the Wuling, is a major mountain range in Southern China that separates the Pearl River Basin from the Yangtze Valley and serves as the dividing line between south and central subtropical zones.
The Northeast China Plain or Northeast Plain, also known as the Manchurian Plain or Songliao Plain, is a lowland plain in Northeast Asia located in a vast, elongated basin.
The Nyenchen Tanglha Mountains are a mountain range and subrange of the Transhimalaya System, located in Tibet and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

The Qinling or Qin Mountains, formerly known as the Nanshan, are a major east and west mountain range in southern Shaanxi Province, China. The mountains mark the divide between the drainage basins of the Yangtze and Yellow River systems.

The Sanriku Coast is a coastal region on the Pacific Ocean, extending from southern Aomori Prefecture, through Iwate Prefecture and northern Miyagi Prefecture in northeastern Honshu, which is the main island of Japan.

The Sichuan Basin, formerly transliterated as the Szechwan Basin, sometimes called the Red Basin, is a lowland region in southwestern China. It is surrounded by mountains on all sides and is drained by the upper Yangtze River and its tributaries.
The Stone Forest or Shilin is a notable set of limestone formations located in Shilin Yi Autonomous County, Yunnan, China.
The Taebaek Mountains are a mountain range that stretches across North Korea and South Korea. They form the main ridge of the Korean Peninsula.
The Taihang Mountains are a Chinese mountain range running down the eastern edge of the Loess Plateau in Shanxi, Henan and Hebei provinces.
The Three Gorges are three adjacent and sequential gorges along the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, in the hinterland of the People's Republic of China, known for their scenery.
Xiling Gorge is a gorge on the Yangtze River in Hubei province, China. It is the eastern and large of the Three Gorges.
The Turpan Depression or Turfan Depression is a fault-bounded trough located around and south of the city-oasis of Turpan, in the Xinjiang Autonomous Region in far Western China.
The Wudang Mountains are a mountain range in the northwestern part of Hubei, China. They are home to a famous complex of Taoist temples and monasteries.
The Yangtze Plain is made up of a series of alluvial plains along the Yangtze River and its major tributaries.
The Anadyr Highlands are a mountainous area in the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Far Eastern Federal District, Russia.
The Byrranga Mountains are a mountain range in the middle of the Taymyr Peninsula, Siberia, Russia. They are one of the least known areas of the Arctic.

The Chersky Range is a chain of mountains in northeastern Siberia between the Yana and Indigirka Rivers. Administratively, the area of the range belongs to the Sakha Republic, although a small section in the east is within Magadan Oblast.
The Dzhugdzhur or Jugjur, meaning big bulge in Evenki, are a mountain range along the western shores of the Sea of Okhotsk, located in Khabarovsk Krai in the far east of Siberia.

Dzungaria, also known as Northern Xinjiang or Beijiang, is a geographical subregion in Northwest China, consisting of the northern half of Xinjiang. It is bound by the Altai Mountains to the north and the Tian Shan mountain range to the south.
The Fergana Valley, also commonly spelled the Ferghana Valley, in Central Asia crosses eastern Uzbekistan, southern Kyrgyzstan and northern Tajikistan.
The Khangai Mountains form a range in central Mongolia, west of Ulaanbaatar.

The Khyber Pass is a mountain pass in the Khyber District of the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, along the international border with Afghanistan. It connects the town of Landi Kotal to the Valley of Peshawar.
The Kolyma Mountains or Kolyma Upland, is a system of mountain ranges in northeastern Siberia, lying mostly within the Magadan Oblast, along the shores of the Sea of Okhotsk in the Kolyma region.

The Pamir Mountains are a mountain range in Central Asia and South Asia. They are located at a junction with other notable mountain ranges, namely the Tian Shan, the Karakoram, the Kunlun, the Hindu Kush, and the Himalayas.
The Putorana Plateau or the Putorana Mountains is a mountainous area in Russia. It is a large massif or plateau crossed by mountain ranges.
The Sayan Mountains are a mountain range in southern Siberia, spanning southern Russia and northern Mongolia. The system is traditionally divided into the Western and Eastern Sayan.
The Sikhote-Alin is a mountain range in Primorsky and Khabarovsk Krais in Russia, extending to the northeast of the Russian seaport of Vladivostok on the Pacific Ocean.
Tang-e Gharu, also known as Tang-e Gharo, is a gorge and a mountain pass in the Hindu Kush mountain range of Kabul Province, Afghanistan. The Kabul River passes through the gorge, flowing eastward.
The Turan Depression, Turan Lowland or Turanian Basin is a low-lying desert basin region stretching from southern Turkmenistan through Uzbekistan to Kazakhstan.
The Verkhoyansk Range is a mountain range in the Sakha Republic, Russia, near the settlement of Verkhoyansk, known for its frigid climate. It is part of the East Siberian Mountains.
The Wakhan Corridor is a protruding strip of territory mainly in the Wakhan District of Badakhshan Province in northeastern Afghanistan.
The Yablonovy Mountains form a continuous mountain range spanning Transbaikal, Siberia, Russia. This integrated system serves as the primary watershed between the Arctic and Pacific Oceans.
The Annamite Range is a major mountain range of Mainland Southeast Asia, extending through Laos, Vietnam, and a small area in northeast Cambodia.

The Arakan Mountains, natively referred as Rakhine Yoma and technically known as the Southern Indo-Burman Range, are a mountain range in western Myanmar, between the coast of Rakhine State and the Central Myanmar Basin.
The Chocolate Hills are a geological formation in the Philippine province of Bohol. Many hills are spread across the province.
The Dieng Plateau, often called simply Dieng, is a plateau in Central Java, Indonesia that forms the floor of the caldera complex on the Dieng Volcanic Complex.
The Shan Hills, also known as Shan Highland, is a vast mountainous zone that extends through Yunnan to Myanmar and Thailand.
Taal Volcano, also known as Taal Caldera, is a large caldera filled by Taal Lake in the Philippines. It is located in the province of Batangas south of Manila.
The Tenasserim Hills or Tenasserim Range is the geographical name of a long mountain chain, part of the Indo-Malayan mountain system in Southeast Asia.
The Aare Gorge is a section of the river Aare that carves through a limestone ridge near the town of Meiringen, in the Bernese Oberland region of Switzerland.
The Apuan Alps are a mountain range in northern Tuscany, Italy. They are included between the valleys of the Serchio and Magra rivers.
The Apuseni Mountains, meaning Western Mountains in Romanian, are a mountain range in Transylvania, Romania, which belongs to the Western Romanian Carpathians.

The Belogradchik Rocks are a group of strangely shaped sandstone and conglomerate rock formations located on the western slopes of the Balkan Mountains near the town of Belogradchik in northwest Bulgaria.
The Bucegi Mountains are located in central Romania, south of the city of Brasov. They are part of the Southern Carpathians group of the Carpathian Mountains.

The Ciudad Encantada, English for Enchanted City, is a geological site near the city of Cuenca, in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain, in which the erosive forces of weather and the waters of the nearby Jucar river have formed rock shapes.
The Dinaric Alps, also Dinarides, are a mountain range in Southern and South-Central Europe, separating the continental Balkan Peninsula from the Adriatic Sea.
The Externsteine is a distinctive sandstone rock formation located in the Teutoburg Forest, near the town of Horn-Bad Meinberg in the Lippe district of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia.
The North European Plain is a geomorphological region in Europe that covers all or parts of Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, and Poland.
Finnish Lakeland or the Finnish lake district is a large landscape region in central eastern Finland. The hilly, forest-covered landscape is dominated by drumlins and by long sinuous eskers.
The Fulda Gap is an area between the Hesse-Thuringian border, the former Inner German border, and Frankfurt am Main, containing two corridors of lowlands.

The Great Glen, also known as Glen Albyn or Glen More, is a glen in Scotland running from Inverness on the edge of the Moray Firth, in an approximately straight line to Fort William at the head of Loch Linnhe.
The Harz, also called the Harz Mountains, is a highland area in northern Germany. Its rugged terrain extends across parts of Lower Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, and Thuringia.
The Saslonch Group, or the Sassolungo Group, is a massif in the western Dolomites of the Italian Alps. It separates Val Gardena from the Fassa valley.
The Melnik Earth Pyramids are rock formations, known as hoodoos, situated at the foothills of the Pirin mountain range in south-western Bulgaria.
The Ordesa Valley is a glacial valley in Aragon, in the Spanish Pyrenees which forms part of the Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park.
The Pindus, Pindos or Pindhos is a mountain range located in Northern Greece and Southern Albania.
The Mallos de Riglos, English for Mallets of Riglos, are a set of conglomerate rock formations, located in the municipality of Las Penas de Riglos, in the Hoya de Huesca comarca, in Aragon, Spain.
The Salzkammergut is a resort area in Austria, stretching from the city of Salzburg eastwards along the Alpine Foreland and the Northern Limestone Alps to the peaks of the Dachstein Mountains.
The Santorini caldera is a large, mostly submerged volcanic caldera located in the southern Aegean Sea, north of Crete in Greece. Visible above water is the circular Santorini island group.
Slovak Paradise is a mountain range in eastern Slovakia. It is a part of the Spis-Gemer Karst, which in turn is a part of the Slovak Ore Mountains, a major subdivision of the Western Carpathians.
The Suwalki Gap, also known as the Suwalki corridor, is a sparsely populated area around the border between Lithuania and Poland.
The Verdon Gorge is a river canyon located in the Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur region of Southeastern France.

Kata Tjuta, also known as The Olgas and officially gazetted as Kata Tjuta or Mount Olga, is a group of large, domed rock formations or bornhardts in the southern part of the Northern Territory, central Australia.
The MacDonnell Ranges, or Tjoritja in the Arrernte language, is a mountain range in southern Northern Territory.
Musgrave Ranges is a mountain range in Central Australia, straddling the boundary of South Australia and the Northern Territory, extending into Western Australia.
The New Guinea Highlands, also known as the Central Range or Central Cordillera, is a long chain of mountain ranges on the island of New Guinea.

The Nullarbor Plain is part of the area of flat, almost treeless, arid or semi-arid country of southern Australia, located on the Great Australian Bight coast with the Great Victoria Desert to its north.
Oued El Abiod, English for Abiod Valley, is a wadi that forms a mountain pass in the Aures massif, located in the Saharan Atlas in northeastern Algeria.

Amojjar Pass is a mountain pass in the Adrar Plateau in the centre of Adrar, near Atar, Mauritania. The pink-brown sandstone of the pass was worn away by repeated cycles of extreme dryness interrupted by torrential rain.
The Andringitra Massif, meaning desert of rocks, is a granite massif located within Andringitra National Park in Madagascar.
Ankarana Special Reserve is a protected area in northern Madagascar. It is a small, partially vegetated plateau composed of middle Jurassic limestone.

The High Atlas, also called the Grand Atlas, is a mountain range in central Morocco, North Africa, the high part of the Atlas Mountains. The High Atlas rises in the west at the Atlantic Ocean and stretches in an eastern direction.

Balancing rocks are found in many parts of Zimbabwe. These geomorphological features are formed of igneous rocks. Particularly noteworthy balancing rocks are located in Matobo National Park and near the township of Epworth.
The Dades Gorges, also referred to as Dades Valley, are a series of rugged wadi gorges carved out by the Dades River in Morocco. The river originates in the High Atlas range of the Atlas mountains.
El Kantara is a town and commune in the eponymous El Kantara Province in Algeria, serving as the provincial capital.
Fouta Djallon is a highland region in the center of Guinea, roughly corresponding with Middle Guinea, in West Africa.

The Great Escarpment is a major topographical feature in Africa that consists of steep slopes from the high central Southern African plateau downward in the direction of the oceans that surround southern Africa on three sides.
The Highveld is the portion of the South African inland plateau which has a high altitude, thus excluding the Lesotho mountain regions to the south-east of the Highveld.
The Hoggar Mountains are a highland region in the central Sahara in southern Algeria, along the Tropic of Cancer. The mountains are home to the Ahaggar Cultural Park.
The Jugurtha Tableland is a large mesa near the town of Kalaat es Senan, Tunisia, which stands high above the Ez-Zghalma plain.
The Mandara Mountains are a volcanic range extending along the northern part of the Cameroon and Nigeria border, from the Benue River in the south to the north-west of Maroua in the north.
The Marrah Mountains or Marra Mountains are a range of volcanic peaks in a massif in Sudan. They are the high mountains of Sudan.

The Rwenzori, also known as the Ruwenzori, Rwenzururu or Rwenjura, are a range of mountains in eastern equatorial Africa, located on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The Tibesti Mountains are a mountain range in the central Sahara, primarily located in the extreme north of Chad, with a small portion located in southern Libya.
The Todgha Gorges are a series of limestone river canyons, or wadi, in the eastern part of the High Atlas Mountains in Morocco, near the town of Tinghir.

Emi Koussi, also known as Emi Koussou, is a high pyroclastic shield volcano that lies at the southeast end of the Tibesti Mountains in the central Sahara, in the northern Borkou Region of northern Chad.
Menengai Crater is a massive shield volcano with a huge caldera, in the Great Rift Valley, Kenya.

Mount Nyiragongo is an active stratovolcano in the Virunga Mountains associated with the Albertine Rift. It is located inside Virunga National Park, in the North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Ras Dashen is the high mountain in Ethiopia. Located in the Simien Mountains National Park in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region.
Mount Stanley, also known as Mount Ngaliema, is a mountain located in the Rwenzori range. It is the high mountain of both the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
Teide or Mount Teide is an active stratovolcano on the Spanish island of Tenerife, part of the Canary Islands. Its summit is the high point in Spain.
Toubkal, also Jbel Toubkal or Jebel Toubkal, is a mountain in central Morocco, located in the Toubkal National Park. It is the high peak in Morocco and the Atlas Mountains.
Trou aux Cerfs, also known as Murr's Volcano, is a dormant, crater lake, cinder cone volcano with a well-defined cone and crater. It is located in Curepipe, Mauritius.
Mount Erebus is an active volcano located on Ross Island in the Ross Dependency in Antarctica.
Mount Sidley is a dormant volcano in Antarctica, and a member of the Volcanic Seven Summits. It is a massive, mainly snow-covered shield volcano.

Mount Ararat, officially Mount Agri, also known as Masis, is a snow-capped and dormant compound volcano and a stratovolcano in eastern Turkey. It consists of two major volcanic cones: Greater Ararat and Little Ararat.
Avachinsky, also known as Avacha or Avacha Volcano or Avachinskaya Sopka, is an active stratovolcano in Russia. It is situated on the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East.
The Bromo, or Mount Bromo, is an active somma volcano, a Hindu pilgrimage site, and part of the Tengger mountains, in East Java, Indonesia.
Mount Damavand is a dormant stratovolcano in Iran. It is the high peak in Iran and Western Asia.
Hallasan is a shield volcano comprising much of Jeju Island in South Korea. Its summit is the high point in the country.
Ismoil Somoni Peak is the high mountain in Tajikistan. The mountain is named after Ismail Samani, a ruler of the Samanid Empire.
Mount Kinabalu is the high mountain in Malaysia and Maritime Southeast Asia, located on the island of Borneo in Sabah.
Klyuchevskaya Sopka is an active stratovolcano, the high mountain of Siberia and a high active volcano of Eurasia. Its steep, symmetrical cone rises inland from the Bering Sea.
Koryaksky or Koryakskaya Sopka is an active volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East. It lies within sight of the administrative center of Kamchatka Krai, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky.

Mayon, also known as Mount Mayon and Mayon Volcano, is an active stratovolcano in the province of Albay in Bicol, Philippines. A popular tourist destination, it is renowned for its perfect cone owing to its symmetric conical shape.
Mount Merapi is an active stratovolcano located on the border between the province of Central Java and the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia.
Mount Paektu or Mount Baekdu is an active stratovolcano on the Chinese and North Korean border. In China, it is known as Changbai Mountain.
Mount Papandayan is a complex stratovolcano, located in Garut Regency, to the southeast of the city of Bandung in West Java, Indonesia.
Sahand is a massive, heavily eroded stratovolcano in East Azerbaijan Province, northwestern Iran.
Mount Tambora, or Tomboro, is an active stratovolcano in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Located on Sumbawa in the Lesser Sunda Islands, volcanism is the result of subduction zones.
Yu Shan or Yushan, also called Mount Niitaka during Japanese rule, is the high mountain in Taiwan.
Mount Emei, alternatively Mount Omei, is a mountain in Sichuan Province, China, and is one of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains of China. Mount Emei sits at the western rim of the Sichuan Basin.
The Fanjingshan or Mount Fanjing, located in Tongren, Guizhou province, is the high peak of the Wuling Mountains in southeastern China.
Hengshan, also known as Mount Heng, is a mountain in southcentral China's Hunan Province known as the southern mountain of the Five Great Mountains of China.
Mount Heng, also known by its Chinese name Hengshan, is a mountain in north-central China's Shanxi Province, known as the northern mountain of the Five Great Mountains of China.
Mount Hua is a mountain near the city of Huayin in Shaanxi Province, east of Xian. It is the Western Mountain of the Five Great Mountains of China and has a long history of religious significance.
Huangshan, literally meaning the Yellow Mountain, is a mountain range in southern Anhui province in eastern China. It was renamed because of a legend that the Yellow Emperor once made alchemy here.
Mount Jiuhua, in Chizhou, Anhui Province in China, is an important Buddhist site and natural scenic spot.
Mount Lu, or Lushan, is a mountain in Jiujiang, Jiangxi, China. It was also known as Kuanglu in ancient times.
Mount Putuo is an island in Putuo District, Zhoushan, Zhejiang, China. It is a renowned site in Chinese Buddhism and the sacred place of the bodhisattva Guanyin.

Mount Song is an isolated mountain range in north central China, in Henan Province, along the southern bank of the Yellow River. It is known in literary and folk tradition as the central mountain of the Five Great Mountains of China.
Mount Wutai, also known as Wutaishan and Mount Qingliang, is a sacred Buddhist site at the headwaters of the Qingshui in Shanxi Province, China.

Annapurna is a mountain in the Annapurna range of Gandaki Province, north central Nepal. It is the tenth high mountain in the world at eight thousand and ninety one metres above sea level and is well known for the difficulty and danger involved in its ascent.

Broad Peak is the twelfth high mountain in the world, at eight thousand and fifty one metres above sea level. It is one of the eight-thousanders, and lies in the Karakoram range spanning Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, and Xinjiang, China.
Cho Oyu is the sixth high mountain in the world, at eight thousand one hundred and eighty eight metres above sea level. Cho Oyu means Turquoise Goddess in Tibetan.
Dhaulagiri, in Nepal, is the seventh high mountain in the world, at eight thousand one hundred and sixty seven metres above sea level, and the high mountain within the borders of a single country.

Gasherbrum I, originally surveyed as K five, and also known as Hidden Peak, is the eleventh high mountain in the world, at eight thousand and eighty metres above sea level. It lies between Shigar District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, and Tashkurgan in China.

Gasherbrum II, originally surveyed as K four, is the thirteenth high mountain in the world, at eight thousand and thirty five metres above sea level. It lies in the Karakoram, on the border between Gilgit-Baltistan and China.

Lhotse is the fourth high mountain on Earth, after Mount Everest, K two, and Kangchenjunga. The main summit is on the border between the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and the Khumbu region of Nepal.
Kangchenjunga is the third high mountain in the world. Its summit lies at eight thousand five hundred and eighty six metres in a section of the Himalayas, the Kangchenjunga Himal.
Makalu is the fifth high mountain on Earth. It lies in the Mahalangur Himalayas, nineteen kilometres southeast of Mount Everest, on the China-Nepal border.

Manaslu is the eighth high mountain in the world, at eight thousand one hundred and sixty three metres above sea level. It is in the Mansiri Himal, part of the Nepalese Himalayas, in west central Nepal.
Nanga Parbat, known in Shina as Diamer, is the ninth high mountain on Earth, with its summit at eight thousand one hundred and twenty six metres above sea level.

Shishapangma, or Shishasbangma or Xixiabangma, is the fourteenth high mountain in the world, at eight thousand and twenty seven metres above sea level. It is the low eight-thousander, and lies entirely within Tibet.
Mount Asama is an active stratovolcano in central Honshu, the main island of Japan. The volcano is very active on Honshu.
Mount Hotaka, also known as Mount Hotakadake, is one of the hundred Famous Japanese Mountains. It lies in Japan's Hida Mountains.

Mount Kita is a mountain of the Akaishi Mountains, the Southern Alps, in Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It is the second high mountain in Japan, after Mount Fuji, and is known as the Leader of the Southern Alps.
Sakurajima is an active stratovolcano, formerly an island and now a peninsula, in Kagoshima Prefecture in Kyushu, Japan. It is a very active volcano in Japan.
Mount Athos is a mountain on the Athos peninsula in northeastern Greece, directly on the Aegean Sea. It is an important center of Eastern Orthodox monasticism.

Ben Nevis is the high mountain in Scotland, the United Kingdom, and the British Isles. It stands at the western end of the Grampian Mountains in the Highland region of Lochaber, close to the town of Fort William.
Benbulbin, sometimes Benbulben or Ben Bulben, is a steep-sided and flat-topped mountain in County Sligo, Ireland. It is part of the Dartry Mountains, in an area sometimes called Yeats Country.
The Eiger is a mountain of the Bernese Alps, overlooking Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland, just north of the main watershed and border with Valais.
The Grossglockner, or just Glockner, is the high mountain in Austria and high mountain in the Alps east of the Brenner Pass. It is part of the larger Glockner Group of the Hohe Tauern range.
Hekla, or Hecla, is an active stratovolcano in the south of Iceland. It is one of the active volcanoes of Iceland, with many eruptions in and around it since the year twelve ten.

The Jungfrau is one of the main summits of the Bernese Alps, between the southern canton of Bern and the northern canton of Valais, halfway between Interlaken and Fiesch. Together with the Eiger and Monch, it forms a massive wall.
Kinnekulle is a flat-topped mountain in the county of Vastergotland, southwestern Sweden, on the eastern shore of lake Vanern.
The Monch is a mountain in the Bernese Alps, in Switzerland. Together with the Eiger and the Jungfrau, it forms a highly recognisable group of mountains, visible from far away.
Mount Parnassus is a mountain range in Central Greece that is, and historically has been, culturally and religiously valuable to the Greek nation and the earlier Greek city-states.

Stromboli is an island in the Tyrrhenian Sea, off the north coast of Sicily, containing Mount Stromboli, one of the four active volcanoes in Italy. It is one of the seven Aeolian Islands and the mythological home of Aeolus.

The Zugspitze is the high peak of the Wetterstein Mountains and the high mountain in Germany. It lies south of the town of Garmisch-Partenkirchen in Bavaria, and the Austria-Germany border is on its western summit.
Cape Farewell is a headland on the southern shore of Egger Island, Nunap Isua Archipelago, Greenland. As the southern point of the country, it is one of the important landmarks of Greenland.
Cape Crillon, known as Cape Nishinotoro in Japan, is the southern point of Sakhalin. The cape was named by Frenchman Jean-Francois de La Perouse, who was a European to discover it.
Cape Eluanbi or Oluanpi, also known by other names, is the southern point on the island of Taiwan. It lies in Eluanbi Park within the Hengchun Township in Pingtung County.
Cape Lopatka is the southern point of Kamchatka Peninsula, Russia. It lies about eleven kilometres north of Shumshu, the northern island of the Kuril Islands.
Cape Zhelaniya is a headland in the Russian Federation. It is an important geographical landmark. The area in the vicinity of the cape is a desolate place, exposed to bitter Arctic winters.
The Isthmus of Chignecto is an isthmus bordering the Maritime provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia that connects the Nova Scotia peninsula with the main part of North America.

The Isthmus of Perekop, literally the Isthmus of the Trench, is the narrow strip of land that connects the Crimean Peninsula to the mainland of Ukraine. It projects between the Black Sea to the west and the Syvash.
South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands is a British Overseas Territory in the southern Atlantic Ocean. It is a remote and inhospitable collection of islands.
The De Long Islands are an uninhabited archipelago often included as part of the New Siberian Islands, lying northeast of Novaya Sibir.
Mount Caubvick is a mountain in Canada on the border between Labrador and Quebec, in the Selamiut Range of the Torngat Mountains. It is the high point of Quebec and of Newfoundland and Labrador.
Mount Fairweather is a mountain east of the Pacific Ocean on the Canada-United States border. It is the tall mountain in British Columbia.

Mount Logan is the high mountain in Canada, and the second high peak in North America after Denali. The mountain was named after Sir William Edmond Logan, a Canadian geologist and founder of the Geological Survey of Canada.
Mount Saint Elias is a mountain near the Pacific Ocean on the Yukon-Alaska border. It is the second high mountain in both Canada and the United States.
Volcan de Agua, Spanish for Volcano of Water, also known as Junajpu by the Maya, is an extinct stratovolcano in the departments of Sacatepequez and Escuintla in Guatemala.
The Irazu Volcano is an active volcano in Costa Rica, in the Cordillera Central near the city of Cartago.

Santa Maria Volcano is a large active volcano in the western highlands of Guatemala, in the Quetzaltenango Department near the city of Quetzaltenango. It is part of the mountain range of the Sierra Madre.
Nevado de Toluca is a stratovolcano in central Mexico, west of Mexico City near the city of Toluca. It is the fourth high of Mexico's peaks, after Pico de Orizaba, Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl.
Paricutin is a cinder cone volcano in the Mexican state of Michoacan, near the city of Uruapan. The volcano surged suddenly from the cornfield of a local farmer.
Citlaltepetl, otherwise known as Pico de Orizaba, is an active volcano and the high volcano in North America, as well as the high mountain in Mexico.
Popocatepetl is an active stratovolcano in the states of Puebla, Morelos, and Mexico in central Mexico. It lies in the eastern half of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt.
The Volcan de Colima, also known as Volcan de Fuego, is part of the Colima Volcanic Complex, consisting of Volcan de Colima, Nevado de Colima and the eroded El Cantaro. It is the young of the three.
Mount Adams is a stratovolcano in the Cascade Range of Washington, United States. It is the second high mountain in Washington and a prominent feature within the Cascade Volcanic Arc.

Mount Baker, also known as Koma Kulshan or simply Kulshan, is an active glacier-covered andesitic stratovolcano in the Cascade Volcanic Arc and the North Cascades of Washington State in the United States.
Mount Blackburn is the high peak in the Wrangell Mountains of Alaska in the United States.
Black Elk Peak, formerly known as Harney Peak, is the high natural point in the Black Hills mountain range and the United States state of South Dakota.
Borah Peak, also known as Mount Borah or Beauty Peak, is a mountain in the western United States and the high summit in Idaho. It lies in central Idaho in the central section of the Lost River Range.

Mount Elbert is the high summit of the Rocky Mountains of North America. It is also the high point in the United States state of Colorado and the second high summit in the contiguous United States after Mount Whitney.

Mount Gannett is a peak in the Chugach Mountains of eastern Alaska, United States, east of the city of Anchorage. It was named by Lawrence Martin of the Geological Survey in nineteen eleven for Henry Gannett.
Glacier Peak, or Dakobed, is a stratovolcano in the United States state of Washington. It lies in the Glacier Peak Wilderness in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
Mount Graham is a mountain in Graham County, Arizona, United States, northeast of Tucson. In Western Apache it is called Big Seated Mountain.
Grand Teton is the high mountain of the Teton Range in Grand Teton National Park in northwest Wyoming. Below its north face is Teton Glacier.

Mount Hood is an active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range and is a member of the Cascade Volcanic Arc. It was formed by a subduction zone on the Pacific Coast and rests in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States.

Mount Mitchell, Attakulla in Cherokee, is the high peak of the Appalachian Mountains and the high peak in mainland North America east of the Mississippi River. It lies near Burnsville in Yancey County, North Carolina.
Pikes Peak, or Americas Mountain, is an ultra-prominent fourteener of the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains of North America. It is the eastern fourteener in the United States.

Mount Rainier, also known as Tahoma, is a large, active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range of the Pacific Northwest in the United States. The mountain lies in Mount Rainier National Park, south of Seattle.
Mount Shasta is a potentially active stratovolcano at the southern end of the Cascade Range in Siskiyou County, California. It is the second high peak in the Cascades.
Mount Washington is an ultra-prominent mountain in the state of New Hampshire. It is the high peak in the Northeastern United States.
Wheeler Peak is the tall mountain in the Snake Range and in White Pine County, in Nevada, United States. It is the second high peak in Nevada, just behind Boundary Peak.

Mount Whitney is a mountain in the Sierra Nevada range of California, and is the high point in the contiguous United States. It lies in east central California along the border of Inyo and Tulare counties.
Mount Williamson is the second high mountain in both the Sierra Nevada range and the state of California.
Aoraki or Mount Cook is the high mountain in New Zealand. It is situated in the Southern Alps, the mountain range that runs the length of the South Island.

Haleakala, or the East Maui Volcano, is a massive, active shield volcano that forms much of the Hawaiian Island of Maui. The western part of the island is formed by another volcano, Mauna Kahalawai, also referred to as the West Maui Mountains.

Mount Ruapehu is an active stratovolcano at the southern end of the Taupo Volcanic Zone and North Island volcanic plateau in New Zealand. It lies northeast of Ohakune and southwest of the southern shore of Lake Taupo, within Tongariro National Park.
Ulawun is an active stratovolcano in West New Britain Province, on the island of New Britain in Papua New Guinea. It is the high mountain in New Britain and the second in the Bismarck Archipelago.
Whakaari or White Island, Maori Te Puia Whakaari, literally the dramatic volcano, is an active andesite stratovolcano off the east coast of the North Island of New Zealand.
Cerro Sarisarinama is a tepui, a flat-topped mountain in Jaua-Sarisarinama National Park at the far southwest of Bolivar State, Venezuela, near the border with Brazil.
Chimborazo is a stratovolcano in Ecuador and the Cordillera Occidental range of the Andes.

Cotopaxi is an active stratovolcano in the Andes Mountains, in Cotopaxi National Park in Cotopaxi Province, south of Quito and northeast of the city of Latacunga, Ecuador. It is the second high summit in Ecuador, after Chimborazo.

Monte Fitz Roy, also known as Cerro Chalten, is a mountain in Patagonia, on the border between Argentina and Chile. It lies in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, near El Chalten village and Viedma Lake.
Galeras is an active stratovolcano in the Colombian department of Narino, near the departmental capital Pasto.
Illimani is a prominent fold mountain within the Cordillera Real of Bolivia, a subrange of the greater Andes, southeast of La Paz.
Llullaillaco is a dormant stratovolcano on the border between Argentina and Chile. It is part of the Llullaillaco National Park and lies in the Puna de Atacama, a region of tall volcanoes.
Misti is a volcano in the southern Peruvian Andes, rising above Arequipa, the second large city of Peru. It has a steep conical profile and two nested summit craters.
Nevado Sajama is an extinct volcano and the high peak in Bolivia. The mountain is in Sajama Province, in Oruro Department.
Pico Bolivar is the high mountain in Venezuela. It lies in Merida State.
Pico da Neblina is the high mountain in Brazil. It rises in northwestern Amazonas, in the Serra da Neblina of the Serra do Imeri, near the southern edge of the Guiana Highlands.
Sugarloaf Mountain, Portuguese Pao de Acucar, is a peak in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on a peninsula at the mouth of Guanabara Bay.
Nevado Ojos del Salado is a dormant complex volcano in the Andes on the Argentina-Chile border. It is the high volcano on Earth and the high peak in Chile.

Tronador is an extinct stratovolcano in the southern Andes, along the border between Argentina and Chile, near the Argentine city of Bariloche. The mountain was named Tronador, Spanish for Thunderer, by locals in reference to the sound of falling seracs.

Bondi Beach is a beach and the surrounding suburb in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. It lies east of the Sydney central business district, in the local government area of Waverley Council, in the Eastern Suburbs.
Copacabana is a Brazilian neighbourhood in the South Zone of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is prominently known for its balneario beach, which is one of the famous in the world.
The Caves of Aggtelek Karst and Slovak Karst are a series of karst caves spread out over a large area along the border of Hungary and Slovakia.
Aven Armand is a limestone cave in the Cevennes National Park of France, in the Lozere departement, between Meyrueis and Sainte-Enimie, known for a tall stalagmite.
The Kimberley Mine, or Tim Kuilmine, Afrikaans Groot Gat, literally Big Hole, is an open-pit and underground mine in Kimberley, South Africa.

The Cango Caves are in Precambrian limestones at the foothills of the Swartberg range near the town of Oudtshoorn, in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. The principal cave is a popular tourist cave.

The Candelaria Caves are a large natural cave system in the highland-lowland transition of Alta Verapaz in Guatemala, between the municipalities of Chisec and Raxruha. The caves are famous for their peculiar karst phenomena and significance to Mayan history.
The Cave of Swallows, also called the Cave of the Swallows, is an open-air pit cave in the municipality of Aquismon, San Luis Potosi, Mexico.
The Chinhoyi Caves, previously the Sinoia Caves, are a group of limestone and dolomite caves in north central Zimbabwe.

The Eisriesenwelt, German for World of the Ice Giants, is a natural limestone and ice cave in Werfen, Austria, south of Salzburg. The cave is inside the Hochkogel mountain in the Tennengebirge section of the Alps.
Fingal's Cave is a sea cave on the uninhabited island of Staffa, in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland, known for its natural acoustics.
The Frasassi Caves are a karst cave system in the municipality of Genga, Italy, in the province of Ancona, Marche. They are among the famous show caves in Italy.
The Caves of Han-sur-Lesse are a natural complex of caves in Belgium. A major Belgian tourist attraction, the caves lie in Wallonia, on the outskirts of the village of Han-sur-Lesse.
Son Doong Cave, in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, Quang Tri province, Vietnam, is a large natural cave. It lies near the Laos-Vietnam border and has an internal, fast-flowing subterranean river.
The Holloch, English Hellhole, is a long cave in the municipality of Muotathal in Switzerland. It is also notable for having great depth.
The Jeita Grotto is a system of two separate, but interconnected, karstic limestone caves. The caves are in the Nahr al-Kalb river valley within the locality of Jeita, north of Beirut.

The Jenolan Caves are limestone caves within the Jenolan Karst Conservation Reserve in the Central Tablelands region, west of the Blue Mountains, in Jenolan, Oberon Council, New South Wales, in eastern Australia.
Jewel Cave National Monument contains Jewel Cave, a long cave with many miles of mapped passageways.
La Verna is a show cave in the commune of Sainte-Engrace in the department of Pyrenees-Atlantiques in France. A mined tunnel leads into the Salle de la Verna, a huge chamber in a show cave.
Lechuguilla Cave is a cave in Carlsbad Caverns National Park, New Mexico, United States, known for its unusual geology, rare formations, and pristine condition.
Ledenika is a cave in the northwestern parts of the Balkan Mountains, near the Bulgarian city of Vratsa.
Leviathan Cave, also known as the Grotte de Leviathan, is a lava tube in eastern Kenya.
The Lurgrotte karst cave is a large cave in the Eastern Alps of Styria, Austria. It lies north of Graz and crosses the Tannenben karst region.
Neptune's Grotto is a stalactite cave near the town of Alghero on the island of Sardinia, Italy. The cave was discovered by local fishermen and has since developed into a popular tourist attraction.
Optymistychna Cave, Ukrainian for optimistic, is a gypsum cave near the Ukrainian village of Korolivka, Chortkiv Raion, Ternopil Oblast.
Pinargozu Cave, Turkish for eye of the water, is a cave west of the town of Yenisarbademli in Isparta Province, Turkey. It is considered the long cave in Turkey.
Postojna Cave is a long karst cave system near Postojna, southwestern Slovenia. It is one of the top tourism sites of the country.

Scarisoara Cave is one of the big ice caves in the Apuseni Mountains of Romania, in the western part of the Romanian Carpathians. It is considered a show cave and one of the natural wonders of Romania.
Sof Omar Caves is the long cave in Ethiopia.
Thien Duong Cave, or Paradise Cave, is a cave in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, a World Heritage Site.
Veryovkina Cave is a cave in Abkhazia, Georgia. It is a deep cave on Earth, in the Arabika Massif, in the Gagra mountain range of the Western Caucasus.
Etretat is a commune in the Seine-Maritime department in the Normandy region of Northwestern France. It is a tourist and farming town near Le Havre.
Cap de Formentor is the northern point of Mallorca, on the Formentor peninsula.

Delicate Arch is a freestanding natural arch in Arches National Park, near Moab in Grand County, Utah, United States. The arch is a widely recognized landmark in Arches National Park and is depicted on Utah license plates.

Mons Klint is a stretch of limestone and chalk cliffs along the eastern coast of the Danish island of Mon in the Baltic Sea, and a World Heritage Site. Some of the cliffs fall a sheer drop to the sea below.
The Old Man of Hoy is a sea stack on Hoy, part of the Orkney archipelago off the north coast of Scotland. Formed from Old Red Sandstone, it is one of the tall stacks in the United Kingdom.
Perce Rock is a huge sheer rock formation in the Gulf of Saint Lawrence on the tip of the Gaspe Peninsula in Quebec, Canada, off Perce Bay. Perce Rock appears from a distance like a ship under sail.
La Portada is a natural arch on the coast of Chile, north of Antofagasta. It is one of fifteen natural monuments included among the protected areas of Chile.

Puente del Inca, English Bridge of the Inca, is a natural arch that forms a bridge over the Las Cuevas River, a tributary of the Mendoza River. It lies near the small village of Puente del Inca, in Las Heras Department, Mendoza Province, Argentina.
Rainbow Bridge is a natural arch in southern Utah, United States. It is one of the large natural arches in the world.
Meteor Crater, or Barringer Crater, is an impact crater east of Flagstaff and west of Winslow in the desert of northern Arizona, United States.
The Popigai impact structure is the eroded remnant of an impact crater in northern Siberia, Russia. It is a large verified impact structure on Earth.
The Sudbury Basin, also known as Sudbury Structure or the Sudbury Nickel Irruptive, is a major geological structure in Ontario, Canada. It is among the old and large known impact structures on Earth.
The Vredefort impact structure is one of the large impact structures on Earth. The crater, which has since been worn away, was large when it was formed.

The Bonneville Salt Flats are a densely packed salt pan in Tooele County in northwestern Utah, United States. A remnant of the Pleistocene Lake Bonneville, it is the large salt flat west of the Great Salt Lake.

Chott el Djerid, also spelled Sciott Gerid and Shott el Jerid, is a chott, a large endorheic salt lake in central Tunisia. The name can be translated from the Arabic into English as Lagoon of the Land of Palms.

The Etosha Pan is a large endorheic salt pan, forming part of the Cuvelai-Etosha Basin in the north of Namibia. It is a vast hollow in the ground in which water may collect or in which a deposit of salt remains after water has evaporated.
The Dune of Pilat, also called Grande Dune du Pilat, is the tall sand dune in Europe. It lies in La Teste-de-Buch in the Arcachon Bay area, France, southwest of Bordeaux along the Atlantic coastline.
The Badain Jaran Desert is a desert in Gansu and Inner Mongolia, China.
The Great Salt Desert, or Kavir Desert, Persian Dasht-e Kavir, meaning Low Plains, is a large desert lying in the middle of the Iranian Plateau.
Lut Desert, Persian Dasht-e Lut, meaning Plain of Emptiness, is a desert with both extensive salt flats and dunes in the provinces of Kerman and Sistan-Baluchestan, Iran.
The Great Basin Desert is part of the Great Basin between the Sierra Nevada and the Wasatch Range in the western United States.
The Great Sandy Desert is an interim Australian bioregion in the northeast of Western Australia, straddling the Pilbara and southern Kimberley regions and extending east into the Northern Territory.
The Karoo is a semidesert natural region of South Africa. No exact definition of what constitutes the Karoo is available, so its extent is also not precisely defined.
The Kyzylkum Desert, Uzbek Qizilqum, is a large desert. Its name means Red Sand in Turkic languages.

The Loess Plateau is a plateau in north central China formed of loess, a clastic silt-like sediment formed by the accumulation of wind-blown dust. It is located southeast of the Gobi Desert and is surrounded by the Yellow River.
The Libyan Desert is a geographical region filling the northeastern Sahara Desert, from eastern Libya to the Western Desert of Egypt and far northwestern Sudan.

Death Valley is a desert valley in Eastern California, United States, in the northern Mojave Desert, bordering the Great Basin Desert. The World Meteorological Organization lists Death Valley as the site of a very hot surface temperature recorded on Earth.
The Nubian Desert is in the eastern region of the Sahara Desert, spanning northeastern Sudan and northern Eritrea, between the Nile and the Red Sea.
The Painted Desert is a United States desert of badlands in the Four Corners area, running from near the east end of Grand Canyon National Park and southeast into Petrified Forest National Park.
The Patagonian Desert, also known as the Patagonian Steppe, is a large desert in Argentina. It is located primarily in Argentina.
Pobiti Kamani, tubular concretions formed around rising methane-bearing fluid plumes, is a desert-like rock phenomenon on the northwest Varna Province border in Bulgaria.
Rabjerg Mile is a migrating coastal dune between Skagen and Frederikshavn, Denmark. It is a large moving dune in Northern Europe.
The Rub al Khali is a desert encompassing much of the southern third of the Arabian Peninsula. The desert covers parts of Saudi Arabia, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, and Yemen.
The Sechura Desert is a coastal desert south of the Piura Region of Peru along the Pacific coast and inland to the foothills of the Andes Mountains.

The Seven Coloured Earths are a geological formation and prominent tourist attraction in the Chamarel plain of the Riviere Noire District in southwestern Mauritius. It is a relatively small area of sand dunes comprising sand of seven distinct colours.

The Sonoran Desert is a hot desert and ecoregion in North America that covers parts of the northwestern Mexican states of Sonora, Baja California, and Baja California Sur, as well as part of the Southwestern United States, in Arizona and California.
The Syrian desert, also known as the North Arabian desert, the Jordanian steppe, the Syrian steppe, or the Badiya, is a region of desert, semi-desert, and steppe in West Asia.

Al-Ahsa Oasis, also known as Al-Hasa or Hajar, is an oasis and historical region in eastern Saudi Arabia. Al-Ahsa Governorate, which makes up much of the Eastern Province of the country, is named after it.
Bahariya Oasis is a depression and a naturally rich oasis in the Western Desert of Egypt.
Beni Abbes, also known as the Pearl of the Saoura, and also as the White Oasis, is a town and commune in western Algeria in Bechar Province.
Bilma is an oasis town and commune in northeast Niger. It lies protected from the desert dunes under the Kaouar Cliffs and is the large town along the Kaouar escarpment.
Dakhla Oasis, or Dakhleh Oasis, is one of the seven oases of the Western Desert of Egypt. It lies in the New Valley Governorate, between the oases of Farafra and Kharga.
Ein Gedi, also spelled En Gedi, meaning spring of the kid, is an oasis and a nature reserve in Israel, west of the Dead Sea, near Masada and the Qumran Caves.
The Kharga Oasis, literally the outer, is one of the western oases of Egypt. It is in the Western Desert of Egypt.
Nefta, or Naftah, is a Tunisian municipality and an oasis in Tozeur Governorate north of the Chott el Djerid.

The Llanos is a vast tropical grassland plain east of the Andes in Colombia and Venezuela, in northwestern South America. It is an ecoregion of the tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas, and shrublands biome.

The Serengeti is a geographical region in Africa, spanning the Mara and Arusha Regions of Tanzania and extending to southwestern Kenya. The protected area within the region includes the Serengeti National Park.

The Sudanian savanna, or Sudan region, is a broad belt of tropical savanna that runs east and west across the African continent, from the Ethiopian Highlands in the east to the Atlantic Ocean in the west.

The Atlantic Forest, Portuguese Mata Atlantica, is a moist broadleaf forest that extends along the Atlantic coast of Brazil from Rio Grande do Norte state in the northeast to Rio Grande do Sul state in the south.

The Black Forest is a large forested mountain range in the state of Baden-Wurttemberg in southwest Germany, bounded by the Rhine Valley to the west and south and close to the borders with France and Switzerland. It is the source of the Danube and Neckar rivers.
The boreal forest of Canada is a vast region comprising a large part of the circumpolar boreal forest that rings the Northern Hemisphere.
The Borneo lowland rain forests is an ecoregion, within the tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests biome, of the large island of Borneo in Southeast Asia.
The Hyrcanian forests are a zone of lush lowland and montane forests near the shores of the Caspian Sea in Iran and Azerbaijan. The forest is named after the ancient region of Hyrcania.

The Pacific temperate rainforests of western North America is one of the large temperate rain forest regions on the planet. They lie along the western side of the Pacific Coast Ranges along the Pacific Northwest Coast.
Sherwood Forest consists of the remnants of an ancient royal forest in Nottinghamshire, in the East Midlands region of England. It is associated with the legend of Robin Hood.
The Virgin Komi Forests is a natural UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Northern Ural Mountains of the Komi Republic, Russia. It is a large virgin forest in Europe.
Protected areas or conservation areas are locations that receive protection because of their recognized natural or cultural values.

A nature reserve, also known as a wildlife refuge, wildlife preserve, wildlife reserve, sanctuary, biosphere reserve or bioreserve, is a protected area of importance for flora, fauna, funga, or features of geological or other special interest.
Central Kalahari Game Reserve is an extensive national park in the Kalahari Desert of Botswana. Established in nineteen sixty one, it is larger than the Netherlands.
The Comoe National Park is a Biosphere Reserve and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Zanzan and Savanes districts of northeastern Ivory Coast. It is the large protected area in West Africa.
The Ennedi Plateau is in the northeast of Chad, in the regions of Ennedi-Ouest and Ennedi-Est. It is considered a part of the group of mountains known as the Ennedi Massif.
Golden Gate Highlands National Park is in Free State, South Africa, near the Lesotho border.
Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park is a large peace park that is in the process of being formed.
Kruger National Park is a national park in South Africa in the provinces of Limpopo and Mpumalanga in the northeast of the country.
Manovo-Gounda St Floris National Park is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Central African Republic prefecture Bamingui-Bangoran, near the Chad border.

Maasai Mara, sometimes also spelt Masai Mara and locally known simply as the Mara, is a large national game reserve in Narok County, Kenya, contiguous with the Serengeti National Park in Tanzania. It is named in honour of the Maasai people.
The Okapi Wildlife Reserve is a wildlife reserve in the Ituri Forest in the northeast of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, near the borders with South Sudan and Uganda.
Altai Nature Reserve is a Russian zapovednik, a strict nature reserve, in the Altai Mountains of south Siberia, Russia. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Golden Mountains of Altai.
Band-e Amir National Park is in the central Bamyan Province of Afghanistan. It was established as a national park to promote and protect the natural beauty of a series of intensely blue lakes.
Chitwan National Park is a national park of Nepal, established as Royal Chitwan National Park. It was granted the status of a World Heritage Site.
Goreme Historical National Park is a national park in Cappadocia in central Turkey. It is in Nevsehir Province.
The Great Arctic State Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia. It is the large reserve of Russia and Eurasia, as well as one of the large in the world.
Jim Corbett National Park is a national park in the Nainital district of the state of Uttarakhand, India. It is named in honour of Jim Corbett, who had played a leading role in its establishment.
