Lorentz National Park is an Indonesian national park in the provinces of Central Papua, Highland Papua and South Papua, in the southwest of western New Guinea.
Hoh Xil or Kekexili, Mongolian for Blue Ridge, is an isolated region in the northeastern part of Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

Kronotsky Nature Reserve, also Kronotsky Biosphere Zapovednik, is a Russian zapovednik, a strict nature reserve, reserved for the study of natural sciences in the remote Russian Far East, on the coast of the Kamchatka Peninsula.
Phong Nha-Ke Bang is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site in central Quang Tri Province in the North Central Coast region of Vietnam.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park is a protected area in the Philippines. The park is in the Saint Paul Mountain Range on the western coast of the island of Palawan.
Setonaikai National Park is a Japanese national park, comprising areas of the Seto Inland Sea of Japan and of ten bordering prefectures.
Sundarbans National Park is a national park in West Bengal, India, and core part of tiger reserve and biosphere reserve. It is part of the Sundarbans on the Ganges Delta.
Taroko National Park is one of the national parks in Taiwan and was named after the Taroko Gorge, the landmark gorge of the park carved by the Liwu River.

The Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Yunnan province, China. It lies within the drainage basins of the upper reaches of the Jinsha, Lancang and Nujiang rivers.
The Tropical Rainforest Heritage of Sumatra site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It comprises three Indonesian national parks on the island of Sumatra.
The Tunka or Tunkinsky National Park is a national park in south central Siberia. It covers a mountainous region centered on the Irkut River valley.
Wadi Rum, also known as the Valley of the Moon or Red mountains, is a valley cut into the sandstone and granite rock in southern Jordan, near the border with Saudi Arabia.

Wulingyuan is a scenic and historical site in the Wulingyuan District of South Central China's Hunan Province. It is noted for quartzite sandstone pillars and peaks across the site, along with many ravines.
Bohemian Paradise is a natural and cultural region in the Czech Republic. It is a designated protected landscape area.
The Cevennes is a cultural region and range of mountains in south central France, on the southeast edge of the Massif Central.
The Chaine des Puys is a north-south oriented volcanic field in the Massif Central of France, comprising cinder cones, lava domes, and maars and explosion craters.

The Curonian Spit, sometimes called Courish Split, is a thin, curved sand-dune spit that separates the Curonian Lagoon from the Baltic Sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site shared by Lithuania and Russia.
Dartmoor is an upland area in southern Devon, South West England. The moorland and surrounding land has been protected by National Park status.
The Dolomites or Pale Mountains are a mountain range in northeastern Italy. They form part of the Southern Limestone Alps.
Donana National Park is a natural reserve in Andalusia, southern Spain, in the provinces of Huelva, Cadiz and Seville.

El Torcal de Antequera is a nature reserve in the Sierra del Torcal mountain range south of the city of Antequera, in the province of Malaga in Andalusia, Spain. It is known for its unusual landforms.
The Gulf of Porto is a gulf of the Mediterranean Sea on the western facade of the island of Corsica, France, well known for its dramatic coloration and rugged cliffs.

Hyde Park is a historic urban park in Westminster, Greater London. A Royal Park, it is the large of the parks and green spaces that form a chain from Kensington Palace through Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park.
Nenets Nature Reserve is a Russian zapovednik, a strict nature reserve, in the northeast of European Russia on the coast of the Barents Sea and the delta of the Pechora River.
Peneda-Geres National Park, also known simply as Geres, is a national park in Norte Region, Portugal. It is the old protected area of Portugal.
Russian Arctic National Park is a national park of Russia. It covers a large and remote area of the Arctic Ocean, the northern part of Novaya Zemlya, and Franz Josef Land.

Saxon Switzerland is a hilly climbing area and national park in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains. It is around the Elbe valley southeast of Dresden in Saxony, Germany, adjoining Bohemian Switzerland in the Czech Republic.
Snowdonia, or Eryri, is a mountainous region and national park in North Wales. It contains the mountains of Wales over three thousand feet high, including Snowdon.
Stora Sjofallet, literally The Great Lake Falls, is a national park in Norrbotten County in northern Sweden, in Gallivare Municipality and Jokkmokk Municipality.
Yugyd Va National Park is a national park in the Komi Republic, a republic of Russia. It is a large national park in Europe.
Huanglong is a scenic and historic interest area in the northwest part of Sichuan, China. It is in the southern part of the Minshan mountain range.
Quicksand, also known as sinking sand, is a colloid consisting of fine granular material, such as sand, silt or clay, and water. It forms in saturated loose sand when the sand is suddenly agitated.

A tidal bore, often simply given as bore in context, is a tidal phenomenon in which the leading edge of the incoming tide forms a wave of water that travels up a river or narrow bay, reversing the direction of the current.

A hoodoo, also called a tent rock, fairy chimney, or earth pyramid, is a tall, thin spire of rock formed by erosion. Hoodoos typically consist of relatively soft rock topped by harder, less easily eroded stone that protects each column from the elements.
An ice cave is any type of natural cave, often a lava tube or limestone cave, that contains significant amounts of perennial ice.

A yardang is a streamlined protuberance carved from bedrock or any consolidated or semiconsolidated material by the dual action of wind abrasion by dust and sand and deflation, the removal of loose material by wind turbulence.
A dry lake bed, also called a playa, is a basin or depression that formerly contained a standing surface water body, which disappears when evaporation processes exceed recharge.

Natural salt flats or salt pans are flat, open expanses of ground covered with salt and other minerals, usually shining white under the sun. They are found in deserts and are natural formations, unlike salt evaporation ponds, which are artificial.

A shoal is a natural submerged ridge, bank, or bar that consists of, or is covered by, sand or other unconsolidated material, and rises from the bed of a body of water close to the surface or above it, which poses a danger to navigation.
A mud volcano or mud dome is a landform created by the eruption of mud or slurries, water and gases. Several geological processes may cause the formation of mud volcanoes.
Pingos are intrapermafrost ice-cored hills. They are typically conical in shape and grow and persist in permafrost environments, such as the Arctic and subarctic.

A drumlin is an elongated hill in the shape of an inverted spoon or half-buried egg formed by glacial ice acting on underlying unconsolidated till or ground moraine. The name is derived from the Irish word droimnin, little ridge.

Acadia National Park is a national park of the United States along the mid-section of the Maine coast, southwest of Bar Harbor. The park includes about half of Mount Desert Island, part of Isle au Haut, and the tip of the Schoodic Peninsula.
Arches National Park is a national park of the United States in eastern Utah. The park is adjacent to the Colorado River, north of Moab, Utah.
Badlands National Park, Lakota Makhosica, is a national park of the United States in southwestern South Dakota. The park protects sharply eroded buttes and pinnacles.
Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park is a national park of the United States in western Colorado and managed by the National Park Service.

Bryce Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States in southwestern Utah. The major feature of the park is Bryce Canyon, which, despite its name, is not a canyon but a collection of giant natural amphitheaters.
Carlsbad Caverns National Park is a national park of the United States in the Guadalupe Mountains of southeastern New Mexico. The primary attraction of the park is the show cave Carlsbad Cavern.
Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve is a national monument and national preserve in the Snake River Plain in central Idaho.
Death Valley National Park is a national park of the United States that straddles the California-Nevada border, east of the Sierra Nevada.
Everglades National Park is a United States national park that protects the southern part of the original Everglades ecosystem in Florida.
Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve is a national park of the United States that protects portions of the Central Brooks Range in northern Alaska.
Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve is a national park of the United States in Southeast Alaska, west of Juneau.
Grand Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States in northwestern Arizona. The central feature of the park is the Grand Canyon, a gorge of the Colorado River.
Grand Teton National Park is a national park of the United States in northwestern Wyoming. The park includes the major peaks of the Teton Range.
Joshua Tree National Park is a national park of the United States in southeastern California, named after the endemic Joshua tree found in the park.
La Amistad International Park, in Spanish Parque Internacional La Amistad, is a transboundary protected area in Latin America, shared between Costa Rica and Panama.
Mammoth Cave National Park is a national park of the United States in south central Kentucky. It encompasses portions of Mammoth Cave, a long known cave system in the world.
Mount Rainier National Park is a national park of the United States in the state of Washington. The park was established as a national park in the year eighteen ninety nine.

The National Mall is a landscaped park near the downtown area of Washington, D.C., the capital city of the United States. It contains and borders a number of museums of the Smithsonian Institution, art galleries, cultural institutions, and memorials.

Olympic National Park is a national park of the United States in Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula. The park has four regions: the Pacific coastline, the west-side temperate rainforest, alpine areas, and the forests of the drier east side.
Petrified Forest National Park is a national park of the United States in northeastern Arizona. Named for its large deposits of petrified wood, the park is in the desert.
Rocky Mountain National Park is a national park of the United States in north central Colorado, within the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains.
Saguaro National Park is a national park of the United States in southeastern Arizona. The park consists of two separate areas, the Tucson Mountain District and the Rincon Mountain District.
Sian Kaan Biosphere Reserve is a biosphere reserve in Tulum Municipality in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Sequoia National Park is a national park of the United States in the southern Sierra Nevada east of Visalia, California.

The Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park is the union of Waterton Lakes National Park in Canada and Glacier National Park in the United States. Both parks are declared Biosphere Reserves by UNESCO.
White Sands National Park is a national park of the United States in New Mexico and completely surrounded by White Sands Missile Range. The park is in the Tularosa Basin.
Wind Cave National Park is a national park of the United States north of the town of Hot Springs in western South Dakota. It was established by President Theodore Roosevelt.
Wood Buffalo National Park is a large national park of Canada. It is in northeastern Alberta and the southern Northwest Territories.

Zion National Park is a national park of the United States in southwestern Utah near the town of Springdale. Located at the junction of the Colorado Plateau, Great Basin, and Mojave Desert regions, the park has a unique geography.
The Jau National Park is a national park in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. It is one of the large forest reserves in South America, and part of a World Heritage Site.
Lencois Maranhenses National Park is a national park in Maranhao state in northeastern Brazil, just east of the Baia de Sao Jose.
Nahuel Huapi National Park is the old national park in Argentina, established as Parque Nacional del Sud. It surrounds Nahuel Huapi Lake in the foothills of the Patagonian Andes.
Serra da Capivara National Park is a national park in the northeastern region of Brazil. The area has many prehistoric paintings.
The Serra do Mar is a system of mountain ranges and escarpments in southeastern Brazil.
Gannett Peak is the high mountain peak in the United States state of Wyoming. It lies in the Wind River Range within the Bridger Wilderness of the Bridger-Teton National Forest.

Yugansky Nature Reserve is a Russian zapovednik, a strict ecological reserve, in the basin of the Bolshoy Yugan River, a left tributary of the Ob River. The reserve is in the central part of the West Siberian Plain.
The European Plain, also referred to as the Great European Plain, is a large plain in Europe and a major feature of one of four major topographical units of Europe, the Central and Interior Lowlands.
The International zone of the Sea of Okhotsk, known by its nickname the Peanut Hole, is an area of international waters at the center of the Sea of Okhotsk.

The kitamaebune was a shipping route, and also the ships involved, in Japan from the Edo period to the Meiji era. The route went from Osaka through the Seto Inland Sea and the Kanmon Straits to ports in Hokuriku on the Sea of Japan and later to Hokkaido.
A genet is a member of the genus Genetta, which consists of small African carnivorans. The common genet is the sole genet present in Europe and occurs in the Iberian Peninsula, Italy and France.

Maras, subfamily Dolichotinae, are a group of rodents in the family Caviidae. These large relatives of guinea pigs are common in the Patagonian steppes of Argentina, but also live in Paraguay and elsewhere in South America.
Hypericum perforatum, commonly known as Saint John's wort, is a flowering plant in the family Hypericaceae. It is a hairless, perennial herb with woody roots, yellow flowers marked by black glands.
Morchella esculenta, commonly known as common morel, morel, yellow morel, true morel, morel mushroom, and sponge morel, is a species of fungus in the family Morchellaceae of the Ascomycota.
Salmonella enterica, formerly Salmonella choleraesuis, is a rod-shaped, flagellate, facultative anaerobic, Gram-negative bacterium and a species of the genus Salmonella.

The Astoria-Megler Bridge is a steel cantilever through-truss bridge in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States that spans the lower Columbia River. It carries a section of a highway from Astoria, Oregon, to Megler, Washington.
Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Bridge is a long roadway bridge in Qingdao, Shandong Province, China, which is part of the Jiaozhou Bay Connection Project.

In geochemistry, paleoclimatology, archaeology, and paleoceanography, delta carbon thirteen is a normalized ratio of the two stable isotopes of carbon, carbon thirteen and carbon twelve, reported in parts per thousand.

In geochemistry, paleoclimatology and paleoceanography, delta oxygen eighteen is a measure of the deviation in ratio of stable isotopes oxygen eighteen and oxygen sixteen. It is commonly used as a measure of the temperature of precipitation.
In calculus, the squeeze theorem, also known as the sandwich theorem, is a theorem regarding the limit of a function that is bounded between two other functions.
The Fisher-Kasteleyn-Temperley algorithm, named after Michael Fisher, Pieter Kasteleyn, and Neville Temperley, counts the number of perfect matchings in a planar graph in polynomial time.
A period on the periodic table is a row of chemical elements. All elements in a row have the same number of electron shells.
A material is a substance or mixture of substances that constitutes an object. Materials can be pure or impure, living or non-living matter.

Ununennium, also known as eka-francium or element one hundred and nineteen, is a hypothetical chemical element. Ununennium is the temporary systematic name used until the element has been discovered, confirmed, and a permanent name approved.
Fluorosulfuric acid is an inorganic compound. It is one of the strong acids commercially available.
In chemistry, an oxonium ion is any cation containing an oxygen atom that has three bonds and a positive formal charge. A simple oxonium ion is the hydronium ion.
Potassium perchlorate is an inorganic salt. Like other perchlorates, this salt is a strong oxidizer when the solid is heated at high temperature.
In chemical engineering, process design is the choice and sequencing of units for desired physical and chemical transformation of materials.
Thomson scattering is the elastic scattering of electromagnetic radiation by a free charged particle, as described by classical electromagnetism. It is the low-energy limit of Compton scattering.
The discovery of the neutron and its properties was central to the extraordinary developments in atomic physics in the early part of the twentieth century.
Wien's approximation, also sometimes called Wien's law or the Wien distribution law, is a law of physics used to describe the spectrum of thermal radiation, frequently called the blackbody function.

There are many known moons of the planet Jupiter. This number does not include a number of meter-sized moonlets thought to be shed from the inner moons, nor possible irregular moons that were briefly captured by telescopes.
Chiron is a ringed small Solar System body in the outer Solar System, orbiting the Sun between Saturn and Uranus. It was an early identified member of a class of objects now known as centaurs.
Epsilon Eridani, proper name Ran, is a star in the southern constellation of Eridanus. It is visible from much of the surface of Earth.

WISE zero eight five five minus zero seven one four is a brown dwarf of spectral class Y, in the constellation Hydra. It was discovered by Kevin Luhman using data from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer.
Cancri Ae, officially named Janssen, is an exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like host star. The exoplanet has a mass of several Earth masses and a diameter about twice that of the Earth.

The Bug Nebula, also known as the Butterfly Nebula, is a bipolar planetary nebula in the constellation Scorpius. The structure in this planetary nebula is among the complex ever seen in any planetary nebulae.
The Scutum-Centaurus Arm, also known as Scutum-Crux arm, is a long, diffuse curving streamer of stars, gas and dust that spirals outward from the proximate end of the central bar of the Milky Way.
The star cluster R one hundred and thirty six is the central concentration of stars that lies at the centre of the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Messier Forty-nine is a giant elliptical galaxy in the equatorial constellation of Virgo. This galaxy was discovered by astronomer Charles Messier.
Messier Seventy-seven, also known as the Squid Galaxy, is a barred spiral galaxy in the constellation Cetus. It was discovered by Pierre Mechain, who originally described it as a nebula.
Messier One hundred and six is an intermediate spiral galaxy in the constellation Canes Venatici. It was discovered by Pierre Mechain.
The Centaurus A group is a complex group of galaxies in the constellations Hydra, Centaurus, and Virgo. The group may be roughly divided into two subgroups.
The Maffei group, also known as the IC three forty two Group, corresponds to one or two galaxy groups close to the Local Group.
The Huge Large Quasar Group is a possible structure or pseudo-structure of quasars, referred to as a large quasar group, that measures billions of light-years across.
The Local Void is a vast, empty region of space, lying adjacent to the Local Group. It is now known to be composed of three separate sectors, separated by bridges of wispy filaments.
A supernova in the galaxy NGC five two five three was discovered shortly after it had reached its maximum brightness. In terms of apparent brightness, it was a bright supernova.

In August two thousand and six, the International Astronomical Union adopted a new definition of the term planet, which stated that, in the Solar System, a planet is a celestial body in orbit around the Sun with sufficient mass to assume hydrostatic equilibrium.

In celestial mechanics, clearing the neighbourhood, or dynamical dominance, around the orbit of a celestial body describes the body becoming gravitationally dominant such that there are no other bodies of comparable size other than its natural satellites.
A minor-planet moon is an astronomical object that orbits a minor planet as its natural satellite.
Gamma-ray burst emission mechanisms are theories that explain how the energy from a gamma-ray burst progenitor is turned into radiation.
Gamma-ray burst progenitors are the types of celestial objects that can emit gamma-ray bursts. These bursts show an extraordinary degree of diversity.
An S-type star, or just S star, is a cool giant star with approximately equal quantities of carbon and oxygen in its atmosphere.

A yellow supergiant is a star, generally of spectral type F or G, having a supergiant luminosity class. They are stars that have evolved away from the main sequence, expanding and becoming more luminous.

A flare star is a variable star that can undergo unpredictable dramatic increases in brightness for a few minutes. It is believed that the flares on flare stars are analogous to solar flares in that they are powered by magnetic energy stored in the atmospheres of the stars.
An H I region is a cloud in the interstellar medium composed of neutral atomic hydrogen, in addition to the local abundance of helium and other elements.
A galaxy group or group of galaxies is an aggregation of galaxies comprising a few gravitationally bound members, each at least as luminous as the Milky Way.

The type-cD galaxy is a galaxy morphology classification, a subtype of type-D giant elliptical galaxy. Characterized by a large halo of stars, they can be found near the centres of some rich galaxy clusters.

A Lyman-alpha emitter is a type of distant galaxy that emits Lyman-alpha radiation from neutral hydrogen. Known emitters are extremely distant, and because of the finite travel time of light they provide glimpses into the history of the universe.

Solar phenomena are natural phenomena which occur within the atmosphere of the Sun. They take many forms, including solar wind, radio wave flux, solar flares, coronal mass ejections, coronal heating and sunspots.
The NASA and IPAC Extragalactic Database is an online astronomical database for astronomers that collates and cross-correlates astronomical information on extragalactic objects.

The Two Micron All-Sky Survey was an astronomical survey of the whole sky in infrared light. It took place in two different locations, at a Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in Arizona and at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile.
